Description: Providing ramp 1.20 mt. wide and up to 3 mt lonag  with 1:10 slop and using brickwork in foundation and pcc and also 25 mm thick black granite stone stone strips not less than 100mmm in width in show toothed fashion for the vikalang persons (for slope ramp) and also fixing  M.S. pipe railing of 50mm dia pipe in 3rows supported by M.S. angel of 75x75x6mm size at every corner and 1.5mtr center to center incl. fixing in concreate block 0.35x0.35x0.35 incl. cutting jointing welding threading drilling and apply one coat of anticorrosive paint and 3coat of approved quality oil paint also providing and fixing 25mm th. granite stone strips not less then 100mm in width in show to toothed fashion for the Handicap Person Etc,. Completed and directed as par design and directed by engg. incharge.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• The ramp shall be constructed using brick masonry in foundation with cement mortar of appropriate proportion, over a base of plain cement concrete (PCC) of suitable grade. The ramp surface shall be finished with 25 mm thick black granite stone strips of not less than 100 mm width, laid in a saw-tooth (anti-skid/tactile) pattern to ensure safe movement for physically challenged persons.
  • The handrail shall be made of mild steel pipe of 50 mm diameter, provided in three rows, supported on M.S. angle posts of size 75 × 75 × 6 mm at corners and at maximum 1.50 m center-to-center spacing. The posts shall be fixed in concrete blocks of size 0.35 m × 0.35 m × 0.35 m.
  • All steel components shall be treated with one coat of anti-corrosive primer and finished with three coats of approved quality oil paint. Granite shall be of approved quality, uniform thickness, and free from cracks or defects. All materials shall conform to relevant standards such as IS 456 and IS 800 or equivalent.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall include excavation, construction of foundation, PCC base, and brick masonry to form the ramp structure with a uniform slope of 1:10 as specified. The surface shall be properly compacted, levelled, and finished.
  • The 25 mm thick granite strips shall be fixed over the ramp surface in a saw-tooth pattern to provide anti-skid properties and tactile guidance. Proper alignment, spacing, and bonding shall be ensured.
  • The M.S. pipe railing shall be fabricated, erected, and fixed in position by cutting, welding, threading, and drilling as required. The railing shall be securely anchored in concrete blocks and aligned properly. All weld joints shall be ground smooth, and painting shall be carried out after proper surface preparation.
  • The finished ramp shall be even, stable, and safe for use, with proper slope, alignment, and aesthetic finish. All work shall be carried out as per approved design and instructions of the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The ramp shall be measured in square meters (Sqm) of plan area or as specified in the schedule, in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include cost of excavation, PCC, brickwork, granite strips, steel railing, concrete blocks, painting, labour, materials, tools, and all operations required to complete the work.
  • No separate payment shall be made for excavation, fixing, welding, painting, or tactile strips, as these shall be deemed included in the item rate. The item shall be measured as completed and accepted as per the directions of the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Square Meter.

Description: Providing & fixing of Aluminium Composite Panel (ACP), 3 mm thick in required colours for interiors/exteriors consisting of two layers of aluminium skins of 0.25 mm thick sandwiching a thermo plastic core in continuous lamination process with PVDF coating for interior/exterior grades ensuring long colour and no fungal attacks. Base frame work with aluminium sections shall be fixed over the brick work/MS and the above aluminium panels shall be fixed to the frame work as cladding.It includes cost of labour, materials, accessories, adhesives, scaffolding, wastages, transport, taxes, fixing into a neat finish in aesthetic point of view, without any undulations in facias all complete as per drawing and instruction of engineer in-charge.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• The Aluminium Composite Panel (ACP) shall be 3 mm thick consisting of two aluminium skins of 0.25 mm thickness each, bonded to a thermoplastic core under continuous lamination process. The outer surface shall be coated with PVDF (Polyvinylidene Fluoride) coating suitable for exterior/interior applications, ensuring long-lasting colour, weather resistance, and protection against fungal attack.
  • The ACP sheets shall be of approved make, uniform thickness, free from defects, warping, or surface irregularities. The supporting framework shall be made from aluminium sections of suitable size and thickness, designed to withstand wind load and other structural requirements.
  • All accessories such as brackets, cleats, fasteners, sealants (silicone), adhesives, and fixing hardware shall be of approved quality. The materials shall conform to relevant standards such as IS 14762 or equivalent.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall include fabrication and fixing of ACP cladding over aluminium framework complete in all respects as per approved drawings and instructions of the Engineer-in-Charge. The base aluminium framework shall be securely fixed to brickwork or M.S. structure using appropriate fasteners, ensuring proper alignment, plumb, and level.
  • The ACP panels shall be cut, bent, and fixed over the framework using suitable methods such as screwing, riveting, or adhesive fixing, as per design requirements. Necessary grooves, joints, and edge finishing shall be provided to achieve proper panel alignment and expansion allowance.
  • All joints shall be sealed with approved quality silicone sealant to ensure water tightness. The surface shall be finished neatly without undulations, dents, or visible defects. Proper scaffolding, safety measures, and handling shall be ensured during installation.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The ACP cladding shall be measured in square meters (Sqm) of finished surface area, in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include cost of ACP sheets, aluminium framework, accessories, sealants, adhesives, labour, scaffolding, transportation, wastage, and all operations required to complete the work.
  • No separate payment shall be made for framework, fasteners, cutting, jointing, or sealing, as these shall be deemed included in the item rate. The item shall be measured as completed and accepted as per the directions of the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Square Meter.

Description: Providing &fixing 110 mm dia 6.0 kgf/cm2 working pressure polythene pipes (pvc pipe) of approved quality of isi brand for rain water spout minimum length of pipe not less than 60cm and fixing with wall c.m (1:1) pipes should be provided at maximum interval of 1 mtr c/c etc.comp.as per directed.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• The rain water spout pipe shall be of 110 mm diameter PVC/polythene pipe having working pressure of 6.0 kgf/cm², of approved quality and make, conforming to relevant IS standards such as IS 4985 or equivalent. The pipe shall be of ISI marked brand, free from cracks, holes, or manufacturing defects.
  • The pipe length shall not be less than 600 mm (0.60 m) and shall be suitable for use as rainwater outlet/spout. The fixing material shall include cement mortar 1:1 (1 cement : 1 coarse sand) for embedding and securing the pipe in position.
  • All materials including cement and sand shall be of approved quality and conform to relevant standards.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The rain water spout pipe shall be measured on number basis (Each), in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include cost of pipe, cement mortar, labour, cutting, fixing, sealing, and all materials and operations required to complete the work.
  • No separate payment shall be made for making holes, sealing joints, or incidental works, as these shall be deemed included in the item rate. The item shall be measured as completed and accepted as per the directions of the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Nos.

Description: Providing and laying cement concrete 1:4:8 (1- Cement : 4- coarse sand : 8- hand broken stone aggregates 40 mm nominal size) and curing complete excluding cost of formwork in (A) Foundation and Plinth

sections.title: Materials
sections.description: • Water shall conform to M-1. Cement shall conform to M-3. Sand shall conform to M-6 stone aggregate 40 mm. nominal size shall conform to M-12.

subsections.title: General
subsections.description: • Before stating concrete the bed of foundation trenches shall be cleared of all loose materials, leveled, watered and rammed as directed.

subsections.title: Proportion of Mix
subsections.description: • The proportion of cement, sand and coarse aggregate shall be one part of cement. 4 parts of sand and 8 parts of stone aggregates and shall be measured by volume.

subsections.title: Mixing
subsections.description: • The concrete shall be mixed in a mechanical mixer at the site of work. Hand mixing may however be allowed for smaller quantity of work if approved by the Engineer-in-charge. When hand mixing is permitted by the Engineer-in-charge in case "of break-down of machineries and in the interest of the work, it shall be carried out on a water tight platform and care shall be taken to ensure that mixing is continued until the mass is uniform in colour and consistency, However in such case 10% more cement than otherwise period 1 1/2 to 2 minutes. The quantity of water shall be just sufficient to produce a dense concrete of required workability for the purpose.

subsections.title: Transporting & Placing the Concrete
subsections.description:
• The concrete shall be handed from the place, of mixing to the final position in not more than 15 minutes by the method as directed and shall be placed into its final-position, compacted and finished within 30 minutes of mixing with water i.e. before the setting commences.
  • The concrete shall be laid in layers of 15 cms. to 20 cms.
  • The concrete shall be rammed with heavy iron rammers and rapidly to get the required compaction and to allow ail the interstices to be filled with mortar.

subsections.title: Curing
subsections.description: • After the final set, the concrete-shall be kept continuously wet if required by pounding for a period of not less then 7 days form the date of placement.

sections.title: Mode Of Measurement & Payment
sections.description:
• The concrete shall be measured for its length, breadth and depth, limiting dimensions to those specified on plan or as directed.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one cubic meter.

Description: Providing & supplying approval quality of heavy duty wheel chair with standard specification with seat belt and hand brack etc. completd.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• The wheelchair shall be of heavy-duty type, of approved make and quality, designed for use by physically challenged persons. The frame shall be made of high-strength steel or equivalent material, with corrosion-resistant finish and robust construction suitable for regular use.
  • The wheelchair shall be equipped with standard features including comfortable seat and backrest, safety seat belt, hand brakes, footrests, armrests, and rear wheels with hand rims for manual operation. The front wheels shall be of swivel type for easy maneuverability. The seat and backrest shall be cushioned and covered with durable, washable material of approved quality.
  • The wheelchair shall have adequate load carrying capacity, smooth rolling wheels, and reliable braking system. All components shall be of approved quality, free from defects, and conforming to relevant standards such as IS 6571 or equivalent.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall include supplying and delivering the heavy-duty wheelchair complete in all respects at site as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge. The wheelchair shall be fully assembled, tested, and ready for use.
  • All moving parts such as wheels, brakes, and folding mechanisms (if applicable) shall be properly checked to ensure smooth and safe operation. The seat belt and braking system shall function effectively. The wheelchair shall be stable, properly balanced, and free from manufacturing defects.
  • The supplier shall ensure proper handling and delivery without damage. Any defective parts shall be replaced before handing over. The final product shall be demonstrated for proper functioning to the satisfaction of the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The wheelchair shall be measured on number basis (Each), in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include cost of wheelchair, accessories (seat belt, brakes, footrest, armrest), transportation, delivery, and all incidental charges required to complete the item.
  • No separate payment shall be made for accessories or minor fittings, as these shall be deemed included in the item rate. The item shall be measured as completed and accepted as per the directions of the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Nos.

Description: Providing and fixing modular indicating call bell.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• The call bell shall be of modular type with indicating facility, of approved make and quality, suitable for installation in offices, control rooms, or residential/commercial buildings. The unit shall consist of a bell push switch and an indicator unit with audible bell and visual indication (light/LED).
  • The modular components shall be compatible with standard modular switch plates and boxes. The bell unit shall operate on standard electrical supply and shall be complete with necessary accessories such as modular switch, indicator lamp, bell unit, wiring terminals, and mounting box.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall include supplying and fixing of the modular indicating call bell complete in all respects. The bell push switch shall be installed at the designated location, and the bell unit with indicator shall be installed at the required position as per layout.
  • Necessary wiring connections shall be carried out using suitable insulated wires, properly routed through conduits or casing as required. All connections shall be secure and properly insulated. The modular plate shall be fixed neatly, ensuring proper alignment and finish.
  • The system shall be tested after installation to ensure proper functioning of both audible bell and visual indicator. The installation shall be completed without damaging surrounding surfaces and shall be to the satisfaction of the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The modular indicating call bell shall be measured on number basis (Each), in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include cost of modular bell, switch, indicator, wiring, accessories, labour, fixing, testing, and commissioning complete.
  • No separate payment shall be made for wiring, modular plates, or incidental items, as these shall be deemed included in the item rate. The item shall be measured as completed and accepted as per the directions of the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Nos.

Description: CCS - 2200 AHUJA brand Counter Communication System on controll / inquiry room

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• The system shall be a counter communication system of approved make such as Ahuja Model CCS-2200 or equivalent, designed for clear two-way communication between operator and public across counters or partitions.
  • The system shall consist of a master unit and a remote unit with built-in microphones and speakers, suitable for hands-free communication. It shall have adjustable volume control, noise reduction capability, and echo-free sound transmission. The unit shall operate on standard power supply and shall be provided with all necessary accessories such as power adaptor, interconnecting cables, microphone units, and mounting fixtures.
  • All components shall be of approved quality, robust construction, and suitable for continuous operation in control rooms or inquiry counters.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall include supplying, installing, testing, and commissioning of the counter communication system complete in all respects. The master unit shall be installed at the operator side and the remote unit at the public/customer side as per approved layout.
  • All wiring and connections shall be carried out neatly, ensuring proper routing and protection of cables. The system shall be fixed securely on the counter or wall as required. Necessary drilling, fixing, and mounting arrangements shall be carried out carefully without damaging existing surfaces.
  • The system shall be tested for clear voice transmission, proper functioning of volume control, and absence of noise or distortion. The installation shall be completed to the satisfaction of the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The counter communication system shall be measured on number basis (Each), in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include cost of equipment, accessories, wiring, installation, testing, commissioning, labour, and all incidental works required to complete the item.
  • No separate payment shall be made for cables, fittings, mounting accessories, or testing, as these shall be deemed included in the item rate. The item shall be measured as completed and accepted as per the directions of the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Nos.

Description: Providing and fixing 0.4mm thick Stainless steel plate of with embosing the braille lipi signages on the top rail of the hand rail fixed on ramp .(Size - 9" x 4").

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• The signage plate shall be made from 0.4 mm thick stainless steel sheet of Grade 304 quality, having a smooth, corrosion-resistant finish. The plate shall be provided with embossed Braille (Braille Lipi) signage, accurately formed to ensure proper tactile readability for visually impaired users.
  • The size of the plate shall be 9 inches × 4 inches (approximately 230 mm × 100 mm). The embossing shall be precise, with proper spacing and height of Braille dots as per accessibility requirements. The plate shall be suitable for fixing on the top rail of handrails installed on ramps.
  • All materials used shall be of approved quality, free from defects, and resistant to wear, corrosion, and environmental exposure.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall include fabrication, supplying, and fixing of the stainless steel Braille plate on the top surface of the handrail at the specified location. The plate shall be fixed using suitable adhesive or mechanical fasteners as approved, ensuring firm bonding without affecting the finish of the handrail.
  • Proper alignment and positioning shall be maintained to ensure accessibility and ease of use. The fixing shall be done carefully without damaging the handrail surface. The Braille embossing shall be clear, accurate, and properly oriented.
  • The finished plate shall be smooth, securely fixed, and free from sharp edges, scratches, or defects. The installation shall comply with accessibility guidelines and instructions of the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The Braille plate shall be measured on number basis (Each) for the specified size (9" × 4"), in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include cost of stainless steel plate, Braille embossing, fixing materials (adhesive/fasteners), labour, and all incidental works required to complete the item.
  • No separate payment shall be made for fixing accessories or surface preparation, as these shall be deemed included in the item rate. The item shall be measured as completed and accepted as per the directions of the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Nos.

Description: Providing and laying cement concrete 1:2:4 (1- Cement : 2- Coarse sand : 4- graded stone aggregates 20 mm nominal size) and curing complete excluding cost of formwork in (A) Foundation and Plinth

sections.title: Materials
sections.description: • Water shall conform to M-1. Cement shall conform to M-3. Sand shall conform to M-6. Grit shall conform to M-8. Graded stone aggregate 20 mm nominal size shall conform to M-12.

subsections.title: General
subsections.description:
• The concrete mix is not required to be designed by preliminary testes. The proportion of the concrete mix shall be 1:2:4 (1 cement : 2 coarse sand : 4 graded stone aggregate 20 mm. nominal size) by volume concrete work shall have exposed concrete surface or as specified in the item.
  • The designation ordinary M-100, M-150, M-200, M-250 specified as per I.S. correspond approximately to 1:3:6, 1.2:4, 1:1:1/2:3 and 1:1:2 nominal mix of ordinary concrete by volume respectively.
  • The water cement ratios shall not be more than specified in the above table. The cement content of the mix specified in the table shall be increased if the quantity of water in mix has to be met eased to overcome the difficulties of placements and compaction so that the water-cement ratio specified in the table is not exceeded.
  • Workability of the concrete shall be controlled by maintaining a water -cement-ratio that is found to give a concrete mix which is just sufficient wet to be placed and compacted without difficulty with the means available.
  • The maximum size of course aggregate shall be as large as possible within the limits specified but in no case greater than one forth of the minimum thickness of the member provided that the concrete can be placed without difficulty so as to surround all reinforcement thoroughly and to fill the corners of the form. 
  • For reinforced concrete work; coarse aggregates having a nominal size of 20 mm. are generally considered satisfactory.
  • For heavily reinforced concrete members as in the case of ribs of main beams, the nominal maximum size of coarse aggregate should usually be restricted to 5 mm. less than the minimum clear distance between the main bar or 5 mm. less than the minimum cover to the reinforcement whichever is smaller.
  • Where the reinforcement is widely spaced as in solid slabs, limitations of size of the aggregate may not be so important, and the nominal maximum size may some times be as great as or greater than the minimum cover.
  • Admixture maybe used in concrete only with approval of Engineer-in-charge based upon the evidence that with the passage of time neither the compressive strength of concrete is reduced not are other requisite qualities of concrete and steel impaired by the use of such admixtures.

subsections.title: Workmanship
subsections.description: • Proportioning shall be done by volume, except which shall be measured in terms of bags of 50 kg. weight, the volume of one such bag being taken as 0.0342 cu. meter Boxes of suitable size shall be used for measuring sand aggregate. The size of boxes (internal) shall be 35 x 25 cms. and 40 cms deep while measuring the aggregate and sand the boxes shall be filled without shaking ramming or hammering. The proportioning of sand shall be on the basis of its dry volume and in case of damp saner, allowances for bulk age shall be made.

subsections.title: Mixing
subsections.description:
• The concrete shall be handed from the place, of mixing to the final position in not more than 15 minutes by the method as directed and shall be placed into its final-position, compacted and finished within 30 minutes of mixing with water i.e. before the setting commences.
  • The concrete shall be laid in layers of 15 cms. to 20 cms.
  • For all work, concrete shall be mixed in a mechanical mixed which along with other accessories shall be. kept in first class working condition and so maintained throughout the construction Measured quantity of aggregate, sand and cement required for each batch shall be poured into the claim of the mechanical mixer while it is continuously running. After half a minute of dry mixing measured quantity of water required for each batch of concrete mix shall be added gradually and mixing continued for another one and a half minute Mixing shall be continued till materials are uniformly distributed and uniform colour of the entire mass is obtained and each individual particle of the coarse aggregate shows complete coating of mortar containing its proportionate amount of cement. In no case shall the mixing he done for less than 2 minutes after-oil ingredients have been put into the mixer.
  • When hand mixing is permitted by the Engineer-in-charge for small jobs or for certain other reasons, it shall be done on the smooth watertight platform large enough to allow efficient tuning over the ingredients of concrete before and after adding water Mixing platform shall be so arranged that no foreign malarial gets mixed with concrete nor does the mixing water flow out. Cement in required number of bags shall be spread in n layer of uniform thickness on the mixing platform. Dry coarse and fine aggregate and cement shall then be mixed thoroughly be turning over to get a mixture to uniform colour. Specified quantity water shall then be added gradually through a rose can and the mass turned over till a mix of required consistency is obtained. In hand mixing quantity of cement shall be increased by 10 percent above that specified.
  • Mixers which haw been out of use for more than 30 minutes shall be thoroughly cleaned before putting in a new batch. Unless otherwise agreed to by the Engineer in-charge the first batch of concrete from the mixture shall contain only two thirds of normal quantity of coarse aggregate Mixing plant shall be thoroughly cleaned before changing from one type of cement to another.

subsections.title: Consistency
subsections.description: • The degree of consistency which shall depend upon the nature of the work and methods of vibration of concrete, shall be determined by regular slump tests in accordance with I.S. 1199-193. The skimp of 10 mm. to 25 mm shall be adopted when vibrators are used and 80 mm. when vibrators are not used.

subsections.title: Inspection
subsections.description:
• Contractor shall give the Engineer-in-charge due notice before placing any concrete in the forms to permit him to inspect and accept the false work and forms as to their strength, alignment and general fitness but such inspection shall not relieve the contractor of his responsibility for the safely of men machinery materials and for results obtained immediately before concreting all forms shall be thoroughly cleaned.
  • Centering design and its erection shall be got approved from the engineer-in-charge. One carpenter with helper shall invariably be kept present throughout the period of concreting. Movement of labour and other persons shall be totally prohibited for reinforcement laid in position. For access to different parts suitable mobile platforms shall be provided so that steel reinforcement in position is not disturbed. For ensuring proper cover, mortar blocks of suitable size shall be cast and tied to the reinforcement. Timber kapachi or metal pieces shall not be used for this purpose.

subsections.title: Transporting and laying
subsections.description:
• The method of transporting and placing concrete shall be as approved. Concrete shall be so transported and placed that no contamination, segregation or loss of its constituent material takes place. All from work shall be cleaned and made free from standing   water   dust,   show   or   ice   immediately   before   placing   of   concrete. No concrete shall be placed in any part of the structure until the approval of the engineer-in-charge has been obtained.
  • Concreting shall proceed continuously over the area between construction joints. Fresh concrete proper contraction joint is formed. Concrete shall be compacted in its final position within 30 minutes of its discharge from the mixer. Except where otherwise agreed to by the engineer-in-charge, concrete shall be deposited in horizontal layers to a compacted depth of not more than 0.45 meter when internal vibrators are used and not exceeding 0.30 meter in all other cases.
  • Unless otherwise agreed to by the Engineer-in-charge concrete shall be dropped in to place from a height exceeding 2 meters. When trucking or chutes are used they shall be kept close and used in such a way as to avoid segregation. When concreting has to be resumed on a surface which has hardened, it shall be roughened, swept clean, thoroughly wetted and covered with a 13 mm. thick layer of mortar composed of cement and sand in the same ratio as in the concrete mix itself. This 13 mm. layer of mortar shall be freshly mixed and placed immediately before placing of new concrete. Where concrete has not fully hardened, all lateness shall be removed by scrubbing the wet surface with wire or bristle brushes, care being taken to avoid dislodgement of any particles of coarse aggregate. The surface shall then be thoroughly wetted, all free water removed and then coated with neat cement grout. The first layer of concrete to be placed on this surface shall not exceed 150 mm. in thickness and shall be well rammed against old work, particular attention being given to corners and close spots.
  • All concrete shall be compacted to produce a dense homogeneous mass with the assistance of vibrators, unless otherwise permitted by the Engineer-in-charge for exceptional cases, such as concreting under water, where vibrators cannot be used. Sufficient vibrators in serviceable condition shall be kept at site so that spare equipment is always available in the even of breakdowns. Concrete shall be judged to be compacted when the mortar fills the spaces between the coarse aggregate and begins to cream up to form an even surface. Compaction shall be completed before the initial setting stats i.e. within 30 minutes of addition of water to dry mixture. During compaction, it shall be observed that needle vibrators are not applied on reinforcement which is likely to destroy the bond between concrete and reinforcement.

subsections.title: Curing
subsections.description: • Immediately after compaction, concrete weather including rain, running water, shocks, vibration, traffic, rapid temperature charges, frost and drying out process. It shall be covered with wet sacking has Sian or other similar absorbent material approved, soon after the initial set, and shall be kept continuously wet for a period of not less than 14 days from the date of placement. Masonry work over foundation concrete may be started after 48 hours of its laying but curing of concrete shall be continued for a minimum period of 14 days.

subsections.title: Sampling and testing of concrete
subsections.description:
• Samples from fresh concrete shall be taken as per I.S. 1199-1959 and cubes shall be made, cured and tested at 7 days of 28 days as per requirements in accordance with I.S. 526-1959. A random sampling procedure shall be adopted to ensure that each concrete batch shall have a reasonable chance of being tested i.e. the sampling should be spread over the entire period of concreting and cover all mixing units. The minimum frequency of sampling of concrete of each grade shall be in accordance with following:
            Quantity of Concrete In Work   No. Of Samples
                            1-5 cmt     1
                            6-15 cmt 2
                           16-30 cmt     3
                           31-50 cmt            4
  • Note :  At least one simple shall be taken from each shift, Ten test specimens shall be made from each sample, five for testing at 7 days and the remaining five at 28 days. The samples of concrete shall be taken on each day of concreting as per above frequency. The number of specimens may be suitably increased  as  deemed  necessary  by  the  Engineer-in-charge  when  procedure  of  tests  given  above reveals a poor quality of concrete and in other special cases.
  • The average of the group of cubes cast for each day shall not be less than the specified cube strength of 150 K/g Cm 2 at 28 days. 20% of the cubes cast for each day may have value less than the specified strength provided the lowest value is not less than 85% of the specified strength. If the concrete made in accordance with the proportions given for a particular grade does not yield the specified strength, such concrete shall be classified as belonging to the appropriate lower grade. Concrete made in accordance with the Proportions given for a particular grade shall not, however be placed in a higher grade on the ground that the test strength are higher then the minimum specified.

subsections.title: Stripping
subsections.description:
• The Engineer-in-charge shall be informed in advance by the contractor of hr> intention to strike the form work. While fixing  the  time  of  removal  of  form  work,  due  consideration  shall  be  given  to  local  conditions, character of the structure, the weather and other conditions that influence the setting of concrete and of the materials used in the mix. In normal circumstances (generally where temperatures are above 20.C) and where ordinary concrete is used, forms may be struck after expire or periods specified in item No.9.1 (A) for respective item of form work.
  • All form work shall be removed without causing any shock or vibration as would damage the concrete. Before the soft and struts are removed, the concrete surface shall be gradually exposed, where necessary in order to ascertain that concrete has sufficiently hardened. Centering shall be gradually and uniformly lowered in such a manner as to permit the concrete to take stresses due to its own weight uniformly and gradually. Where internal metal tiles are permitted, they or their removable parts shall be extracted without causing any damage to the concrete and remaining holes filled with mortar. No permanently embedded metal part shall have less than 25 mm. cover to the finished concrete surface. Where it is intended to re-use the form work, it shall be cleaned and made good to the satisfaction of the Engineer-in-charge. After removal of form work and shutting, the Executive Engineer shall inspect the work and satisfy by random checks that concrete produced is of good quality.
  • Immediately after the removal of forms, all exposed bolts etc. passing through the cement concrete member and used for stuttering or any other purpose shall be cut inside the cement concrete member to a depth of at least 25 m. below the surface of the concrete and the resulting holes be filled by cement mortar, all fins, caused by form joints, all cavities produced by the removal of form tiles and all other holes and depressions, honeycomb spots, broken edges or comers and other defects, shall be thoroughly cleaned", saturated with water and carefully pointed an rendered true with mortar of cement and fine aggregate mixed in proportions used in the grade of concrete that is being furnished and of as dry consistency as is possible to use. Considerable pressure shall be applied in filling and pointing to ensure through filling in all voids. Surface which are pointed shall be kept moist for a period of 24 hours. If rock pockets/honeycombs in the opinion of the Engineer-in-charge are of such an extent or character as to effect the strength of the structure materially or to endanger the life of the steel reinforcement, he may declare the concrete defective and require the removal and replacement of the portions of structure affected.

sections.title: Mode Of Measurement & Payment
sections.description:
• The consolidated cubical contents of concrete work as specified in item shall be measured. No deduction shall be made for (a) Ends of dissimilar materials such as joints, beams, posts, girders, falters, purling trusses, corbels and steps etc., up to 500 Sq, Cm. in section.
  • The rate includes cost of all materials labour, tools and plant required for mixing, placing in position, vibrating and compacting, finishing, as directed, curing and all other incidental expenses for producing center of specified strength. The rate excludes the cost of form work.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one cubic meter.

Description: Providing and fixing required size Stainless steel plate of 1.0mm thickness with regular printed signage at top in black colour at top part of plate and respective brialle lipi sgnages at bottom part the plate , S.S. Plate to be fixed on 10mm thick clear acrylic sheet , this whole assembly to be fixed on wall with four numbers of SS studs etc complete as per instructions of engineer in-charge.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• The signage shall be made from 1.0 mm thick stainless steel plate of Grade 304 quality, having a smooth, corrosion-resistant surface finish. The top portion of the plate shall have printed signage in black colour with clear and legible text or symbols as per approved design. The bottom portion shall include embossed Braille (Braille Lipi) signage, accurately formed for tactile readability.
  • The stainless steel plate shall be mounted on a 10 mm thick clear acrylic sheet of approved quality, providing rigidity and aesthetic appearance. The complete assembly shall be fixed using stainless steel studs (minimum four numbers) and necessary fasteners, all made of stainless steel Grade 304.
  • All materials including stainless steel sheet, acrylic sheet, printing, braille embossing, studs, and fasteners shall be of approved make, free from defects, and conforming to relevant standards.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall include fabrication, supplying, and fixing of stainless steel braille signage complete in all respects as per approved design and instructions of the Engineer-in-Charge. The signage content shall be accurately printed and braille text shall be properly embossed with correct spacing and alignment.
  • The stainless steel plate shall be securely bonded or fixed to the acrylic backing. The entire assembly shall be mounted on the wall using stainless steel studs, ensuring proper spacing from the wall surface and firm anchorage.
  • Proper marking, drilling, and fixing shall be carried out carefully to avoid damage to the wall surface. The signage shall be installed at appropriate height and location as per accessibility standards and drawings. The finished unit shall be aligned, levelled, and free from scratches, dents, or defects.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The signage shall be measured on square feet (Sft), in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include cost of stainless steel plate, acrylic sheet, braille embossing, printing, studs, fasteners, labour, fabrication, transportation, and fixing complete.
  • No separate payment shall be made for accessories, drilling, or incidental works, as these shall be deemed included in the item rate. The item shall be measured as completed and accepted as per the directions of the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Square Feet.

Description: Providing and fixing Grab Bars (for physically challenged persons ) of Stainless Steel , 32mm dia , 18(G) 1.2mm wall thickness , brushed finish , ASIS 304 Grade of following sizes of standars make with necessary with necessary fixture & fastenings of S .S.-304 grade, load carrying capacity of 130Kg, etc complete of standard make like CERA , EURONICS etc as per the nstructions of Engineer in-charge. (C) U shaped wall mounted hand rail with hinge 600(L)x100(D)

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• The grab bar shall be made from stainless steel pipe of 32 mm diameter and 18 gauge (1.2 mm wall thickness), conforming to Grade 304 stainless steel of approved quality. The surface finish shall be brushed (satin/matt) to provide durability, corrosion resistance, and aesthetic appearance.
  • The grab bar shall be designed for wall mounting with a hinged mechanism allowing it to be folded up or down as required. It shall have a minimum load carrying capacity of 130 kg. All mounting brackets, hinge assembly, screws, anchor fasteners, and accessories shall be made of stainless steel Grade 304.
  • The product shall be of standard make such as CERA, Euronics, or equivalent approved brand. All materials shall be new, free from defects, and approved by the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall include supplying and fixing the grab bar at the specified location on wall as per approved drawings and instructions. The wall surface shall be prepared, and suitable holes shall be drilled for fixing the grab bar using appropriate anchor fasteners.
  • The grab bar shall be securely fixed using stainless steel screws and fasteners to ensure stability and safety during use. Proper alignment, level, and projection (150 mm from wall) shall be maintained. Care shall be taken to avoid damage to wall finishes during installation.
  • The installed grab bar shall be firm, properly aligned, and capable of withstanding the specified load without deformation or loosening. The finished surface shall be clean, smooth, and free from scratches or defects.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The grab bar shall be measured on Set basis for the specified size (600 mm × 100 mm), in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include cost of materials, stainless steel fixtures, fasteners, labour, drilling, fixing, and all incidental works required to complete the item.
  • No separate payment shall be made for fixtures, drilling, or accessories, as these shall be deemed included in the item rate. The item shall be measured as completed and accepted as per the directions of the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Set.

Description: Painting lines, dashes, arrows, letters etc on roads , Air- fields and like in two coats with road marking paint , brushing including cleaning the surface of all dirt, dust and other foreign matter (ii) over 10cm in width.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• The work shall be carried out using approved quality road marking paint suitable for application on roads, airfields, and similar surfaces. The paint shall be durable, weather-resistant, quick drying, and capable of withstanding traffic wear and environmental conditions. The paint shall have good adhesion to bituminous and concrete surfaces and shall maintain visibility under day and night conditions.
  • The paint shall conform to relevant standards such as IS 164 or equivalent specifications for road marking applications. The colour and shade shall be as approved by the Engineer-in-Charge (generally white, yellow, or other specified colours).

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall include thorough cleaning of the surface to remove all dust, dirt, grease, oil, and loose materials by brushing or other suitable means to ensure proper adhesion of paint. The markings shall be set out accurately as per approved drawings, dimensions, and alignment.The work shall include thorough cleaning of the surface to remove all dust, dirt, grease, oil, and loose materials by brushing or other suitable means to ensure proper adhesion of paint. The markings shall be set out accurately as per approved drawings, dimensions, and alignment.
  • The paint shall be applied in two coats using brush or approved mechanical method to achieve uniform thickness and finish. Each coat shall be allowed to dry properly before applying the subsequent coat. The markings shall include lines, dashes, arrows, letters, symbols, and other traffic indicators as required.
  • The finished markings shall be clear, sharp, and uniform in thickness and width (over 10 cm as specified), free from streaks, overlaps, or irregularities. Necessary precautions shall be taken to protect freshly painted surfaces from traffic until fully dry.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The road markings shall be measured in square meters (Sqm) for areas exceeding 10 cm in width, in accordance with IS 1200. Alternatively, where specified, linear measurements may be converted into area for payment.
  • The rate shall include cost of materials, surface preparation, labour, application of two coats, tools, and all incidental works required to complete the item. No separate payment shall be made for cleaning, setting out, protection, or wastage, as these shall be deemed included in the item rate.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Square Meter.

Description: Providing & Laying cement concrete M-250 for all type of R.C.C. Work using 12 to 20 mm size black trap metal of approved quality as an aggregate incl. watering, curing, scaffolding, centering incl. cost of formwork and using machine mixed design cement concrete & compacted with vibrators incl. finishing the surface etc. as directed as per detailed drawing & design & as instructed by the engineer incharge etc.complete.(A) Foundation & Plinth
