Unless otherwise agreed to by the Engineer in-charge the first batch of concrete from the mixture shall contain only two thirds of normal quantity of coarse aggregate Mixing plant shall be thoroughly cleaned before changing from one type of cement to another.

subsections.title: Consistency
subsections.description: • The degree of consistency which shall depend upon the nature of the work and methods of vibration of concrete, shall be determined by regular slump tests in accordance with I.S. 1199-193. The skimp of 10 mm. to 25 mm shall be adopted when vibrators are used and 80 mm. when vibrators are not used.

subsections.title: Inspection
subsections.description:
• Contractor shall give the Engineer-in-charge due notice before placing any concrete in the forms to permit him to inspect and accept the false work and forms as to their strength, alignment and general fitness but such inspection shall not relieve the contractor of his responsibility for the safely of men machinery materials and for results obtained immediately before concreting all forms shall be thoroughly cleaned.
  • Centering design and its erection shall be got approved from the engineer-in-charge. One carpenter with helper shall invariably be kept present throughout the period of concreting. Movement of labour and other persons shall be totally prohibited for reinforcement laid in position. For access to different parts suitable mobile platforms shall be provided so that steel reinforcement in position is not disturbed. For ensuring proper cover, mortar blocks of suitable size shall be cast and tied to the reinforcement. Timber kapachi or metal pieces shall not be used for this purpose.

subsections.title: Transporting and laying
subsections.description:
• The method of transporting and placing concrete shall be as approved. Concrete shall be so transported and placed that no contamination, segregation or loss of its constituent material takes place. All from work shall be cleaned and made free from standing   water   dust,   show   or   ice   immediately   before   placing   of   concrete. No concrete shall be placed in any part of the structure until the approval of the engineer-in-charge has been obtained.
  • Concreting shall proceed continuously over the area between construction joints. Fresh concrete proper contraction joint is formed. Concrete shall be compacted in its final position within 30 minutes of its discharge from the mixer. Except where otherwise agreed to by the engineer-in-charge, concrete shall be deposited in horizontal layers to a compacted depth of not more than 0.45 meter when internal vibrators are used and not exceeding 0.30 meter in all other cases.
  • Unless otherwise agreed to by the Engineer-in-charge concrete shall be dropped in to place from a height exceeding 2 meters. When trucking or chutes are used they shall be kept close and used in such a way as to avoid segregation. When concreting has to be resumed on a surface which has hardened, it shall be roughened, swept clean, thoroughly wetted and covered with a 13 mm. thick layer of mortar composed of cement and sand in the same ratio as in the concrete mix itself. This 13 mm. layer of mortar shall be freshly mixed and placed immediately before placing of new concrete. Where concrete has not fully hardened, all lateness shall be removed by scrubbing the wet surface with wire or bristle brushes, care being taken to avoid dislodgement of any particles of coarse aggregate. The surface shall then be thoroughly wetted, all free water removed and then coated with neat cement grout. The first layer of concrete to be placed on this surface shall not exceed 150 mm. in thickness and shall be well rammed against old work, particular attention being given to corners and close spots.
  • All concrete shall be compacted to produce a dense homogeneous mass with the assistance of vibrators, unless otherwise permitted by the Engineer-in-charge for exceptional cases, such as concreting under water, where vibrators cannot be used. Sufficient vibrators in serviceable condition shall be kept at site so that spare equipment is always available in the even of breakdowns. Concrete shall be judged to be compacted when the mortar fills the spaces between the coarse aggregate and begins to cream up to form an even surface. Compaction shall be completed before the initial setting stats i.e. within 30 minutes of addition of water to dry mixture. During compaction, it shall be observed that needle vibrators are not applied on reinforcement which is likely to destroy the bond between concrete and reinforcement.

subsections.title: Curing
subsections.description: • Immediately after compaction, concrete weather including rain, running water, shocks, vibration, traffic, rapid temperature charges, frost and drying out process. It shall be covered with wet sacking has Sian or other similar absorbent material approved, soon after the initial set, and shall be kept continuously wet for a period of not less than 14 days from the date of placement. Masonry work over foundation concrete may be started after 48 hours of its laying but curing of concrete shall be continued for a minimum period of 14 days.

subsections.title: Sampling and testing of concrete
subsections.description:
• Samples from fresh concrete shall betaken as per I.S. 1199-1959 and cubes shall be made, cured and tested at 7 days of 28 days as per requirements in accordance with I.S. 526-1959. A random sampling procedure shall be adopted to ensure that each concrete batch shall have a reasonable chance of being tested i.e. the sampling should be spread over the entire period of concreting and cover all mixing units. The minimum frequency of sampling of concrete of each grade shall be in accordance with following:
    Quantity Of Concrete in Work No. Of Samples
     1 - 5 Cmt 1
     6 - 15 Cmt 2
     16  30 Cmt 3
     31 - 50 Cmt 4
  • Note :  At least one simple shall be taken from each shift, Ten test specimens shall be made from each sample, five for testing at 7 days and the remaining five at 28 days. The samples of concrete shall be taken on each day of concreting as per above frequency. The number of specimens may be suitably increased  as  deemed  necessary  by  the  Engineer-in-charge  when  procedure  of  tests  given  above reveals a poor quality of concrete and in other special cases.
  • The average of the group of cubes cast for each day shall not be less than the specified cube strength of 150 K/g Cm 2 at 28 days. 20% of the cubes cast for each day may have value less than the specified strength provided the lowest value is not less than 85% of the specified strength. If the concrete made in accordance with the proportions given for a particular grade does not yield the specified strength, such concrete shall be classified as belonging to the appropriate lower grade. Concrete made in accordance with the Proportions given for a particular grade shall not, however be placed in a higher grade on the ground that the test strength are higher then the minimum specified.

subsections.title: Stripping
subsections.description:
• The Engineer-in-charge shall be informed in advance by the contractor of hr> intention to strike the form work. While fixing  the  time  of  removal  of  form  work,  due  consideration  shall  be  given  to  local  conditions, character of the structure, the weather and other conditions that influence the setting of concrete and of the materials used in the mix. In normal circumstances (generally where temperatures are above 20.C) and where ordinary concrete is used, forms may be struck after expire or periods specified in item No.9.1 (A) for respective item of form work.
  • All form work shall be removed without causing any shock or vibration as would damage the concrete. Before the soft and struts are removed, the concrete surface shall be gradually exposed, where necessary in order to ascertain that concrete has sufficiently hardened. Centering shall be gradually and uniformly lowered in such a manner as to permit the concrete to take stresses due to its own weight uniformly and gradually. Where internal metal tiles are permitted, they or their removable parts shall be extracted without causing any damage to the concrete and remaining holes filled with mortar. No permanently embedded metal part shall have less than 25 mm. cover to the finished concrete surface. Where it is intended to re-use the form work, it shall be cleaned and made good to the satisfaction of the Engineer-in-charge. After removal of form work and shutting, the Executive Engineer shall inspect the work and satisfy by random checks that concrete produced is of good quality.
  • Immediately after the removal of forms, all exposed bolts etc. passing through the cement concrete member and used for stuttering or any other purpose shall be cut inside the cement concrete member to a depth of at least 25 m. below the surface of the concrete and the resulting holes be filled by cement mortar, all fins, caused by form joints, all cavities produced by the removal of form tiles and all other holes and depressions, honeycomb spots, broken edges or comers and other defects, shall be thoroughly cleaned", saturated with water and carefully pointed an rendered true with mortar of cement and fine aggregate mixed in proportions used in the grade of concrete that is being furnished and of as dry consistency as is possible to use. Considerable pressure shall be applied in filling and pointing to ensure through filling in all voids. Surface which are pointed shall be kept moist for a period of 24 hours. If rock pockets/honeycombs in the opinion of the Engineer-in-charge are of such an extent or character as to effect the strength of the structure materially or to endanger the life of the steel reinforcement, he may declare the concrete defective and require the removal and replacement of the portions of structure affected.
  • The Above specification of ordinary concrete shall be followed except that the concrete mix shall be designed form preliminary tests. The proportioning of cement and aggregates shall be done by weight and necessary precautions shall be taken in the production to ensure that the required work cube strength is attained and maintained. The controlled concrete shall be in grades of M-100, M-150, M-200, M-250, M-300, M-350 & M-400 with prefix controlled added to it. The letter M refers to mix and the numbers specify 28 days works cube compressive strength of 150 mm. cubes of the mix expressed in Kg./Crnt.

subsections.title: Proportion of Mix
subsections.description:
• The proportion of cement, sand and coarse aggregate shall be determined of weight. The weight batch machine shall be used for maintaining proper control over the proportion of aggregates as per mix design. The strength requirements of different grades of concrete shall be as under:
    Grade Concrete Compressive strength of 15 cms. cubes in Kg./Cmt. at 28 days, conducted in accordance with I.S. 516-1959.
    Preliminary test Min.    		 Work test Min.
    M-150 200 150
    M-200 260 200
    M-250 320 250
    M-300 380 300
    M-350 440 350
    M-400 500 400
  • In all cases, the 28 days compressive strength specified in above be the criteria for acceptance or rejection of the concrete. Where the strength of a concrete mix as indicated by tests, lies in between the strength of any two grades specified in the above table, such concrete shall be classified in for purpose as concrete belonging to the lower of the grades between which its strength lies.
  • The proportions for ingredients chosen shall be such that concrete has adequate workability for conditions prevailing on the work question and can be property compacted with means available except where ft can be shown to the satisfaction of the Engineer-in-charge, that supply of properly graded aggregate of uniform quality can be maintained till the completion of work, grading of aggregate shall be controlled by obtaining the coarse aggregates in different sizes and bending them in the right proportions as required. Aggregates of different sizes shall be stocked in separate stock piles. The required quantity of material shall be stock piled several hours, preferably a day before use. The grading of coarse and fine aggregate shall be checked as frequently as possible, the frequency for a given job being determined by Engineer-in-charge to ensure that the suppliers are maintaining the uniform grading as approved for samples used in the preliminary tests. 
  • In proportioning concrete, the quantity of both cement and aggregate shall be determined by weight. Where the weight of cement is determined by accepting the maker's weight per bag, a reasonable number of bags shall be weighted separately to check the net weight. Where cement is weighted form bulk stocks at site and not by bags, it shall be weighed separately from the aggregate. Water, shall either be measured by volume in calibrated tanks or weighed. All measuring equipment shall be maintained in clean, and serviceable condition. Their accuracy shall be periodically checked.
  • It is most important to keep the specified water cement ratio constant and at its correct value. To this end, moisture content in both fine and coarse aggregates shall be determined by the Engineer-in-charge according to the weather conditions. The amount of mixing water shall then be adjusted to compensate for variations in the moisture content. For the determination of moisture content in the aggregates. I.S. 2386 (Part-Ill) shall be referred to. Suitable adjustments shah also be made in the weights of aggregates due to variation in their moisture content. Minimum quantity of cement to be used in controlled concrete shall not be less than 220 kg./M-3 in plain concrete and not less than 250 kg/M-3 in reinforced concrete.

sections.title: SPECIFICATIONS FOR FORMWORK, CENTERING AND SCAFFOLDING

subsections.title: Materials
subsections.description: • Formwork shall be in plywood, sawn timber or steel as required for walls, stairs, slab, beams, columns, parapets, etc. for all concrete work.

subsections.title: Workmanship
subsections.description: • The formwork shall conform to the shape, lines and dimensions as shown on the drawings and shall be so constructed so as to remain sufficiently rigid and water-tight, during placement and compaction of the concrete. Adequate arrangement shall be made by the Contractor to safe guard against any settlements of the formwork during the course of concreting and after concreting.

subsections.title: Centering
subsections.description:
• The centering, which has been got approved should be sufficiently strong and safe before, during and after pouring concrete and should be so erected that it would allow removal of forms in proper sequence without damaging either the concrete or the forms to be removed.
  • The props of centering shall be provided on firm foundation or base of sufficient strength to carry the loads, without any settlement.

subsections.title: Scaffolding
subsections.description:
• All scaffolding, hoisting arrangements and ladders etc, required for facilitating of concrete shall be provided and removed on completion work by Contractor, at his own expense. The scaffolding, hoisting arrangement, ladders etc shall be strong enough to withstand all live, dead and impact loads expected to act. The Contractor shall be solely responsible for the safety of the scaffolding, hoisting arrangement, ladders, work and workmen etc.
  • The scaffolding, hoisting arrangement and ladders shall allow easy approach to the work spot and afford easy inspection.

sections.title: Mode Of Measurement & Payment
sections.description:
• The consolidated cubical contents of concrete work as specified in item shall be measured. No deduction shall be made for (a) Ends of dissimilar materials such as joints, beams, posts, girders, falters, purling trusses, corbels and steps etc., up to 500 Sq, Cm. in section.
  • The Above specifications of shall be followed, except that the controlled concrete R.C.C. work as specified in item shall be measured under this item. The rate includes cost of form work.
  • The rate include cost of all materials labour, tools and plant required for mixing, placing in position vibrating and compacting, finishing as directed, curing and all other incidental expenses as well as test charges for producing concrete of specified strength. The rate includes the cost of form work but excluding the cost of reinforcement.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one cubic meter.

Description: providing and laying 15 mm thick heavy duty vitrified Tectile / platform heavy duty tile in flooring over 20 mm (average) base of cement mortar 1:6 ( 1 cement : 6 sand ) and jointed with colour cement slurry of jasalmer / teracotta colour , vitrified tiles of approved make.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• The flooring shall be done using 15 mm thick heavy-duty vitrified tactile/platform tiles of approved make, shade, and texture, suitable for heavy traffic areas. The tiles shall be of uniform size, shape, and thickness, free from cracks, warping, or surface defects.
  • The base shall consist of cement mortar 1:6 (1 cement : 6 coarse sand), using cement conforming to IS 269 or equivalent and clean, well-graded coarse sand. The joints shall be filled with coloured cement slurry in approved shade such as Jaisalmer or terracotta colour, ensuring proper bonding and aesthetic finish.
  • All materials including cement, sand, tiles, and pigments shall be of approved quality and conform to relevant standards.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall include preparation of the base surface by cleaning, leveling, and removing all dust, loose particles, and foreign matter. A cement mortar bed of average 20 mm thickness in proportion 1:6 shall be laid, compacted, and levelled to the required slope and alignment.
  • The vitrified tactile/platform tiles shall be laid over the prepared mortar bed in proper line, level, and pattern as per approved drawings. The tiles shall be pressed firmly to ensure full bedding without voids. Necessary spacers shall be used to maintain uniform joints.
  • After laying, the joints shall be filled with coloured cement slurry of approved shade. Excess slurry shall be cleaned off, and the surface shall be wiped clean. The flooring shall be kept moist and properly cured for the specified period to ensure strength and durability.
  • The finished surface shall be even, true to line and level, non-slippery, and free from lipping, cracks, or defects. The tactile features shall be properly aligned for functional use as per design requirements.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The flooring shall be measured in square feet (Sft) for the finished area, in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include cost of tiles, cement mortar bed, coloured slurry, labour, curing, cleaning, and all materials and operations required to complete the work.
  • No separate payment shall be made for surface preparation, joint filling, curing, wastage, or incidental works, as these shall be deemed included in the item rate. The item shall be measured as completed and accepted as per the directions of the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Square Feet.

Description: Providing and supplying M.S. Almari size ( 1.80 x 0.45 x 0.90 ) having high strength, flawless finish double door with 22 gauge including with One coat of anticorrosive paint & two coats of oil paint for protection.  as per shown in detailed drawing and instructions of engineer-in-charge.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• The almirah shall be fabricated using mild steel sheet of 22 gauge thickness of approved quality conforming to IS 2062. The frame and body shall be made from suitable M.S. sections to ensure adequate strength, rigidity, and durability. The almirah shall be of double-door type with internal shelves/partitions as per approved drawing.
  • All components including doors, shelves, back panel, and side panels shall be made from M.S. sheet of specified thickness. The unit shall be provided with necessary hardware such as hinges, locking arrangement, handles, tower bolts, and other accessories of approved make.
  • The entire surface shall be treated with one coat of anti-corrosive primer followed by two coats of approved quality oil paint to provide protection against corrosion and to achieve a smooth and uniform finish. All materials used shall be new, free from defects, and approved by the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall include fabrication, supplying, and placing of M.S. almirah complete in all respects. The fabrication shall involve cutting, bending, welding, and assembling of M.S. sheets and sections to form a rigid and stable structure.
  • The doors shall be properly aligned and fitted with hinges to ensure smooth opening and closing. Locking arrangements shall be installed accurately to provide proper security. Shelves shall be fixed firmly inside the almirah as per design.
  • All weld joints shall be ground smooth and finished properly. The surface shall be thoroughly cleaned to remove rust, oil, and scale before applying primer and paint. Painting shall be carried out uniformly without streaks, runs, or defects.
  • The completed almirah shall be transported to site and placed in position as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge. The finished unit shall be stable, well-aligned, and aesthetically acceptable.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The almirah shall be measured on number basis (Each) for the specified size (1.80 m × 0.45 m × 0.90 m), in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include cost of materials, fabrication, welding, hardware fittings, primer, painting, labour, transportation, and placing at site complete.
  • No separate payment shall be made for fasteners, fittings, wastage, or accessories, as these shall be deemed included in the item rate. The item shall be measured as completed and accepted as per the directions of the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Nos.

Description: • Providing TMT Bar FE 500D reinforcement for R.C.C. work including bending, binding and placing in position complete.(A) Ground Floor

sections.title: Materials
sections.description: • Mild steel bars shall conform to M-18, Thermo Mechanically Treated steel bars (high yield strength steel deformed bars) shall conform to M-19, Mild steel binding wires shall conform to M-21.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall consist of furnished and placing reinforcement to the shape and dimensions shown as on the drawings or as directed.
  • Steel shall be clean and free from rust and loose mill scale at the time of fixing in position and subsequent concreting.
  • Reinforcing steel shall conform accurately to the dimensions given in the bar bending schedules shown on relevant drawings.  Bars shall be bent cold to specified shape and dimensions or as directed, using a proper bar bender, operated by hand or power to attain proper radius of bends, bars shall not be bent or straightened in a manner that will injure the material.  Bars bent during transportation or handling shall be straightened before being used on the work. They shall not be heated to facilitate bending. Unless otherwise specified for mild steel a "U" type hook at the end of each bar shall invariably be provided to  main reinforcement.  The radius of the bend shall not  be less than straight part of the bar beyond the end of the curve shall be at least four times the diameter of the bar. In case which are not round and in case of deformed bars,  the diameter  shall be taken as the diameter of the circle having an equivalent effective area. The hooks shall be suitably encased to prevent any splitting of the concrete. The cold twisted steel bears shall be used without hooks at the ends. Deformed bars without hooks shall, however, comply with relevant anchorage requirements.
  • All  the  reinforcement bars shall be accurately  placed  in exactly the same position as shown on the drawings, and shall be securely held in position during placing of concrete by annealed binding wire not less than 1 mm. in size,  and  by using stay blocks or  metal  chair  spacers, metal handers, supporting wires or other approved devices at sufficiently close intervals. Bars shall not be allowed to sag between supports nor displaced during concreting or any other operations  of the work.  All devices used  for positioning shall be of non-corrodible material. Wooden and metal supports shall not extend to the surface of the concrete, except where shown on the drawings. Placing bars on layers of freshly laid concrete as the work progresses for adjusting bar spacing shall not be allowed. Pieces of broken stone or brick wooden blocks shall not be used. Layers of bars shall be separated by spacer bars, precast mortar blocks or other approved devices.  Reinforcement after being placed in position shall be maintained  in a clean condition until completely embedded in  concrete. Special care shall be exercised to prevent any displacement of reinforcement in concrete already placed.  To prevent reinforcement from corrosion, concrete cover shall  be provided as indicated on drawings. All the bars are to be spliced and which are likely to be exceeding 10 days shall be protected by a thick coat of neat cement grout.
  • Bars crossing each other where required shall be secured by binding wires (annealed) of size not less than 1 mm. in such a manner that they do not slip over each other at the time of fixing and concreting.
  • As far as possible, bars of full length shall be used, in case this is not possible, overlapping of bars shall be done as directed. when practicable, overlapping bars shall not touch each other, but be kept apart by 25 mm. or 125 times the maximum size of the coarse aggregate whichever is greater between them.  Where not feasible, overlapping bars shall be bound with annealed wires, not less than 1 mm. thick twisted tight. The overlaps shall be staggered for different bars and located at points, along the span where neither shear nor bending moment is maximum.
  • Where ever  indicated  on  the drawings or  desired  by  the  Engineer-in-charge, bars shall be joined by couplings which shall have a cross section sufficient to transmit the full stresses of bars. The ends of the bars that are joined by coupling shall be upset for sufficient length so that the effective cross section at the base of threads is not less than the normal cross section of the bar. Threads shall be standard threads. Steel for coupling shall conform to I.S-226.
  • When permitted or specified on the drawings, joints of reinforcement bars shall be welded so as to transmit their full stresses.  Welded joints shall preferably be located at points when steel will not be subjected to more than 75% of the maximum permissible stresses and welds so staggered that at any one section not more than 20% of the rods are welded.  Only  electric welding using a process which excludes air from molten and conforms to any or all other special provisions for the work shall be accepted. Suitable means shall be provided for holding bars securely in postion during welding. It shall be ensured that no voids are left in welding and when welding is done in two or three stages, previous surface shall be cleaned properly.  Ends of the bars shall be cleaned of all loose scale, rust, grease, paint and other foreign matter before welding. Only competent welders shall be employed on the work. The  M.S. electrodes  used  for  welding shall conform  to  I.S. 814. Welded pieces of reinforcement shall be tested.  Specimen shall be taken from the actual site and their number and frequency of test shall be as directed.

sections.title: Mode Of Measurement & Payment
sections.description:
• Reinforcement shall be measured in length including overlaps, separately for different diameters as actually used in the work. Where welding or coupling is resorted to, in place do lap joints, such joints shall be measured for payment as equivalent length of overlap as per design requirement.  From the length so measured, the weight of reinforcement shall  be calculated in tonnes on the same basis of as per M-18,19,20,21 even though steel is supplied to the contractor by the department on actual weight. Length shall include hooks at the ends.  Wastage and annealed steel wire for binding shall not be measured and the cost of these items shall be deemed to be included in the rate for reinforcement.
  • The rate for reinforcement includes cost of steel binding wires, its transporting from departmental store to work site, cutting, bending, placing and fixing in position as shown on the drawings and as directed. It shall also include all devices for keeping reinforcement in approved position, cost of joining as per approved method and all wastage and spacer bars.
  • The rate shall be for unit of one Kg.

Description: Supplying of MS Bunk bed ( for 2 Person sleeping arrengment ) of required size as per suggested by engg. Incharge incl. providing 1 coat of red oxide and successive 2 coats of stoving enamel (TA grey) backed in electric oven including Mattress, Bed sheet and cushion etc. comp. as directed.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• The bunk bed shall be fabricated using mild steel sections of approved quality conforming to IS 2062. The frame shall be made from suitable M.S. square/rectangular hollow sections or angles of adequate thickness to ensure strength and stability. The bed shall be designed for two-person sleeping arrangement (upper and lower berth) of required size as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The entire steel framework shall be treated with one coat of red oxide primer and finished with two coats of stoving enamel paint (TA grey shade), baked in an electric oven to achieve a smooth, durable, and corrosion-resistant finish.
  • The bed shall be supplied complete with accessories including mattress, bed sheets, and cushions of standard quality. All materials used shall be new, free from defects, and approved by the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall include fabrication, supplying, and placing of the M.S. bunk bed complete in all respects. The steel frame shall be fabricated by cutting, welding, grinding, and assembling the members to form a rigid and stable structure. Proper supports, ladder (if required), and safety guard rails for the upper berth shall be provided to ensure user safety.
  • All weld joints shall be properly finished and smooth. The surface shall be cleaned thoroughly to remove rust, oil, and scale before applying primer and stoving enamel paint. The painting shall be uniform, smooth, and free from runs or defects.
  • The bed shall be delivered to site and placed in proper position as directed. Mattress, bed sheet, and cushion shall be provided and properly arranged. The complete unit shall be stable, level, and suitable for use, as approved by the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The bunk bed shall be measured on number basis (Each), in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include cost of steel materials, fabrication, welding, finishing, primer, painting, stoving process, accessories (mattress, bed sheet, cushion), labour, transportation, and placing at site complete.
  • No separate payment shall be made for fittings, welding, wastage, or accessories, as the same shall be deemed included in the item rate. The item shall be measured as completed and accepted as per the directions of the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Nos.

Description: Providing fixing And arranging Multiflex rack/Library rack of size 1800(H) x 1200 (W) x 448(D) mm made high strength CR/HR steel confirming to IS 5986:2002/ IS 2062 :2006 by using steel confirming to is 5986- with minimum yield strength of 255 MPa vertical angels of size 35x35x1.6mm with holes Slotted of flanges of pitch 19.05 mm provided for adjusting loading levels which are made up of 5 bend pannels of 1300 x 448 x 1.25 mm size with bend border mounted on and C bends at all end with all Endge finished with Trigular support plate 75X75X1.25 mm and all nuts and bolts etc finish and all the components having powder coating with thoroughly anti rust treatment including all necessary fixture, fastners, fittings, labour material machinary etc complete as per photograph as selecte and directed by Engineer Incharge Overall size : 1800(H) x 1200 (W) x 448(D)

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• The rack shall be fabricated using high strength CR/HR steel conforming to IS 5986 and IS 2062, having minimum yield strength of 255 MPa. The vertical members shall be made from steel angles of size 35 × 35 × 1.6 mm, provided with slotted holes at a pitch of 19.05 mm to facilitate adjustable shelf levels.
  • The shelves shall be made from 1.25 mm thick steel sheets, formed into 5-bend panels of size approximately 1300 mm × 448 mm, with edges bent and reinforced using C-type bends on all sides for added strength. Each shelf shall be supported with triangular support plates of size 75 × 75 × 1.25 mm.
  • All nuts, bolts, and fasteners shall be of approved quality. The entire rack system shall be treated with anti-rust process and finished with powder coating of approved colour and thickness to ensure durability, corrosion resistance, and aesthetic appearance.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall include fabrication, supplying, assembling, and arranging the multiflex/library rack complete in all respects as per approved design, drawings, or sample photograph. The vertical angle frames shall be erected in plumb and aligned properly. Shelves shall be fixed at required levels using nut-bolt arrangement through pre-slotted holes, allowing flexibility for height adjustment.
  • All components shall be accurately fabricated with proper bending, cutting, punching, and finishing. Edges shall be smooth and free from sharp projections. The rack shall be assembled securely ensuring stability, load-bearing capacity, and rigidity.
  • The entire unit shall be powder coated after proper surface preparation including cleaning, de-rusting, and chemical treatment. The rack shall be installed at site in proper position, true line, and level as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge. The work shall include all materials, labour, tools, machinery, handling, transportation, and fixing complete.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The rack shall be measured on number basis (Each) for the specified size (1800 mm × 1200 mm × 448 mm), in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include cost of steel, fabrication, bending, punching, powder coating, nuts and bolts, fittings, labour, transportation, and installation complete.
  • No separate payment shall be made for fasteners, supports, coatings, wastage, or accessories, as these shall be deemed included in the item rate. The item shall be measured as completed and accepted as per the directions of the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Nos.

Description: Prov. and laying Tremix design mix cement concrete M-250 in roads / drive ways using  coarse sand and graded stone aggregates 20 to 25 mm nominal size in appropriate quantity as per specification, mechanically vibrated using and surface screed vibrators, vaccume pump power floater, power trovel, concrete floor cutter etc. Including approved quality floor hardener @ 2 kg/smt on top surface and Fill Fiber incl. steel form work with  200 mm M.S. channel sections incl. proper curing and providing and filling construction joint and dummy joints  with "shalitax" primer silflex sheet not less than 20 mm th. incl. rounding the edges and cutting the groove by using concrete cutter  in zigzac pattern  upto 1/3 depth of the RCC thicknes and not less than 10 mm in width and filling the grooved by dummy joints with bitumen sealing compound of grade-A Including making all necessary arrangments for expansion joints at every 15 mtr's square or as per site situation with filling bitumen etc. complete. Note :- This item will be excluded of reinforcement but Including centering, shuttering, MS form work, necessary tools & plants and all required materials etc. comp. as directed by Engg. In charge.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• Water shall conform to M-1. Cement shall conform to M-3. Sand shall conform to M-6. Grit shall conform to M-8 Course aggregate shall conform M-12.
  • Floor hardener shall be of approved make, metallic or non-metallic type, and shall be applied at the rate of 2 kg per square meter to improve abrasion resistance and surface durability. Fiber reinforcement shall be polypropylene or equivalent synthetic fibers conforming to IS 16481, uniformly mixed in concrete as per manufacturer’s recommendations to control shrinkage cracks. Joint filler boards shall be compressible, non-extruding type with minimum thickness of 20 mm conforming to IS 1838. Bitumen sealing compound used for joints shall be of approved Grade-A quality conforming to IS 1834, and primer shall conform to IS 3384 to ensure proper adhesion.

subsections.title: General
subsections.description:
• The concrete mix is not required to be designed by preliminary testes. The proportion of the concrete mix shall be 1:2:4 (1 cement : 2 coarse sand : 4 graded stone aggregate 20 mm. nominal size) by volume concrete work shall have exposed concrete surface or as specified in the item.
  • The designation ordinary M-100, M-150, M-200, M-250 specified as per I.S. correspond approximately to 1:3:6, 1.2:4, 1:1:1/2:3 and 1:1:2 nominal mix of ordinary concrete by volume respectively.
  • The water cement ratios shall not be more than specified in the above table. The cement content of the mix specified in the table shall be increased if the quantity of water in mix has to be met eased to overcome the difficulties of placements and compaction so that the water-cement ratio specified in the table is not exceeded.
  • Workability of the concrete shall be controlled by maintaining a water -cement-ratio that is found to give a concrete mix which is just sufficient wet to be placed and compacted without difficulty with the means available.
  • The maximum size of course aggregate shall be as large as possible within the limits specified but in no case greater than one forth of the minimum thickness of the member provided that the concrete can be placed without difficulty so as to surround all reinforcement thoroughly and to fill the corners of the form. 
  • For reinforced concrete work; coarse aggregates having a nominal size of 20 mm. are generally considered satisfactory.
  • For heavily reinforced concrete members as in the case of ribs of main beams, the nominal maximum size of coarse aggregate should usually be restricted to 5 mm. less than the minimum clear distance between the main bar or 5 mm. less than the minimum cover to the reinforcement whichever is smaller.
  • Where the reinforcement is widely spaced as in solid slabs, limitations of size of the aggregate may not be so important, and the nominal maximum size may some times be as great as or greater than the minimum cover.
  • Admixture maybe used in concrete only with approval of Engineer-in-charge based upon the evidence that with the passage of time neither the compressive strength of concrete is reduced not are other requisite qualities of concrete and steel impaired by the use of such admixtures.

subsections.title: Workmanship
subsections.description: • Proportioning shall be done by volume, except which shall be measured in terms of bags of 50 kg. weight, the volume of one such bag being taken as 0.0342 cu. meter Boxes of suitable size shall be used for measuring sand aggregate. The size of boxes (internal) shall be 35 x 25 cms. and 40 cms deep while measuring the aggregate and sand the boxes shall be filled without shaking ramming or hammering. The proportioning of sand shall be on the basis of its dry volume and in case of damp saner, allowances for bulk age shall be made.

subsections.title: Mixing
subsections.description:
• The concrete shall be handed from the place, of mixing to the final position in not more than 15 minutes by the method as directed and shall be placed into its final-position, compacted and finished within 30 minutes of mixing with water i.e. before the setting commences.
  • The concrete shall be laid in layers of 15 cms. to 20 cms.
  • For all work, concrete shall be mixed in a mechanical mixed which along with other accessories shall be. kept in first class working condition and so maintained throughout the construction Measured quantity of aggregate, sand and cement required for each batch shall be poured into the claim of the mechanical mixer while it is continuously running. After half a minute of dry mixing measured quantity of water required for each batch of concrete mix shall be added gradually and mixing continued for another one and a half minute Mixing shall be continued till materials are uniformly distributed and uniform colour of the entire mass is obtained and each individual particle of the coarse aggregate shows complete coating of mortar containing its proportionate amount of cement. In no case shall the mixing he done for less than 2 minutes after-oil ingredients have been put into the mixer.
  • When hand mixing is permitted by the Engineer-in-charge for small jobs or for certain other reasons, it shall be done on the smooth watertight platform large enough to allow efficient tuning over the ingredients of concrete before and after adding water Mixing platform shall be so arranged that no foreign malarial gets mixed with concrete nor does the mixing water flow out. Cement in required number of bags shall be spread in n layer of uniform thickness on the mixing platform. Dry coarse and fine aggregate and cement shall then be mixed thoroughly be turning over to get a mixture to uniform colour. Specified quantity water shall then be added gradually through a rose can and the mass turned over till a mix of required consistency is obtained. In hand mixing quantity of cement shall be increased by 10 percent above that specified.
  • Mixers which haw been out of use for more than 30 minutes shall be thoroughly cleaned before putting in a new batch. Unless otherwise agreed to by the Engineer in-charge the first batch of concrete from the mixture shall contain only two thirds of normal quantity of coarse aggregate Mixing plant shall be thoroughly cleaned before changing from one type of cement to another.

subsections.title: Consistency
subsections.description: • The degree of consistency which shall depend upon the nature of the work and methods of vibration of concrete, shall be determined by regular slump tests in accordance with I.S. 1199-193. The skimp of 10 mm. to 25 mm shall be adopted when vibrators are used and 80 mm. when vibrators are not used.

subsections.title: Inspection
subsections.description:
• Contractor shall give the Engineer-in-charge due notice before placing any concrete in the forms to permit him to inspect and accept the false work and forms as to their strength, alignment and general fitness but such inspection shall not relieve the contractor of his responsibility for the safely of men machinery materials and for results obtained immediately before concreting all forms shall be thoroughly cleaned.
  • Centering design and its erection shall be got approved from the engineer-in-charge. One carpenter with helper shall invariably be kept present throughout the period of concreting. Movement of labour and other persons shall be totally prohibited for reinforcement laid in position. For access to different parts suitable mobile platforms shall be provided so that steel reinforcement in position is not disturbed. For ensuring proper cover, mortar blocks of suitable size shall be cast and tied to the reinforcement. Timber kapachi or metal pieces shall not be used for this purpose.

subsections.title: Transporting and Laying
subsections.description:
• The method of transporting and placing concrete shall be as approved. Concrete shall be so transported and placed that no contamination, segregation or loss of its constituent material takes place. All fromwork shall be cleaned and made free from standing   water   dust,   show   or   ice   immediately   before  placing   of   concrete. No concrete shall be placed in any part of the structure until the approval of the engineer-in-charge has been obtained.
  • Concreting shall proceed continuously over the area between construction joints. Fresh concrete proper contraction joint is formed. Concrete shall be compacted in its final position within 30 minutes of its discharge from the mixer. Except where otherwise agreed to by the engineer-in-charge, concrete shall be deposited in horizontal layers to a compacted depth of not more than 0.45 meter when internal vibrators are used and not exceeding 0.30 meter in all other cases.
  • Unless otherwise agreed to by the Engineer-in-charge concrete shall be dropped in to place from a height exceeding 2 meters. When trucking or chutes are used they shall be kept close and used in such a way as to avoid segregation. When concreting has to be resumed on a surface which has hardened, it shall be roughened, swept clean, thoroughly wetted and covered with a 13 mm. thick layer of mortar composed of cement and sand in the same ratio as in the concrete mix itself. This 13 mm. layer of mortar shall be freshly mixed and placed immediately before placing of new concrete. Where concrete has not fully hardened, all lateness shall be removed by scrubbing the wet surface with wire or bristle brushes, care being taken to avoid dislodgement of any particles of coarse aggregate. The surface shall then be thoroughly wetted, all free water removed and then coated with neat cement grout. The first layer of concrete to be placed on this surface shall not exceed 150 mm. in thickness and shall be well rammed against old work, particular attention being given to corners and close spots.
  • All concrete shall be compacted to produce a dense homogeneous mass with the assistance of vibrators, unless otherwise permitted by the Engineer-in-charge for exceptional cases, such as concreting under water, where vibrators cannot be used. Sufficient vibrators in serviceable condition shall be kept at site so that spare equipment is always available in the even of breakdowns. Concrete shall be judged to be compacted when the mortar fills the spaces between the coarse aggregate and begins to cream up to form an even surface. Compaction shall be completed before the initial setting stats i.e. within 30 minutes of addition of water to dry mixture. During compaction, it shall be observed that needle vibrators are not applied on reinforcement which is likely to destroy the bond between concrete and reinforcement.

subsections.title: Curing
subsections.description: • Immediately after compaction, concrete weather including rain, running water, shocks, vibration, traffic, rapid temperature charges, frost and drying out process. It shall be covered with wet sacking has Sian or other similar absorbent material approved, soon after the initial set, and shall be kept continuously wet for a period of not less than 14 days from the date of placement. Masonry work over foundation concrete may be started after 48 hours of its laying but curing of concrete shall be continued for a minimum period of 14 days.

subsections.title: Sampling and testing of concrete
subsections.description:
• Samples from fresh concrete shall betaken as per I.S. 1199-1959 and cubes shall be made, cured and tested at 7 days of 28 days as per requirements in accordance with I.S. 526-1959. A random sampling procedure shall be adopted to ensure that each concrete batch shall have a reasonable chance of being tested i.e. the sampling should be spread over the entire period of concreting and cover all mixing units. The minimum frequency of sampling of concrete of each grade shall be in accordance with following:
    Quantity Of Concrete in Work No. Of Samples
     1 - 5 Cmt 1
     6 - 15 Cmt 2
     16  30 Cmt 3
     31 - 50 Cmt 4
  • Note :  At least one simple shall be taken from each shift, Ten test specimens shall be made from each sample, five for testing at 7 days and the remaining five at 28 days. The samples of concrete shall be taken on each day of concreting as per above frequency. The number of specimens may be suitably increased  as  deemed  necessary  by  the  Engineer-in-charge  when  procedure  of  tests  given  above reveals a poor quality of concrete and in other special cases.
  • The average of the group of cubes cast for each day shall not be less than the specified cube strength of 150 K/g Cm 2 at 28 days. 20% of the cubes cast for each day may have value less than the specified strength provided the lowest value is not less than 85% of the specified strength. If the concrete made in accordance with the proportions given for a particular grade does not yield the specified strength, such concrete shall be classified as belonging to the appropriate lower grade. Concrete made in accordance with the Proportions given for a particular grade shall not, however be placed in a higher grade on the ground that the test strength are higher then the minimum specified.

subsections.title: Stripping
subsections.description:
• The Engineer-in-charge shall be informed in advance by the contractor of hr> intention to strike the form work. While fixing  the  time  of  removal  of  form  work,  due  consideration  shall  be  given  to  local  conditions, character of the structure, the weather and other conditions that influence the setting of concrete and of the materials used in the mix. In normal circumstances (generally where temperatures are above 20.C) and where ordinary concrete is used, forms may be struck after expire or periods specified in item No.9.1 (A) for respective item of form work.
  • All form work shall be removed without causing any shock or vibration as would damage the concrete. Before the soft and struts are removed, the concrete surface shall be gradually exposed, where necessary in order to ascertain that concrete has sufficiently hardened. Centering shall be gradually and uniformly lowered in such a manner as to permit the concrete to take stresses due to its own weight uniformly and gradually. Where internal metal tiles are permitted, they or their removable parts shall be extracted without causing any damage to the concrete and remaining holes filled with mortar. No permanently embedded metal part shall have less than 25 mm. cover to the finished concrete surface. Where it is intended to re-use the form work, it shall be cleaned and made good to the satisfaction of the Engineer-in-charge. After removal of form work and shutting, the Executive Engineer shall inspect the work and satisfy by random checks that concrete produced is of good quality.
  • Immediately after the removal of forms, all exposed bolts etc. passing through the cement concrete member and used for stuttering or any other purpose shall be cut inside the cement concrete member to a depth of at least 25 m. below the surface of the concrete and the resulting holes be filled by cement mortar, all fins, caused by form joints, all cavities produced by the removal of form tiles and all other holes and depressions, honeycomb spots, broken edges or comers and other defects, shall be thoroughly cleaned", saturated with water and carefully pointed an rendered true with mortar of cement and fine aggregate mixed in proportions used in the grade of concrete that is being furnished and of as dry consistency as is possible to use. Considerable pressure shall be applied in filling and pointing to ensure through filling in all voids. Surface which are pointed shall be kept moist for a period of 24 hours. If rock pockets/honeycombs in the opinion of the Engineer-in-charge are of such an extent or character as to effect the strength of the structure materially or to endanger the life of the steel reinforcement, he may declare the concrete defective and require the removal and replacement of the portions of structure affected.
  • The Above specification of ordinary concrete shall be followed except that the concrete mix shall be designed form preliminary tests. The proportioning of cement and aggregates shall be done by weight and necessary precautions shall be taken in the production to ensure that the required work cube strength is attained and maintained. The controlled concrete shall be in grades of M-100, M-150, M-200, M-250, M-300, M-350 & M-400 with prefix controlled added to it. The letter M refers to mix and the numbers specify 28 days works cube compressive strength of 150 mm. cubes of the mix expressed in Kg./Crnt.

subsections.title: Proportion of Mix
subsections.description:
• The proportion of cement, sand and coarse aggregate shall be determined of weight. The weight batch machine shall be used for maintaining proper control over the proportion of aggregates as per mix design. The strength requirements of different grades of concrete shall be as under:
    Grade Concrete Compressive strength of 15 cms. cubes in Kg./Cmt. at 28 days, conducted in accordance with I.S. 516-1959.
    Preliminary test Min.    		 Work test Min.
    M-150 200 150
    M-200 260 200
    M-250 320 250
    M-300 380 300
    M-350 440 350
    M-400 500 400
  • In all cases, the 28 days compressive strength specified in above be the criteria for acceptance or rejection of the concrete. Where the strength of a concrete mix as indicated by tests, lies in between the strength of any two grades specified in the above table, such concrete shall be classified in for purpose as concrete belonging to the lower of the grades between which its strength lies.
  • The Tremix concrete flooring work shall be executed in accordance with IS 456 and IS 10262 using approved design mix concrete of grade M25. The subgrade or base shall be properly prepared, compacted to the required density, and finished to correct line and level, free from loose soil, debris, oil, or standing water. Steel formwork using MS channels shall be fixed rigidly in true alignment, properly supported, and oiled to prevent adhesion of concrete, conforming to IS 2062. Concrete shall be machine batched by weight, thoroughly mixed, and transported to the site without segregation and placed within the specified time. It shall be laid in panels not exceeding 15 m × 15 m in a continuous operation to avoid cold joints, and uniformly spread and compacted using needle vibrators and screed vibrators ensuring complete compaction without over-vibration.
  • Immediately after placing and leveling, the Tremix vacuum dewatering process shall be carried out by placing filter mats and applying vacuum pressure to remove excess water and enhance surface strength and density. Floor hardener shall be uniformly applied at the rate of 2 kg per square meter in two stages over the semi-plastic concrete surface after the evaporation of bleed water, ensuring proper bonding without addition of extra water. The surface shall then be finished using power floaters followed by power trowels to achieve a smooth, dense, and uniform finish free from undulations and defects.
  • Construction joints shall be provided at locations of stoppage of work and shall be straight and properly aligned. Dummy joints shall be formed by saw cutting within 12 to 24 hours of concreting, to a depth equal to one-third of the slab thickness and not less than 10 mm in width, in a regular or zig-zag pattern as specified. Expansion joints shall be provided at intervals of 15 meters or as directed, using approved compressible filler boards of minimum 20 mm thickness. All joints shall be thoroughly cleaned, primed, and sealed with approved hot-applied bitumen sealing compound conforming to IS 1834 to ensure watertightness and flexibility.
  • Edges shall be neatly finished and rounded to prevent chipping. Curing shall commence within 24 hours of finishing and shall be continued for a minimum period of 7 days, preferably 14 days, by ponding or other approved methods as per IS 456 to prevent surface cracking and ensure proper strength development. The finished surface shall be true to line and level within specified tolerances, smooth, hard, and free from cracks, honeycombing, laitance, or surface dusting. Any defective work not meeting the specified standards shall be repaired or replaced as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: SPECIFICATIONS FOR FORMWORK, CENTERING AND SCAFFOLDING

subsections.title: Materials
subsections.description: • Formwork shall be in plywood, sawn timber or steel as required for walls, stairs, slab, beams, columns, parapets, etc. for all concrete work.

subsections.title: Workmanship
subsections.description: • The formwork shall conform to the shape, lines and dimensions as shown on the drawings and shall be so constructed so as to remain sufficiently rigid and water-tight, during placement and compaction of the concrete. Adequate arrangement shall be made by the Contractor to safe guard against any settlements of the formwork during the course of concreting and after concreting.

subsections.title: Centering
subsections.description:
• The centering, which has been got approved should be sufficiently strong and safe before, during and after pouring concrete and should be so erected that it would allow removal of forms in proper sequence without damaging either the concrete or the forms to be removed.
  • The props of centering shall be provided on firm foundation or base of sufficient strength to carry the loads, without any settlement.

subsections.title: Scaffolding
subsections.description:
• All scaffolding, hoisting arrangements and ladders etc, required for facilitating of concrete shall be provided and removed on completion work by Contractor, at his own expense. The scaffolding, hoisting arrangement, ladders etc shall be strong enough to withstand all live, dead and impact loads expected to act. The Contractor shall be solely responsible for the safety of the scaffolding, hoisting arrangement, ladders, work and workmen etc.
  • The scaffolding, hoisting arrangement and ladders shall allow easy approach to the work spot and afford easy inspection.

sections.title: Mode Of Measurement & Payment
sections.description:
• The consolidated cubical contents of concrete work as specified in item shall be measured. No deduction shall be made for (a) Ends of dissimilar materials such as joints, beams, posts, girders, falters, purling trusses, corbels and steps etc., up to 500 Sq, Cm. in section.
  • The Above specifications of shall be followed, except that the controlled concrete R.C.C. work as specified in item shall be measured under this item. The rate includes cost of form work.
  • The rate include cost of all materials labour, tools and plant required for mixing, placing in position vibrating and compacting, finishing as directed, curing and all other incidental expenses as well as test charges for producing concrete of specified strength. The rate includes the cost of form work but excluding the cost of reinforcement.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one cubic meter.

Description: Low Height Back Unit Storage (1.50 X 0.45 X 0.75) (LxDxH) Providing and fixing the Low height storage for 18mm thick (Plywood Board) post forming laminated top with 6mm thick plywood at backside finished with 1mm. thick approved laminate, made out of 18mm thick plywood with exterior side 1mm. and interior side 0.6mm. Approved laminate. Storage unit box (measurement shown in drawing) with wooden bedding patti/PVC, lock and telescopic channel. Shutter should be made of 18mm. thick  post forming Plywood with magnet, multiple drawer lock, S.S. legs (75mm height) in bottom, auto hinges of HAFELE or equivalent. Including all materials and labour etc. complete as per shown in detailed drawing and instructions of engineer-in-charge.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• The storage unit shall be fabricated using 18 mm thick plywood board of BWR grade conforming to IS 303. The top shall be finished with post-formed decorative laminate of approved make, shade, and texture. The external surfaces shall be laminated with 1.0 mm thick laminate, while the internal surfaces shall be finished with 0.6 mm thick laminate of approved quality.
  • The back panel shall be made from 6 mm thick plywood, finished with laminate as specified. The shutters shall be made from 18 mm thick post-forming plywood with laminate finish. All exposed edges shall be properly sealed and finished.
  • The unit shall be provided with approved quality hardware including locks, handles, telescopic channels, magnetic catchers, and auto hinges (such as Hafele or equivalent). Stainless steel legs of 75 mm height shall be provided at the bottom for support. Wooden bedding patti or PVC supports shall be used where required. All materials shall be new, free from defects, and approved by the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall include cutting, fabrication, assembling, and fixing of the storage unit as per approved drawings and dimensions. The carcass shall be constructed using 18 mm plywood ensuring proper alignment, strength, and durability. The back panel shall be securely fixed to maintain rigidity of the unit.
  • The top shall be post-formed and smoothly finished with laminate. Shutters shall be fabricated accurately and installed using auto hinges, ensuring proper opening and closing. Magnetic catchers and locking arrangements shall be installed for secure operation.
  • Internal compartments and shelves shall be provided as per design. Telescopic channels shall be installed wherever drawers are provided to ensure smooth sliding. All laminate surfaces shall be properly bonded and finished without bubbles, wrinkles, or defects.
  • The unit shall be supported on stainless steel legs of 75 mm height and properly aligned in position. All edges shall be machine finished, and joints shall be tight and durable. The complete unit shall be fixed in true line, level, and position at site as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The storage unit shall be measured on number basis (Each) for the specified size (1.50 m × 0.45 m × 0.75 m), in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include cost of all materials, laminates, adhesives, hardware fittings, SS legs, labour, fabrication, transportation, and fixing complete.
  • No separate payment shall be made for edge banding, fittings, wastage, polishing, or accessories, as these shall be deemed included in the item rate. The item shall be measured as completed and accepted as per the directions of the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Nos.

Description: Visitors Chair :- Providing and supplying Fixed based chair with PU molded cushion with MS pipe with hard chrome frame structure and white foam layer for seat and molded PU foam. White foam layer for back, both covered with thick cloth and draped with cloth of approved shade and texture with 2 years replacement guarantee. The chair to have wide polyurethane arm rest of approved shape. Chair should be completed in suitable shape. Rates to be inclusive of all taxes and free delivery at site. Selection of chair should be as approved by engineer-in-charge.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• The chair shall be of fixed base type constructed using a strong M.S. pipe frame structure of approved quality, finished with hard chrome plating to provide durability and corrosion resistance. The seat and back shall be provided with high-density polyurethane (PU) molded foam cushioning, supported with an additional white foam layer for enhanced comfort.
  • Both seat and back shall be upholstered with thick fabric of approved shade and texture, ensuring proper finish and durability. The chair shall be provided with wide polyurethane armrests of approved design for comfortable support. All materials, including frame, foam, fabric, and fittings, shall be of approved make and quality. The chair shall be supplied with a minimum two-year replacement guarantee against manufacturing defects.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall include supplying, assembling, and placing the fixed base visitor chair complete in all respects at site. The M.S. pipe frame shall be properly fabricated, bent, welded, and finished with hard chrome plating, ensuring smooth surface and uniform finish.
  • The seat and back cushions shall be securely fixed to the frame with proper alignment. Upholstery shall be neatly executed without wrinkles, loose stitching, or defects. Armrests shall be firmly fixed and properly aligned.
  • All joints shall be strong and stable, ensuring the chair remains balanced and durable under regular use. The chair shall be checked for structural stability, finish, and comfort before delivery. The finished product shall be aesthetically acceptable and suitable for office or public use as approved by the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The chair shall be measured on number basis (Each), in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include cost of materials, manufacturing, supply, transportation, assembly, delivery at site, and all taxes.
  • No separate payment shall be made for accessories, fittings, or minor components, as these shall be deemed included in the item rate. The item shall be measured as completed and accepted as per the directions of the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Nos.

Description: Low Back Chair :- Providing and supplying the Low Back Chair revolving based on synchro tilting mechanism with gas lift for adjustable height and medium curved back with seat and back PU molded cushion with MS pipe frame structure and while foam layer for seat and molded PU foam. White foam layer for back covered with thick cloth and draped with cloth of an approved shade. 5 legged revolving molded nylon chair based with good quality of PU castors with 2 years replacement guarantee. The chair to have wide polyurethane arm rest of the approved shape. Complete chair should be in suitable shape. Rates to be inclusive of all taxes and free delivery on site. Selection of chair should be as approved by engineerin- charge.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• The chair shall be of low back type with ergonomic design, constructed using a sturdy M.S. pipe frame structure of approved quality. The seat and back shall be provided with high-density polyurethane (PU) molded foam cushioning for durability and comfort. The foam shall be supported with an additional white foam layer and upholstered with thick fabric of approved shade and texture.
  • The chair shall be equipped with a synchro-tilting mechanism and a gas lift system for smooth and adjustable height control. The base shall consist of a five-legged revolving molded nylon structure of high strength. The chair shall be fitted with high-quality PU castors to ensure smooth mobility and long service life.
  • Armrests shall be made of polyurethane material of approved design, providing adequate support and comfort. All materials and components shall be of approved make and quality. The chair shall be supplied with a minimum two-year replacement guarantee against manufacturing defects.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall include supplying, assembling, and placing the low back revolving chair at site complete in all respects. All components including the base, gas lift, synchro-tilting mechanism, seat, backrest, armrests, and castors shall be properly assembled and securely fixed.
  • The mechanism shall function smoothly for reclining and height adjustment without noise or jerks. Upholstery work shall be neatly executed, free from wrinkles, uneven stitching, or defects. All joints and connections shall be firm, ensuring proper balance and stability of the chair.
  • The chair shall be tested for smooth rotation, mobility, and operational efficiency before handing over. The finished chair shall be comfortable, durable, and aesthetically suitable for office use, as approved by the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The chair shall be measured on number basis (Each), in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include cost of materials, manufacturing, supply, transportation, assembly, delivery at site, and all taxes.
  • No separate payment shall be made for accessories, fittings, or minor components, as these shall be deemed included in the item rate. The item shall be measured as completed and accepted as per the directions of the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Nos.

Description: Medium Back Chair :- Providing and supplying the Medium Back Chair revolving based on synchro tilting mechanism with gas lift for adjustable height and medium curved back with seat and back PU molded cushion with MS pipe frame structure and while foam layer for seat and molded PU foam. White foam layer for back covered with thick cloth and draped with cloth of an approved shade. 5 legged revolving molded nylon chair based with good quality of PU castors with 2 years replacement guarantee. The chair to have wide polyurethane arm rest of the approved shape. Complete chair should be in suitable shape. Rates to be inclusive of all taxes and free delivery on site. Selection of chair should be as approved by engineer in charge.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• The chair shall be of medium back type with ergonomic design, consisting of a strong internal frame made of M.S. pipe structure of approved quality. The seat and back shall be provided with high-density polyurethane (PU) molded foam cushioning, ensuring comfort and durability. The foam shall be covered with a layer of white foam and upholstered with high-quality fabric of approved shade and texture.
  • The chair shall be equipped with a synchro-tilting mechanism and gas lift system for adjustable seat height. The base shall be a five-legged revolving type made of molded nylon of superior strength and durability. The chair shall be fitted with high-quality PU castors for smooth movement.
  • Armrests shall be made of polyurethane material of approved shape and design, providing adequate support. All components shall be of approved make and quality, and the chair shall be supplied with a minimum two-year replacement guarantee against manufacturing defects.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall include supplying, assembling, and placing the medium back revolving chair at site as per requirements. The chair shall be properly assembled with all components including base, gas lift, mechanism, seat, backrest, armrests, and castors.

Description: Brick work using common burnt clay building bricks having crushing strength not less than 35 kg./Sq.Cm. in Cement Mortar 1:6  (1- Cement : 6 -fine sand) (B)  Conventional incl. watering,curing,scaffolding and racking out joints etc. comp as per directed by eng. incharge. (A) Foundation & Plinth

sections.title: Materials
sections.description: • Water shall conform to M-1. Cement mortar shall conform to M-11. Bricks shall conform to M-15.

subsections.title: Proportion
subsections.description: • The proportion of the cement mortar shall be 1:6 (1 cement: 6 fine sand) by volume.

subsections.title: Wetting of bricks
subsections.description: • The bricks required for masonry shall be thoroughly wetted with clean water for about two hours before use or as directed. The cessation of bubbles, when the bricks are wetted with water is as indication of through wetting of bricks.

subsections.title: Laying
subsections.description:
• Bricks shall be laid in English bond unless directed otherwise. Half or cut bricks shall not be used except when necessary to complete to bond; closures in such case shall be cut to required size and used near the ends of walls.
  • A layer of mortar shall be spread on full width for suitable length of the lower course. Each brick shall first be property bedded and set home by gently tapping with handle of trowel or wooden mallet. Its inside face shall be flushed with mortar before the next brick is laid and pressed against it. On completion of course, the vertical joints shall be fully filled from the top with mortar.
  • The walls shall be taken up truly in plumb. All courses shall be laid truly horizontal and all vertical joint shall be truly vertical. Vertical joints in alternate course shall generally be directly one over the other. The thickness of brick course shall be kept uniform.
  • The brick shall be laid with frog up wards. A set of tools comprising of wooden straight edges, man son's spirit level, square half meter rub, and pins, string and plumb shall be kept on the site of work for frequent checking during the progress of work.
  • Both the faces of walls of thickness greater than 23 cms. shall be kept in proper place. All the connected brick work shall be kept not more than one meter over the rest of the work. Where this is not possible, the work shall be raked back according to bond (and not left toothed) at an angle not steeper than 45 degrees.
  • All futures, pipes, outlets of water, hold fasts of doors and windows etc. which are required to be built in wall shall be embedded in cement mortar

subsections.title: Joints
subsections.description:
• Bricks shall be so laid that all joints are quite flush with mortar. Thickness of joints shall not exposed 12 mm. The face joints shall be raked out as directed by raking tools daily during the progress of work, when the mortar is still green so as to provide key for plaster or pointing to done.
  • The face of brick shall be cleaned the very day on which the work is laid and all mortar dropping removed.

subsections.title: Curing
subsections.description: • Green work shall be protected from rain suitably. Masonry work shall be kept moist on all the faces for a period of seven days. The top of masonry work shall be kept well wetted at the close of the day.

subsections.title: Preparation of foundation bed
subsections.description: • If the foundation is to be laid directly on the excavated bed, the shall be leveled, cleared of all loose materials, cleaned and wetted before stating masonry, If masonry is to be laid on concrete footing, the top of concrete shall be cleaned and moistened. The contractor shall obtain the engineer's approval for the foundation bed before foundation masonry is started. When pucca flooring is to be provided flush with the top to plinth, the inside plinth offset shall be kept lower than the outside plinth top by the thickness of the flooring.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The measurements of this item shall be taken for the brick masonry fully completed in foundation up to plinth. The limiting dimensions not exceeding those shown on the plinths or as directed shall be final. Battered tapered and curved portions shall be measured net.
  • No deduction shall be made from the quantity of brick work, for any extra payment made for embedding in masonry or making holes in respect of following items:
  • Ends of joists, beams, posts, girders, purlins, trusses, corbel, steps etc. where cross sectional area does not exceed 500 Sq.Cm.
  • Openings not exceeding 1000 Sq.Cm.
  • Wall plates and bed plates, bearing of slabs, chajjas and the like whose thickness does not exceed 10 Cms. and the bearing does not extend to the full thickness of wall.
  • Drainage holes, and recesses for cement concrete blocks to embed hold fasts for doors, windows etc.
  • Iron fixtures, pipes up to 300 mm. dia hold fasts, and doors and windows built into masonry and pipes etc. for concealed wiring.
  • Forming chases of section not exceeding 350 -Sq. Cm. in masonry.
  • Apertures for fire places shall not be deducted nor shall be paid for separately.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one cubic meter.

Description: Construction Septic tank inside dimention of 4.00 m in length & 2.5 m in width & 1.50 m depth including excavating any type of soil as shown and mentioned in the drawing,providing and laying 0.10 m thick plain cement concrete 1:3:6 ( 1 cement : 3 coarse sand : 6 graded stone agg.) 40 mm thick IPS flooring at bottom with brick masonary 0.23 m  thick walls CM 1:5 ( 1 cement :5 coarse sand ) and intermediate partition CM 1:4 & RCC Top slabs12 cms thick in  1:2:4 (1 cement : 2 coarse sand : 4 graded stone agg) including reinforcement as per design  and 15 mm thick cement plaster in CM 1:4 with floating coat of neat cement slurry inside, top and around tank below 15 cm on ground level, Also provide Two nos CI Manhole frame and cover of size 60 cm x 45 cm & 75 mm dia. PVC 10 kgf / Sq cm pressure  air vent pipe in 3.00 length with cowl etc complete as per direction of Engineer in charge.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• All materials used shall be of approved quality and conform to relevant Indian Standards. Cement shall be Ordinary Portland Cement conforming to IS 269. Fine and coarse aggregates shall conform to IS 383. Bricks shall be of first-class quality conforming to IS 1077.
  • Plain cement concrete for the base shall be in proportion 1:3:6 using 40 mm nominal size aggregates. RCC work for the slab shall be in 1:2:4 mix with reinforcement steel conforming to IS 1786. PVC pipes for vent shall be 75 mm dia of pressure class 10 kg/cm² conforming to IS 4985. C.I. manhole frames and covers shall be of approved quality and standard dimensions (600×450 mm).
  • Mortar for brick masonry shall be in CM 1:5 for walls and CM 1:4 for partition. Plaster shall be 15 mm thick in CM 1:4 with a smooth finish using neat cement slurry. All materials shall be new, free from defects, and approved by the Engineer-in-Charge prior to use.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall include excavation of septic tank pit of required size (4.00 m × 2.50 m × 1.50 m internal dimensions) in all types of soil, maintaining proper line, level, and safety precautions. The bottom shall be properly leveled and compacted before laying 100 mm thick PCC (1:3:6) as base.
  • Over the PCC base, IPS flooring shall be laid and finished smooth. The side walls shall be constructed in 230 mm thick brick masonry in CM 1:5 in true line and level. Intermediate partition walls shall be constructed in CM 1:4 as per design to divide chambers properly.
  • After masonry, 15 mm thick internal plaster in CM 1:4 shall be applied on all inner surfaces, including floor and walls, finished with a floating coat of neat cement slurry to make the surface smooth and watertight. External plaster shall also be applied up to 150 mm below ground level.
  • The top of the tank shall be covered with 120 mm thick RCC slab in 1:2:4 mix, including reinforcement and centering/shuttering as per design. Two nos. cast iron manhole frames and covers (600×450 mm) shall be fixed in position for access.
