  • A 75 mm dia PVC vent pipe of 3.0 m height shall be installed with proper fixing and provided with a cowl at the top to allow safe release of gases. All joints shall be properly sealed and the structure shall be cured adequately.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The septic tank shall be measured on a per number (Each) basis for the specified internal dimensions, in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include excavation, PCC, IPS flooring, brick masonry, partition walls, plastering, RCC slab with reinforcement and formwork, manhole covers, vent pipe with cowl, labour, curing, and all incidental works required for complete construction.
  • No separate payment shall be made for excavation, shuttering, reinforcement, curing, or minor accessories, as these shall be deemed included in the item rate. The item shall be measured as completed and accepted as per directions of the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Nos.

Description: Masonary work using Aerated light weight concrete block having crushing strength not less than 35 kg/sqcm for super structure above plinth level upto floor two level in cement mortar 1:5 ( 1 cement : 5 fine sand ) complete as per Technical Specification.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• All materials used in masonry work with aerated lightweight concrete (AAC) blocks shall conform to relevant Indian Standards and approved technical specifications. AAC blocks shall be factory-made, uniform in size, shape, and quality, having a minimum compressive strength of 35 kg/cm² and conforming to IS 2185 Part 3. The blocks shall be lightweight, well-cured, free from cracks, damage, or surface defects, and shall have accurate dimensions to ensure proper bonding and minimal mortar joints. Cement used shall be Ordinary Portland Cement (OPC) 43 or 53 grade conforming to IS 8112 or IS 12269, or Portland Pozzolana Cement (PPC) conforming to IS 1489, and shall be fresh and free from lumps.
  • Fine aggregate (sand) shall be clean, well-graded, and free from silt, clay, organic matter, and other deleterious substances, conforming to IS 383 and tested as per IS 2386. Water used for mixing mortar shall be clean and potable, free from harmful salts, oils, and organic impurities, and shall conform to IS 456. Cement mortar shall be prepared in the proportion of 1:5 (one part cement to five parts fine sand) by volume using proper mixing to achieve uniform consistency and workability.
  • Where required, suitable admixtures or bonding agents may be used in accordance with IS 9103, subject to approval. All materials shall be stored properly to prevent contamination and deterioration, and shall be tested and approved before use. Only materials conforming to the specified standards and approved by the Engineer-in-Charge shall be used in the work.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The masonry work using aerated lightweight concrete (AAC) blocks shall be carried out in accordance with relevant provisions of IS 2185 Part 3 and IS 456. The blocks shall be properly cured and moistened lightly before laying to prevent excessive absorption of water from the mortar. The masonry shall be set out to correct line, level, and alignment, and construction shall proceed true to plumb using proper templates, levels, and string lines. Cement mortar of proportion 1:5 (one part cement to five parts fine sand) shall be prepared in small batches to maintain workability and used within its initial setting time. Mortar joints shall be uniform and shall not exceed 10–12 mm in thickness, ensuring full bedding and proper bonding between blocks.
  • Blocks shall be laid with frog (if any) facing upwards and with staggered vertical joints to ensure proper bond, maintaining a minimum lap of one-third the block length. Each block shall be firmly bedded in mortar and tapped gently into position without disturbing adjacent blocks. All vertical joints shall be fully filled with mortar, and no hollow joints shall be permitted. The masonry shall be raised uniformly, with height of lift not exceeding 1.5 meters in a day, and proper curing shall be carried out for a minimum period of 7 days to prevent shrinkage cracks and ensure strength development.
  • Openings, corners, and junctions shall be constructed carefully with proper bonding, and necessary provisions for electrical conduits, pipes, and fixtures shall be made without damaging the masonry. Lintels, sills, and bands shall be provided as per drawings, and the masonry shall be properly toothed or keyed at junctions with RCC members. The finished surface shall be even, true to line and plumb, and free from cracks, bulging, or misalignment. All scaffolding shall be sound and properly erected, and workmanship shall ensure minimal wastage and neat finishing. Any defective or damaged work shall be dismantled and redone as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The measurement of masonry work in aerated lightweight concrete (AAC) blocks shall be carried out in accordance with the provisions of IS 1200 Part 2. The quantity shall be measured in cubic meters (m³) for the actual volume of masonry executed, calculated as length × breadth (thickness of wall) × height, based on the finished dimensions of the work. No deductions shall be made for openings up to 0.1 m² in area, and no extra measurement shall be made for jambs, soffits, or sills of such small openings. For openings exceeding 0.1 m², deductions shall be made for the full opening area, and corresponding additions shall be made for jambs, lintels, and sills, if separately specified.
  • The thickness of masonry shall be measured as the nominal thickness including mortar joints. Measurements shall be taken for different wall thicknesses and different types of mortar under separate items. No extra payment shall be made for scaffolding, curing, raking of joints, or for lifting materials to any height, as these are deemed to be included in the item rate. Reinforcement, if any, embedded in masonry shall be measured and paid separately unless otherwise specified. Chases, holes, or openings required for services shall not be measured separately and are deemed to be included in the rate unless otherwise stated.
  • All measurements shall be taken net as fixed in position, and the rate shall include the cost of all materials, labour, tools and plants, wastage, and all incidental charges required to complete the work in accordance with the specifications and as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one cubic meter.

Description: Providing cement vata ( 10 cm x 10 cm size ) quarter round in cement mortar 1:1 including neat cement finishing, watering etc. complete

sections.title: Materials
sections.description: • Water shall conform to M-1 .Cement mortar shall conform to M-11.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description: • The work of cement vata of 10 cms x 10 cms. size shall be earned out at Functions of parapets and terraces as directed. The vata shall he finished in quarter round shape. The work shall be earned out in the nest workman like manner. The inter portion of rain water pipe shall be rounded off properly during constructing the vata. The work shall be cured for 7 days.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The work shall be measured for finished item in running meter.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one running meter.

Description: Constructing a soak well of 2.5 m in inside diametre & 6.00 m deep of excavation any type soil with 0.23 m thick honey comb brick masonary wall 2.50 m from bottom & 0.30 m solid at top in cement mortar 1:6 ( 1 cement: 6 Sand) based on 0.10 cm thick CC 1:4:8  (1 cement : 4 coarse sand : 8 hand broken stone aggregate 40mm nominal size) & R.C.C. top slab 0.12 m thick in CC 1:2:4 including cost of form work & Reinforcement as per detail drawings or as directed by Engineer -in- charge

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• The materials used in the construction of soak well shall be of approved quality. Cement shall be Ordinary Portland Cement conforming to IS 269. Sand shall be clean, well-graded and conform to IS 383. Coarse aggregates shall be hard, durable, and conform to relevant standards for 40 mm nominal size.
  • Bricks used for honeycomb masonry shall be of first-class quality, well burnt, and conforming to IS 1077. Concrete for base shall be of grade 1:4:8 using 40 mm nominal size aggregates, and RCC slab shall be of mix 1:2:4 with reinforcement steel conforming to IS 1786. All reinforcement shall be clean, free from rust, and properly bent as per drawings.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall include excavation for soak well of 2.5 m internal diameter and 6.0 m depth in all types of soil, ensuring proper safety measures during excavation. The bottom shall be leveled and prepared, and a 100 mm thick cement concrete base (1:4:8) shall be laid using 40 mm aggregates.
  • The side walls shall be constructed using 230 mm thick honeycomb brick masonry for a height of 2.50 m from the bottom to allow percolation of water into the surrounding soil. The upper portion of 0.30 m height shall be constructed as solid brick masonry in cement mortar 1:6 to provide structural stability.
  • The masonry shall be built in true line and level with proper bonding and joints. After completion of masonry, the top shall be covered with a 120 mm thick RCC slab in cement concrete 1:2:4, including necessary reinforcement and formwork as per design and drawings.
  • Proper curing shall be carried out for all concrete and masonry work. The site shall be kept clean, and all work shall be executed in a safe and workmanlike manner. The finished soak well shall be stable, properly aligned, and fully functional as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The soak well shall be measured on a per number (Each) basis for the specified size (2.5 m dia × 6.0 m deep), in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include excavation, PCC base, brick masonry (honeycomb and solid), RCC slab with reinforcement and formwork, labour, curing, and all incidental works required for complete construction.
  • No separate payment shall be made for excavation, dewatering (if minor), centering, reinforcement, or curing, as these shall be deemed included in the item rate. The item shall be measured as completed and accepted as per directions of the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Nos.

Description: Providing throating or plaster drip and moulding to R.C.C. Chajja etc.comp

sections.title: Materials
sections.description: • Water shall conform to M-1. Cement shall conform to M-3. Sand shall conform to M-6 Cement mortar shall conform to M-11

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description: • The work shall be carried out as directed. The proportion of mix for finishing shall be in C.M. 1:2 by volume. Curing shall be done for not less than 7 days. The work shall be carried our in best workman like manner. The thwarting or plaster drip and mounding shall be one centimeter in thickness.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The work shall be measured for finished item in running meter.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one running meter.

Description: Providing 20 mm thick double coat mala cement plaster on interior brick/ concrete work for plastering comprising of base coat of 12 mm thick cement plaster in cement mortar 1: 4 ( 1 cement 4 coarse sand) in rough finishing and 8 mm thick top coat of cement mortar 1 : 2 ( 1 cement : 2 coarse sand) finished with trovel including scaffolding curing etc. complete. up to any floor any height    etc completed as directed by E.I.C/PMC including Providing and applying 3 mm thick Texture Plaster Terre Plaette (Specturm , Coral or equivalent) incoprating fine fillments made of polymer and aggergating natural stone powder with making grooves on base coat of  20 mm thick smooth mala plaster (which paid seperately) etc. complete.Colour and shade as approved by Architect/ Engineer in charge for at all floor ,all height..

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• The cement plaster shall be prepared using Ordinary Portland Cement conforming to IS 269 or equivalent, and clean, well-graded coarse sand conforming to IS 383. The plaster shall consist of a base coat of 12 mm thickness in cement mortar 1:4 (1 cement : 4 coarse sand) and a top coat of 8 mm thickness in cement mortar 1:2 (1 cement : 2 coarse sand).
  • The texture finish shall be 3 mm thick “Terre Palette” or equivalent (Spectrum, Coral, or approved make), composed of polymer-based binders, fine fillers, and natural stone aggregates. The material shall be of approved shade and texture as selected by the Architect/Engineer-in-Charge and shall be suitable for durable decorative finish. All materials shall be fresh, free from impurities, and approved prior to use.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall include preparation of the surface by cleaning, removing dust, loose particles, oil, and foreign matter to ensure proper bonding. The base coat of 12 mm thick cement plaster in CM 1:4 shall be applied uniformly on the prepared surface and finished rough to provide key for the next layer.
  • After initial setting, the second coat of 8 mm thick plaster in CM 1:2 shall be applied over the base coat and finished smooth with trowel to achieve a total thickness of 20 mm mala plaster. Proper curing shall be carried out for at least 7 days to ensure strength and durability.
  • Grooves shall be made on the plaster surface as per design and drawing to receive the texture finish. Over the prepared plaster surface, 3 mm thick texture plaster (Terre Palette or equivalent) shall be applied uniformly using suitable tools to achieve the desired decorative finish and pattern.
  • Scaffolding shall be provided as required for execution at all heights. The finished surface shall be even, free from cracks, undulations, or defects, and shall match the approved sample in colour, shade, and texture. The entire work shall be executed in a neat and workmanlike manner as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge/PMC.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The plastering and texture finish work shall be measured in square meters (Sqm) of finished surface area, in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include the cost of materials, labour, scaffolding, surface preparation, base plaster, finishing plaster, grooves, texture coating, curing, and all incidental works required for complete execution.
  • No separate payment shall be made for scaffolding, grooves, curing, or minor accessories, as these shall be deemed included in the item rate. The measurement shall be based on the actual finished surface area as accepted by the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Square Meter.

Description: Uncoursed Rubble Masonry with hard stone of approved quality in foundations and plinth in Cement Mortar 1:6 (1-cement : 6-coarse sand including levelling up etc. complete

sections.title: Materials
sections.description: • The cement mortar shall conform to M-11. Stone shall conform to M-16.

subsections.title: Dressing of stones
subsections.description: • Stone used for un coursed rubble masonry work shall be hammer dressed on the sides, and beds in which such a way as to close with the adjacent stone in the masonry work as strongly as possible. The face stones shall be dressed in such a manner as to give a specified pattern such as polygonal facing etc. The face of the stones shall be so dressed that bushing on the exposed face shall not project by more than 40 mm. from the general wall surface and on the face to be plastered, it shall not project by more than 19 mm., not shall have depressions more than 10 mm. from the average wall surface.

subsections.title: Laying
subsections.description:
• All the stone shall be sufficiently wetted before laying to prevent absorption of water from mortar. The wall shall be built true to plumb (of true to required batter when so specified). All connected walls in a structure shall be raised up informally and regularly. However if for any specific reason, one part of masonry is required to be left behind the wall shall be racked back at an angle not steeper than 45. Vertical toothed joints in masonry shall not be allowed. The work shall be carried out regularly and masonry of any day wall not be raised by more than 1 meter in height.
  • The stone shall be laid in an uncoarsed fashion, or random facing etc. However the masonry is required to be brought to level at various stages viz. plinth level window still level, roof level and any other level specifically shown in the drawings. This may be done first by adjusting the laying of stone to one level and then by providing leveling coarse of cement concrete 1:6:12 (1 cement: sand : 12 graded stone aggregate 20 mm. nominal size) or as otherwise specified.
  • Proper bonding shall be achieved by closely filling in adjacent stones as well as by using bond stones or through stones as described herein below. Face stones shall extend back sufficiently, and bond well with the masonry. The stone shall be carefully set so as to break joints and avoid formation of vertical joints. The depth of stone from the face of wall inwards shall not be less than weight or breadth at the face. The hearing or interior filling of the wall shall consist of rubble stones which may be of nay shape. Neither the face stone nor the hearing stone shall be so small to pass through circular ring of 150 mm. internal diameter in any direction nor shall any of them shall have minimum thickness 100 mm.
  • All stone shall be carefully laid, hammered down by a wooden mallet into position and solidly embedded in mortar, chips and spawns of stone may be used wherever necessary to avoid thick mortar bends or joints at the same time ensuring that no hollow space is left any where in the masonry. The chips used shall not be more than 20% by volume of masonry. The hearting shall be laid nearly level with face stones except that at about one meter intervals vertical bond stone or plumes projecting about 150 to 200 mm. shall be firmly embedded to from vertical bounding in masonry.

subsections.title: Bond
subsections.description: • Bond stones or through stones running right across the thickness of the wall shall be provided in wall up to 600 mm. thick. In thicker walls two stones overlapping each other by at least 150 mm. shall be provided across the thickness of the wall to form bond stones. There shall be at least one bond stone for every 0.5 sq. mt of wall surface. The bond stone shall be marked by a distinguishing letter during construction for subsequent verification and shall be laid staggered in sub sequent layers.

subsections.title: Quoins
subsections.description: • The quoins or corners stones shall be selected stone neatly dressed with hammer and/or chisel to form the required corner angle and laid header and stretcher alternatively, The bed top surface of quoins shall be chiseled dressed to give horizontal joints. The quoins shall have a uniform chisel draft of at least 25 mm. width at four edges of each exposed face, all the edges of the same face being in one plane. No quoins stone shall be smaller than 0.025 cum. in volume.

subsections.title: Jamb Stones
subsections.description: • The jamb stone shall be made with stone specified for quoins, that the stone provided on the jambs shall have their length equal to thickness of wall up to 600 mrn. and a line of headers shall be provided for walls thicker than 600 mm. as specified for bond.

subsections.title: Joints
subsections.description: • All the joints shall be completely filled with mortar and width shall not exceed 25 mm. when plastering of pointing is not required to be done, the joints shall be struck flush and finished simultaneously while laying the stone. Otherwise the joints shall be racked to a minimum depth of 20 mm. by a racking tools, during progress of laying while the mortar is still green.

subsections.title: Scaffolding
subsections.description: • Single or double scaffolding shall be used. The scaffolding shall be strong and sound. The holes left in masonry for supporting scaffolding shall be filled and made good before plastering.

subsections.title: Curing
subsections.description: • Green work shall be protected from rains by covering the same. Masonry shall be kept constantly moist on all the faces for a period of at least 7 days. The top of masonry shall be flooded at close of the day.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• All work shall be measured on the basis of finished dimensions and measured net except where otherwise specified. Only specified dimensions shall be allowed. Anything extra shall be ignored. The masonry work in foundation and plinth shall be measured under this item. No deduction shall be made, not extra payment made for the following:
  • Ends of joints, beams, spots, girders, rafters, purloins, trusses, corbles, etc. each up to 500 sq. cm. in section.
  • Opening each up to 0.1 sq.m.
  • Wall plates and bed plates, bearing of chhaja and like up to 10 cm. depth (bearing of floor and roof slabs shall be deducted from masonry).
  • Drain holes and recesses for cement concrete blocks to embed hold fasts for doors windows.
  • Building in the masonry iron fixtures pipes up to 300 mm. dia. hole fasts of doors and windows.
  • Forming theses in masonry up to section of 350 sq.cm.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one cubic meter.

Description: Providing and fixing PUF Insulated continueous sandwich panels for walls of total thickness  not less than 40 mm and width 1.0 m made out from continue line method on automatic plant.Panel shall have 0.35 mm thick pre coated GI sheet on both side of Polyurethane Foam confirming to IS 12436:1988.The Precoated sheet shall be of minimum 240 mpa steel grade confirming to IS 14246:1995  and shall have zinc coating of minimum 120 gsm as per IS:277:1992 , 5-7 microns epoxy primer on both side of the sheet and polyester top coat 15-18 micron.The PPGI Sheet shall have plastic protective guard film of minimum 25 microns  to avoid scratches during trasportation.The panels shall be vertically joined together by tongue and groove joints. The PU Foam shall be self-extinguishing, fire retardant type having minimum density of 40 Kg/Cu.mt.( +, - 2 Kgs) including 0.25 mm thick craft paper edging on both edges. The panels shall be fixed to the steel frame structure with minimum 5mm thick self tapping GI screws of required length and nos. with minimum spacing of 300 mm c/c.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• The sandwich panels shall be factory manufactured using a continuous production line on an automatic plant, having total thickness not less than 40 mm and standard width of 1.0 m. The panels shall consist of polyurethane foam (PUF) core sandwiched between two pre-coated galvanized iron (PPGI) sheets.
  • The PPGI sheets shall be 0.35 mm thick on both sides, made from steel of minimum 240 MPa grade conforming to IS 14246 and shall have a minimum zinc coating of 120 GSM as per IS 277. The sheets shall be coated with 5–7 microns epoxy primer on both sides and 15–18 microns polyester top coat, and shall be protected with a minimum 25-micron plastic protective film to prevent scratches during transportation and handling.
  • The core material shall be rigid polyurethane foam conforming to IS 12436, self-extinguishing and fire-retardant type, with a density of 40 ± 2 kg/m³. The panels shall have tongue-and-groove type interlocking joints for proper sealing and structural integrity. Edges shall be provided with 0.25 mm thick kraft paper edging. All fasteners shall be self-tapping G.I. screws of minimum 5 mm diameter, along with necessary washers and accessories of approved quality.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall include supplying, handling, erecting, and fixing PUF insulated sandwich panels in position as per approved drawings and directions of the Engineer-in-Charge. The panels shall be installed vertically and properly aligned to form a continuous wall surface.
  • The panels shall be joined together using tongue-and-groove joints to ensure tight fitment, structural stability, and thermal insulation. Proper care shall be taken during handling to avoid damage to the panels or protective coating. The panels shall be fixed to the supporting steel framework using self-tapping G.I. screws of suitable length at spacing not exceeding 300 mm center to center.
  • All joints shall be properly aligned and sealed where required to ensure airtightness and weather resistance. The protective film shall be removed after installation without damaging the surface. Necessary cutting and adjustments shall be carried out neatly to suit site conditions.
  • The finished work shall be rigid, properly aligned, thermally insulated, weather resistant, and aesthetically uniform as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The PUF sandwich panel work shall be measured in square meters (Sqm) of finished wall surface area, in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include the cost of panels, fasteners, fixing accessories, labour, erection, cutting, jointing, and all incidental works required for complete installation.
  • No separate payment shall be made for overlaps, fasteners, wastage, jointing, or minor accessories, as these shall be deemed included in the item rate. The measurement shall be based on actual installed area as accepted by the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Square Meter.

Description: Providing & Fixing fibre weather shed with 25 X 25 mm size medium guage square pipe with preparing the bracket incl. cutting the pipe welding and preparing front side corner shape with using approved quality of fibre sheet incl. fixing with nail on top edge and silicon for leakage purpose and joint at wall level with making nitch in wall to protect leakage of the water from wall etc. comp. with applying silicon solution at corner and every joints of fibre sheets and applying three coat black enamel paint to all fabricated structure etc. comp. as directed.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• The weather shed shall be made using approved quality fibre sheets (FRP/Polycarbonate type as specified), suitable for exterior use, weather resistant, and capable of withstanding wind and rain. The supporting framework shall consist of M.S. square pipes of size 25 mm × 25 mm of medium gauge, conforming to relevant standards such as IS 4923. The steel sections shall be straight, free from defects, and suitable for fabrication.
  • All fasteners such as nails, screws, and fixtures shall be of approved quality and corrosion resistant. Sealant used shall be silicone-based of approved make to ensure watertight joints. Paint shall consist of one coat of primer and three coats of approved quality black enamel paint for protection of steel members. All materials shall be new and approved by the Engineer-in-Charge prior to use.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall include fabrication and fixing of the weather shed using 25×25 mm M.S. square pipes, including cutting, welding, and forming brackets as per required shape and size. The front side shall be properly shaped and aligned to provide proper slope for rainwater drainage.
  • The brackets shall be securely fixed to the wall using appropriate anchoring methods. Necessary niches (grooves) shall be made in the wall at the junction to properly insert and seal the fibre sheet edges to prevent water leakage. The fibre sheets shall be fixed over the framework using suitable fasteners such as nails or screws, ensuring firm fixing and proper alignment.
  • All joints between sheets and at wall junctions shall be sealed using approved silicone sealant to ensure complete waterproofing. Special care shall be taken to seal corners and overlaps to avoid leakage.
  • After fabrication and fixing, all steel members shall be cleaned and provided with one coat of primer followed by three coats of black enamel paint. The completed weather shed shall be rigid, properly aligned, leakproof, and aesthetically finished as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The weather shed shall be measured in square meters (Sqm) of projected area, in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include the cost of fibre sheets, M.S. framework, fabrication, welding, fixing, sealant, painting, labour, and all incidental works required for complete installation.
  • No separate payment shall be made for brackets, fasteners, sealants, cutting, welding, painting, or minor accessories, as these shall be deemed included in the item rate. The measurement shall be based on the actual area installed and accepted by the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Square Meter.

Description: Supplying & fixing 6 mm th. Impreganted wired glass incl. cutting if necessary at 2.4 M. high & 0.60 M wide with approved wire mesh with all its accessories necessary fixtures and fastenings, wire clips, additional M.S. support, if required and applying approved quality putty or teak beading as per direction of the engineer inc charge etc. comp. as directed.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• The glass shall be 6 mm thick impregnated wired glass of approved quality and make, conforming to relevant Indian Standards such as IS 5437. The glass shall have embedded wire mesh uniformly distributed within the glass, providing improved safety and fire resistance. It shall be free from cracks, bubbles, waviness, or other defects and shall be of approved dimensions (2.40 m height × 0.60 m width or as specified).
  • All accessories such as wire clips, fasteners, M.S. supporting members (if required), putty or teak wood beading shall be of approved quality. The putty used shall be suitable for glazing work and resistant to weathering, while teak beading (if used) shall be properly seasoned and finished. All materials shall be new and approved by the Engineer-in-Charge prior to use.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall include supplying, cutting, and fixing 6 mm thick wired glass in position as per approved drawings and directions of the Engineer-in-Charge. The glass shall be carefully cut to required size, ensuring smooth and proper edges without chipping or cracking.
  • The glass shall be fixed in frames or openings using suitable wire clips, fasteners, and additional M.S. supports wherever required to ensure proper stability and safety. Proper care shall be taken during handling and installation to avoid breakage or damage to the glass.
  • The glass shall be secured using approved quality putty or teak wood beading, ensuring firm fixing and proper sealing against dust and water ingress. All edges shall be neatly finished, and the glass shall be aligned properly in position.
  • The finished work shall be neat, secure, properly aligned, and free from defects as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The wired glass work shall be measured in square meters (Sqm) of the area of glass fixed, in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include the cost of glass, cutting, fixing, clips, fasteners, putty or beading, M.S. supports (if required), labour, and all incidental works required for complete installation.
  • No separate payment shall be made for wastage, cutting, fixing accessories, or labour involved, as these shall be deemed included in the item rate. The measurement shall be based on the actual area fixed and accepted by the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Square Meter.

Description: Supplying, fabrication and erecting and fixing in position M.S.gutter of 1.00 M girth & shape as per detailed drawing made out from 3.15mm th. M.S. plate incl. cutting, holes, drilling, welding etc. with all necessary accessories such as nuts, bolts etc. incl. providing 40mm X 6mm MS flat at  1.20 mtrs. & provding  25mm X 6mm MS flat at  8.00 mtrs. C/C in each strips with fixing the gutter in line level on existing MS structure as per directed . Also incl. providing one coat of anticorrosive paint and two coats of synthetic enemel paint of approved quality etc. comp. as directed.(incl. removing rusted MS gutter from roof by using welding machine, chine pully block, incl. using necessary tools and plants like rope ladder or scaffolding work incl. taking due care during the work incl. stacking the servicible material and desposal of unservicibal materials comp. as  directed

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• The gutter shall be fabricated from 3.15 mm thick mild steel (M.S.) plate of approved quality conforming to relevant standards such as IS 2062. The M.S. plate shall be free from defects, rust, laminations, or surface irregularities and shall be suitable for fabrication of gutter sections as per approved drawings.
  • Stiffening members shall include M.S. flats of size 40 mm × 6 mm spaced at 1.20 m center to center and 25 mm × 6 mm flats at 8.00 m center to center, ensuring adequate rigidity and strength of the gutter. All accessories such as nuts, bolts, washers, and fasteners shall be of approved quality and compatible with the structure.
  • Protective coatings shall include one coat of approved anti-corrosive primer followed by two coats of synthetic enamel paint of approved brand and shade. All materials shall be new and approved by the Engineer-in-Charge prior to use.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall include removing the existing damaged or rusted M.S. gutter carefully using appropriate tools such as welding machines, chain pulley blocks, ropes, ladders, or scaffolding, ensuring safety and preventing damage to surrounding structures. Serviceable materials shall be properly stacked, and unserviceable materials shall be disposed of as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.

  • The new gutter shall be fabricated from 3.15 mm thick M.S. plates as per detailed drawings, including cutting, bending, edge preparation, drilling holes, and welding to form the required shape and size (1.00 m girth). Stiffeners using 40×6 mm and 25×6 mm M.S. flats shall be provided at specified intervals to ensure structural stability.

  • The fabricated gutter shall be erected and fixed in position on the existing M.S. structure in true line and level, ensuring proper slope for drainage of rainwater. Fixing shall be done using suitable fasteners such as nuts, bolts, and welding as required. All joints shall be properly welded and finished smooth to prevent leakage.
  • After fabrication and fixing, the entire gutter surface shall be thoroughly cleaned to remove rust, dust, and scale, followed by application of one coat of anti-corrosive primer and two coats of synthetic enamel paint to protect against corrosion and weathering.
  • The completed work shall be rigid, leakproof, properly aligned, and finished neatly as per approved drawings and directions of the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The M.S. gutter shall be measured in Kg along the centerline of the gutter, in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include the cost of materials, fabrication, removal of existing gutter, erection, fixing, stiffeners, welding, fasteners, painting, labour, tools, and all incidental works required for complete installation.
  • No separate payment shall be made for removal of old gutter, scaffolding, cutting, welding, painting, or accessories, as these shall be deemed included in the item rate. The measurement shall be based on the actual length installed and accepted by the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Kg.

Description: Supplying & fixing 25x6 mm size M.S. flat over the roof incl. drilling holes at 1.05 M. c/c and providing 10mm dia. G.I. 'J' or 'L' hooks with nits, washers, bitumen washers etc. & applying 3 coats of approved paint to steel work etc. comp. as directed.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• The M.S. flat shall be of size 25 mm × 6 mm, made from mild steel of approved quality, conforming to relevant Indian Standards such as IS 2062. The flat shall be straight, free from defects such as cracks, bends, and surface irregularities, and shall be of uniform cross-section.
  • The fixing accessories shall include 10 mm diameter G.I. ‘J’ or ‘L’ hooks, nuts, washers, and bitumen washers of approved quality to ensure proper fastening and weather resistance. All fasteners shall be corrosion resistant and suitable for roof application. Paints used for protective coating shall be of approved brand and quality, including primer and finishing coats suitable for steel surfaces exposed to weather conditions.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall include supplying, cutting, fabricating, and fixing 25×6 mm M.S. flats over the roof as per approved drawings and directions of the Engineer-in-Charge. The M.S. flats shall be laid in proper alignment and fixed securely at intervals of approximately 1.05 meters center to center.
  • Holes shall be drilled accurately in the M.S. flats at required spacing to accommodate 10 mm diameter G.I. ‘J’ or ‘L’ hooks. The hooks shall be fixed with nuts, washers, and bitumen washers to ensure firm anchorage and leakproof fixing at roof level. Proper tightening shall be ensured to avoid loosening due to vibration or environmental effects.
  • After fixing, the entire M.S. flat surface and exposed steel components shall be thoroughly cleaned to remove rust, dust, and loose particles. The steel work shall then be provided with one coat of approved anti-corrosive primer followed by three coats of approved quality paint of required shade to ensure durability and protection against corrosion and weathering.
  • The finished work shall be neat, properly aligned, securely fixed, and executed in a workmanlike manner as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The M.S. flat work shall be measured in running meters (Rmt) of installed length, in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include the cost of M.S. flats, G.I. hooks, nuts, washers, bitumen washers, drilling, fixing, fabrication, painting (all coats), labour, tools, and all incidental works required for complete installation.
  • No separate payment shall be made for fasteners, consumables, painting materials, or labour involved in fixing, as these shall be deemed included in the item rate. The measurement shall be taken for actual length installed and accepted by the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Kg.

Description: Providing & laying bela masonary using bela stones of approved quality and set in c.m. (1:6) incl. dressing the stones to required size & shape incl. racking out the joints incl. watering, curing, scaffolding etc. comp. as directed. (A) Ground Floor

sections.title: Materials
sections.description: • The stone or bela shall be white hard sand stone or block. The stone shall be sound hard rough and durable. It shall be free form skin. The thickness of bela or block shall not be less than 15 cms. or as directed. The mortar used shall consist. One part of cement and 6 parts of fine sand. Cement mortar shall conform to M-11.

subsections.title: Dressing of Stones
subsections.description: • Stone shall be chiseled on all the sides so that all six sides shall be in a rectangular shape and all the stones shall be so dressed that the bushing of the exposed face shall not project nor depressions for the general wall surfaces. The size of bela or block shall be as per thickness of the wall to be constructed or as directed.

subsections.title: Laying
subsections.description:
• All the stone shall be sufficiently wetted before laying to prevent absorption of water from mortar. All connected Walls in a structure shall normally be raised up uniformly and regularly. The vertical joint shall not be allowed and also it shall not be more than 12 mm. in thickness.
  • Proper bonding shall be made by laying bela or block side by side each other with lime mortar on bed as well as in between two bela or block vertically.

subsections.title: Bond Stones
subsections.description: • Bond stones or through stones running right across the thickness of the wall shall be provided in walls up to 450 mm. thick. In thicker walls two bela or blocks or laying each other by at least 150 mm. each other shall be provided across the thickness of the wall to bond stone. Such bond stone shall be at least one for every 1.0 sq. mt. area of the wall surface.

subsections.title: Joints
subsections.description: • All the joints shall be completely filled up with mortar and their thickness shall not exceed by 12 mm. When plastering or pointing is not required to be done, the joints shall be struck flush and finished, simultaneously while laying the stone. Otherwise the joints shall be raked to a minimum depth of 20 mm. during process of laying while mortar is still green.

subsections.title: Scaffolding
subsections.description: • Single or double scaffolding shall be used. It shall be strong and sound. The holes left in masonry for supporting shall be made good before plastering.

subsections.title: Curing
subsections.description: • Green work shall be cured fir a period of 7 days continuously.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The work shall be measured on the basis of finished dimensions. No dedication shall be made nor extra payment shall be made for the following:
  • (a) Ends of joint, beams, posts, girders, rafters, purlins, corbels etc., each up to 500 sq.cms. in section
  • (b) Opening each up to 0.10 Sq.m.
  • (c) Small plates and bed plates, bearing of chhajas and like up to 10 cms. depth (bearing or floor and roof shall" be deducted from masonry),
  • (d) Drain holes and recesses for cement concrete blocks to embedded hold fasts of one cubic meter.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one cubic meter.

Description: Providing ridges or hips 600 mm overall in plain G.I. sheet class-3 fixed with G.I.J. or L Hooks and nuts 8mm dia G.I. Limpet and bitumen washer complete. (1) 0.80 mm thick sheet.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• The ridges or hips shall be made from 0.80 mm thick plain galvanized iron (G.I.) sheet of Class-3, conforming to relevant Indian Standards such as IS 277. The sheets shall have uniform zinc coating, be free from rust, defects, waviness, or surface irregularities, and shall be suitable for roofing applications.
  • The ridge/hip sections shall be properly formed to a total width of 600 mm to suit the roof profile. Fixing accessories shall include 8 mm diameter G.I. ‘J’ or ‘L’ hooks, G.I. limpet washers, nuts, and bitumen washers of approved quality to ensure firm and leakproof fixing. All fasteners shall be corrosion-resistant and compatible with the roofing system.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall include supplying, cutting, bending, and fixing of G.I. ridge or hip pieces of 600 mm overall width to match the roof profile as per approved drawings and directions of the Engineer-in-Charge. The ridge/hip sheets shall be properly shaped and aligned along the ridge or hip line of the roof.
  • The sheets shall be fixed to the roofing system using 8 mm dia G.I. ‘J’ or ‘L’ hooks, nuts, and washers including bitumen washers to ensure watertight fixing and prevent leakage at fixing points. Proper overlapping shall be maintained between adjacent ridge/hip pieces to ensure continuity and weatherproofing.
  • Care shall be taken during installation to maintain alignment, slope, and neat finish. All joints and laps shall be properly sealed to prevent water ingress. The work shall be executed carefully without damaging the roofing sheets or coating. The finished ridge/hip shall be rigid, leakproof, properly aligned, and aesthetically uniform as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The ridge or hip work shall be measured in Square (Smt) along the ridge/hip line, in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include the cost of G.I. sheets, cutting, bending, hooks, nuts, washers, bitumen washers, labour, fixing, and all incidental works required for complete installation.
  • No separate payment shall be made for overlaps, fasteners, sealants, or minor accessories, as these shall be deemed included in the item rate. The measurement shall be based on the actual length installed and accepted by the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Square Meter.

Description: (B) Providing & Fixing  0.5mm th. PPGI sheet for North Light Curve 1 meter wide

sections.title: Materials
sections.description: • The sheet shall be suitable for forming into North Light Curve profile of 1.0 meter width and shall possess adequate flexibility and strength to maintain the curved shape without cracking or deformation. All accessories such as self-drilling screws, EPDM washers, sealants, flashing, and fixing clips shall be of approved quality and compatible with the roofing system. The material shall be free from defects, scratches, or coating damage and shall be approved by the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall include supplying, cutting, bending, and fixing 0.5 mm thick PPGI sheets to form North Light Curve roofing of 1.0 meter width as per approved drawings and directions of the Engineer-in-Charge. The sheets shall be properly curved to the required profile using appropriate methods without damaging the coating.
  • The sheets shall be laid in position with proper overlapping and alignment to ensure watertightness and uniform appearance. Fixing shall be done using self-drilling screws with EPDM washers or approved fixing system to prevent leakage and ensure firm anchorage. All joints, laps, and edges shall be properly sealed with suitable sealants to avoid water ingress.
  • Care shall be taken during handling and installation to avoid scratches, dents, or damage to the painted surface. The sheets shall be fixed securely to the supporting structure, maintaining proper slope, alignment, and curvature. The finished work shall be leakproof, properly aligned, and aesthetically uniform as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• TheNorth Light Curve work shall be measured in running meters (Rmt) of finished surface area of the North Light Curve, in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include  accessories, fasteners, sealants, labour, cutting, bending, fixing, and all incidental works required for complete installation.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Running Meter.

Description: Providing 10mm thick cement plaster in single coat on brick/concrete walls for Ceiling / Soffit of Stairs for interior plastering upto floor two level and finished even and smooth in (i)Cement mortar 1:3 (1-cement:3-sand)   incl. finishing with a floating coat of neat cement slurry as instructed by the engineer incharge etc.complete (A) Ground Floor

sections.title: Materials
sections.description: • Water shall conform to M-1. The cement mortar of proportion 1:3 shall conform to M-13.

subsections.title: Scaffolding
subsections.description: • Wooden bullies, bamboos, planks, trestles and other scaffolding shall be sound. These shall be properly examined before erection and use. Stage scaffolding shall be provided for ceiling plaster which shall be independent of the walls.

subsections.title: Preparation of back-ground
subsections.description:
• The surface shall be cleaned of all dust, loose mortar droppings, traces of algae, efflorescence and other foreign matter by water or by brushing. Smooth surface shall be toughened by wire brushing if it is not hard and by hacking if it is hard. In case of concrete surface, if a chemical retarded has been applied to the form work, the surface shall be roughened by wire brushing and all the resulting dust and loose particles cleaned off and care shall be taken that none of the readers if left on the surface. Trimming of projections on brick/concrete surfaces where necessary shall be carried out to get an even surface.
  • Raking of joints in case of masonry where necessary shall be allowed to dry out for sufficient period before carrying out the plaster work.
  • The work shall not be soaked but only damped evenly before applying the plaster. If the surface becomes dry, such area shall be moistened again.
  • For external plaster, the pestering operation shall be started from top floor and carried downwards. For internal plaster, the plastering operations may be-started wherever the building frame and cladding work are ready and the temporary supports of the ceiling resting on the wall of the floor have been removed. Ceiling plaster shall be completed before starting plaster to walls.

subsections.title: Application of plaster
subsections.description:
• The plaster about 15x15 cms. shall be first applied horizontally and vertically at not more than 2 meters intervals over the entire surface to serve as gauge. The surfaces of these gauges shall be truly in plane of the finished plastered surface. The mortar shall then be applied in uniform surface slightly more than the specified thickness, then brought to a true surface by working a wooden straight edge reaching across the gauges with small upward and sideways movements at a time. Finally, the surface shall be finished off true with a trowel or wooden float according as a smooth or a smooth or a sandy granular texture is required Excessive troweling or overworking the float shall be avoided. All corners, arises, angles and junctions shall be truly vertical or horizontal as the case may be and shall be carefully finished. Hounding or chamfering, corners, arises junctions etc. shall be carried out with proper templates to be size required.
  • Cement plaster shall be used within half an hour after addition of water. And mortar or plaster which is partially set shall be rejected and removed forthwith from the site.
  • In suspending the work at the end of the day, the plaster shall be left out clean to the line both horizontally and vertically, when recommencing the plaster, the edges of the old work shall be scraped clean and wetted with cement putty before plaster is applied to the adjacent areas to enable the two to properly join together. Plastering work shall be closed at the end of the day on the body of the wall and nearer than 15 cm. to any corners or arises. It shall not be closed on the body of features such as plaster bands and cornices not at the corners or arises. Horizontal joints in plaster work shall not also occur on parapet tops and copings as these invariably lead to leakage. No portion of the surface shall be left out initially to be packed up later on.
  • Each coat shall be kept damp continuously till the next coat is applied or for a minimum period of 7 days. Moistening shall commence as soon as plaster is hardened sufficiently. Soaking of walls shall be avoided and only as much water as can be readily absorbed shall be used, excessive evaporation on the sunny or windward side of building in hot air or dry weather shall be prevented by hanging matting or gunny bags oh the outside of the plaster and keeping them wet.
  • The coat of cement and fine sand mortar of proportion V1 (1.5 mm thick about) shall be applied to the plastered surface with a trowel to provide uniform texture while the bas;. coat is still plastic.
  • In any continuous face of wall the finishing treatment should be carried out continuously and day lo day breaks made to coincide with architectural breaks in order to avoid unsightly Junctions

subsections.title: Curing
subsections.description: • All the plaster work shall be kept damp continuously for a period 7 days.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The rate shall include the cost of all materials, labour and scaffolding etc. involved in the operations described under workmanship.
  • All plastering shall be measured in square meters unless otherwise specified. Length breadth or height shall be measured correct to a centimeter.
  • Thickness of the plaster shall be exclusive of the thickness of the key i.e. grooves or open joints in brick work, stone work etc. or space between laths. Thickness of plaster shall be average thickness with minimum 10 mm. at any point on this surface.
  • This item includes plastering up to floor two level.
  • The measurement of wall plastering shall be taken between the walls or partition (dimensions before plastering being taken) for length and from the top of floor or skirting to ceiling for height. Depth of cover of cornices if any shall be deducted.
  • Soffits of stairs shall be measured as plastering on ceilings, following soffits shall be measured separately.
  • For jambs, soffits, sills etc. for openings not exceeding 0.5 sq. met each in area for ends of joints beams, posts, girders, steps etc. not exceeding 0.5 sq. mt each in area and for openings exceeding 0.5. sq. mt and not exceeding 3.00 sq. mt. in each area deductions and additions shall be made in the following manners.
  • No deductions shall be made for ends of joints, beams, posts etc. and openings not exceeding 0.5 sq. mt each and no addition shall be made for reveals, jambs, soffits, sils etc. of these openings, for finish to plaster around ends of joints, beams posts etc.
  • Deduction for openings exceeding 0.5 sq. mt but not exceeding 3 sq.mt. each shall be made as follows and no addition shall be made for ravels, jambs, soffits, sills etc. of these openings, (i) When both faces of all wall are plastered with same plaster, deduction shall be made for one face only, (ii) When two faces of wall are plastered with different types of plasters or if one face is plastered and the other pointed, deductions shall be made from the plaster or pointing on the side of frame for door, window etc. on which width of reveals is less than that on the other side but no deductions shall be made on the other side. Where width of reveals on both faces of all are equal, deductions of 50% of area of opening on each face shall be made from areas of plaster and / or pointing as the case may be.
  • For openings having door frames equal to or projecting beyond the thickness of wall, full deduction for opening shall be made from each plastered face of the wall.
  • in case of openings of area above 3 sq. mt. each, deduction shall be made for openings but jambs, soffits sand sills shall be measured.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of One sq. meter.

Description: Providing & Fixing window having extruded aluminium colour anodized  section frame main outer size 63.5 x38.1x1.95mm(Jindal or Hindalco section No.4605 @ Wt.1.094 Kg/Rmt) horizontal Two Track member size 61.85x31.75x1.2mm(of Jindal or Hindalco section No.8687 @ Wt.of 0.695 Kg/mt.) vertical member of size 61.85x 31.75x1.3mm (of Jindal or Hindalco section No. 8758 @ wt of 0.659 Kg/Mt.) with Sluiding shutter of horizontal member size 40x18x1.29mm (of Jindal or Hindalco section No. 8949 @ wt.of 0.456 kg/mt.) vertical member of size 40x18x1.29mm (of jindal or Hindalco section No.8947 @ wt.of 0.456 Kg/ mt./section 8948 @ wt of 0.457 kg/mt.) with 5mm thick transperant bronze colour tinted float glass with colour anodized aluminium fittings & fixtures with transparent silicon sealant glass fixing to frame as per detail including 12 mm square M.S. bars 100mm C/C in 25x6 mm M.S.Flate as a frame with One coat of anticorrosive paint & two coats of oil paint as a safty grill for protaction.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• All materials used for providing and fixing aluminium sliding windows shall conform to relevant Indian Standards and approved makes such as Jindal or Hindalco. The aluminium sections shall be extruded sections conforming to IS 733 and IS 1285, and shall be colour anodized with a uniform anodic coating of not less than 15 microns thickness as per IS 1868. The main outer frame shall be of size 63.5 × 38.1 × 1.95 mm, and the sliding shutter sections, verticals, and horizontals shall be of specified sizes and weights as per approved section details.
  • Glass used shall be 5 mm thick transparent bronze tinted float glass conforming to IS 14900, free from bubbles, waves, or defects. All fittings and fixtures such as rollers, locks, handles, and fasteners shall be of approved quality aluminium or stainless steel, smooth in operation, and compatible with the system. Silicon sealant used for glass fixing shall be of approved make, weather-resistant, and suitable for glazing applications.
  • The safety grill shall be fabricated using 12 mm square mild steel bars spaced at 100 mm center-to-center, fixed in a frame of 25 × 6 mm MS flat, conforming to IS 2062. The MS grill shall be treated with one coat of approved anticorrosive primer and finished with two coats of oil paint of approved shade. All materials shall be new, free from defects, and approved by the Engineer-in-Charge before installation.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The aluminium sliding window shall be fabricated and installed in accordance with approved drawings and manufacturer’s specifications. The aluminium frames shall be accurately cut, machined, and assembled with proper mitred joints to ensure rigidity, alignment, and smooth operation. The frames shall be fixed in position true to line, level, and plumb using suitable fasteners, screws, and packing materials, ensuring firm anchorage with the surrounding masonary or RCC without distortion.
  • Sliding shutters shall be properly assembled and fitted with rollers to ensure smooth, noiseless movement within the track. The glass panes shall be cut to required sizes and fixed in the shutters using appropriate rubber gaskets and sealed with approved transparent silicon sealant to ensure watertightness and airtightness. Care shall be taken to avoid any damage to glass or aluminium surfaces during fixing. All joints between frame and wall shall be properly sealed to prevent ingress of water.
  • The MS safety grill shall be fabricated to the required size, welded properly with uniform spacing of bars, and fixed securely to the window frame or adjacent structure. The grill shall be cleaned, primed with one coat of anticorrosive paint, and finished with two coats of oil paint, ensuring uniform coverage and proper drying between coats. The entire installation shall be neat, free from scratches, dents, or defects, and all moving parts shall be checked for proper functioning. Protective films on aluminium sections shall be removed only after completion of work, and the finished window shall be cleaned and handed over in perfect condition.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The aluminium sliding window shall be measured in square meters (m²) for the actual area of the opening covered, calculated as width × height of the outer frame, in accordance with IS 1200 Part 14. The rate shall include the cost of all materials such as aluminium sections, glass, fittings, fixtures, sealants, and all labour, tools, and plants required for fabrication and installation. The cost of anodizing, glazing, and fixing of shutters shall be deemed to be included in the item rate.
  • The MS safety grill, if included in the item, shall also be measured in square meters unless specified otherwise, and its cost including fabrication, welding, painting, and fixing shall be included in the rate. No separate measurement shall be made for small fittings, screws, sealants, or for cutting, wastage, or fixing accessories. All work shall be measured net as fixed in position, and no extra payment shall be made for scaffolding, lifting, or any incidental works required to complete the installation as per specifications and as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of One sq. meter.

Description: Providing and fixing window having extruded aluminum Colour anodized Three track section frame of DOMAL section , main outer size 65.00 x 25.00 x 1.95 mm,@ Wt 0.779Kg / Rmt,with sliding shutters of  member size 65mm x 18mm x 1.29mm @ wt.of 0.677Kg/mt,  with 5 mm thick transparent bronze colour tinted float glass with powder coated aluminum fittings and fixtures and transparent silicon sealant glass fixing to frame including mosquito Jali as per details etc complete for window.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• All materials used for providing and fixing aluminium sliding windows shall conform to relevant Indian Standards and approved makes. The aluminium sections shall be extruded sections conforming to IS 733 and IS 1285, and shall be colour anodized with an anodic coating thickness not less than 15 microns as per IS 1868. The main outer frame shall be three-track section of size 65.00 × 25.00 × 1.95 mm weighing approximately 0.779 kg per running meter, and the sliding shutter sections shall be of size 65 mm × 18 mm × 1.29 mm weighing approximately 0.677 kg per running meter, as per approved section details.
  • Glass used shall be 5 mm thick transparent bronze colour tinted float glass conforming to IS 14900, free from visible defects such as bubbles, waves, or distortions. All fittings and fixtures including rollers, handles, locks, stoppers, and fasteners shall be of approved powder-coated aluminium or stainless steel and shall ensure smooth and durable operation. Silicon sealant used for glazing shall be of approved make, weather-resistant, and compatible with aluminium and glass surfaces.
  • The mosquito mesh (jali) shall be made of high-quality nylon, fiberglass, or aluminium mesh, tightly fixed in an aluminium frame, resistant to corrosion and wear, and properly fitted within the third track for smooth sliding operation. All materials shall be new, of approved quality, and free from defects, and shall be inspected and approved by the Engineer-in-Charge prior to installation.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The aluminium sliding window shall be fabricated and installed in accordance with approved drawings and manufacturer’s specifications. The aluminium frames shall be accurately cut, machined, and assembled with proper mitred joints to ensure rigidity, alignment, and smooth operation. The frames shall be fixed in position true to line, level, and plumb using suitable fasteners, screws, and packing materials, ensuring firm anchorage with the surrounding masonary or RCC without distortion.
  • Sliding shutters shall be assembled properly and fitted with rollers to ensure smooth, easy, and noiseless sliding within the three-track frame. The glass panes shall be cut accurately to size and fixed securely within the shutter sections using rubber gaskets and sealed with approved transparent silicon sealant to ensure proper bonding and watertightness. The mosquito mesh shutter shall be installed in the designated track, ensuring smooth movement and proper alignment without sagging or gaps.
  • All joints between the aluminium frame and the wall shall be sealed properly to prevent leakage of air and water. Care shall be taken to protect the aluminium surfaces and glass from scratches, dents, or damage during handling and fixing. All fittings and accessories shall be properly aligned and securely fixed. The completed window shall operate smoothly, and all shutters including glass and mesh panels shall be checked for proper functioning. The finished work shall be neat, clean, and free from defects, and protective coatings or films shall be removed after completion.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The aluminium sliding window with mosquito mesh shall be measured in square meters (m²) for the actual area of the opening covered, calculated as the overall width multiplied by the overall height of the outer frame, in accordance with IS 1200 Part 14. The rate shall include the cost of all materials such as aluminium sections, glass, mosquito mesh, fittings, fixtures, sealants, and all labour, tools, and plants required for fabrication and installation. The cost of anodizing, glazing, fixing of shutters, and provision of mosquito mesh shall be deemed to be included in the item rate.
  • No separate measurement shall be made for individual components such as tracks, shutters, mesh panels, fittings, screws, sealants, or for cutting, wastage, and fixing accessories. All work shall be measured net as fixed in position, and no extra payment shall be made for scaffolding, transportation, or any incidental operations required to complete the work as per specifications and as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of One sq. meter.

Description: (A) Providing and fixing Pre Painted Galvenlium Iron (PPGI) Sheet high tensile steel profile roofing steel of TATA Durashine or JSW make in total coated 0.50 mm th. and having tensile strength 550 mpa in approved colour, size, shape, depth, pitch of corrugation. The roofing sheets shall be fixed with polymer coated G.I. "J" or "L" hooks, bolts and nuts 8 mm dia. with bitumen & GI limpet washer filled with white lead complete excluding the cost of purlin, rafters and  trusses complete. No extra payment shall be made of overlaps etc. comp. as directed by engg. in charge.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description: • Corrugated G.I. sheets shall conform to M-24.

subsections.title: Spacing of purlines
subsections.description:
• One purlines shall be provided at the ridge and one at the eaves. The spacing of other purlines for 1.8 mm. thick G.I. sheet shall not exceed 1.80 metres. The purlin shall coincide with the centre line of the end lap. The ridge purlins shall be placed in such a way that the ridges can be fixed properly. The portion overhanging the wall support shall not be more than one fourth of the spacing ofpurlins.
  • The top surfaces of the purlins shall be painted before the sheets are fixed over them. Embedded portions of purlins shall be finished with two coats of coal-tar.

subsections.title: Laying of sheets
subsections.description:
• The sheets shall be laid in purlins to a true plane with the line of corrugations truly parallel or normal to the sides of area to be covered. The sheets shall not generally be built into gables and parapets. They shall be bent up along their side edges close to the wall, and the junction shall be protected by suitable flushing or by projecting drip course.
  • The laps at end shall be provided 150 mm. minimum for roof slopes 1 in 2 (1 vertical: 2 horizontal) and steeper but 200 mm. shall be provided for flatter slopes than those above. The side lap shall be provided two ridges of corrugations at eachside.
  • The sheets shall be cut to the dimensions or the shape of the roof either along their lengths or thier width or in slant across the line of corrugations at hips and valleys. The sheets shall be cut carefully with a straight edge and chisel to give a straight finish. The sheets shall be laid such that the laps are turned away from the usual direction of local heavyrain.

subsections.title: Fixing of sheets
subsections.description:
• Sheets shall be fixed to the purlins or other roof members such as hips or valley rafter etc. with ‘j’ or ‘L' galvanized hook bolts, and galvanized nuts 8 mm. dia. with bitumen limpet washers and G.I. washers. Limpet washers with white lead shall be used. Length of hook bolt shall be varied to suit the site requirement. Bolts shall be sufficiently long so that after fixing the project above the top of their nuts by not less than 12 mm. The grip of ‘j’ or ‘L' hook bolts on the sides of purlins shall not be less than 25 mm.There shall be minimum of three hooks bolts placed at the ridge of corrugations in each sheet in every purlin, and their spacing shall not exceed 300 mm. Coach screw shall not be used for fixing the sheets to purlin, where the slopes of roof are note less than 1 :2.5 degree ( 1 vertical and 2.5 horizontal). Sheets shall be jointed together at the side laps by galvanized iron bolts and nuts 25 mm. x 6 mm. size each bolt with a bitumen and G.I. limpact washer filled with white lead. Where the overlaps at the sides extend to two corrugations, these bolts shall be placed zig-zag over the two over lapping corrugations, so that the ends of the overlapping sheets are drawn tightly to wards each other. The spacing of same bolts shall not exceed 600 mm. along each of the staggered rows.
  • Holes for all bolts shall be drilled and not punched in the ridges of the corrugations from the under side, while the sheets are on the ground. The holes in the sheets shall be at least 50 mm. from the edge. Sheets drilled wrongly shall be rejected. The holes in the washers shall be of the exact diameter of the hook bolts or the seam bolts. The nuts shall be tightened from above to give a leak- proof roof.
  • The roof when completed shall be true to lines and slops and shall be leak-proof.
  • After fixing, the entire M.S. flat surface and exposed steel components shall be thoroughly cleaned to remove rust, dust, and loose particles. The steel work shall then be provided with one coat of approved anti-corrosive primer followed by three coats of approved quality paint of required shade to ensure durability and protection against corrosion and weathering.
  • The finished work shall be neat, properly aligned, securely fixed, and executed in a workmanlike manner as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The measurements of PPGI sheet roof shall be taken for finished work in superficial area in general plane (not girthed on the roof). The laps between the P.P.G.I, sheets both at their ends and along the side edges shall not be measured. The overlaps of P.P.G.I, sheets over the valley piece and their under lap the ridge, hip and flashing piece shall be included in the measurements.
  • No deductions in measurement shall be made for opening for chimney stacks, sky lights etc., of area up to 0.40 sq.mt. nor extra be paid for extra labour in cutting and for wastage etc., in forming such openings.
  • The rate of roof shall include the cost of all materials and labour involved in all operations described above. The rate also includes the cost of provision/ erection and removal of the scaffolding, benching, ladders, templates and tools required for the proper execution and erection of the work. The rate includes the cost of purlins, rafters andtrusses.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Square Meter.

Description: Providing & Fixing standard extruded of alluminium section of size 63 mm X 38.10 mm X 1.2 mm (Jindal section : 2434, @ Wt. 0.643 kg/mt) with colour anodized alluminium frame for ventilation with 5 mm thick frosted glass as details etc. comp. for ventilation

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• All materials used for providing and fixing aluminium ventilators shall conform to relevant Indian Standards and approved makes such as Jindal or equivalent. The aluminium sections shall be extruded sections conforming to IS 733 and IS 1285, and shall be colour anodized with an anodic coating thickness not less than 15 microns as per IS 1868. The frame shall be of standard extruded aluminium section of size 63 mm × 38.10 mm × 1.2 mm (Jindal section 2434) having a weight of approximately 0.643 kg per running meter, and shall be free from defects, warping, or surface damage.
  • Glass used shall be 5 mm thick frosted (obscured) glass conforming to IS 14900, ensuring uniform opacity, free from bubbles, scratches, or distortions. All fittings and fixtures such as hinges, stays, screws, and fasteners shall be of approved quality aluminium, stainless steel, or suitable non-corrosive material. Silicon sealant used for fixing glass shall be of approved make, weather-resistant, and compatible with aluminium and glass surfaces. All materials shall be new, of approved quality, and shall be inspected and approved by the Engineer-in-Charge prior to use.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The aluminium ventilator shall be fabricated and installed in accordance with approved drawings and specifications. The aluminium sections shall be accurately cut, machined, and assembled to form a rigid frame with proper joints, ensuring true line, level, and plumb. The frame shall be securely fixed in the opening using suitable fasteners, screws, and packing materials, ensuring firm anchorage without distortion or damage to the surrounding structure.
  • The frosted glass shall be cut to the required size and fixed properly within the frame using suitable rubber gaskets or beading, and sealed with approved silicon sealant to ensure proper fixing and prevent air or water leakage. All fittings such as hinges or stays (if operable type) shall be properly aligned and securely fixed to ensure smooth operation. Care shall be taken during handling and installation to prevent scratches, cracks, or damage to aluminium surfaces and glass.
  • All joints between the frame and wall shall be properly sealed. The finished ventilator shall be neat, properly aligned, and free from defects, with smooth edges and clean surfaces. Any protective film on aluminium sections shall be removed after completion, and the unit shall be cleaned and handed over in perfect working condition.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The aluminium ventilator shall be measured in square meters (m²) for the actual area of the opening covered, calculated as width multiplied by height of the outer frame, in accordance with IS 1200 Part 14. The rate shall include the cost of all materials such as aluminium sections, glass, fittings, fixtures, sealants, and all labour, tools, and plants required for fabrication and fixing. The cost of anodizing, glazing, and all incidental works shall be deemed to be included in the item rate.
  • No separate measurement shall be made for fittings, screws, sealants, cutting, wastage, or fixing accessories. All work shall be measured net as fixed in position, and no extra payment shall be made for scaffolding, lifting, or any incidental operations required to complete the work as per specifications and as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of One sq. meter.

Description: Reparing of Exsiting door as per Requirenment 6'' long stopper, 6'' long S.S. Hinges,  or 12'' long both side aldrop, to IS 733 and IS 1285, fixed with rawl plug abd screws or fixing clips ,or with expansion hold fasteners including necessary filling up of gaps at junctions, at top ,bottom and sides with required PVC/ Neoprene felt, glass of approved make etc. Aluminum sections shall be smooth, rust free ,straight.mitred and jointed mechanically wherever required including cleat angles aluminum snap beading for glazing /paneling, CP Brass/ Stainless steel screws, Stoppers all fixtures & fasteners in  Anodized aluminum works Door etc. complete as per architectural drawings and the direction of Engineer in Charge.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• All materials used for repairing the existing aluminium door shall conform to relevant Indian Standards and shall be of approved quality. Aluminium sections, if replaced or adjusted, shall conform to IS 733 and IS 1285, and shall be smooth, straight, free from defects, corrosion, or warping. All hardware fittings such as 6-inch long stoppers, 6-inch stainless steel hinges, and 12-inch long aldrop (both side) shall be of approved make and of durable quality, free from defects and properly finished. Screws, fasteners, and fixing accessories shall be of CP brass or stainless steel to prevent corrosion and ensure long service life.
  • Glass, wherever required for replacement or refixing, shall be of approved make and quality, free from scratches, bubbles, or distortions, and suitable for the intended application. PVC or neoprene felt used for sealing gaps shall be of approved quality, flexible, and resistant to weathering. Aluminium snap beading used for glazing or panel fixing shall be of matching section and finish. Cleat angles and fixing clips shall be of suitable aluminium or non-corrosive material. All materials shall be new or in good reusable condition (for existing components), and shall be approved by the Engineer-in-Charge before use.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The repairing of existing aluminium door shall be carried out carefully to restore proper alignment, functionality, and appearance as per the requirements and directions of the Engineer-in-Charge. The door shall be dismantled partially where required, and defective or damaged components such as hinges, stoppers, aldrops, fasteners, or glass shall be replaced with new approved materials. Aluminium sections shall be checked for alignment and straightness, and any distortions shall be rectified. Joints shall be properly mitred and mechanically fixed using cleat angles or suitable connectors to ensure rigidity.
  • The door frame and shutter shall be fixed or refixed in correct line, level, and plumb using rawl plugs, screws, fixing clips, or expansion hold fasteners as required. All fittings such as hinges, stoppers, and aldrops shall be properly aligned and securely fixed to ensure smooth and proper operation of the door. Glass panes, if replaced, shall be cut to size and fixed using aluminium snap beading and sealed properly to avoid looseness or rattling.
  • All gaps at junctions, including top, bottom, and sides, shall be filled with approved PVC or neoprene felt to ensure proper sealing and prevent air or water leakage. Care shall be taken to avoid damage to existing aluminium surfaces, and any scratches or minor damages shall be rectified. The repaired door shall operate smoothly without friction, misalignment, or noise, and all fixtures shall be tested for proper functioning. The finished work shall be clean, neat, and complete in all respects as per architectural drawings and instructions.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The repairing of existing aluminium door shall be measured on a lump sum (each) basis or per number of doors repaired, unless otherwise specified, in accordance with the relevant provisions of IS 1200. The rate shall include the cost of all materials such as hinges, stoppers, aldrops, glass (if replaced), PVC/neoprene felt, fasteners, and all labour, tools, and plants required for dismantling, repairing, refixing, and finishing the door.
  • No separate measurement shall be made for individual components such as fittings, screws, sealants, minor adjustments, or gap filling, as these are deemed to be included in the item rate. The work shall be measured as completed and accepted, and the rate shall include all incidental charges required to complete the work in accordance with specifications and as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.
