  • The rate shall be for a unit of One Nos.

Description: Supplying & fixing 25x6 mm size M.S. flat over the roof incl. drilling holes at 1.05 M. c/c and providing 10mm dia. G.I. 'J' or 'L' hooks with nits, washers, bitumen washers etc. & applying 3 coats of approved paint to steel work etc. comp. as directed.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• The M.S. flat shall be of size 25 mm × 6 mm, made from mild steel of approved quality, conforming to relevant Indian Standards such as IS 2062. The flat shall be straight, free from defects such as cracks, bends, and surface irregularities, and shall be of uniform cross-section.
  • The fixing accessories shall include 10 mm diameter G.I. ‘J’ or ‘L’ hooks, nuts, washers, and bitumen washers of approved quality to ensure proper fastening and weather resistance. All fasteners shall be corrosion resistant and suitable for roof application. Paints used for protective coating shall be of approved brand and quality, including primer and finishing coats suitable for steel surfaces exposed to weather conditions.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall include supplying, cutting, fabricating, and fixing 25×6 mm M.S. flats over the roof as per approved drawings and directions of the Engineer-in-Charge. The M.S. flats shall be laid in proper alignment and fixed securely at intervals of approximately 1.05 meters center to center.
  • Holes shall be drilled accurately in the M.S. flats at required spacing to accommodate 10 mm diameter G.I. ‘J’ or ‘L’ hooks. The hooks shall be fixed with nuts, washers, and bitumen washers to ensure firm anchorage and leakproof fixing at roof level. Proper tightening shall be ensured to avoid loosening due to vibration or environmental effects.
  • After fixing, the entire M.S. flat surface and exposed steel components shall be thoroughly cleaned to remove rust, dust, and loose particles. The steel work shall then be provided with one coat of approved anti-corrosive primer followed by three coats of approved quality paint of required shade to ensure durability and protection against corrosion and weathering.
  • The finished work shall be neat, properly aligned, securely fixed, and executed in a workmanlike manner as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The M.S. flat work shall be measured in running meters (Rmt) of installed length, in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include the cost of M.S. flats, G.I. hooks, nuts, washers, bitumen washers, drilling, fixing, fabrication, painting (all coats), labour, tools, and all incidental works required for complete installation.
  • No separate payment shall be made for fasteners, consumables, painting materials, or labour involved in fixing, as these shall be deemed included in the item rate. The measurement shall be taken for actual length installed and accepted by the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Kg.

Description: Providing  and fixing Anodized aluminum works for Door of size 8mm th. pre laminated particle board, 5mm th. transparent glass/bronze color tinted float glass, 63× 38× 2.65mm outer frame-Vertical/Horinzontal, 85×44×2.70mm shutter vertical member, 85×44×2.00mm shutter horizontal member, 6'' long stopper, 6'' long S.S. Hinges, 12'' long both side aldrop,Partly glazed and partly pre-laminated with extruded built up standard tubular and other section of approved make confirming to IS 733 and IS 1285, fixed with rawl plug abd screws or fixing clips ,or with expansion hold fasteners including necessary filling up of gaps at junctions, at top ,bottom and sides with required PVC/ Neoprene felt, glass of approved make etc. Aluminum sections shall be smooth, rust free ,straight.mitred and jointed mechanically wherever required including cleat angles aluminum snap beading for glazing /paneling, CP Brass/ Stainless steel screws, Stoppers all fixtures & fasteners etc. complete as per architectural drawings and the direction of Engineer in Charge.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• All materials used for repairing the existing aluminium door shall conform to relevant Indian Standards and shall be of approved quality. Aluminium sections, if replaced or adjusted, shall conform to IS 733 and IS 1285, and shall be smooth, straight, free from defects, corrosion, or warping. All hardware fittings such as 6-inch long stoppers, 6-inch stainless steel hinges, and 12-inch long aldrop (both side) shall be of approved make and of durable quality, free from defects and properly finished. Screws, fasteners, and fixing accessories shall be of CP brass or stainless steel to prevent corrosion and ensure long service life.
  • The paneling shall consist of 8 mm thick pre-laminated particle board conforming to IS 12823, and glazing shall be done using 5 mm thick transparent or bronze colour tinted float glass conforming to IS 14900, free from defects such as bubbles, scratches, or distortions. All fittings and fixtures including 6-inch long stoppers, 6-inch stainless steel hinges, and 12-inch long both-side aldrops shall be of approved make and good quality. Screws and fasteners shall be of CP brass or stainless steel to prevent corrosion. PVC or neoprene felt used for sealing gaps shall be of approved quality, durable and flexible. Aluminium snap beading, cleat angles, and fixing clips shall be of suitable matching sections and non-corrosive material. All materials shall be new, free from defects, and approved by the Engineer-in-Charge before use.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The aluminium door shall be fabricated and installed in accordance with approved architectural drawings and specifications. The aluminium sections shall be accurately cut, mitred, and mechanically jointed using cleat angles or suitable connectors to form rigid frames and shutters true to line, level, and plumb. The outer frame shall be fixed in position using rawl plugs, screws, fixing clips, or expansion hold fasteners, ensuring firm anchorage to the surrounding structure without distortion.
  • The shutter shall be fabricated with proper alignment and assembled with both pre-laminated particle board panels and glass panels as specified, ensuring neat and secure fixing using aluminium snap beading. Glass shall be carefully cut to size and fixed properly with suitable gaskets or sealant to prevent rattling and ensure durability. All fittings such as hinges, stoppers, and aldrops shall be properly aligned and securely fixed to ensure smooth and proper operation of the door.
  • All gaps at the junctions of the frame with masonry or RCC at top, bottom, and sides shall be properly filled with approved PVC or neoprene felt to ensure proper sealing and prevent ingress of air or water. Care shall be taken to avoid damage to aluminium surfaces during fabrication and installation, and any scratches or defects shall be rectified. The completed door shall operate smoothly without any binding or noise, and all components shall be checked for proper functioning. The finished work shall be clean, neat, and in accordance with the specifications and directions of the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The aluminium door shall be measured in square meters (m²) based on the actual area of the opening covered, calculated as width multiplied by height of the outer frame, in accordance with IS 1200 Part 14. The rate shall include the cost of all materials such as aluminium sections, pre-laminated board, glass, fittings, fixtures, fasteners, sealants, and all labour, tools, and plants required for fabrication and installation.
  • No separate measurement shall be made for fittings, screws, snap beading, cleat angles, sealing materials, or minor adjustments, as these are deemed to be included in the item rate. The work shall be measured net as fixed in position, and the rate shall include all incidental operations such as cutting, wastage, transportation, scaffolding, and finishing required to complete the work as per specifications and as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of One Square Meter.

Description: Providing and fixing of Self Supported Structure Less curve Roofing systems with proper overlapping and seaming b/w different sheets without making holes or preventing the overturning the roof by wind addition made up from superior quality, structural grade steel. Base metal width 912 mm, Steel Grade : Grade D and Thickness 0.90 mm to 1.00 mm BMT, 0.95 mm to 1.05 mm APT with tolerance of +/- 0.04 mm for span up to 17 Mtr, Regular Modified Polyester Imported Color Coated Galvalume Steel having Profiled width of 625 mm +/-10mm. Design, supply, & fabrication of self supported single span arch roof fabricated from mechanically seamed manufactured by American Hydraulic Machines to profiles of Imported Galvalume Cold Rolled Structural Steel coils as per standard ASTM A792, Steel Sheet, Aluminum-Zinc Alloy Coated by Hot-Dip Process. The work should be carried out by specilialize and approved agency only. The rate of item is including fitting as per standard specification.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• The roofing system shall be a self-supported, structure-less curved (arch) roofing system made from superior quality structural grade steel, designed to span up to 17 meters without intermediate supports. The system shall consist of imported Galvalume cold rolled steel coils conforming to ASTM A792 standards, coated with aluminum-zinc alloy by hot-dip process for enhanced corrosion resistance and durability.
  • The base metal width shall be approximately 912 mm, with a profiled width of 625 mm ±10 mm. The steel sheet thickness shall be in the range of 0.90 mm to 1.00 mm (BMT) and 0.95 mm to 1.05 mm (APT) with a permissible tolerance of ±0.04 mm. The steel shall be of Grade D or equivalent structural grade, with regular modified polyester color coating of approved shade and finish.
  • The roofing sheets shall be mechanically curved and formed using specialized American hydraulic machines to achieve the required arch profile. The system shall be self-supporting and designed to withstand wind loads, live loads, and environmental conditions without the need for additional structural framework. Proper overlapping and seaming between sheets shall be ensured to provide a continuous, leakproof, and rigid roofing system without any perforations or holes in the sheets.
  • All materials shall be of approved make, sourced from specialized and approved agencies only, and shall comply with relevant industry standards and manufacturer specifications.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall include design, supply, fabrication, transportation, and installation of self-supported curved roofing sheets as per approved structural design and drawings. The installation shall be carried out by experienced and approved specialized agencies having expertise in such roofing systems.
  • The roofing sheets shall be erected and mechanically seamed using appropriate seaming machines to ensure tight interlocking between panels, providing structural integrity and weatherproofing. Proper alignment, curvature, and anchoring at supports (if any end supports are provided) shall be ensured to resist wind uplift and other environmental forces.
  • The sheets shall be laid in true alignment with proper overlapping and seaming, without any perforation or drilling on the sheet surface, thereby maintaining the integrity of the roofing system. Care shall be taken during handling and installation to avoid damage to the coating and profile of the sheets.
  • The completed roofing system shall be rigid, leakproof, aesthetically uniform, and capable of withstanding specified loads. All work shall be executed strictly as per manufacturer’s specifications, approved design, and directions of the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The roofing work shall be measured in square meters (Sqm) of finished curved roof area in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include the cost of design, materials, fabrication, transportation, machinery, erection, seaming, labour, and all incidental works required for complete installation.
  • No separate payment shall be made for curvature forming, seaming, overlaps, accessories, machinery usage, or labour, as these shall be deemed included in the item rate. The measurement shall be based on the actual plan projection or surface area as specified in the contract drawings and as accepted by the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one square Meter.

Description: Providing & fixing 35mm.th. Flush Door Solid Double Core type Both Face water proof Ply Vennered & 1.5 mm th.laminate  shall be pasted on both side with adhesives as specified by the manufacturers. The laminate shall be as per approved shade & texture, of make incl. Sal wood frames of finished size 12cm x 7cm.incl. S.S. Hinges with nessary screws & Anodized aluminum fixtures & fastenings For all Floor

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• Flush door shall conform to M-30. Plywood shall conform to M-37. Anodized aluminum butt hinges Shall conform to M-43.
  • The door frame shall be made of well-seasoned sal wood of finished size 120 mm × 70 mm, free from knots, cracks, or decay, and treated against termite and fungal attack as per IS 401. All fittings and fixtures such as stainless steel hinges, handles, and anodized aluminium fasteners shall be of approved make and quality, corrosion-resistant, and suitable for heavy-duty use. Screws shall be of stainless steel or CP brass. All materials shall be new, of standard quality, and shall be approved by the Engineer-in-Charge prior to use.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The flush door shutter and frame shall be installed in accordance with approved drawings and specifications. The sal wood frame shall be accurately cut, assembled, and fixed in position true to line, level, and plumb, using suitable holdfasts or fasteners, ensuring firm anchorage to the masonry or RCC structure. The frame shall be properly aligned and securely fixed before fixing the shutter.
  • The flush door shutter shall be fixed to the frame using approved stainless steel hinges of suitable size and number, ensuring proper alignment and smooth operation. The laminated surfaces shall be finished uniformly without bubbles, wrinkles, or defects, and edges shall be neatly finished and sealed. Care shall be taken to protect the laminate from damage during handling and fixing.
  • The item covers the requirement of preparation of shutters for doors, windows, clerestory windows. their supply and fixing.

subsections.title: Shutters
subsections.description:
• Paneled shutters shall be constructed in the form of timber frame work of styles andrails with panel inserted of type as specified in the detailed drawings. Panel shall be fixed by providing grooves in the style and rails. The style and rails shall be Joined to each other by mortise and tenon joints at right angles.
  • All members of the shutters shall be stwithout any warp or bow and shall have smooth. well planed faces at right angles to eachother.
  • The size of styles and rails shall be as per drawings or as directed. Styles and rails of shutters shall be made of one pieceonly.

subsections.title: Timber panelling
subsections.description:
• Thickness of the panel shall be as specified in the item as shown in the drawing or as directed. If the panel is made from more than one piece the pieces shall be finished as shown in the detailed drawings and shall be joined with continuous groove with specified size. The end pieces of the panel and the top and bottom of the panel shall be provided with continuous tongue to frame intogroove of the frame shutter. An air space of 1.5 mm. shall be left in the groove of frame of shutter while framing the panels in it.
  • The faces of the panel as well as various pieces of the panel shall be closely fitted to the sizes of the grooves.
  • Finishing of the corners of raised panel edges shall be done as shown in drawings or as directed.
  • The thickness specified shall be finished thickness and no tolerance will be permitted.

subsections.title: Fixtures and Fastenings
subsections.description: • All fittings and fixtures shall be properly aligned and securely fixed with appropriate screws. Necessary clearances shall be maintained between the frame and shutter to ensure smooth opening and closing without friction or noise. The entire assembly shall be checked for proper functioning, alignment, and finish. The completed door shall be free from defects such as warping, uneven surfaces, or improper fixing, and shall be cleaned and handed over in perfect condition as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge. The rate shall include anodizes aluminum butt hinges including fixing with iron screws.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The flush door shall be measured in square meters (m²) based on the clear area of the door opening, calculated as width multiplied by height of the shutter, in accordance with IS 1200 Part 12. The rate shall include the cost of door shutter, sal wood frame, laminate finish on both sides, adhesives, fittings, fixtures, fasteners, and all labour, tools, and plants required for complete installation.
  • No separate measurement shall be made for hinges, screws, adhesives, or minor accessories, as these are deemed to be included in the item rate. The work shall be measured net as fixed in position, and the rate shall include all incidental charges such as cutting, wastage, transportation, and fixing required to complete the work as per specifications and as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one sq.metre.

Description: Providing and fixing FRP frame size 100 x 50mm and 28mm thick FRP Depress pannel shutter having extra reinforcement on sides and edges and in gel coat finish. The core of the shutter is to be filled up with injected fire retardant grade polyurethane foam done insitu alongwith embedded wooden pieces for stiffening and also for taking hinges and fixtures. The whole FRP frame and shutter is to be water proof, weather proof, termite proof and resistance to mild acid/Alkali.rates are to be inclusive of S.S.hinges with necessary screws and alluminium fixtures and fastening.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• All materials used for providing and fixing Fibre Reinforced Plastic (FRP) door frames and shutters shall be of approved make and conform to relevant Indian Standards. The FRP door frame shall be of size 100 mm × 50 mm, manufactured from high-quality fibre reinforced polymer composite with uniform thickness, free from surface defects, cracks, or distortions. The FRP shutter shall be 28 mm thick depressed panel type, integrally moulded with additional reinforcement at edges and sides to ensure rigidity and durability. The external surface shall be finished with smooth gel coat, providing a uniform finish and resistance to weathering.
  • The core of the shutter shall be filled with injected fire-retardant grade polyurethane foam, conforming to IS 12406, applied in-situ to ensure complete filling without voids. Suitable embedded wooden inserts shall be provided within the shutter at hinge and fixture locations for proper fixing and load transfer. The entire FRP assembly shall be waterproof, weatherproof, termite-proof, and resistant to mild acids and alkalis.
  • All fittings and fixtures such as stainless steel hinges shall be of approved quality and corrosion-resistant, fixed with appropriate stainless steel screws. Aluminium fixtures and fasteners shall be anodized and of approved make. All materials shall be new, free from defects, and shall be approved by the Engineer-in-Charge prior to installation.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The FRP door frame and shutter shall be installed in accordance with approved drawings and manufacturer’s specifications. The frame shall be fixed in position true to line, level, and plumb using suitable holdfasts, screws, or fasteners, ensuring firm anchorage to the surrounding masonry or RCC structure. The frame shall be properly aligned and supported during fixing to prevent distortion.
  • The FRP shutter shall be accurately aligned and fixed to the frame using stainless steel hinges of approved size and number, ensuring smooth and proper operation. Care shall be taken while handling and installation to prevent damage to the FRP surface or gel coat finish. The embedded wooden inserts provided within the shutter shall be used for fixing hinges and other fixtures to ensure firm and secure fixing.
  • All fixtures such as handles, latches, and fasteners shall be properly aligned and securely fixed. Necessary clearances shall be maintained between frame and shutter for smooth opening and closing without friction. All joints between frame and wall shall be properly sealed to prevent ingress of water. The completed door shall be checked for alignment, smooth operation, and finish, and shall be free from defects such as warping, cracks, or surface damage. The finished work shall be neat, clean, and in accordance with specifications and directions of the Engineer-in-Charge.

The rate shall include the cost of FRP frame, FRP shutter, polyurethane foam core, embedded wooden inserts, gel coat finish, fittings, fixtures, fasteners, and all labour, tools, and plants required for complete installation.
  • No separate measurement shall be made for hinges, screws, fasteners, sealing materials, or incidental works, as these are deemed to be included in the item rate. The work shall be measured net as fixed in position, and the rate shall include all incidental charges such as transportation, lifting, fixing, and finishing required to complete the work as per specifications and as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.

Description: Providing & fixing 8 mm thick Polycarbonate panel consist UV protected multicell / microcell structure having panel width of 600 / 900 mm to ensure best performance against windload, live load, vibration & visual appearance made of DANPALON/ SOLALITE / EVERLITE or TUFFLITE or its equivalent brand. Panel shall be manufactured with vertical standing seam at both sides of the panel. The height of the standing seam is minimum 8 mm to ensure best connectore engagement. panel shall be fixed with snap on connectore with conti. double wall aluminium spacer along the standing seam to ensure best performence against wind up lift/herrican effect with a grip-lock double tooth locking mechanism. panel shall be co-extruded UV protected. panel ends shall be sealed with anti dust aluminium tape & aluminium profiles (mill finish) This includes the cost of labour incl. all accessories req. to fix this panels as per approved shades/colour and direction of engg. in charge. Comp. as per detail drawing & design.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• The polycarbonate panels shall be 8 mm thick multiwall (multi-cell / microcell) type, UV protected, co-extruded sheets of approved make such as DANPALON, SOLALITE, EVERLITE, TUFFLITE or equivalent. The panels shall have vertical standing seam on both sides with a minimum seam height of 8 mm to ensure proper interlocking and connector engagement.
  • The panels shall be of standard width (600 mm / 900 mm as required) and shall be manufactured to ensure high resistance against wind load, live load, vibration, and provide uniform visual appearance. The panels shall be UV stabilized to protect against weathering, yellowing, and degradation due to sunlight exposure. The ends of the panels shall be sealed with anti-dust aluminium tape and finished with aluminium profiles of mill finish as per manufacturer’s recommendations.
  • All accessories including snap-on connectors, aluminium spacers (continuous double-wall type), locking mechanisms (double tooth grip-lock system), fasteners, sealants, and supporting profiles shall be of approved quality and compatible with the panel system. The system shall be designed to provide structural stability, weather resistance, and durability as per approved design and drawings.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall include supplying, fabricating, and fixing 8 mm thick polycarbonate multiwall panels in position as per approved drawings and instructions of the Engineer-in-Charge. The panels shall be installed using snap-on connectors with continuous double-wall aluminium spacers along the standing seams to ensure proper alignment, locking, and resistance against uplift and wind effects.
  • The panels shall be carefully handled during installation to avoid scratches, cracks, or damage. The standing seams shall be properly interlocked with connectors ensuring a tight and secure fit. All joints shall be properly aligned to maintain uniform appearance and structural integrity. Necessary supports, frames, and sub-structures (if required) shall be properly prepared before fixing the panels.
  • The panel ends shall be sealed using anti-dust aluminium tape and finished with aluminium profiles to prevent ingress of dust, moisture, and insects. Proper sealing and fixing shall be ensured to make the installation weatherproof and durable. All work shall be executed as per manufacturer’s specifications and approved design, maintaining proper alignment, level, and finish.
  • The completed installation shall be neat, structurally sound, weather resistant, and aesthetically pleasing, as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The polycarbonate panel work shall be measured in square meters (Sqm) of finished surface area, in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include the cost of panels, connectors, aluminium spacers, profiles, sealing materials, accessories, labour, fixing, and all incidental works required for complete installation.
  • No separate payment shall be made for accessories, fittings, wastage, or labour involved, as these shall be deemed included in the item rate. The measurement shall be based on actual installed area as per approved drawings and accepted by the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one square Meter.

Description: Providing and fixing M.S. grills of required pattern to wooden frames of windows etc. with M.S. flats at required spacings and frame alround, square or round bars with round headed bolts and nuts or by screws (A) Plain Grill.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description: • the structural steel shall conform to M-22.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The M.S. Grill shall be prepared as per the drawing or as directed for fixing to wooden frames of windows etc.
  • The grill shall be fabricated to the designs and patterns shown in the drawings and the weight shall be as directed, and the joints shall be riveted or welded as shown in the plan or as directed. The grill so formed shall be fixed into the frames of the windows etc. before they are erected in position. 
  • The Outside strip frame of the grill shall be housed to its full thickness into the recess cut into the frame of the windows etc., The grill shall be fixed to the frame with number of bolts and nuts or screws vix. bolt nut/' screw per 30 cm. of the length of outer strip subject to a minimum of 2 Nos. on each side of the frame or as indicated in the drawing or as directed.
  • The bolts and nuts or screws shall be counter sunk and shall be fixed with the top of their heads flush with the face of the framestrips.

Description: Providing & fixing at site of work rolling shutter to suit clear opening, made out of 18G & 65 mm wide laths of deep convex corrugation complete with one piece construction of partly or fully grill type as directed incl. side guides 65x25mm made out from 20 mm dia. bars & 3.15mm th. M.S. plate, pressed bottom rail, the top spring shall be made out of best spring steel wires incl. locking arrangments on bottom side, push & pull type incl. prov. 1 coat of anticorrosive paint & 2 coats of approved quality oil paint with all necessary fittings, accessories as required incl. top over etc. comp. as directed (out to out measurement shall be paid)

sections.title: Materials
sections.description: • the rolling dhutter shall conform to M-32.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The rolling shutter shall be fabricated and installed to suit the clear opening as per approved drawings and site requirements. The shutter curtain shall be formed by interlocking corrugated laths into a continuous sheet and fixed to the barrel/shaft in a single-piece construction. The guide channels shall be properly aligned and securely fixed to the masonry or structural supports using suitable fasteners, ensuring correct vertical alignment and smooth operation.
  • The barrel assembly with spring mechanism shall be installed at the top, properly balanced to facilitate easy manual operation by push and pull action. The spring shall be correctly tensioned to ensure smooth lifting and lowering of the shutter without jerks or excessive force. The bottom rail shall be properly fixed and aligned, and locking arrangements shall be installed and tested for proper functioning.
  • All components shall be assembled accurately, ensuring proper clearances between the shutter curtain and guide channels. The entire system shall operate smoothly without noise, jamming, or misalignment. The shutter shall be painted with one coat of anticorrosive primer followed by two coats of approved oil paint, ensuring uniform coverage and proper drying between coats. The completed shutter shall be tested for smooth operation, proper locking, and overall performance, and shall be handed over in a clean and fully functional condition as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The rolling shutter shall be measured in square meters (m²) based on the overall out-to-out dimensions of the shutter, including guide channels and top assembly, as specified, in accordance with IS 1200. The area shall be calculated as width multiplied by height of the opening including the shutter assembly.
  • The rate shall include the cost of all materials such as MS laths, guide channels, spring mechanism, bottom rail, locking arrangements, fittings, accessories, primer, and paint, along with all labour, tools, and plants required for fabrication and installation. No separate measurement shall be made for individual components such as springs, brackets, bearings, locking devices, painting, or fasteners, as these are deemed to be included in the item rate.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Square Meter.

Description: Providing, laying and jointing in true line and level 160 diametre U.P.V.C (Type B) conforming to IS 13592-1992 with one end plain and other end socketed with rubber ring, & fittings conforming to ISI 14735-1999 of approved make for drainage system pipe line,  pipe shall be jointed with each other with rubber lubricant, pipe shall be fixed on wall using of PVC clamp of the size 160 mm diametre x 210 mm length x 196 mm heigh at every 2000 mm center to center or shall be concealed in walls as directed including necessary fittings such as bends, shoes etc. including testing of pipes and joints and jointed with adhesive solvent cement including cost of all materials.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• The U.P.V.C. pipes shall be of 160 mm diameter, Type B, conforming to IS 13592, of approved make and quality, suitable for drainage and soil waste discharge systems. The pipes shall be of one end plain and the other end socketed with rubber ring (ring fit) arrangement for leakproof jointing.
  • All fittings such as bends, tees, shoes, couplers, reducers, and other accessories shall conform to IS 14735 and shall be of matching make and compatible with the pipes. The rubber ring used for jointing shall be of approved quality, durable, and capable of providing watertight joints. PVC clamps and supporting accessories shall be of required size and approved quality. All materials shall be new, free from defects, and approved by the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall include supplying, laying, cutting, jointing, and fixing 160 mm diameter U.P.V.C. Type B pipes in true line and level as per approved drawings and directions of the Engineer-in-Charge. The pipes shall be laid either on walls using suitable PVC clamps at spacing not exceeding 2.0 meters center to center or concealed in walls as directed.
  • The pipes shall be joined using rubber ring (push-fit) joints with proper use of rubber lubricant to ensure smooth insertion and leakproof connection. All joints shall be properly aligned and seated to avoid leakage or misalignment. Necessary fittings such as bends, shoes, tees, and other accessories shall be used wherever required to complete the pipeline layout.
  • Clamps shall be fixed securely to support the pipes and prevent sagging or displacement. Care shall be taken during handling, cutting, and installation to avoid damage to pipes and fittings. After installation, the entire pipeline shall be tested for leakage and proper functioning. Any defects shall be rectified immediately.
  • The finished installation shall be neat, properly aligned, securely fixed, and fully functional as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The UPVC pipe work shall be measured in running meters (Rmt) for the specified diameter (160 mm), in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include the cost of pipes, fittings, rubber rings, clamps, lubricant, labour, cutting, jointing, fixing, testing, and all incidental works required for complete installation.
  • No separate payment shall be made for fittings, clamps, jointing materials, or labour involved in installation, as these shall be deemed included in the item rate. The item shall be measured as completed and accepted as per the directions of the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Running Meter.

The collapsible gate shall fixed at the sites by fixing the double channels in the T-iron rail and also by hold fasts bolted to the end double channel and fixed in the masonary of the side walls or the otherwise. In case where the collapsible gate is not required to the lintels, beams or slop above, a tee iron suitably designed may be fixed at the top embedded in masonary and provided with necessary clamps and roller arrangement at the top. All the adjoining work damaged while fixing of gate shall be made good to match the existing work without any extra payment. All the members of the collapsible gate including T-iron shall be thoroughly cleaned of rust, seals, dust etc. and given a priming coat or red lead Before fixing the min position.

Description: Constructing manhole with RCC top slab in 1:2:4 mix (1 cement : 2 coarse sand : 4 graded stone agreegate 20 mm nominal size) foundation concrete 1:3:6 (1 cement : 3 coarse sand : 6 brick bats 40 to 50 mm size) inside plastering 15 mm thick with CM 1:5 (1 cement : 5 coarse sand) finished with floating coat of neat cement and making channels in C.C. 1:2:4 (1 cement : 2 coarse sand : 4 stone agreegate 20 mm nominal size) finished smooth complete incl. curing and testing (1) inside size 900 mm X 1200 mm and 1.5 mm deep including C.I. cover with frame size 560 mm diameter total weith of cover & frame to be not less than 128 kg (wt. of cover 64 kg & wt. of frame 64 kg) (A) with 230 mm th. walls of brick masonary using brick having crushing strength not less than 356 kg / sq.cm. in cement mortar 1:5 (1 cement : 5 coarse sand) (1) A type depth 0.90 metre for 150 mm diameter sewer.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description: • Water shall conform to M-l. Cement shall conform to M-6. Burnt bricks shall conform to M-156. Brick bats of 40 to 50 mm. size shall conform to M-14. Stone coarse aggregate of 20 mm. nominal size shall conform to M-l2. Grit shall conform to M-8. Cement mortar of specified proportion shall conform to M-11. The cast iron manhole cover of 560 mm. dia. with frame shall conform to I.S. 1726-1966.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description: The manholes of different types and sizes as specified shall be constructed in sewer line at such places and to such levels and dimension as shown in drawing or as directed.

subsections.title: Bed Concrete
subsections.description:
• The manholes of different types and sizes as specified shall be constructed in sewer line at such places and to such levels and dimension as shown in drawing or as directed.
  • The manhole shall be built on a bed of cement concrete 1:3:6 (1 cement : 3 coarse sdand : 6 brick bats) (40 to 50 mm. nominal size) to the thickness of the bed concrete shall be 15 cms. For manhole upto I.M. depth and 20 cms. for manholes over metre and upto 2 metres. depth and 30 cms. For manhole upto 1.M. depth and 20 cms. for manholes over metre and upto 2 metres, depth and 30 cms. for manholes of greater depth.
  • Projection of bed concrete beyond the masonry wall shall be 15 cms.

subsections.title: Walls
subsections.description: • The walls of manhole shall be carried out with burnt bricks using bricks, having crushing strength not less than 35 Kg/Cm2 in CM. 1:5 (1 cement : 5 coarse sand). The thickness of brick masonry wall shall be 230 mm. The jointing face of such brick shall be well buttered with cement mortar before laying so as to ensure full joints.

subsections.title: Plaster
subsections.description: • The inside of walls shall be plastered 15 mm. thick with CM. 1:5 (1 cement : 5 coarse sand) are finished with floating coat of neat cement. All angles shall be rounded to 7.50 cms. radius and all rendered in internal surface shall have hard in pervious finish obtained by using a steel trowel. The external joints of masonry shall be finished smooth.

subsections.title: Channels & Benching
subsections.description:
• Channels shall be semicircular in the bottom half and of diameter equal to the sewer. Above the horizontal diameter, the sides shall be extended vertically to the same level as the crown of the out going pipe and the top edge shall be suitably rounded off. The branch channels shall also be similarly constructed with respect to the benching but at their junction with the main channel an appropriate fall suitably rounded off in the direction of flow in the main channel shall begiven.
  • The channel and benching shall be done in C.C. 1:2:4 (1 cement : 2 coarse sand : 4 graded stone aggregate 20 mm. nominal size) rising at a slop in line from edges of channel. The channels of the bottom of the chamber shall be plastered with CM. 1:2 (1 cement : 2 coarse sand) and steel trowelled smooth.

subsections.title: The Cover Slab
subsections.description: • The cover slab of R.C.C. 1:2:4 (1 cement : 2 coarse sand : 4 graded stone aggregate 20 mm. nominal size) 15 cms. thick reinforced with 10 mm. bars at 15 cms. C/C both ways, surface and edges finished fair. Full bearing equal to the width of wall shall be given to the slab on all sides The frame of manhole cover shall be emnbedded firmly in R.C.R., slab so that the top of the frame remains flush with the top of R.C.C.slab.

subsections.title: Testing
subsections.description:
• Manhole shall be tested by filling with water to a depth not exceeding 1.2 M. as directed.
  • completion of work, manhole covers shall be scaled by means of thick grease.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment

sections.title: Materials

The height of 450 mm. shall be measured from the top of the bed concrete to the top of the C.I. frame. The size of grating indicate the clear internal dimensions of the C.I. frame of the grating.

  • The walls and the bed concrete of chambers shall be plastered inside with 12 mm. thick cement plaster 1:3 (1 cement : 3 coarse sand) finished smooth.

The frames of the gully grating shall be fixed on the top of masonry walk is of the chamber in 15 cms. thick CC. 1:2:4 (1 cement : 2 coarse sand : 4 graded stone aggregate 20 mm. nominal size) laid over the full thickness of walls.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description: • (1) Water shall conform to M-l. (2) Cement mortar of proportion 1.5 shall conform to M-ll. (3) Burnt brick shall conform to M-15. (4) The S.W. Galley trap of 150 mm. x 100 mm. size shall conform to M- 70.

sections.title: Workmanship

subsections.title: Fixing
subsections.description:
• The gully trap shall be fixed over cement concrete 1:5:10 (1 cement : 5 and : 10 graded brick bats aggregate, 40 mm. nominal size) foundation, 650 mm. square.and 100 mm. thick. The depth of top of concrete below the ground level shall be 675 mm. The jointing of glilley outlet to the branch drain shall be done similar to jointing of S.W. pipe as described in item No". 24.1. (A)

(inside) size shall then be fixed on the top of the brick masonry with C.C 1:2:4 (1 cement : 2 coarse sand : 4 graded aggregate 20 mm. nominal size) 40 mm. thick and rendered smooth. The finished top of the cover shall be left about 40 mm. above the adjoining ground level so as to exclude the surface water form entering the gulley trap.

Description: Providing, laying (to level or slopes) and jointing reinforced concrete Light duty non-pressure Pipes I.S. class NP2 of the following internal diameter with collars and butt ends prepared for collar joints including testing of joints complete.  ( C ) 600 mm dia

sections.title: Materials
sections.description: • The reinforced concrete light duly non-pressure pipes of specified diameter shall conform to I.S. 458- 1971.

subsections.title: The pipes and fittings
subsections.description:
• The pipes and fittings after they are laid shall be tested to hydraulic pressure of 6 Kg./sq.cm.  The pipe shall be slowly and carefully charged with water allowing all air to escape and avoiding all stock and water hammer. The draw off takes and stock shall then be closed and specified hydraulic pressure shall be applied gradually. The pressure gauge must be accurate . The pipes and fittings shall be tested in sections as the work of laying proceeds, veeping the joints exposed for inspection during the testing.
  • The width and depth of the trenches shall be 30 cms. and depth of trenches 60 cms.
  • At joints, the trench width shall be widened where necessary. The work of excavation and refilling shall be done true to line, and gradient in accordance with general specifications of earth work in trenches.
  • The pipes shall be painted with two coats of anti-corrosive bitumastic paint of approved quality. The pipe shall be laid on a layer of 75 mm. sand filled upto 150 mm. above the pipe if so specified. The remaining portion of trench shall be then filled with excavated earth. The surplus earth shall be disposed of as directed.
  • When the excavation is done in rock the bottom shall be cut deep enough to permit the pipe to be laid and cushion of sand 75 mm. In case of bigger diameter of tube where the pressure is very high, thrust block of cement concrete 1:2:4(1 cement :2 coarse sand:4 grade stone aggregate of 20 mm. nominal size) shall be constructed on all bends to transmit the hydraulic thrust without in pairing the ground and spreading it over' a sufficient area if sospecified.
  • The Above Specifications shall be followed for work of trenches except that the excavation in trenches shall be for reinforced concrete pipes of specified diameter.

subsections.title: Laying
subsections.description:

Description: Providing, laying and jointing in true line and level heavy duty P.V.C. Pipe of approved quality and make including fitting as approved by Engineer-in-charge. Pipe shall be fixed underground incl.  excavation and refilling the same with watering, curing, consolidating, ramming etc. comp. as directed.including testing of pipe and joints and fixing the same with adhesive solvent and including cost of all materials.  (D) 300 mm dia

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• The heavy duty PVC pipes shall be of 100 mm nominal diameter of approved quality and make, suitable for underground drainage or water conveyance applications. The pipes and fittings shall conform to relevant Indian Standards such as IS 4985 (or equivalent as applicable), and shall be free from defects such as cracks, deformations, or surface irregularities.
  • All fittings such as bends, tees, couplers, reducers, and end caps shall be of matching make and compatible with the pipes. Jointing materials shall include approved solvent cement/adhesive suitable for PVC pipes to ensure leakproof and durable joints. All materials shall be new, of approved make, and subject to approval by the Engineer-in-Charge before use.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall include providing, laying, cutting, jointing, and fixing 100 mm dia heavy duty PVC pipes in true line and level as per approved drawings and directions of the Engineer-in-Charge. The pipes shall be laid underground at the required depth after proper excavation of trenches in all types of soil.
  • The trench shall be excavated to the required width and depth, and the bottom shall be properly leveled and prepared to provide a firm bedding for the pipe. The pipes shall be carefully laid and joined using solvent cement ensuring clean, leakproof, and properly aligned joints. Necessary fittings shall be used wherever required to complete the pipeline alignment.
  • After laying and jointing, the pipeline shall be tested for leakage and proper functioning. The trench shall then be refilled with selected excavated material in layers, watered, rammed, and consolidated properly to avoid settlement. Care shall be taken to avoid damage to the pipes during backfilling and compaction.
  • The completed work shall be neat, properly aligned, and fully functional as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The PVC pipe work shall be measured in running meters (Rmt) for the specified diameter (100 mm), in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include the cost of pipes, fittings, excavation, laying, jointing, solvent cement, testing, refilling, compaction, and all incidental works required for complete installation.
  • No separate measurement shall be made for fittings, excavation, refilling, jointing materials, or labour, as these shall be deemed included in the item rate. The work shall be measured as completed and accepted as per the directions of the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Running Meter.

Description: Providing, laying and jointing in true line and level U.P.V.C. Pipe (SCH-40) including fitting of PRINCE / SUPREME / ASTRAL / FINOLEX or equivalent or as approved by Engineer-in-charge. Pipe shall be fixed on the wall with the help of clamp at every two meter c/c or shall be concealed as directed including necessary fittings etc. including testing of pipe and joints and fixing the same with adhesive solvent and including cost of all materials. (F) 50 mm dia

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• The U.P.V.C. pipes shall be of Schedule-40 (SCH-40) of 50 mm nominal diameter, of approved make such as Prince, Supreme, Astral, Finolex or equivalent, conforming to relevant Indian Standards such as IS 4985. The pipes and fittings shall be of uniform quality, free from defects, cracks, or deformations, and suitable for pressure water supply systems.
  • All fittings such as elbows, tees, couplers, reducers, unions, and end caps shall be of matching make and compatible with the pipes. Jointing materials shall include approved solvent cement/adhesive suitable for U.P.V.C. pipes, ensuring leakproof joints. Clamps, supports, screws, and fasteners used for fixing shall be of corrosion-resistant material of approved quality. All materials shall be new and approved by the Engineer-in-Charge prior to use.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall include supplying, laying, cutting, jointing, and fixing of 50 mm diameter U.P.V.C. pipes in true line and level as per approved drawings and directions of the Engineer-in-Charge. The pipes shall be properly cut to required lengths and joined using solvent cement, ensuring clean, leakproof, and properly aligned joints.
  • The pipes shall be fixed either on walls using suitable clamps at intervals not exceeding 2.0 meters center to center or concealed within walls or floors as directed. Proper supports shall be provided to avoid sagging or misalignment. All fittings such as elbows, tees, and couplers shall be installed as required to complete the piping network.
  • Care shall be taken to ensure proper alignment, slope (where applicable), and secure fixing of pipes. After installation, the entire pipeline shall be tested under pressure to check for leakage at joints and fittings. Any defects or leakage observed shall be rectified immediately. The finished installation shall be neat, properly aligned, and fully functional as per specifications.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment

subsections.title: Jointing the pipes
subsections.description: • The pipes and sockets shall be accurately cut the ends of the pipes and fittings should be absolutely free from dirt and dust. The outside surface of the pipes and the inside of the fittings shall then be roughened with emery paper, and then solvent cement shall be applied to the matching surface and pushed home and joint. Since solvent cement is aggressive to P.V.C. care must be taken to avoid applying excessive cement to the inside of pipe sockets as any surplus cement cannot be wiped off after joining. Empty solvent cement tins, brushes, rags aof paper unpregnated with cement should be buried in the trenches, they should be gathered, not left scattered about, as they can prove to be a hazard to animals, which may chew them.

subsections.title: Laying pipes in trenches
subsections.description:
• The pipes shall be laid over uniform relatively soft tine grained soil found to be free of presence of hard objects such as large fints, rocky projections, large tree roots, etc. The width of the trenches shall be minimum width required for working.
  • The pipes laid underground shall not be less than one metre from the ground level. The pipe shall be positioned in the trenches so as to avoid any induced stresses due to retraction. Any deviation required shall to be obtained by using proper type of rubber ring joints.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The description of each item, shall unless otherwise stated, be held to include where necessary, conveyances and delivery, handling, unloading, storing,  fabrication hoisting, all labour for finishing to required shape and size setting fitting in position, straight, cutting and waste, return of packing etc.
  • The length shall be measured on running metre basis of finished work. The length shall be taken along the centre line of the pipe and fittings. The pipes fixed to walls, ceiling, floors etc. shall be measured and paid under this item.
  • All the work shall be measured in decimal system as fixed in its place, subject to tolerance given below unless otherwise stated.
    • [i] Dimension shall be measured to the nearest 0.01 metre.
    • [ii] Area shall be worked out to the nesrest 0.01 Sq.mt.
  • In case of fittings of unequal bore, the largest bore shall be measured for the test.
  • Testing of pipe lines, fittings and joints included for providing all plant and appliances necessary for obtaining access to the work to be tested and carrying out the tests.
  • The rate includes galvanised steel tubing with screwed socket joints, together with all fittings (such as bends, sockets, springs, elbows, tees, crosses, short pieces, clamps and plug unions etc.) and fixing complete with clamping wall-hooks, wooden plugs etc. and also cutting screwing and waste and for making forged (or hand made) bends on piping as required. The rate also includes cutting through walls, floors etc. and their making good and painting exposed threads with anti-corrosive paint as above and testing. Where tubes are to be fixed to wall, ceiling and flooring, the rates shall not include painting of pipes, providing sleeves and sand filling under floor for which separate payment shall be made.
  • The rate include painting of pipes and sand filling all round tubes for which separate payment shall not be made. The length shall be measured on running metre basis.
  • The Above Specifications shall be Followed except that the P.V.C. pipes of specified dia. shall be paid under this item.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one running metre.

Description: Supplying , fabricating and eracting at site of work M.S. steel for column trusses, rafters, purlins, bolts, nuts, foundation bolts glazing frames etc. as per detailed drawing & design with brackets, gusset plates, base plates, top plates, cleats, stiffners etc. incl. cutting, bending, drilling holes, welding, etc. incl. supplying nuts & bolts of required size incl. providing one coat of anti-corrosive paint & two coats of approved alluminium or oil paint etc. comp. as directed.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description: • The structured steel work shall conform to M-22. Red lead paint shall conform to I.S : 102-1962.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The steel sections as specified or required, shall be cut, square and to correct lengths, as per drawings and design. The cut ends exposed to view shall be finished smooth. No two pieces shall be welded or otherwise jointed to make up the required length of member, except as indicated in the drawing or as directed. All straightening and shaping to form shall be done by application of pressure and not by hammering. Any bending or cutting shall be carried out in suet] a manner as not to impair the strength of the metal. All operations shall be done in cold state unless otherwise directed/permitted.
  • Steel riveted or bolted in built up sections, frame work.
  • The steel structure as shown in the drawings or as per direction of the Engineer-in-charge shall be laid out on a level platform to full scale and to full size in parts. A steel tape shall be used for measurements to ensure maximum accuracy.
  • Wooden templates 12 mm. to 19 mm. thick or metal sheet template shall be made to correspond to each connecting gussets plate and rivet holes shall be accurately marked on them and drilled. The templates shall be laid on the steel members and holes of the steel members shall also be marked for curing. The base of steel column and the .position of Anchor bolts shall be carefully set out.
  • All stiffeners shall be formed by pressure and where practicable the metal shall not to be cut and welded in making these. In major work', or whore so specified, shop drawings giving complete details and information for the fabrication of the component parts of the structure including location, type, size, (origin and details or rivets, bolts or weld shall be prepared in advance of the actual fabrication and as distinctly marked or stenciled with paint with the identification mark as given in the stop drawings. The bars shall be thickened at the ends, so as to provide for screwed threads and gradually tapered off to meet their normal section.
  • Great accuracy shall be observed in fabrication of various member, so that these can be assembled without being unduly packed, stained, or forced into position and when build up, shall be true and tree from twists, brinks, buckles, or open joints.
  • Before making holes in individual members for fabrication the steel work intended to be riveted or belted together shall be as ambled or clamped properly and tightly so as to ensure close abutting or lapping or the surfaces of the different members. All softeners shall bear tightly both at top and bottom without being drawn or caulked. The abutting joints shall be cut or crossed true and straight and fitted close together. Web splice plates and tillers under stiffened shall be cut to fit within 3 mm. or flange Angles Web plates of Girders shall have no cover. Plates, shall have their ends flush with the top of angles forming the flanges unless otherwise required. The web plates when spiced ^.hall have clearance of not more than 6 mm. The erection, clearance for created ends of members connecting steel shall preferably be not greater than i.5 mm. The erection clearance at the ends o' beams without web cleats shall not be more than 3 mm. at each end but where for a practical reason greater clearance is necessary, suitably designed seating shall be provided.
  • Pains and rollers shall be accurately tuned to gauge. These straight and smooth and free from flows. The roller bearing shall be provided with adequate arraignments fur holding the girders or truss resting on it. In columns caps and bases, the ends of shifts together with the attached gussets Angles, channels etc after riveting together shah be accurately mechanized so that the parts connected Butt against each other over the entire surfaces of contact connecting angles or channels shall he fabricated and placed in position with greater accuracy so that they are nut unduly reduced in thickness by machining. The ends of bearing stiffeners shall be mechanized or ground to tit tightly both at the top and bottom, Alt holes shall generally be drilled to the required size and at required, position. Sub punching shall be permitted provided it is done 3 mm. or less in diameter and reamer thereafter to the require size. The holes for rivets and bolts shall be larger by 0 4. to 6 mm. than the nominal diameter of rivets or black holts depending upon me diameter of rivets.
  • Holes shall have their axis perpendicular to the surface bored through. The drilling or remarrying shall be free from burrs, and the holes should be clean and accurate holes for counter sunk bolts shall be made in such a mariner that their heads fit flush with the surface after fixing.
  • The fabrication work shall be completed in workshop as far as it is practicable to do so. Site joints shall be done with rivets and fitted bolts or black bolts, as shown in the drawings or as directed. Generally the following principles shall govern the use of reverts turned and fitted bolts, and block bolts.
  • Rivets and turned and fitted bolts shall be used where the connections is such that slip under load has to be avoided.
  • Black bolts may be used very sparingly where a force is carried through a connection without impact, vibration or reversal or stresses.

subsections.title: Riveting
subsections.description:
• The parts assembled for riveting shall be in close contact with each other and the bearing stiffeners shall bear tightly both at top and bottom without being drawn or caulked. Members to be riveted shall be properly pinned or bolted and rigidly held to gather while riveting. Drifting of holes shall no! be permitted Except to draw the parts together and the drifting tools so used shall have maximum diameter not exceeding, the nominal diameter of rivets or bolls. Drifting done during assembling shall not distort the metal 01 enlarge the holes.
  • The shanks of rivets shall project beyond the plate-surface sufficiently so as to fill hole thoroughly and form the required head after riveting.
  • The riveting shall be done by hydraulic or pneumatic process. However, where such facilities air not available, hand riveting may be permitted. The rivet shall be heated red hot, care being taken to control the temperature of heating so as not to burn the steel. Rivers of diameter less than 10 mm. may be fitted cold. Rivets shall be of heat finish with heads full and of equal size. All loose, burnt or badly formed reverts with concentric or deficient heads shall be cut out and replaced. The heads of rivets shall be central to shanks and shall grip the assembled member firmly. In cutting out rivets, care shall be taken so as not be injure assembled members, caulking or reequipping shall not be permitted.
  • For testing rivets, a hammer weighing approximately 0 25 kg shall be used. Both heads of the rivets shall be tapped, slack rivets will give a hollow sound and a jar.
  • All rivet heads shall be painted with red lead paint within a week of their fixing.
  • All bolt heads and nuts shall be hexagonal arid of equal size unless specified otherwise. The screwed heads shall conform to I.S. 1363-1960 and the threaded surface shall not be tapered. The bolts shall be of such length so as to project two clear threads beyond the nuts when fixed in position and these shall lit in the holes without any shakes. The nut shall be fit in the threaded ends of bolts properly.
  • Where turned and fitted bolts are required to be used in place of rivets shall be provided with washers not less than 6 mm. thick so that the nut when tightened shall not bear on the unthreaded body of the bolt Tapered washers shall be provided for all heads and nuts bearing on leveled surfaces. The threaded portion of the bolt shall not be within the thickness of the parts bolted together, the faces of the bolt heads and nuts abutting against steel members shall be machine finished. Where there is a risk of the nut being removed or becoming loose due to vibrations or reversal of stresses, these shall be secured from slackening by me use of locknuts, spring washers, cross-cutting or hammering down of threads as directed.
  • Bolts, nuts, and-washers shall be thoroughly cleaned and dipped m double boiled linseed oil before use. The whole steel work shall be painted with a coat of priming coat of red lead, as per relevant specification of painting.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The steel work shall be measured in general as under:
  • All work shall be measured on the basis of finished dimensions as fixed at site and measured net unless specified otherwise.
  • The weight of steel sections, steel rods, and steel strips in finished work shall be calculated Hum standard weight on the same basis on which steel is supplied to Contractor by department or those given in relevant I S : if steel is arranged by the contractor.
  • The weight of steel plates and strips shall be taken from relevant I.S. based on 7.35 kg./ sq. meter fur every millimeter sheet thickness if steel is supplied to the contractor by department.
  • Unless otherwise specified, weight of cleats, brackets, packing pieces, bolts, nuts, washer, distance pieces, separators, diaphragm gusset (taking overall square dimensions) fish plates etc. shall lie added to the weight of respective items.
  • In riveted work allowance is to be made for weight of rivet hands. No deductions shall be made for rivet or bolts holes excluding holes for anchor or holding down bolts.
  • For forged steel and steel castings, weight shall be calculated on the basis of 7850 kg./cum.
  • Unless otherwise specified, no allowance shall be made for the weld metal in case of welded steel structure.
  • Dimensions other than cross sections and thickness of plates shall be measured to nearest 0.001m
  • Mill tolerance shall be ignored when weight is determined by calculation.
  • The rate includes cost of all material, labour, erection, hoisting scaffolding, protective measure, required for proper completion of the item of work. This shall also include conveyance and delivery handling, loading, unloading and storing etc. required for completing the item described above including necessary wastage involved.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Kg.

Description: Supplying, fabricating and erecting at site for Service Pit and other steelwork of steel structure using approved brand like TATA, Zindal or equivalent for Service Pitand other steelwork of steel structure incl bolts, nuts, foundation bolts, runners,angle section as per Required etc. as per detailed drawing & design with brackets, gusset plates, base plates, cleats, stiffners incl. cutting, bending, drilling holes and welding work as per ISS incl. supplying nuts, bolts of required size incl. providing one coat of approved anti-corrosive paint & two coats of approved  oil paint etc. comp. as directed.(For Service Pit and other steel work)

sections.title: Materials
sections.description: • The structured steel work shall conform to M-22. Red lead paint shall conform to I.S : 102-1962.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The steel sections as specified or required, shall be cut, square and to correct lengths, as per drawings and design. The cut ends exposed to view shall be finished smooth. No two pieces shall be welded or otherwise jointed to make up the required length of member, except as indicated in the drawing or as directed. All straightening and shaping to form shall be done by application of pressure and not by hammering. Any bending or cutting shall be carried out in suet] a manner as not to impair the strength of the metal. All operations shall be done in cold state unless otherwise directed/permitted.
  • Steel riveted or bolted in built up sections, frame work.
  • The steel structure as shown in the drawings or as per direction of the Engineer-in-charge shall be laid out on a level platform to full scale and to full size in parts. A steel tape shall be used for measurements to ensure maximum accuracy.
  • Wooden templates 12 mm. to 19 mm. thick or metal sheet template shall be made to correspond to each connecting gussets plate and rivet holes shall be accurately marked on them and drilled. The templates shall be laid on the steel members and holes of the steel members shall also be marked for curing. The base of steel column and the .position of Anchor bolts shall be carefully set out.
  • All stiffeners shall be formed by pressure and where practicable the metal shall not to be cut and welded in making these. In major work', or whore so specified, shop drawings giving complete details and information for the fabrication of the component parts of the structure including location, type, size, (origin and details or rivets, bolts or weld shall be prepared in advance of the actual fabrication and as distinctly marked or stenciled with paint with the identification mark as given in the stop drawings. The bars shall be thickened at the ends, so as to provide for screwed threads and gradually tapered off to meet their normal section.
  • Great accuracy shall be observed in fabrication of various member, so that these can be assembled without being unduly packed, stained, or forced into position and when build up, shall be true and tree from twists, brinks, buckles, or open joints.
  • Before making holes in individual members for fabrication the steel work intended to be riveted or belted together shall be as ambled or clamped properly and tightly so as to ensure close abutting or lapping or the surfaces of the different members. All softeners shall bear tightly both at top and bottom without being drawn or caulked. The abutting joints shall be cut or crossed true and straight and fitted close together. Web splice plates and tillers under stiffened shall be cut to fit within 3 mm. or flange Angles Web plates of Girders shall have no cover. Plates, shall have their ends flush with the top of angles forming the flanges unless otherwise required. The web plates when spiced ^.hall have clearance of not more than 6 mm. The erection, clearance for created ends of members connecting steel shall preferably be not greater than i.5 mm. The erection clearance at the ends o' beams without web cleats shall not be more than 3 mm. at each end but where for a practical reason greater clearance is necessary, suitably designed seating shall be provided.
  • Pains and rollers shall be accurately tuned to gauge. These straight and smooth and free from flows. The roller bearing shall be provided with adequate arraignments fur holding the girders or truss resting on it. In columns caps and bases, the ends of shifts together with the attached gussets Angles, channels etc after riveting together shah be accurately mechanized so that the parts connected Butt against each other over the entire surfaces of contact connecting angles or channels shall he fabricated and placed in position with greater accuracy so that they are nut unduly reduced in thickness by machining. The ends of bearing stiffeners shall be mechanized or ground to tit tightly both at the top and bottom, Alt holes shall generally be drilled to the required size and at required, position. Sub punching shall be permitted provided it is done 3 mm. or less in diameter and reamer thereafter to the require size. The holes for rivets and bolts shall be larger by 0 4. to 6 mm. than the nominal diameter of rivets or black holts depending upon me diameter of rivets.
  • Holes shall have their axis perpendicular to the surface bored through. The drilling or remarrying shall be free from burrs, and the holes should be clean and accurate holes for counter sunk bolts shall be made in such a mariner that their heads fit flush with the surface after fixing.
  • The fabrication work shall be completed in workshop as far as it is practicable to do so. Site joints shall be done with rivets and fitted bolts or black bolts, as shown in the drawings or as directed. Generally the following principles shall govern the use of reverts turned and fitted bolts, and block bolts.
  • Rivets and turned and fitted bolts shall be used where the connections is such that slip under load has to be avoided.
  • Black bolts may be used very sparingly where a force is carried through a connection without impact, vibration or reversal or stresses.

subsections.title: Riveting
subsections.description:
• The parts assembled for riveting shall be in close contact with each other and the bearing stiffeners shall bear tightly both at top and bottom without being drawn or caulked. Members to be riveted shall be properly pinned or bolted and rigidly held to gather while riveting. Drifting of holes shall no! be permitted Except to draw the parts together and the drifting tools so used shall have maximum diameter not exceeding, the nominal diameter of rivets or bolls. Drifting done during assembling shall not distort the metal 01 enlarge the holes.
  • The shanks of rivets shall project beyond the plate-surface sufficiently so as to fill hole thoroughly and form the required head after riveting.
  • The riveting shall be done by hydraulic or pneumatic process. However, where such facilities air not available, hand riveting may be permitted. The rivet shall be heated red hot, care being taken to control the temperature of heating so as not to burn the steel. Rivers of diameter less than 10 mm. may be fitted cold. Rivets shall be of heat finish with heads full and of equal size. All loose, burnt or badly formed reverts with concentric or deficient heads shall be cut out and replaced. The heads of rivets shall be central to shanks and shall grip the assembled member firmly. In cutting out rivets, care shall be taken so as not be injure assembled members, caulking or reequipping shall not be permitted.
  • For testing rivets, a hammer weighing approximately 0 25 kg shall be used. Both heads of the rivets shall be tapped, slack rivets will give a hollow sound and a jar.
  • All rivet heads shall be painted with red lead paint within a week of their fixing.
  • All bolt heads and nuts shall be hexagonal arid of equal size unless specified otherwise. The screwed heads shall conform to I.S. 1363-1960 and the threaded surface shall not be tapered. The bolts shall be of such length so as to project two clear threads beyond the nuts when fixed in position and these shall lit in the holes without any shakes. The nut shall be fit in the threaded ends of bolts properly.
  • Where turned and fitted bolts are required to be used in place of rivets shall be provided with washers not less than 6 mm. thick so that the nut when tightened shall not bear on the unthreaded body of the bolt Tapered washers shall be provided for all heads and nuts bearing on leveled surfaces. The threaded portion of the bolt shall not be within the thickness of the parts bolted together, the faces of the bolt heads and nuts abutting against steel members shall be machine finished. Where there is a risk of the nut being removed or becoming loose due to vibrations or reversal of stresses, these shall be secured from slackening by me use of locknuts, spring washers, cross-cutting or hammering down of threads as directed.
  • Bolts, nuts, and-washers shall be thoroughly cleaned and dipped m double boiled linseed oil before use. The whole steel work shall be painted with a coat of priming coat of red lead, as per relevant specification of painting.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The steel work shall be measured in general as under:
  • All work shall be measured on the basis of finished dimensions as fixed at site and measured net unless specified otherwise.
  • The weight of steel sections, steel rods, and steel strips in finished work shall be calculated Hum standard weight on the same basis on which steel is supplied to Contractor by department or those given in relevant I S : if steel is arranged by the contractor.
  • The weight of steel plates and strips shall be taken from relevant I.S. based on 7.35 kg./ sq. meter fur every millimeter sheet thickness if steel is supplied to the contractor by department.
  • Unless otherwise specified, weight of cleats, brackets, packing pieces, bolts, nuts, washer, distance pieces, separators, diaphragm gusset (taking overall square dimensions) fish plates etc. shall lie added to the weight of respective items.
  • In riveted work allowance is to be made for weight of rivet hands. No deductions shall be made for rivet or bolts holes excluding holes for anchor or holding down bolts.
  • For forged steel and steel castings, weight shall be calculated on the basis of 7850 kg./cum.
  • Unless otherwise specified, no allowance shall be made for the weld metal in case of welded steel structure.
  • Dimensions other than cross sections and thickness of plates shall be measured to nearest 0.001m
  • Mill tolerance shall be ignored when weight is determined by calculation.
  • The rate includes cost of all material, labour, erection, hoisting scaffolding, protective measure, required for proper completion of the item of work. This shall also include conveyance and delivery handling, loading, unloading and storing etc. required for completing the item described above including necessary wastage involved.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Kg.

Description: Providing & fixing M.S. grating work using M.S. flats, angles, tees, square, round or hexagonal bars as per detailed drawing and design with 3 coats of approved quality oil paint or aluminium paint incl. cutting, welding and drilling holes etc. comp. as directed.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• The structured steel work shall conform to M-22. Red lead paint shall conform to I.S : 102-1962.
  • All materials used for providing and fixing mild steel (M.S.) grating work shall conform to relevant Indian Standards and approved specifications. The M.S. sections such as flats, angles, tees, square bars, round bars, or hexagonal bars shall be of standard quality mild steel conforming to IS 2062, free from cracks, laminations, rust, or other defects. The sections shall be of specified sizes and dimensions as per detailed drawings and design requirements.
  • All steel members shall be straight, properly rolled, and true to size. Welding electrodes shall conform to IS 814 and shall be suitable for structural steel welding. The paint used shall be of approved quality, either oil paint or aluminium paint, applied over a suitable primer to ensure durability and corrosion resistance. All materials shall be new, of approved make, and shall be inspected and approved by the Engineer-in-Charge prior to use.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:

The steel sections shall be accurately cut to required sizes and assembled in the specified pattern and spacing. Proper care shall be taken to maintain uniform spacing, alignment, and level throughout the grating work. All joints shall be securely welded using appropriate welding techniques to ensure strength and rigidity, and welding shall be continuous and free from defects such as cracks or porosity.
  • Necessary holes shall be drilled accurately wherever required for fixing, and all burrs or sharp edges shall be removed. After fabrication, the entire grating shall be cleaned of rust, scale, oil, or dirt and prepared for painting. One coat of primer shall be applied, followed by three coats of approved quality oil paint or aluminium paint, ensuring uniform coverage and proper drying between coats.
  • The grating shall be fixed in position true to line and level using suitable fasteners, anchors, or welding to supporting members, ensuring firm and secure fixing without distortion. The finished work shall be neat, properly aligned, and free from defects such as uneven joints, misalignment, or poor welding. All work shall be completed as per drawings and directions of the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • Bolts, nuts, and-washers shall be thoroughly cleaned and dipped m double boiled linseed oil before use. The whole steel work shall be painted with a coat of priming coat of red lead, as per relevant specification of painting.

  • All work shall be measured on the basis of finished dimensions as fixed at site and measured net unless specified otherwise.

  • In riveted work allowance is to be made for weight of rivet hands. No deductions shall be made for rivet or bolts holes excluding holes for anchor or holding down bolts.
  • For forged steel and steel castings, weight shall be calculated on the basis of 7850 kg./cum.
  • Unless otherwise specified, no allowance shall be made for the weld metal in case of welded steel structure.

  • Mill tolerance shall be ignored when weight is determined by calculation.
