sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• The necessary materials like AISI 304 grade stainless steel pipes of approved quality & best quality confirming to relevant I.S code. All materials shall be got approved before starting the work. The entire work shall be carried out as per the instruction of Engineer-in-charge. Top rail of 50 mm diameter having 1.50 mm wall thickness, vertical support of 38 mm diameter stainless steel pipe having 1.50 mm with horizontal pipe of 25 mm diameter having 1.50 mm wall thickness and S.S plate of 100 mm diameter x 6.0 mm thick shall be used for executing the railing as per Architect design. The vertical support connected in R.C.C steps at 1200 mm C/C shall be fixed in R.C.C /brick wall / cement concrete masonry in line and level using necessary S.S fixtures & fastenings of the make KICH or as equivalent of approved by Engineer-in-charge shall be used. The entire daso shall be prepared as per design or as per drawing supplied or as directed by Architect.
  • Stainless Steel confirming to AISI 304 Grade Stainless Steel shall be completely anticorrosive and resist the adverse effects of chemicals.
  • It can withstand the corrosion caused by atmospheric / environmental or major chemical reactions.
  • It can resist high temperatures without going under any deformity which makes it highly recommended for fire safety doors in any building.
  • It has remarkable creep strength and Rupture strength.
  • It shall be repelled the Bacteria & shall be made higher degree of hygiene.
  • It shall be of natural finish, it shall not required regular cleaning or maintenance making it most suitable for public places.
  • Wall thickness of pipe shall be of 1.5 mm metal thickness instead of 1.2 mm thickness.
  • It shall tolerate forceful and intense use.
  • Specially developed fixing stud and grubs shall be used to ensure accurate fitting of elements and eliminates shaking of elements.
  • Testing shall be carried out in requisite laboratory for above chemical composition of AISI 304 Grade Stainless Steel & testing result for the same shall be submitted along with bill for claiming the amount of bill. If the results found fail, the fixtures and fastening of the same lot shall be rejected outright.
  • All fixtures and fastening of the make shall be of anti corrosive high grade AISI 304 stainless steel in Glossy & satin combination finish only. Fixtures and fastening of the make fashion. If after erection found daso to be damaged due to erection or due to any type of negligence of the agency, the same shall be replaced without any extra cost.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The stainless steel pipe railing shall be fabricated and installed in accordance with approved drawings and specifications. The S.S. pipes shall be accurately cut to required lengths and assembled to form a rigid railing system with three horizontal members fixed to vertical posts. The vertical posts shall be positioned at corners and at intervals not exceeding 1.5 meters center to center, ensuring proper alignment, spacing, and level.
  • All joints shall be properly welded, threaded, or connected using appropriate fittings, ensuring strong and durable connections. Welding shall be carried out carefully to avoid distortion, and all welded joints shall be ground smooth and finished neatly. Holes shall be drilled accurately wherever required for fixing. The railing posts shall be securely anchored into the concrete blocks of specified size, ensuring firm stability and resistance to movement.
  • Stainless steel sheets used at base connections shall be properly fixed and aligned. Care shall be taken during fabrication and installation to prevent scratches, dents, or damage to the stainless steel surface. The finished railing shall be smooth, free from sharp edges, and properly polished where required. The completed work shall be true to line, level, and plumb, and all components shall be checked for strength, alignment, and finish. The railing shall be handed over in a clean and defect-free condition as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The stainless steel pipe railing shall be measured in running meters (Rmt) based on the actual length of railing installed along the centerline, in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include the cost of all materials such as S.S. pipes, sheets, concrete blocks, fittings, fasteners, and all labour, tools, and plants required for cutting, welding, threading, drilling, fabrication, and fixing.
  • No separate measurement shall be made for joints, welds, base plates, concrete blocks, fasteners, or incidental works, as these are deemed to be included in the item rate. The work shall be measured net as fixed in position, and the rate shall include all incidental charges such as transportation, lifting, and finishing required to complete the work as per specifications and as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description: • All materials used for removing and refixing or replacing the door closer shall be of approved make and good quality. The new door closer shall be of standard hydraulic type suitable for the door size and weight, with adjustable closing speed and latching action, and shall be complete with all accessories such as mounting plate, upper and lower arms, brackets, and fixing screws. The door closer shall be durable, corrosion-resistant, and capable of smooth and controlled operation. All components shall be made from high-quality metal with proper surface finish, and fasteners shall be of stainless steel or corrosion-resistant material. Any additional plates, brackets, or accessories required for proper fixing shall also be of approved quality. All materials shall be new, free from defects, and shall be approved by the Engineer-in-Charge prior to installation.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall include careful dismantling and removal of the existing door closer without causing damage to the door, frame, or surrounding surfaces. The surface shall be cleaned, and any damaged or unsuitable fixing plates, brackets, or accessories shall be replaced as required. The new door closer shall be installed in proper alignment with the door and frame, ensuring correct positioning of the body, mounting plate, and upper and lower arms.
  • All components shall be securely fixed using appropriate screws and fasteners, ensuring firm anchorage and proper functioning. The door closer shall be adjusted to provide smooth and controlled closing action without jerks, slamming, or obstruction. Necessary adjustments to closing speed and latching shall be carried out as per manufacturer’s instructions. Care shall be taken to ensure that the door operates freely and closes properly without misalignment. The completed work shall be neat, and all fittings shall be tested for proper performance. Any minor damages during work shall be made good, and the installation shall be completed as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment

The rate shall include the cost of all materials such as door closer unit, mounting plates, arms, fasteners, and all labour, tools, and plants required for dismantling, fixing, adjustment, and testing.
  • No separate measurement shall be made for minor accessories, screws, adjustments, or incidental works, as these are deemed to be included in the item rate. The work shall be measured as completed and accepted, and the rate shall include all incidental charges required to complete the work as per specifications and as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.

Description: Providing & fixing European type wash down water closet pan of white glazed stoneware of approved quality and make like Perry or its equivalent with "P" or "S" trap incl. jointing the trap with flush pipe @100 mm dia. & joints in c.m. (1:1) incl. prov. black plastic seat and cover with C.P. brass hnges and rubber buffers incl. prov. & fixing 12.5 lit. low level flushing cistern with a pair of brackets with fittings like lead valve, syphon, 15 mm dia. brass ball valve with polythene float, C.P.brass handles, unions and couplings for connections with Inlet, Outlet & over flow pipes etc. all necessary accessories, fixtures & fastenings incl. testing the same for satisfactory functioning etc. comp. as directed.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• The European type water closet shall be white glazed porcelain first quality and shall be of wash down type conforming to I.S. 2556-1973 and I.S. 771-1979.
  • The low-level flushing cistern shall be of 12.5 litres capacity, complete with internal fittings such as lead valve, siphon mechanism, 15 mm diameter brass ball valve with polythene float, CP brass handles, unions, couplings, inlet, outlet, and overflow arrangements. The cistern shall be mounted on suitable brackets of approved quality.
  • The seat and cover shall be made of black plastic with CP brass hinges and rubber buffers of approved make. All fixtures and fittings including CP brass accessories, flush pipes, connecting pipes, screws, fasteners, and jointing materials such as cement mortar (1:1) shall be of approved quality and compatible with the system. All materials shall be new, defect-free, and approved by the Engineer-in-Charge prior to use.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall include supplying, fixing, and installing the European type water closet pan with low-level cistern as per approved drawings and manufacturer’s specifications. The WC pan shall be properly positioned, leveled, and fixed securely to the flooring using cement mortar (1:1) and suitable fasteners.
  • The trap (“P” or “S”) shall be correctly connected to the flush pipe and drainage system using proper jointing materials to ensure leakproof connections. The low-level cistern shall be fixed at the specified height using brackets, ensuring proper alignment and stability. All internal fittings of the cistern shall be assembled and adjusted for smooth and efficient flushing operation.
  • The inlet connection shall be made using 15 mm diameter pipes with brass ball valve and polythene float, ensuring proper water control. Overflow, inlet, and outlet connections shall be properly aligned and sealed. The seat and cover shall be fixed with CP brass hinges and rubber buffers, ensuring smooth operation and durability.
  • All joints shall be tested for leakages by operating the system several times. The entire installation shall be checked for proper flushing, alignment, stability, and leakproof performance. Care shall be taken to avoid damage to sanitary ware during handling and installation. The completed work shall be clean, functional, and satisfactory to the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The European type water closet with low-level cistern shall be measured on a per number (Each) basis, in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include the cost of WC pan, cistern, seat and cover, traps, pipes, fittings, brackets, fasteners, jointing materials, labour, installation, testing, and all incidental works required for completion.
  • No separate measurement shall be made for minor fittings, jointing materials, fixing accessories, or testing, as these are deemed to be included in the item rate. Any additional pipe lengths or major external connections beyond the specified scope shall be measured separately if specified in the BOQ. The work shall be measured as completed and accepted, and payment shall be made as per actual installation directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.

Description: Supplying & fixing heavy duty ceramic tiles of 6 to 7 mm th. & required size  as per approved pattern & design laid over neat cement slurry & cement mortar in (1:3) bedding 12 mm th. average & joint with colour cement slurry incl. special cornices, corners or angles, tiles etc. incl. cost of fixing materials, labour, tools, plants, equipmens incl. all lead & lift at Sanitary Blocks comp. as directed by engg. in charge. (A) Flooring

sections.title: Materials
sections.description: • Water shall conform to M-1 Cement mortar shall conform to M-11.

subsections.title: Bedding
subsections.description:
• The sub grade shall be cleaned, wetted and mopped. The bedding shall then be laid evenly over the surface tamped and corrected to desired level and allowed to harden enough to offer a rigid cushion to tiles and to enable the monsoon to place wooden planks across and squat on it.
  • The ceramic tiles shall be laid on cement mortar bedding of 12 mm. thick in C.M. 1:3. The mortar shall have sufficient plasticity for laying and there shall be no hard lumps that would interfere with the evenness of bedding. The base shall be cleared and well wetted. The mortar shall then be spread in thickness not less than 10 mm. at any place and average 12 mm. thickness. The proportion of the cement mortar shall be as specified in the item.

subsections.title: Fixing Tiles
subsections.description:
• The tiles before laying shall be soaked in water for at least tow hours. Neat gray cement grout at 33 kg/Cement/Sq. mt. of honey like consistency shall be spread over the mortar bedding as directed. The edges of the tiles shall be smeared with neat cement slurry. The tiles shall be well pressed and gently tapped with a wooden mallet till they are properly bedded and in level with the adjoining tiles. There shall be. no hollows in bed or joints. The joints between the tiles shall be as thin as possible in straight line or as per pattern.
  • The tiles shall not have staggered joints. The joints shall be true to centre line both ways. The Nahni trap coming in the flooring shall be so positioned that its grating shall replace only one tile as far as possible. Where full size tiles cannot be fixed they shall be cut (Swan) to the required size and the edges rubbed smooth to ensure straight and true joints. The joints shall be filled with grey cement grout with wire brush or trowel to a depth of 5 mm. and loose material removed. White cement shall be used for pointing the joints. After fixing the tiles finally in an even plane the flooring shall be kept wet and allowed to nature undisturbed for 7 days.

subsections.title: Cleaning
subsections.description: • The surplus cement grout that may have come out of the joints shall be cleaned off before it sets. Once the floor has set, it shall be carefully washed, cleared by dilute acid and dried. Proper precautions and measures shall be taken to ensure that the tiles are not damaged in any way till the completion of the construction.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The work done shall be measured in sq. mt. for visible area of work done. The length and width of the flooring shall be measured not between the faces of skirting or dedos or plastered face of wall as the case may be. The paving under dedo or skirting shall not be measured. No deduction shall be made not extra paid for any opening in the floor of area-up to 0.1 sq.mt. Nothing extra shall be paid for laying the floors at different levels in the same rooms.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Square Meter.

Description: Supplying & fixing heavy duty ceramic tiles of 6 to 7 mm th. & required size  as per approved pattern & design laid over neat cement slurry & cement mortar in (1:3) bedding 12 mm th. average & joint with colour cement slurry incl. special cornices, corners or angles, tiles etc. incl. cost of fixing materials, labour, tools, plants, equipmens incl. all lead & lift at Sanitary Blocks comp. as directed by engg. in charge. (B) Skirting/ Dedo

sections.title: Materials
sections.description: • Water shall conform to M-1 Cement mortar shall conform to M-11.

subsections.title: Preparation of Surface
subsections.description: • In case of brick masonry wall, the joints shall be raked out to a depth of least 15 mm. while the masonry is being laid. In case of concrete wall the surface shall be chiseled and roughed with wire brushes. The surface shall be cleaned and wetted thoroughly before commencing the laying work.

subsections.title: Laying
subsections.description:
• The wall surface shall be covered with 10 mm. thick plaster of cement mortar 1:3 mix and allowed to harden. The plaster shall be roughened with wire brushes both way. The back of tiles shall be floated with grey cement slurry set and edges with white cement slurry in bedding mortar. The tiles shall be gently tapped in position on after the other keeping the joints as thin as possible. Top of skirting or dedo shall be truly horizontal and the joints vertical or as per required pattern.
  • Risers of steps, skirting and dedo shall rest on top of treads or flooring. Where full size tiles be fixed, They shall be cut to the required size and the edges be smoothened.
  • The joints shall be cleaned and flush pointed with white cement. The surface shall be kept wet for seven days. After curing the surface shall be washed clean.

subsections.title: Cleaning
subsections.description: • The surplus cement grout that may have come out of the joints shall be cleaned off before it sets. Once the floor has set, it shall be carefully washed, cleared by dilute acid and dried. Proper precautions and measures shall be taken to ensure that the tiles are not damaged in any way till the completion of the construction.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The rate shall include the cost of all materials and labour required for various operations described above. Risers of steps: skirting and dedo shall be measured in square meters, length and height shall be measured along the finished face of the skirting or dedo including curves, where special such as covers. internal and external angles, etc., used. The length and height shall be measured correct lo the centimeter except in case of risers and skirting where height shall be measured correct to 3 mm.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Square Meter.

Description: Providing and fixing to wall, ceiling and floor galvanised Mild steel tubes (Medium grade) of the following nominal bore, tube fitting and clamps including making good the wall ceiling and floor. (F) 50 mm dia

sections.title: Materials
sections.description: • Galvanised mild steel tubes of specified dia. nominal bore shall conform to I.S. 1239-1990. The galvanised fittings, clamps, etc. required for specified dia. bore pipes shall be of best quality and make as approved by the Engineer-in- charge.(Galvanised iron pipes and fittings shall conform to M-56)

subsections.title: Cutting, Laying & Jointing
subsections.description:
• When the tubes are to be cut or rethreaded, the ends shall be carefully filed out so that no obstruction to bore is offered. The ends of the tubes shall then be threaded conforming to the requirements of I.S. 554- 1955 with pipe dies and taps carefully in such a manner as will not result in slackness of joints when the two pieces are screwed together.
  • The taps and dies shall be used only for straightening screw threads which have become bent or damanged and shall not be used for turning of the threads so as to make them slack as the latter procedure may not result in a water tight joint. The screw threads for the tube and fittings shall be protected from edge until they are fitted.
  • In jointing the tubes, the inside of the socket screwed end of the tubes shall be oiled and smeared with white or red lead and wrapping around with a few turns of fine spun yarn round the screwed end of the tube. The end shall then be tightly screwed in the socket, tees, etc. with a pipe wrench. Care shall be taken that all pipes and fittings are properly jointed so as to make the joints completely water tight and pipes are kept at all times free from dust and dirt during fixing. Burr from the joints shall be removed after screwing. After laying the open ends of the pipes shall be temporarily plugged to prevent access of water, soil or any other foreign matter.
  • Any threads exposed after 3 jointing shall be painted or in the case of underground piping thickly coated with approved anti-corrosive paint to prevent corrosion.

subsections.title: Laying in Trenches
subsections.description:
• The width and depth of the trenches for different diameters of the tubes shall be as - For 15 to 80 mm. dia. tube width of trenches shall be 30 cms. and depth of trenches 60 cms.
    At joints, the trench width shall be widened where necessary. The work of excavation and refilling shall be done true to line and gradient in accordance with general specifications of earth work in trenches.
    The pipes shall be painted with two coats of anti-corrosive bitumastic paint of approved quality. The pipe shall be laid on a layer of 75mm. sand filled upto 150mm. above the pipe if so specified. The remaining portion of trench shall be then filled with excavated earth. The surplus earth shall be disposed of as directed. When the excavation is done in rock the bottom shall cut deep enough to permit the pipe to be laid and cushion of sand 75 mm.  In case of bigger diameter of tube where pressure is very high, thrust block of cement concrete 1:2:4 (1 cement; 2 coarse sand; 4 graded stone aggregate of 20 mm. nominal size) shall be constructed on all bends to transmit the hydraulic thrust without imparing the ground  and spreading it over a sufficient area if so specified.
  • Fixing of Tube Fittings to wall ceiling & floors - In case of fixing of tubes and fittings to the walls or ceilings, these shall run on the surface of the wall or ceiling (not in chase) unless otherwise specified. The fixing shall be done by means of standard pattern, holder clamps keeping the pipes about 15mm. clear of the wall. When it is found necessary to conceal the pipes and when specified so, chasing may be adopted or pipe fixed in ducts or recesses etc. provided that there is sufficient space to work on the pipe with usual tools. The pipe shall not ordinarily be buried in walls or solid floors, where unavoidable pipes may be buried for short distances provided that adequate protection is given against damage and where so required joints are not buried.  Where required M.S. tube sleaves shall be fixed at a place a pipe is passing through a wall or floor for expansion and contraction and other movements. In case the pipe is embeded in walls or floors, it should be painted with anti-corrosive bitumastic paint of approved quality. The pipe should not come in contact with lime mortar or lime concrete as the pipe is affected by lime, under the floors, the pipe shall be laid in layer of sand filling.
  • All pipes and fittings shall be fixed truly vertical and horizontal unless unavoidable. The pipes shall be fixed to walls with standard pattern clamps or required size and shape, one end of which shall be properly plugged or cemented into walls with cement mortar 1:3 (1 cement; 3 coarse sand) and the other tightened round the pipes to hold it securely.  These clamps shall be spaced at regular intervals in straight lengths at 2 M c/c interval in horizontal run and 2.5 M. intervals in vertical run. For pipe of 15 mm. dia. upto 25 mm. dia. the holes in the walls and floors shall be made by drilling with chisel or jumper and not by dismantling the brick or concrete. However, for bigger diameter pipes the holes shall be carefully made of the smallest required size. After fixing the pipe holes shall be made good with cement mortar 1:3 (1 cement; 3 coarse sand) and properly finished to match the adjacent surface.

subsections.title: Testing of Joints
subsections.description:
• After laying and jointing, the pipes and fittings shall be inspected under working conditions of pressure and flow. Any joint found leaking shall be redone, and all leaking pipes removed and replaced without extra cost.
  • The pipes and fittings after they are laid shall be tested to hydraulic pressure of 6 Kg./sq.cm.  The pipe shall be slowly and carefully charged with water allowing all air to escape and avoiding all stock and water hammer. The draw off takes and stock shall then be closed and specified hydraulic pressure shall be applied gradually. The pressure gauge must be accurate . The pipes and fittings shall be tested in sections as the work of laying proceeds, veeping the joints exposed for inspection during the testing.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The description of each item, shall unless otherwise stated, be held to include where necessary, conveyances and delivery, handling, unloading, storing,  fabrication hoisting, all labour for finishing to required shape and size setting fitting in position, straight, cutting and waste, return of packing etc.
  • The length shall be measured on running metre basis of finished work. The length shall be taken along the centre line of the pipe and fittings. The pipes fixed to walls, ceiling, floors etc. shall be measured and paid under this item.
  • All the work shall be measured in decimal system as fixed in its place, subject to tolerance given below unless otherwise stated.
    • [i] Dimension shall be measured to the nearest 0.01 metre.
    • [ii] Area shall be worked out to the nesrest 0.01 Sq.mt.
  • In case of fittings of unequal bore, the largest bore shall be measured for the test.
  • Testing of pipe lines, fittings and joints included for providing all plant and appliances necessary for obtaining access to the work to be tested and carrying out the tests.
  • The rate includes galvanised steel tubing with screwed socket joints, together with all fittings (such as bends, sockets, springs, elbows, tees, crosses, short pieces, clamps and plug unions etc.) and fixing complete with clamping wall-hooks, wooden plugs etc. and also cutting screwing and waste and for making forged (or hand made) bends on piping as required. The rate also includes cutting through walls, floors etc. and their making good and painting exposed threads with anti-corrosive paint as above and testing. Where tubes are to be fixed to wall, ceiling and flooring, the rates shall not include painting of pipes, providing sleeves and sand filling under floor for which separate payment shall be made.
  • The rate include painting of pipes and sand filling all round tubes for which separate payment shall not be made. The length shall be measured on running metre basis.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one running metre.

Description: Providing  and  Fixing double side  polished  kota  stone  slab flooring  over  20  mm.(average)   thick  base  of cement mortar 1:6 (1 cement : 6 coarse sand) or L.M. 1:1.5  laid over and jointed with gray cement slurry including rubbing, polishing and  rounding the outer edge, moulding incl. using adhesive for fixing of shelves etc comp as per directed by eng incharge. [A] 30 mm

sections.title: Materials
sections.description: Water shall conform to M-1. Lime mortar shall conform to M-10. Cement mortar shall conform to M-11 Polished kota stone shall conform to M-49.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• Each slab shall be cut to the required size and shape and fine chisel dressed at all the edges. The sides trust dressed shall have a full contract if a straight edge is laid along. The sides shall be table rubbed with coarse sand before paving. All angles and edges of the slabs shall be true square and free from chippings and giving a plane surface. The thickness shall be 30 mm. (Average) as specified in the item but not less than 25 mm. at any place of the slab.
  • Bedding  for  the  Kota  stone  slabs  shall  be  of  cement  mortar  1:6  (1  cement  :  6  coarse  sand)  or L.M.  1:1.5  of  average  thickness  20  mm  given  in  the  description  of  the  item.  Sub  grade  shall be  cleaned,  wetted  and  mopped  Mortar  of  the  specified  mix  and  thickness  shall  then  be  spread  on an  area  sufficient  to  receive  one  kota  stone  slab.  The  slab  shall  be  washed  clean  before  laying.  It shall  be  laid  on  top,  pressed,  tapped  gently  to  bring  it  in  level  with  the  other  slabs.  If  shall then  be  lifted  and  laid  aside.  Top  surface  of  the  mortar  shall  then  be  corrected  by  adding fresh  mortar  at  hollows  or  depressions.  The  mortar  shall  then  be  allowed  to  harden  bit. Over  this  surface,  cement  slurry  of  honey-like  consistency  shall  be  applied.  The  slab  shall  then  be gently placed in position and tapped with wooden mallet till it is properly padded in level with and close to the adjoining slab. The joint shall be as fine as possible. The slabs fixed in the floor adjoining, the walls shall enter not less than 10 mm. under the plaster, skirting or dedo. The junction between the wan and floor shall be finished neatly. The finished surface shall be true to levels and slopes as directed.
  • The floor shall be kept wet for a minimum period of 7 days so that bedding and joints set properly.
  • Polishing shall be normally commenced after 14 days of laying the stone slab. First polishing shah be done with carborundum stones of 120 grade grit fitted in the heavy machine and then second polishing shall be done with carborundum stone of 220 to 350 grade grit fitted in heavy machine. Water shall be properly used during polishing. The stone shall then be washed clean with water When directed by the Engineer-in-charge, wax polish of approved quality shall be applied on the surface with the help of soft cloth over a clean and dry surface. Then the polishing machine fitted with bobs shall be run over it.
  • The holes required for Nahni traps, pipes and any other fittings shall be made, without any extra cost.
  • The surplus cement grout that may have come out of the joints shall be cleaned off before it sets. Once the floor has set, it shall be carefully washed, cleared by dilute acid and dried. Proper precautions and measures shall be taken to ensure that the tiles are not damaged in any way till the completion of the construction.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The rate shall include the cost of all materials and labour involved in ail the operations described above. The kota stone flooring shall be measured in square meters correct to two places decimal, length and breadth shall be measured correct to a centimeter and between the finished face of skirting dedo plaster and no deduction shall be made nor extra paid for any opening in floor of areas up to 0.1 sq.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Square Meter.

Description: Providing & laying 25 mm th. polished kotah stone of approved quality  with joings in c.m. (1:2) and pure cement incl. 25 mm th. C.m. (1:5) bedding and floating pure cement slurry incl. lining, watering, curing, cutting and dressing the stone to required size & shape incl. laying the flooring in proper line & level incl. machine polishing and finishing with wax etc. comp. as directed. Over  this  surface,  cement  slurry  of  honey-like  consistency  shall  be  applied.  The  slab  shall  then  be gently placed in position and tapped with wooden mallet till it is properly padded in level with and close to the adjoining slab. The joint shall be as fine as possible. The slabs fixed in the floor adjoining, the walls shall enter not less than 10 mm. under the plaster, skirting or dedo. The junction between the wan and floor shall be finished neatly. The finished surface shall be true to levels and slopes as directed.
  • The floor shall be kept wet for a minimum period of 7 days so that bedding and joints set properly.
  • Polishing shall be normally commenced after 14 days of laying the stone slab. First polishing shah be done with carborundum stones of 120 grade grit fitted in the heavy machine and then second polishing shall be done with carborundum stone of 220 to 350 grade grit fitted in heavy machine. Water shall be properly used during polishing. The stone shall then be washed clean with water When directed by the Engineer-in-charge, wax polish of approved quality shall be applied on the surface with the help of soft cloth over a clean and dry surface. Then the polishing machine fitted with bobs shall be run over it.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The risers of steps, skirting or dedo shall be measured in sq. meter Length shall be measured along the finished faces of risers, skirting or dedo. Height shall be measured from finished level of treads of floor to top. Lining of pillars shall be measured under this item.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Square Meter.

Description: Providing and fixing to wall, ceiling and floor galvanised Mild steel tubes (Medium grade) of the following nominal bore, tube fitting and clamps including making good the wall ceiling and floor. (E) 40 mm dia

sections.title: Materials
sections.description: • Galvanised mild steel tubes of specified dia. nominal bore shall conform to I.S. 1239-1990. The galvanised fittings, clamps, etc. required for specified dia. bore pipes shall be of best quality and make as approved by the Engineer-in- charge.(Galvanised iron pipes and fittings shall conform to M-56)

subsections.title: Cutting, Laying & Jointing
subsections.description:
• When the tubes are to be cut or rethreaded, the ends shall be carefully filed out so that no obstruction to bore is offered. The ends of the tubes shall then be threaded conforming to the requirements of I.S. 554- 1955 with pipe dies and taps carefully in such a manner as will not result in slackness of joints when the two pieces are screwed together.
  • The taps and dies shall be used only for straightening screw threads which have become bent or damanged and shall not be used for turning of the threads so as to make them slack as the latter procedure may not result in a water tight joint. The screw threads for the tube and fittings shall be protected from edge until they are fitted.
  • In jointing the tubes, the inside of the socket screwed end of the tubes shall be oiled and smeared with white or red lead and wrapping around with a few turns of fine spun yarn round the screwed end of the tube. The end shall then be tightly screwed in the socket, tees, etc. with a pipe wrench. Care shall be taken that all pipes and fittings are properly jointed so as to make the joints completely water tight and pipes are kept at all times free from dust and dirt during fixing. Burr from the joints shall be removed after screwing. After laying the open ends of the pipes shall be temporarily plugged to prevent access of water, soil or any other foreign matter.
  • Any threads exposed after 3 jointing shall be painted or in the case of underground piping thickly coated with approved anti-corrosive paint to prevent corrosion.

subsections.title: Laying in Trenches
subsections.description:
• The width and depth of the trenches for different diameters of the tubes shall be as - For 15 to 80 mm. dia. tube width of trenches shall be 30 cms. and depth of trenches 60 cms.
    At joints, the trench width shall be widened where necessary. The work of excavation and refilling shall be done true to line and gradient in accordance with general specifications of earth work in trenches.
    The pipes shall be painted with two coats of anti-corrosive bitumastic paint of approved quality. The pipe shall be laid on a layer of 75mm. sand filled upto 150mm. above the pipe if so specified. The remaining portion of trench shall be then filled with excavated earth. The surplus earth shall be disposed of as directed. When the excavation is done in rock the bottom shall cut deep enough to permit the pipe to be laid and cushion of sand 75 mm.  In case of bigger diameter of tube where pressure is very high, thrust block of cement concrete 1:2:4 (1 cement; 2 coarse sand; 4 graded stone aggregate of 20 mm. nominal size) shall be constructed on all bends to transmit the hydraulic thrust without imparing the ground  and spreading it over a sufficient area if so specified.
  • Fixing of Tube Fittings to wall ceiling & floors - In case of fixing of tubes and fittings to the walls or ceilings, these shall run on the surface of the wall or ceiling (not in chase) unless otherwise specified. The fixing shall be done by means of standard pattern, holder clamps keeping the pipes about 15mm. clear of the wall. When it is found necessary to conceal the pipes and when specified so, chasing may be adopted or pipe fixed in ducts or recesses etc. provided that there is sufficient space to work on the pipe with usual tools. The pipe shall not ordinarily be buried in walls or solid floors, where unavoidable pipes may be buried for short distances provided that adequate protection is given against damage and where so required joints are not buried.  Where required M.S. tube sleaves shall be fixed at a place a pipe is passing through a wall or floor for expansion and contraction and other movements. In case the pipe is embeded in walls or floors, it should be painted with anti-corrosive bitumastic paint of approved quality. The pipe should not come in contact with lime mortar or lime concrete as the pipe is affected by lime, under the floors, the pipe shall be laid in layer of sand filling.
  • All pipes and fittings shall be fixed truly vertical and horizontal unless unavoidable. The pipes shall be fixed to walls with standard pattern clamps or required size and shape, one end of which shall be properly plugged or cemented into walls with cement mortar 1:3 (1 cement; 3 coarse sand) and the other tightened round the pipes to hold it securely.  These clamps shall be spaced at regular intervals in straight lengths at 2 M c/c interval in horizontal run and 2.5 M. intervals in vertical run. For pipe of 15 mm. dia. upto 25 mm. dia. the holes in the walls and floors shall be made by drilling with chisel or jumper and not by dismantling the brick or concrete. However, for bigger diameter pipes the holes shall be carefully made of the smallest required size. After fixing the pipe holes shall be made good with cement mortar 1:3 (1 cement; 3 coarse sand) and properly finished to match the adjacent surface.

subsections.title: Testing of Joints
subsections.description:
• After laying and jointing, the pipes and fittings shall be inspected under working conditions of pressure and flow. Any joint found leaking shall be redone, and all leaking pipes removed and replaced without extra cost.
  • The pipes and fittings after they are laid shall be tested to hydraulic pressure of 6 Kg./sq.cm.  The pipe shall be slowly and carefully charged with water allowing all air to escape and avoiding all stock and water hammer. The draw off takes and stock shall then be closed and specified hydraulic pressure shall be applied gradually. The pressure gauge must be accurate . The pipes and fittings shall be tested in sections as the work of laying proceeds, veeping the joints exposed for inspection during the testing.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The description of each item, shall unless otherwise stated, be held to include where necessary, conveyances and delivery, handling, unloading, storing,  fabrication hoisting, all labour for finishing to required shape and size setting fitting in position, straight, cutting and waste, return of packing etc.
  • The length shall be measured on running metre basis of finished work. The length shall be taken along the centre line of the pipe and fittings. The pipes fixed to walls, ceiling, floors etc. shall be measured and paid under this item.
  • All the work shall be measured in decimal system as fixed in its place, subject to tolerance given below unless otherwise stated.
    • [i] Dimension shall be measured to the nearest 0.01 metre.
    • [ii] Area shall be worked out to the nesrest 0.01 Sq.mt.
  • In case of fittings of unequal bore, the largest bore shall be measured for the test.
  • Testing of pipe lines, fittings and joints included for providing all plant and appliances necessary for obtaining access to the work to be tested and carrying out the tests.
  • The rate includes galvanised steel tubing with screwed socket joints, together with all fittings (such as bends, sockets, springs, elbows, tees, crosses, short pieces, clamps and plug unions etc.) and fixing complete with clamping wall-hooks, wooden plugs etc. and also cutting screwing and waste and for making forged (or hand made) bends on piping as required. The rate also includes cutting through walls, floors etc. and their making good and painting exposed threads with anti-corrosive paint as above and testing. Where tubes are to be fixed to wall, ceiling and flooring, the rates shall not include painting of pipes, providing sleeves and sand filling under floor for which separate payment shall be made.
  • The rate include painting of pipes and sand filling all round tubes for which separate payment shall not be made. The length shall be measured on running metre basis.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one running metre.

Description: Providing & constructing of Granite top Sandwitch type Ticket counter & Kitchen Platform as per detail design & drawing of 1.2 mtr. height & 90 cms. wide resting on both side polished kotah stone 25 mm thick top and 40mm thick polished kotah stone vertical support fixing by making grooves with 18 mm thick black granite stone slab top including moulding the external edge of the granite shall be finished with Quarter round molding & mirror polished etc.complete  as directed.

sections.description: • Water shall conform to M-1. Lime mortar shall conform to M-10. Cement mortar shall conform to M-11 Polished kota stone shall conform to M-49. Granite Slab shall conform to M-52.

sections.description:
• The granite top sandwich type ticket counter or kitchen platform shall be constructed strictly as per approved drawings and design, maintaining overall dimensions of approximately 1.20 m height and 0.90 m width. The vertical supports shall be constructed using 40 mm thick polished Kota stone slabs fixed in proper alignment and level on both sides, ensuring stability and strength. The top shall be formed using 25 mm thick polished Kota stone slab, over which the 18 mm thick black granite slab shall be fixed to create a sandwich type construction.
  • Proper grooves shall be made in the supporting structure to securely fix the granite slab, ensuring proper seating and bonding. The granite top shall be accurately cut and fixed with neat joints, and the exposed edges shall be finished with quarter round moulding and mirror polishing to achieve a smooth and aesthetic finish. All joints shall be properly aligned and finished, and any gaps shall be filled with suitable matching material to provide a uniform appearance.
  • Care shall be taken during handling and fixing to avoid damage to the polished surfaces. The entire platform shall be true to line, level, and plumb, with smooth, even surfaces free from undulations or defects. The finished work shall be properly cleaned, and all stains, marks, or excess materials shall be removed. The completed counter/platform shall be robust, aesthetically finished, and in accordance with specifications and directions of the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.description:

The rate shall include the cost of all materials such as granite slab, Kota stone slabs, cement, sand, adhesives, and all labour, tools, and plants required for cutting, grooving, fixing, polishing, and finishing.
  • No separate measurement shall be made for moulding, polishing, grooves, joints, wastage, or incidental works, as these are deemed to be included in the item rate. The work shall be measured net as completed and accepted, and the rate shall include all incidental charges required to complete the work as per specifications and as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Square Meter.

Description: Providing and fixing pre-cast Rubber Dye / steel Dye inter locking concrete block 60mm thick with grade of concrete M300 pnumatic compressed / vibrated mechanically and as per approved design Confirming to IS 15658 : 2006 including 35 mm Sand layer for levelling and filling the joint with sand in proper line and level as per guidlines of IRC : SP 63-2018 etc. Complete.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• All materials used for providing and fixing precast interlocking concrete blocks shall conform to relevant Indian Standards and approved specifications. The interlocking paver blocks shall be machine made using rubber moulds or steel dies, of 60 mm thickness, and shall be manufactured from high-strength concrete of minimum grade M30, conforming to IS 15658. The blocks shall be hydraulically or pneumatically compressed and vibrated to achieve high density, uniform shape, and durability, and shall be free from cracks, chips, or defects.
  • The sand used for bedding and joint filling shall be clean, well-graded, and free from silt, clay, and organic impurities, conforming to IS 383. The bedding sand layer shall be 35 mm thick, properly graded to ensure uniform support and interlock of blocks. All materials shall be new, of approved quality, and shall be inspected and approved by the Engineer-in-Charge prior to use.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The interlocking concrete block paving shall be laid in accordance with approved drawings and guidelines of IRC SP 63-2018. The subgrade shall be properly prepared, compacted, and brought to the required line, level, and camber. The bedding layer of sand of 35 mm thickness shall be uniformly spread, levelled, and lightly compacted to provide a smooth and even base for laying the paver blocks.
  • The precast interlocking blocks shall be laid manually in the specified pattern and alignment, ensuring tight interlocking and uniform joints. Care shall be taken to maintain proper line, level, and surface evenness throughout the work. The blocks shall be compacted using a plate compactor to ensure proper seating into the bedding layer. After laying, clean dry sand shall be spread over the surface and brushed into the joints to fill all gaps completely, followed by further compaction to achieve proper interlock and stability.
  • Edge restraints shall be provided where necessary to prevent lateral movement of blocks. Any damaged or defective blocks shall be removed and replaced. The finished surface shall be even, true to line and level, and free from irregularities, depressions, or loose blocks. The completed work shall be cleaned and handed over in proper condition as per specifications and directions of the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The interlocking concrete block paving shall be measured in square meters (m²) based on the actual area laid, in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include the cost of all materials such as precast paver blocks, bedding sand, joint filling sand, and all labour, tools, and plants required for surface preparation, laying, compaction, and finishing.
  • No separate measurement shall be made for sand bedding, joint filling, compaction, cutting of blocks, wastage, or incidental works, as these are deemed to be included in the item rate. The work shall be measured net as completed and accepted, and the rate shall include all incidental charges required to complete the work as per specifications and as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Square Meter.

Description: Providing & Fixing Precast concrete curb stone of grey cement based concrete block 30 cm length, 30 cm. height & 15 cm thick of M-250 grade concrete as per approved design and incl. excavation in any kind of soil, hardened / asphalted surface for fixing in proper line  & level, filling the joints with C.M. (1:1) etc. incl. applying one coat of wall primer and two coats of approved quality & Brand oil paint in even shade & design given by Engg. in charge etc. comp. as directed.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
All materials used for providing and fixing precast concrete curb stones shall conform to relevant Indian Standards and approved specifications. The curb stones shall be precast using grey cement-based concrete of grade M25, manufactured with properly graded aggregates conforming to IS 383 and cement conforming to IS 8112 or IS 12269. The curb stones shall be of size 30 cm length, 30 cm height, and 15 cm thickness, machine cast, well compacted, cured, and free from cracks, honeycombing, or defects, conforming to IS 456.

Cement mortar used for jointing shall be in proportion 1:1 (cement:sand), using clean, well-graded sand conforming to IS 383. Primer and paint used shall be of approved make and quality, with wall primer suitable for concrete surfaces and oil paint providing durable and uniform finish. All materials shall be new, of approved quality, and shall be inspected and approved by the Engineer-in-Charge prior to use.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The precast concrete curb stones shall be installed in accordance with approved drawings and specifications. Excavation shall be carried out in all types of soil, including hard or asphalted surfaces, to the required depth and width to accommodate the curb stones and necessary bedding. The base shall be properly prepared, levelled, and compacted to ensure stable support.
  • The curb stones shall be placed in position in correct line, level, and alignment as per the layout, ensuring uniform spacing and proper verticality. Cement mortar (1:1) shall be used for jointing between curb stones, and joints shall be properly filled and finished. Necessary adjustments shall be made to maintain continuity and smooth alignment along the length.
  • After fixing, the exposed surfaces of the curb stones shall be cleaned and prepared for painting. One coat of approved wall primer shall be applied, followed by two coats of approved quality oil paint in the specified shade and pattern as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge, ensuring uniform coverage and proper drying between coats. The finished curb stones shall be neat, properly aligned, and free from defects such as cracks, misalignment, or uneven surfaces. The completed work shall be cleaned and handed over in satisfactory condition.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The precast concrete curb stone shall be measured in running meters (Rmt) based on the actual length of curb installed along the alignment, in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include the cost of all materials such as precast curb stones, cement mortar, primer, paint, and all labour, tools, and plants required for excavation, base preparation, fixing, jointing, painting, and finishing.
  • No separate measurement shall be made for excavation, jointing, painting, cutting, wastage, or incidental works, as these are deemed to be included in the item rate. The work shall be measured net as completed and accepted, and the rate shall include all incidental charges required to complete the work as per specifications and as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Running Meter.

  • In case of fittings of unequal bore, the largest bore shall be measured for the test.
  • Testing of pipe lines, fittings and joints included for providing all plant and appliances necessary for obtaining access to the work to be tested and carrying out the tests.
  • The rate includes galvanised steel tubing with screwed socket joints, together with all fittings (such as bends, sockets, springs, elbows, tees, crosses, short pieces, clamps and plug unions etc.) and fixing complete with clamping wall-hooks, wooden plugs etc. and also cutting screwing and waste and for making forged (or hand made) bends on piping as required. The rate also includes cutting through walls, floors etc. and their making good and painting exposed threads with anti-corrosive paint as above and testing. Where tubes are to be fixed to wall, ceiling and flooring, the rates shall not include painting of pipes, providing sleeves and sand filling under floor for which separate payment shall be made.
  • The rate include painting of pipes and sand filling all round tubes for which separate payment shall not be made. The length shall be measured on running metre basis.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one running metre.

Description: Providing   and   laying  broken  china  mosaic   flooring    for terrace using 12 mm to 20 mm  broken pieces of  glazed tiles to be laid over cement mortar 1:3 to plain or slope and  to  be tempered  to  bring   mortar  creme  out upto  surface   using white cement including rounding off junctions and extending   them upto 15 cm along the wall,clearing with water and oxalic acid etc. as directed.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• All materials used for providing and laying broken china mosaic flooring shall conform to relevant Indian Standards and approved specifications. The broken china mosaic shall consist of 12 mm to 20 mm thick pieces of glazed ceramic tiles of approved colour, size, and quality, free from cracks or defects. Cement used shall be Ordinary Portland Cement (OPC) conforming to IS 8112 or IS 12269, and white cement used for finishing shall be of approved make and quality. Fine aggregate (sand) used for mortar shall be clean, well-graded, and free from silt, clay, and organic impurities, conforming to IS 383.
  • Cement mortar shall be prepared in the proportion of 1:3 (one part cement to three parts fine sand) using potable water conforming to IS 456. Oxalic acid used for final cleaning shall be of standard quality. All materials shall be new, of approved quality, and shall be inspected and approved by the Engineer-in-Charge prior to use.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The broken china mosaic flooring shall be laid over the prepared terrace surface, which shall be cleaned, wetted, and brought to the required line, level, or slope as specified. A base layer of cement mortar (1:3) shall be spread evenly to the required thickness, and the broken glazed tile pieces of 12 mm to 20 mm size shall be carefully placed over the mortar bed in a uniform pattern with minimal gaps.
  • The surface shall be properly compacted and tamped to ensure full bedding of the mosaic pieces, and the mortar shall be brought to the surface (creaming) by proper trowelling and tamping. White cement slurry shall be applied to fill the joints and provide a uniform finish. Junctions between the floor and walls shall be neatly rounded and extended up to 15 cm along the wall to form a waterproof skirting.
  • After initial setting, the surface shall be cured adequately and then ground and polished where required to achieve a smooth and even finish. The flooring shall be cleaned thoroughly with water and treated with oxalic acid to remove stains and enhance the finish. Care shall be taken to maintain proper slope for drainage and to avoid undulations or depressions. The finished surface shall be hard, even, non-slippery, and free from cracks or defects, and shall be completed as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The broken china mosaic flooring shall be measured in square meters (m²) based on the actual area laid, including skirting up to 15 cm height, in accordance with IS 1200 Part 13. The rate shall include the cost of all materials such as broken tiles, cement, white cement, sand, oxalic acid, and all labour, tools, and plants required for preparation, laying, curing, finishing, polishing, and cleaning.
  • No separate measurement shall be made for rounding of junctions, skirting up to 15 cm height, curing, polishing, cleaning, or incidental works, as these are deemed to be included in the item rate. The work shall be measured net as completed and accepted, and the rate shall include all incidental charges required to complete the work as per specifications and as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Square Meter.

Description: Providing and laying China Mosaic type water proofing treatment on terrace including (a) Applying neat cement slurry 2.75 Kg./Smt. of cement admix with water proofing compound after cleaning the surface (b)  50 mm thk. Cement Concrete flooring 1:2:4 (1-Cement : 2-Coarse sand : 4-graded stone aggregate 20 mm nominal size) laid in admixed with water proofing compound  including rounding of junctions of walls and slabs (c) after two days of proper curing applying a second coat of cement slurry (d) finishing the surface with 20mm thick cement mortar 1:4 (1 cement : 4 coarse sand) and china mosaic tilling & finally finishing the surface with trowel with white cement slurry (e) after finishing the whole terrace shall be flooded with water for a period of two weeks.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• All materials used for China mosaic waterproofing treatment shall conform to relevant Indian Standards and approved specifications. Cement shall be Ordinary Portland Cement (OPC) 43 or 53 grade conforming to IS 8112 or IS 12269, and shall be fresh and free from lumps. Fine aggregate (coarse sand) shall be clean, well-graded, and free from silt, clay, and organic impurities, conforming to IS 383. Coarse aggregate of 20 mm nominal size shall be hard, durable, and conform to IS 383.
  • Water used for mixing and curing shall be clean and potable, conforming to IS 456. Waterproofing compound shall be of approved make and conform to IS 2645, and shall be used as per manufacturer’s recommendations. Broken china mosaic tiles shall be of approved quality, 12 mm to 20 mm thick, free from defects, and suitable for terrace finishing. White cement used for final finishing shall be of approved make and quality. All materials shall be new, of approved quality, and shall be inspected and approved by the Engineer-in-Charge prior to use.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The terrace surface shall first be thoroughly cleaned of dust, dirt, and loose materials, and properly wetted before application. A coat of neat cement slurry mixed with waterproofing compound at the rate of 2.75 kg of cement per square meter shall be applied uniformly over the prepared surface to ensure proper bonding. Over this, a 50 mm thick layer of cement concrete of mix 1:2:4 using 20 mm nominal size aggregates shall be laid, incorporating approved waterproofing compound, and properly compacted, finished to the required slope for drainage, and ensuring rounding of junctions between slab and walls to prevent water ingress.
  • After a minimum of two days of curing, a second coat of cement slurry mixed with waterproofing compound shall be applied over the concrete surface. Subsequently, a 20 mm thick layer of cement mortar in the proportion of 1:4 shall be laid and finished, over which broken china mosaic tiles shall be evenly placed and embedded, ensuring uniform distribution and proper bonding. The surface shall be finished with white cement slurry and trowelled to achieve a smooth, dense, and aesthetically pleasing finish.
  • Proper curing shall be carried out throughout the process. After completion of the work, the entire terrace shall be ponded with water and kept flooded continuously for a period of two weeks to ensure effective curing and waterproofing performance. The finished surface shall be even, free from cracks, properly sloped for drainage, and fully watertight. All work shall be carried out as per specifications and directions of the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The China mosaic waterproofing treatment shall be measured in square meters (m²) based on the actual area treated on the terrace, in accordance with IS 1200 Part 13. The rate shall include the cost of all materials such as cement, aggregates, waterproofing compound, china mosaic tiles, white cement, and all labour, tools, and plants required for surface preparation, laying, finishing, curing, and water ponding.
  • No separate measurement shall be made for slurry coats, rounding of junctions, curing, water ponding, or incidental works, as these are deemed to be included in the item rate. The work shall be measured net as completed and accepted, and the rate shall include all incidental charges required to complete the work as per specifications and as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Square Meter.

Description: Prov. & laying 50 mm th. I.P.S. flooring in c.c. (1:2:4) using 10 to 20 mm size blact trap metal as an aggregate and finishing the flooring in c.m. (1:2) and pure cement incl. watering, curing, and making chequered impression and laid to proper grade & level etc. comp. as directed.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description: • Water shall conform to M-1. Cement shall conform to M-3. Sand shall conform to M-6. Stone aggregate 20 mm. nominal size shall conform to M-12. Cement concrete of 1:2:4 proportion measured by volume shall conform to relevant specifications of ordinary grade 1:2:4 concrete.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The cement concrete flooring of 50 mm thick (Average) is to be laid as per the site condition. The concrete shall be mixed in a mechanical mixer at the work. Hand mixing may however be allowed for smaller quantities of work and in case of failure of machineries or as permitted by the Engineer-in-charge. It shall be carried out on a water tight platform and care shall be taken to ensure that mixing is continued until the mass is uniform in colour and consistency. However is such cases 10% more cement than otherwise required shall have to be used without any extra cost. The mechanical mixing shall be done for period of 1.1/2 to 2 minutes. The quantity of water shall be just sufficient to produce a dense concrete of required workability for the purpose, Flooring or specified thickness shall be laid in accordance with approved pattern or as directed. Finishing operation   shall  depending   upon  the  temperature and  atmospheric  conditions.  The  surface  shall  be  left  for  some  time  till  moisture  disappears form  it. 
  • Fresh  quantity  of  cement  shall  be  mixed  with  water  to  form  a  thick  slurry  and  spread  over the  surface  while  the  concrete  is  still  green.  Use  of  dry  cement  or  cement  and  sand  mixture sprinkled  on  this  surface  to  stiffen  the  concrete  or  absorb  excessive  moisture  shall  not  be  permitted. The cement slurry shall then be properly pressed twice by means of iron floats, once when the slurry is applied and the second time  when  cement setting and finished floated smooth  The surface  shall  be  marked  with  string  or  B.R.C.  fabric  jali  to  make  the  surface  non-slippery  as  and when directed. The junction of floors with wall plaster, dedo or skirting shall be rounded off where so required up to 25 mm. radius. Flooring in lavatories and bath rooms shall be laid after fixing of water closet and squatting pans and floor traps which shall be plugged while laying the floors and opened after the floors are completed. Any damage done to water supply or sanitary fittings during execution of work shall be made good.
  • After the final set, the concrete shall be kept continuously wet. if required by ponding for a period of not less than 7 days from the date of placement.
  • The form work shall be provided if necessary as directed by Engineer-in-charge. Concreting shall be done as per alternate bay method with necessary centering either by mastic or cement mortar as directed.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The rate shall include the cost of all materials and labour involved in all the operations described above. No deduction shall be made or extra paid for any opening up to 0.1 sq. mt. In area in the floor, nothing extra shall be paid for laying the floor at different levels in the same room or the counter yard.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Square Meter.

Description: Glazed  with Anodised aluminium ( anodised transparent or dyed to required shade according to IS: 1868, Minimum anodic coating of grade AC 15 ) heavy duty extruded built up standard tubular sections/appropriate Z sections and other sections of approved make conforming to IS: 733 and IS : 1285,  fixed with rawl plugs and screws or with fixing clips, or with expansion hold fasts including necessary filling up of gaps at junctions, at top, bottom and sides with required PVC/neoprene felt or sealent of wecker 789 or Dow corning 789 grade so as to make all joints waterproof etc. Aluminium sections shall be smooth, rust free, straight, mitred and jointed mechanically wherever required including cleat angle, aluminium snap beading for glazing / panelling, stainless steel screws as per architectural drawings and the directions of Engineer-in-charge and incl. providing and fixing fully  glazing in aluminium PARTITIONS  with  EDPM gasket  etc. complete as per the architectural  drawings and the directions of engineer-in-charge with 6.0 mm thick plain float glass panel of approved shade,  approved make and size fixed to the frames and frames fixed to the walls. The framed ends shall have required brushings for proper sealing. For Fixed Glazed.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• The aluminium work shall consist of colour anodized aluminium sections of approved make, conforming to relevant Indian Standards such as IS 1868, IS 733, and IS 1285. The anodized coating shall be of minimum grade AC 15, either transparent or dyed to the required shade as approved.
  • The aluminium sections shall be heavy-duty extruded tubular/Z sections, straight, smooth, rust-free, and of approved quality. Glazing shall be done using 6.0 mm thick plain float glass of approved make, shade, and quality. EPDM gaskets, PVC/neoprene felt, aluminium snap beading, stainless steel screws, cleat angles, and other accessories shall be of approved quality and compatible with the system.
  • Sealants such as Dow Corning 789 or equivalent approved silicone sealant shall be used for waterproofing at joints. All fasteners such as rawl plugs, screws, expansion bolts, and fixing clips shall be of corrosion-resistant material and suitable for structural fixing. All materials shall be approved by the Engineer-in-Charge prior to use.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The aluminium partition work shall be executed as per approved architectural drawings and specifications. The aluminium sections shall be cut, fabricated, and assembled accurately using mechanical joints, mitred corners, cleat angles, and snap beading to form a rigid and stable frame.
  • The frames shall be fixed to walls, floors, and ceilings using rawl plugs, screws, fixing clips, or expansion fasteners as required. Proper alignment, level, and plumb shall be maintained during installation. Gaps at junctions, top, bottom, and sides shall be properly filled using PVC/neoprene felt or approved sealant to ensure waterproofing and airtight joints.
  • The 6.0 mm thick float glass panels shall be fixed within the aluminium frame using EPDM gaskets and aluminium snap beading, ensuring firm holding and proper cushioning to avoid direct contact between glass and metal. Care shall be taken to prevent breakage or damage to glass during handling and fixing.
  • All joints shall be sealed properly with approved silicone sealant to prevent water ingress. The finished work shall be neat, clean, properly aligned, and free from distortions, gaps, or visible defects. The work shall be completed strictly as per drawings and to the satisfaction of the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The aluminium fully glazed partition shall be measured in square meters (sqm) of finished glazed surface area, in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include the cost of aluminium sections, glass panels, EPDM gaskets, sealants, fasteners, fixing accessories, labour, fabrication, installation, and all incidental works required for completion.
  • No separate measurement shall be made for aluminium sections, glazing, sealants, gaskets, fixing hardware, cutting, wastage, or minor consumables, as these are deemed to be included in the item rate. Openings shall be deducted as per standard measurement rules. The work shall be measured as completed and accepted, and payment shall be made based on the actual installed area as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of One Square Meter.

Description: Providing and laying rough chiseled dressed stone flooring over 20mm thick base of cement mortar 1:5 (1-Cement : 5-coarse sand) or L.M. 1:1.5 including pointing with cement mortar 1:2 (1-cement : 2-stone dust) etc. complete. (B) 40mm thick

sections.title: Materials
sections.description: • Water shall conform to M-1. Lime mortar shall conform to M-10. Cement mortar shall conform to M-11 Polished kota stone shall conform to M-49.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• Each slab shall be cut to the required size and shape and fine chisel dressed at all the edges. The sides trust dressed shall have a full contract if a straight edge is laid along. The sides shall be table rubbed with coarse sand before paving. All angles and edges of the slabs shall be true square and free from chippings and giving a plane surface. The thickness shall be 25 mm. (Average) as specified in the item but not less than 20 mm. at any place of the slab.
  • Bedding  for  the  Kota  stone  slabs  shall  be  of  cement  mortar  1:6  (1  cement  :  6  coarse  sand)  or L.M.  1:1.5  of  average  thickness  20  mm  given  in  the  description  of  the  item.  Sub  grade  shall be  cleaned,  wetted  and  mopped  Mortar  of  the  specified  mix  and  thickness  shall  then  be  spread  on an  area  sufficient  to  receive  one  kota  stone  slab.  The  slab  shall  be  washed  clean  before  laying.  It shall  be  laid  on  top,  pressed,  tapped  gently  to  bring  it  in  level  with  the  other  slabs.  If  shall then  be  lifted  and  laid  aside.  Top  surface  of  the  mortar  shall  then  be  corrected  by  adding fresh  mortar  at  hollows  or  depressions.  The  mortar  shall  then  be  allowed  to  harden  bit. Over  this  surface,  cement  slurry  of  honey-like  consistency  shall  be  applied.  The  slab  shall  then  be gently placed in position and tapped with wooden mallet till it is properly padded in level with and close to the adjoining slab. The joint shall be as fine as possible. The slabs fixed in the floor adjoining, the walls shall enter not less than 10 mm. under the plaster, skirting or dedo. The junction between the wan and floor shall be finished neatly. The finished surface shall be true to levels and slopes as directed.
  • The floor shall be kept wet for a minimum period of 7 days so that bedding and joints set properly.
  • Polishing shall be normally commenced after 14 days of laying the stone slab. First polishing shah be done with carborundum stones of 120 grade grit fitted in the heavy machine and then second polishing shall be done with carborundum stone of 220 to 350 grade grit fitted in heavy machine. Water shall be properly used during polishing. The stone shall then be washed clean with water When directed by the Engineer-in-charge, wax polish of approved quality shall be applied on the surface with the help of soft cloth over a clean and dry surface. Then the polishing machine fitted with bobs shall be run over it.
  • The holes required for Nahni traps, pipes and any other fittings shall be made, without any extra cost.
  • The surplus cement grout that may have come out of the joints shall be cleaned off before it sets. Once the floor has set, it shall be carefully washed, cleared by dilute acid and dried. Proper precautions and measures shall be taken to ensure that the tiles are not damaged in any way till the completion of the construction.
  • The Above Specifications shall be followed except that the kota stout-fixed for risers of steps, dedo or skirting in C.M. 1:3 and the polishing shall be done manually instead of machine polishing.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The risers of steps, skirting or dedo shall be measured in sq. meter Length shall be measured along the finished faces of risers, skirting or dedo. Height shall be measured from finished level of treads of floor to top. Lining of pillars shall be measured under this item.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Square Meter.

Description: Providing & Fixing 52 mm thick light weight cement sheet partition wall panel having internal interlocking design incl. fixing GI channel at bottom and top, fixing on existing vitrified tiles or on RCC surface, weight of each 3 ft X 10 ft wall shall not be less than 60 kg. Comp. as per detailed drawing & directed by Engg. In Charge.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• The partition panels shall be 52 mm thick lightweight cement sheet panels of approved make, having internal interlocking design for proper alignment and structural stability. Each panel of size approximately 3 ft × 10 ft shall have a minimum weight of 60 kg and shall be manufactured from high-quality cementitious material reinforced with suitable fibers to provide strength, durability, and resistance to moisture.
  • GI channels used for top and bottom fixing shall be of approved quality, corrosion-resistant, and conforming to relevant standards such as IS 277. Fasteners, screws, anchors, and adhesives shall be of approved make and suitable for fixing on RCC surfaces or vitrified tile surfaces. All materials shall be new, free from defects, and approved by the Engineer-in-Charge prior to use.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall include supplying and fixing of 52 mm thick lightweight cement sheet partition wall panels as per approved drawings and specifications. The work shall involve fixing of GI channels at the bottom and top of the partition line over RCC surface or existing vitrified tile flooring, ensuring proper alignment, level, and rigidity.
  • Cutting of panels, where necessary, shall be done carefully using appropriate tools to achieve required dimensions without damaging the material. Joints between panels shall be finished neatly to provide a uniform appearance. The installation shall ensure stability, strength, and durability of the partition wall.
  • The railing shall be properly tightened and fixed to floor mounts or supporting structures using suitable fasteners. Welding joints shall be smooth, finished, and free from defects. Care shall be taken to maintain proper alignment, level, and aesthetic appearance of the railing system.
  • All work shall be executed in a neat and professional manner without causing damage to existing flooring or surrounding finishes. The completed partition shall be rigid, properly aligned, and in accordance with the directions of the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The partition wall shall be measured in square meters (sqm) of the finished surface area of the installed panels, in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include the cost of panels, GI channels, fasteners, adhesives, labour, cutting, fixing, and all incidental works required for proper installation.
  • No separate measurement shall be made for GI channels, joints, cutting, wastage, or minor consumables, as these are deemed to be included in the item rate. Openings, if any, shall be deducted as per standard measurement practices. The work shall be measured as completed and accepted, and payment shall be made based on the actual installed area as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of One Square Meter.

Description: Repairing & refixing S.S. Pipe railing wherever needed in 3 rows supported by S.S. pipe using required all types of necessary equipments like handrail connection, crossbar ball, hook, bolt and floor mount etc incl. cutting, jointing, welding, threading, drilling & fixing etc. comp. as directed as per directed by engg. in charge.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description: • The materials required for repairing and refixing of stainless steel railing shall be of approved quality and compatible with the existing installation. Stainless steel pipes, fittings, connectors, handrail joints, crossbar balls, hooks, bolts, floor mounts, and other accessories shall be of suitable grade (preferably SS 304 or equivalent) and conform to relevant standards such as IS 6911. Welding consumables, fasteners, and fixing accessories shall be of corrosion-resistant quality and suitable for structural and architectural applications. All materials shall be new or reused components in good condition, subject to approval of the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall include repairing, adjusting, and refixing of existing stainless steel pipe railing wherever required in 3 rows supported by stainless steel vertical posts. The contractor shall carefully inspect the existing railing, identify damaged, loose, or misaligned components, and carry out necessary rectification.
  • The work shall include cutting, jointing, welding, threading, drilling, and fixing of pipes and accessories using appropriate tools and equipment. All joints shall be properly aligned and securely fixed to ensure stability, rigidity, and smooth finish. Damaged fittings such as handrail connectors, bolts, hooks, or mounts shall be repaired or replaced as necessary.
  • The railing shall be properly tightened and fixed to floor mounts or supporting structures using suitable fasteners. Welding joints shall be smooth, finished, and free from defects. Care shall be taken to maintain proper alignment, level, and aesthetic appearance of the railing system.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The repairing and refixing of stainless steel pipe railing shall be measured on a running meter (Rmt) as specified in the BOQ, in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include the cost of labour, tools, welding, cutting, drilling, threading, and all incidental materials required for repair and refixing.
  • No separate measurement shall be made for minor fittings, consumables, or incidental works, as these are deemed to be included in the item rate. Replacement of major components, if any, shall be measured separately if specified. The work shall be measured as completed and accepted, and payment shall be made as per actual executed quantity under the direction of the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of One Running Meter.
