Description: Providing and laying white glazed tiles 6mm thick in flooring treads of steps and landing laid on a bed of 12mm thick cement mortar 1:3 (1-cement : 3-coarse sand ) finishing with flush pointing in white cement.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description: • Water shall conform to M-1 Cement mortar shall conform to.M-11 White glazed tiles shall conform to M-55.

subsections.title: Preparation of Surface
subsections.description: • In case of brick masonry wall, the joints shall be raked out to a depth of least 15 mm. while the masonry is being laid. In case of concrete wall the surface shall be chiseled and roughed with wire brushes. The surface shall be cleaned and wetted thoroughly before commencing the laying work.

subsections.title: Laying
subsections.description:
• The wall surface shall be covered with 10 mm. thick plaster of cement mortar 1:3 mix and allowed to harden. The plaster shall be roughened with wire brushes both way. The back of tiles shall be floated with grey cement slurry set and edges with white cement slurry in bedding mortar. The tiles shall be gently tapped in position on after the other keeping the joints as thin as possible. Top of skirting or dedo shall be truly horizontal and the joints vertical or as per required pattern.
  • Risers of steps, skirting and dedo shall rest on top of treads or flooring. Where full size tiles cannot be fixed, They shall be cut to the required size and the edges be smoothened.
  • The joints shall be cleaned and flush pointed with white cement. The surface shall be kept wet for seven days. After curing the surface shall be washed clean.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The rate shall include the cost of all materials and labour required for various operations described above. Risers of steps: skirting and dedo shall be measured in square meters, length and height shall be measured along the finished face of the skirting or dedo including curves, where special such as covers. internal and external angles, etc., used. The length and height shall be measured correct lo the centimeter except in case of risers and skirting where height shall be measured correct to 3 mm.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Square Meter.

Description: Supplying of Water Tanker Having 5000 Ltr. Capacity as per directed by engg. Incharge.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description: • The water tanker shall have a minimum capacity of 5000 litres and shall be mounted on a suitable vehicle chassis in good working condition. The tank shall be fabricated from approved quality materials such as MS/HDPE, designed to safely carry potable or construction water without leakage or contamination. The tanker shall be fitted with proper inlet and outlet arrangements, valves, hoses, and pumping arrangements if required. All fittings and accessories shall be of approved quality and corrosion-resistant. The tanker and associated components shall comply with applicable transport and safety regulations. Water used shall be clean and suitable for construction purposes, conforming generally to IS 456.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall include supplying and deploying a water tanker of 5000 litre capacity at site as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge. The tanker shall be used for transporting and supplying water for construction activities such as curing, mixing, cleaning, dust suppression, or any other site requirements.
  • The tanker shall be maintained in good working condition throughout the period of deployment, with proper functioning valves, hoses, and fittings to ensure smooth discharge of water. The operation shall be carried out by a skilled driver/operator, ensuring safe driving and handling during loading, transportation, and unloading of water.
  • The tanker shall be positioned at designated locations as per site requirements, and water shall be supplied in a controlled manner without wastage or spillage. Care shall be taken to avoid contamination of water and surrounding areas. All operations shall be carried out safely and efficiently as per the instructions of the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The supplying of water tanker shall be measured on a per nos basis as specified in the BOQ, for a minimum capacity of 5000 litres, in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include the cost of the tanker, vehicle, driver/operator, fuel, maintenance, loading, transportation, and unloading of water.
  • No separate measurement shall be made for fuel, driver charges, minor maintenance, or incidental works, as these are deemed to be included in the item rate. The work shall be measured as completed and accepted, and payment shall be made based on the number of days or trips as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of One Nos.

Description: Construction of Sandwitch type benches for passenger sitting arrangement. Constructing the Brick Masonary pillars 23 cms. X 35 cms X 35 cms size of 2 nos. for support and fininshing with 15 mm th. Cement Plaster in C.M. (1:3)  incl. finishing with neat cement slurry and laying sandwitch type plateform with using bottom 25 mm th. single piece polished kotah stone & top mede with 25 mm th. green marble stone of size 1.20 mtr. & 0.45 mtr. without any joint fixing both the stone with C.M. (1:1) incl. rubbing, polishing & rounding the edge of stone and applying two coats of approved quality distemper exposed face of brick pillars etc. comp. as per detail design & drawing. etc. comp. as directed.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• All materials used for construction of sandwich type benches shall conform to relevant Indian Standards and approved specifications. Brick masonry for supporting pillars shall be constructed using first-class burnt clay bricks conforming to IS 1077, having adequate strength and uniform shape, free from cracks and defects. Cement used shall be Ordinary Portland Cement (OPC) conforming to IS 8112 or IS 12269, and sand shall be clean, well-graded, and conform to IS 383.
  • Plaster shall be 15 mm thick cement plaster in cement mortar 1:3, finished with neat cement slurry. The seating platform shall consist of a sandwich construction with bottom layer of 25 mm thick single-piece polished Kota stone and top layer of 25 mm thick green marble stone of size approximately 1.20 m × 0.45 m, both slabs being of approved quality, free from cracks, veins, or defects, and machine cut to accurate dimensions, conforming to IS 1597 Part 1. Cement mortar (1:1) shall be used for fixing the stone slabs. Distemper used for finishing exposed faces of brick pillars shall be of approved quality and shade. All materials shall be new, of approved make, and shall be inspected and approved by the Engineer-in-Charge prior to use.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The sandwich type bench shall be constructed in accordance with approved drawings and design. Brick masonry pillars of size 23 cm × 35 cm × 35 cm shall be built in proper line, level, and plumb, ensuring adequate strength and stability. The masonry shall be properly cured before plastering. A 15 mm thick cement plaster in cement mortar 1:3 shall be applied on all exposed surfaces of the pillars and finished smoothly with neat cement slurry.
  • The seating platform shall be constructed by first placing the 25 mm thick polished Kota stone slab as the base layer over the prepared supports. Over this, the 25 mm thick green marble slab shall be fixed using cement mortar (1:1), ensuring proper bonding and full contact between layers. The slabs shall be laid without joints (single-piece), properly aligned, and levelled to achieve a smooth seating surface.
  • Edges of the stone slabs shall be neatly rounded and polished to provide a safe and aesthetic finish. Rubbing and polishing shall be carried out to achieve a smooth, glossy surface free from scratches or defects. The exposed plastered surfaces of brick pillars shall be finished with two coats of approved quality distemper in the specified shade. Proper curing shall be carried out for masonry, plaster, and stone work. The completed bench shall be sturdy, level, and aesthetically finished, and shall comply with all specifications and directions of the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The sandwich type bench shall be measured on a per number (Each) basis, in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include the cost of all materials such as bricks, cement, sand, plaster, Kota stone, marble stone, distemper, and all labour, tools, and plants required for masonry, plastering, stone fixing, polishing, painting, and finishing.
  • No separate measurement shall be made for individual components such as pillars, plaster, stone slabs, polishing, rounding edges, or painting, as these are deemed to be included in the item rate. The work shall be measured as completed and accepted, and the rate shall include all incidental charges such as cutting, wastage, curing, transportation, and finishing required to complete the work as per specifications and as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Nos.

Description: Hire Charges For carpentor with one Helper for minor Carpentory works for Wooden chair polishing, drawer repairing with lock change with other type of misc. work for 8 hr. per day comp. as directed by eng. Incharge.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description: • The item mainly involves labour; however, minor consumables and materials required for execution of carpentry work shall be included. These may consist of sandpaper, polish, varnish, adhesives, screws, nails, hinges, locks, and small fittings required for repair and maintenance works. Replacement hardware such as locks or handles shall be of approved quality and compatible with existing furniture. All materials shall be of good quality and approved by the Engineer-in-Charge prior to use. Hand tools such as hammers, saws, chisels, screwdrivers, drills, and polishing tools shall be in good working condition.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall include providing a skilled carpenter along with one helper for carrying out minor carpentry works such as polishing of wooden chairs, repairing of drawers, replacement or fixing of locks, and other miscellaneous carpentry maintenance works as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge. The carpenter shall be experienced and capable of performing work neatly and efficiently.
  • The carpenter with helper shall work for a minimum of 8 hours per day and shall carry out the assigned tasks systematically. Furniture and fixtures shall be handled carefully to avoid damage. Repairs shall be carried out by removing defective parts and fixing or replacing them properly to restore functionality. Polishing work shall be done evenly to achieve a smooth and uniform finish.
  • All fittings such as locks, hinges, and handles shall be properly aligned and securely fixed. The work area shall be kept clean during and after execution. Care shall be taken to minimize disturbance to surroundings. The completed work shall be neat, functional, and satisfactory as per directions of the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The hire charges for carpenter with one helper shall be measured on a per day basis (minimum 8 working hours per day), in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include the cost of carpenter, helper, minor tools, and consumables required for execution of the work.
  • No separate measurement shall be made for tools, minor materials, or incidental works, as these are deemed to be included in the item rate. Major replacement items such as new locks or fittings, if required, shall be measured and paid separately. The work shall be measured as completed and accepted, and payment shall be made based on the number of days engaged as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of One Day.

Description: • Providing & Laying of Granite top & Bottom sandwich type sitting benches in concourse area as per desigh and drawings of 1.80 mts long & 0.90 mts wide sandwich type (both side granite 18 mm thick) including vertical support of three nos of sandwitch type granite shall be finished with quarter round moulding and mirrior polished etc complete as directed with 50 mm S.S. pipe fitting for Back support in Granite design As per given By Architect.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• All materials used for providing and laying granite sandwich type sitting benches shall conform to relevant Indian Standards and approved specifications. The bench shall consist of granite slabs of 18 mm thickness on both top and bottom faces, forming a sandwich structure, using high-quality natural stone conforming to IS 1597 Part 1. The granite shall be of approved colour and shade, free from cracks, veins, or defects, and shall be machine cut to required dimensions of approximately 1.80 m length and 0.90 m width.
  • Vertical supports shall consist of three numbers of sandwich type granite panels of similar specification and thickness, properly finished and structurally adequate to support the bench. Cement mortar or suitable adhesive shall be used for fixing granite slabs, ensuring proper bonding. Stainless steel (S.S.) pipes of 50 mm diameter shall be provided for back support, made from corrosion-resistant material conforming to IS 6911. All fittings, fasteners, and accessories shall be of stainless steel and of approved quality. The granite edges shall be finished with quarter round moulding and mirror polishing. All materials shall be new, of approved quality, and shall be inspected and approved by the Engineer-in-Charge prior to use.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The granite sandwich type bench shall be fabricated and installed in accordance with approved architectural drawings and design. The granite slabs shall be accurately cut, dressed, and assembled to form a sandwich structure with proper alignment and bonding between top and bottom layers. The vertical supports shall be constructed using three granite panels placed at appropriate locations to ensure stability and load-bearing capacity.
  • The granite slabs shall be fixed using suitable mortar or adhesive, ensuring full contact and proper bonding without voids. All joints shall be neatly finished, and the exposed edges shall be shaped with quarter round moulding and mirror polished to achieve a smooth and aesthetic finish. Care shall be taken during handling and installation to prevent chipping or damage to the granite surfaces.
  • The 50 mm diameter stainless steel pipe back support shall be properly fabricated, aligned, and securely fixed into the granite structure using suitable anchoring methods, ensuring stability and durability. All joints and connections shall be properly finished, and sharp edges shall be avoided.
  • The completed bench shall be true to line, level, and dimensions, with a smooth, polished surface free from defects. Proper cleaning shall be carried out after installation. The bench shall be sturdy, stable, and aesthetically finished, and all work shall be completed as per specifications and directions of the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The granite sandwich type sitting bench shall be measured on a per number (Each) basis, in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include the cost of all materials such as granite slabs, vertical supports, stainless steel pipes, fittings, fasteners, adhesives or mortar, and all labour, tools, and plants required for cutting, fixing, polishing, and finishing.
  • No separate measurement shall be made for moulding, polishing, vertical supports, stainless steel back support, or incidental works, as these are deemed to be included in the item rate. The work shall be measured as completed and accepted, and the rate shall include all incidental charges such as cutting, wastage, transportation, lifting, and finishing required to complete the work as per specifications and as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Nos.

Description: Hire charges for Mason with one helper for any type of construction work incl necessary equipment for construction work For min. 8 hr/day at all floors.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description: • The item primarily involves labour; however, minor tools and consumables required for execution of work shall be included. These include hand tools such as trowels, floats, plumb bob, spirit level, measuring tape, pans, buckets, and other necessary equipment required for masonry and general construction work. Any small consumables such as binding wire, nails, or minor accessories required for proper execution shall be included. All tools and equipment shall be in good working condition and suitable for construction activities, and shall be approved by the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall include providing skilled mason along with one helper for carrying out various types of construction activities such as masonry work, plastering, minor repairs, finishing works, and other related civil works as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge. The mason shall be skilled and experienced, capable of executing work accurately as per standard construction practices.
  • The mason with helper shall work for a minimum of 8 hours per day and shall carry out the assigned tasks efficiently and systematically. The helper shall assist in material handling, mixing, and other supporting activities to ensure smooth execution of work. All work shall be executed in proper line, level, and alignment, maintaining required quality and workmanship standards.
  • Care shall be taken to avoid wastage of materials and damage to existing structures or finishes. The work area shall be kept clean during and after execution. All safety precautions shall be followed during working at all floors, including proper handling of tools and materials. The completed work shall be as per specifications and to the satisfaction of the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The hire charges for mason with one helper shall be measured on a per day basis (minimum 8 working hours per day), in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include the cost of mason, helper, minor tools, and all incidental charges required for execution of the work at all floor levels.
  • No separate measurement shall be made for tools, minor consumables, or work at different heights/floors, as these are deemed to be included in the item rate. The work shall be measured as completed and accepted, and payment shall be made based on the number of days and units deployed as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of One Day.

Description: Hire Charges labour for removing and filling all type of Debric incl. construction waste materials and cleaning or any other type work for 9 hr. per day comp. as directed by eng. Incharge.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description: • The item mainly involves provision of labour; however, minor tools and consumables required for execution of work shall be included. These include hand tools such as spades, shovels, baskets, wheelbarrows, brooms, and other necessary equipment for handling and shifting debris. Safety gear such as gloves, masks, and protective equipment shall be provided to labour as required. No major construction materials are involved in this item. All tools and accessories shall be in good working condition and approved by the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall include deployment of labour for carrying out removal, collection, loading, shifting, and filling of all types of debris including construction waste, dust, loose earth, and unwanted materials from the site. The labour shall also perform general cleaning of the site, sweeping, and any other miscellaneous works as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The labourers shall work for a duration of 9 hours per day and shall execute the work efficiently and systematically to maintain cleanliness and proper site conditions. Debris shall be collected, stacked, and disposed of or filled in designated areas within the site or as instructed. Care shall be taken to avoid damage to existing structures, finishes, or services during the work.
  • All operations shall be carried out using proper tools and methods, and safety precautions shall be followed during handling and disposal of materials. The site shall be left clean and free from debris after completion of work. The work shall be carried out to the satisfaction of the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The hire charges for labour shall be measured on a per day basis (9 working hours per day) per labour, in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include the cost of labour, minor tools, safety equipment, and all incidental charges required for execution of the work.
  • No separate measurement shall be made for tools, minor consumables, or incidental works, as these are deemed to be included in the item rate. The work shall be measured as completed and accepted, and payment shall be made based on the number of labourers and days engaged as per directions of the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of One Day.

Description: Hire charges for plumber and one helper to stop leakage from water supply line, water cooler, wash basin, water tap, flush tank, etc incl removing and refiixng necessary parts  in water supply lines and fixing the same with necessary taproll / adhesive and make the line and connections leakproof.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description: • The work mainly involves labour; however, minor consumable materials required for repair shall be of approved quality. These include Teflon tape (thread seal tape), PVC solvent cement, rubber washers, gaskets, adhesives, and small fittings required for making joints leakproof. Replacement of minor parts such as nipples, connectors, or small pipe sections, if required, shall be of approved make and conform to relevant standards such as IS 4985 or IS 1239 depending on the existing system. All materials shall be new, compatible with the existing installation, and approved by the Engineer-in-Charge prior to use.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall include attending to leakage problems in water supply systems such as pipelines, water coolers, wash basins, taps, flush tanks, and other plumbing fixtures. The plumber, along with a helper, shall identify the source of leakage and carry out necessary repairs by dismantling defective components carefully without causing damage to existing fittings.
  • Required parts shall be removed and refixed or replaced as necessary, ensuring proper alignment and jointing. All joints shall be sealed using appropriate materials such as Teflon tape, adhesives, or solvent cement to make them completely leakproof. Care shall be taken to ensure proper tightening without damaging threads or fittings.
  • After completion of repairs, the system shall be tested by running water to check for any leakage. Any defects noticed during testing shall be rectified immediately. The work shall be carried out neatly, ensuring no damage to surrounding finishes, and the area shall be cleaned after completion. The entire system shall be restored to proper working condition as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The hire charges for plumber with one helper shall be measured on a per day or per hour basis, as specified in the BOQ, in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include the cost of labour (plumber and helper), minor consumables such as Teflon tape, adhesives, and small fittings, and all tools required for carrying out the repair work.
  • No separate measurement shall be made for minor materials, tools, travel within site, or incidental works, as these are deemed to be included in the item rate. Major replacement items, if any, shall be measured and paid separately. The work shall be measured as completed and accepted, and the rate shall include all incidental charges required to complete the work as per specifications and as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of One Day.

Description: Hire Charges for front blade tractor for grass cutting incl. removing the surplus stuff, cutting the hips and levelling the ground and filling the same in low laying area incl. all lead and lift etc. comp. as directed.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description: • The front blade tractor (dozer-type attachment) shall be in good working condition, fitted with suitable blade arrangement for cutting grass, removing surface vegetation, trimming humps, and leveling the ground. Fuel (diesel), lubricants, and other operational consumables required for functioning of the equipment shall be included in the item. Any minor tools or accessories required for operation shall be of approved quality. The equipment shall comply with safety standards and shall be approved by the Engineer-in-Charge prior to deployment.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall include cutting of grass and vegetation over the specified area using a front blade tractor, followed by removal of surplus grass, roots, and waste material. The tractor shall also be used for cutting humps, trimming uneven surfaces, and leveling the ground to the required profile.
  • The excavated or removed material shall be transported within the site and used for filling low-lying areas, ensuring proper spreading and leveling. The operation shall be carried out systematically to achieve a uniform and even ground surface. Care shall be taken to avoid damage to existing structures, utilities, or surrounding areas during operation.
  • The equipment shall be operated by skilled personnel, and all safety precautions shall be followed. The finished surface shall be properly leveled, free from unwanted vegetation, and in a neat condition. The work shall be completed efficiently and as per directions of the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The hire charges for front blade tractor shall be measured on a per hour depending on the BOQ conditions, in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include the cost of machinery, fuel (diesel), operator, and all labour, tools, and plants required for grass cutting, removal, leveling, and filling operations.
  • No separate measurement shall be made for fuel consumption, minor tools, shifting within site, or incidental works, as these are deemed to be included in the item rate. The work shall be measured as completed and accepted, and the rate shall include all incidental charges required to complete the work as per specifications and as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of One Per Hour.

Description: Hire charges of tractor with trolly For removing durt, dust, debris of construction materials and threwing away from the premises  incl. transportation with loading unloading and charges for disel incl. all lead and lift etc comp. as directed by engg. Incharge. (C) Min. Lead 15 km. or Above

sections.title: Materials
sections.description: • The tractor with trolley shall be in good working condition, suitable for transportation of construction debris such as dirt, dust, and waste materials. The trolley shall be of adequate capacity, structurally sound, and free from leakage or defects. Fuel (diesel), lubricants, and all operational consumables required for the functioning of the tractor shall be included in the item. All equipment shall comply with applicable safety and transport regulations and shall be approved by the Engineer-in-Charge prior to deployment.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall include loading, transportation, unloading, and disposal of construction debris such as dirt, dust, and waste materials from the site to approved dumping locations within a lead of up to 5 km. Loading shall be carried out manually or mechanically as required, ensuring proper handling and avoiding spillage. The tractor with trolley shall transport the debris safely without causing inconvenience or hazard to traffic and surroundings
  • Unloading shall be done at designated disposal areas as per local authority regulations. Care shall be taken to maintain cleanliness of the site and approach roads during operation. The contractor shall ensure that the equipment is properly maintained and operated by skilled personnel. All safety precautions shall be followed during loading, transportation, and unloading operations. The work shall be executed efficiently and completed as per directions of the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The hire charges of tractor with trolley shall be measured on a per trip basis as specified in the BOQ, considering a Min. lead of 15 km or Above, in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include the cost of tractor with trolley, fuel (diesel), driver, loading and unloading charges, transportation, and all labour, tools, and plants required for execution of the work.
  • No separate measurement shall be made for fuel consumption, loading, unloading, minor delays, or incidental works, as these are deemed to be included in the item rate. The work shall be measured as completed and accepted, and the rate shall include all incidental charges required to complete the work as per specifications and as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of One Per Trip.

Description: Providing 4 legged S.S. benches of grade 304 of size 1.25×0.51×0.45m with S.S. pipe of size 2''×1'' and not less than 18 guage with two vertical supports of S.S. pipe & 3 horizontal supports of pipe with both side welding & fixing with american nuts on existing flooring using the base plate of size 500×100×10mm etc. comp. as directed.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• All materials used for providing and fixing 4-legged stainless steel benches shall conform to relevant Indian Standards and approved specifications. The bench shall be fabricated from stainless steel of Grade 304, conforming to IS 6911, ensuring high corrosion resistance and durability. The structural members shall consist of S.S. pipes of size 2" × 1" (rectangular section) with thickness not less than 18 gauge, free from dents, cracks, or surface defects.
  • The bench shall be of overall size approximately 1.25 m × 0.51 m × 0.45 m, comprising four legs with two vertical supports and three horizontal supports made of S.S. pipes. Base plates shall be of size 500 mm × 100 mm × 10 mm, made of stainless steel or suitable steel with protective finish, used for anchoring the bench to the flooring. Fasteners such as American nuts, bolts, and screws shall be of stainless steel and of approved quality. All materials shall be new, of approved make, and shall be inspected and approved by the Engineer-in-Charge prior to use.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The stainless steel bench shall be fabricated and installed in accordance with approved drawings and specifications. The S.S. pipes shall be accurately cut, aligned, and assembled to form a rigid and stable structure consisting of four legs, two vertical supports, and three horizontal supports. All joints shall be properly welded on both sides to ensure strength and durability, and welds shall be ground smooth and finished neatly without sharp edges or visible defects.
  • The base plates shall be securely welded to the legs and fixed to the existing flooring using appropriate fasteners such as American nuts and bolts, ensuring firm anchorage and stability. Proper alignment and levelling shall be maintained during installation to ensure that the bench is stable and does not wobble.
  • Care shall be taken during fabrication and installation to avoid scratches, dents, or damage to the stainless steel surface. The finished surface shall be smooth and, where required, polished to a uniform finish. All edges shall be rounded or finished properly for safety. The completed bench shall be sturdy, properly aligned, and free from defects, and shall be cleaned and handed over in perfect condition as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The stainless steel bench shall be measured on a per number (Each) basis, in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include the cost of all materials such as stainless steel pipes, base plates, fasteners, and all labour, tools, and plants required for cutting, welding, fabrication, fixing, and finishing.
  • No separate measurement shall be made for welding, polishing, base plates, fasteners, or incidental works, as these are deemed to be included in the item rate. The work shall be measured as completed and accepted, and the rate shall include all incidental charges such as transportation, lifting, and finishing required to complete the work as per specifications and as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Nos.

Description: Cleaning of Septic Tank of minimum depth 4.00 Meter with necessary Equipments such as vaccum and jeter mashine including cost of all materials as directed by the Engineer in Charge.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description: • The work of septic tank cleaning does not involve major permanent materials; however, all consumables and equipment used shall be of approved quality and suitable for the purpose. Cleaning shall be carried out using mechanized equipment such as vacuum suction machines and high-pressure jetting machines of adequate capacity. Disinfectants, deodorizing agents, and safety gear such as gloves, masks, boots, and protective clothing shall be used as required and shall be of approved quality. Water used for jetting and cleaning shall be clean and suitable for the purpose, conforming broadly to IS 456. All equipment and materials shall comply with safety and environmental regulations and shall be approved by the Engineer-in-Charge prior to use.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The septic tank cleaning shall be carried out using mechanized methods without manual handling of sewage, ensuring safety and hygiene. The tank shall be opened carefully, and sludge, scum, and wastewater shall be removed using vacuum suction equipment. High-pressure jetting machines shall be used to clean the inner walls, floor, and inlet/outlet pipes thoroughly, removing all deposits, blockages, and accumulated waste.
  • All operations shall be carried out with proper safety precautions, ensuring no direct human contact with sewage, and workers shall use appropriate protective equipment. Care shall be taken to avoid damage to the septic tank structure, pipes, and fittings during cleaning. The removed waste shall be transported and disposed of at approved disposal locations in accordance with local municipal and environmental regulations.
  • After cleaning, the tank shall be inspected to ensure complete removal of sludge and proper functioning of inlet and outlet systems. The site shall be cleaned, disinfected, and restored to hygienic condition. The work shall be executed efficiently, safely, and as per directions of the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The septic tank cleaning shall be measured on a per SQmt basis for tanks of specified minimum depth (4.0 m or as mentioned), in accordance with IS 1200. Alternatively, measurement may be based on capacity (kilolitres) if specified.
  • The rate shall include the cost of all labour, equipment such as vacuum and jetting machines, consumables, safety measures, transportation, and disposal of waste. No separate measurement shall be made for opening/closing covers, safety arrangements, water, or incidental works, as these are deemed to be included in the item rate. The work shall be measured as completed and accepted, and the rate shall include all incidental charges required to complete the work safely and hygienically as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge..
  • The rate shall be for a unit of One Square Meter.

Description: Finishing wall with weather proof exterior emulsion paint on wall surface (two coats) to give an required shape even shade after thoroughly brushing the surface to remove all dirt, and remains of loose powdered materials.etc complete

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• All materials used for finishing external wall surfaces shall be of approved quality and conform to relevant Indian Standards. The exterior emulsion paint shall be weather proof type, suitable for exterior applications, resistant to sunlight, rain, and atmospheric conditions, conforming to IS 15489. The paint shall be of approved make, colour, and shade, providing durable and uniform finish.
  • The surface preparation materials such as primers (if required), putty, and cleaning tools shall be of approved quality. Water used for dilution and surface cleaning shall be clean and free from impurities, conforming to IS 456. All materials shall be new, properly stored, and approved by the Engineer-in-Charge prior to use.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The wall surface shall be thoroughly prepared before application of paint. All dust, dirt, grease, loose particles, and flaky materials shall be removed by brushing, scraping, or other approved methods to obtain a clean and sound surface. Any minor surface defects such as cracks or undulations shall be rectified using suitable putty or filler to achieve a smooth base.
  • After proper surface preparation, the exterior emulsion paint shall be applied in two coats using brush, roller, or spray as per manufacturer’s recommendations. Each coat shall be applied uniformly to achieve an even shade and smooth finish, and sufficient time shall be allowed for drying between coats. Care shall be taken to avoid streaks, patches, or brush marks.
  • The painting shall be carried out under suitable weather conditions, avoiding application during rain or extreme temperatures. Adjacent surfaces shall be protected from paint splashes. The finished surface shall be uniform in colour, free from defects, and properly finished to the required appearance. The work shall be completed neatly and as per directions of the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The exterior emulsion painting shall be measured in square meters (m²) based on the actual area of wall surface painted, in accordance with IS 1200 Part 13. The rate shall include the cost of all materials such as paint, primer (if used), putty, and all labour, tools, and plants required for surface preparation, application, and finishing.
  • No separate measurement shall be made for surface cleaning, minor repairs, scaffolding, or incidental works, as these are deemed to be included in the item rate. The work shall be measured net as completed and accepted, and the rate shall include all incidental charges required to complete the work as per specifications and as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Square Meter.

Description: Removing submercible pump with motor, Cable, Column Pipe etc. from bore incl. using necessary equipment like tripod, chain pully etc. incl. reinstalling the same in bore with taking due care etc. comp. as directed

sections.title: Materials
sections.description: • All materials involved in the work shall be those already installed, including submersible pump, motor, column pipes, cables, and accessories. Any minor consumables required such as jointing materials, insulation tape, gaskets, nuts, bolts, and clamps shall be of approved quality and suitable for the system. Electrical cables, if required to be reused or replaced partially, shall conform to relevant standards such as IS 694. All replacement materials, if any, shall be new, free from defects, and approved by the Engineer-in-Charge prior to use.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall include careful dismantling and removal of the existing submersible pump set along with motor, column pipes, cables, and all accessories from the borewell using appropriate equipment such as tripod, chain pulley block, clamps, and lifting tools. Proper precautions shall be taken during dismantling to avoid damage to the pump, pipes, cables, and borewell casing.
  • .All components shall be handled carefully and inspected during removal for any damage or wear. After removal, the pump set shall be reinstalled in the same borewell in proper sequence. Column pipes shall be reconnected securely with proper alignment, ensuring leak-proof joints. Electrical cables shall be properly connected, insulated, and secured to avoid damage during operation.
  • The pump shall be lowered carefully into the borewell using suitable equipment, ensuring correct positioning and alignment. After installation, necessary testing shall be carried out to check proper functioning of the pump, including electrical connections and water discharge. The entire operation shall be carried out safely and efficiently without causing damage to existing installation, and the system shall be handed over in working condition as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The work of removing and reinstalling the submersible pump set shall be measured on a per number (Each) basis, in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include the cost of all labour, tools, and equipment such as tripod, chain pulley, clamps, and all incidental materials required for dismantling, handling, reinstalling, and testing.
  • No separate measurement shall be made for individual components such as pipes, cables, lifting arrangements, or minor consumables, as these are deemed to be included in the item rate. The work shall be measured as completed and accepted, and the rate shall include all incidental charges required to complete the work safely and as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of One Nos.

Description: Applying two coats of putty & two coats of primer of approved brand and manufacture on new wall surface to give an even shade including thoroughly brushing the surface free from mortar dropping and other foreign matter and sand papered smooth.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• All materials used for surface preparation of walls shall be of approved quality and conform to relevant Indian Standards. Wall putty shall be white cement-based putty of approved make, suitable for interior/exterior application, providing smooth and uniform finish, conforming to IS 15477. Primer shall be of approved brand, compatible with the finishing paint system, and suitable for new plastered surfaces, ensuring proper adhesion and sealing of the substrate.
  • Water used for mixing and application shall be clean and free from impurities, conforming to IS 456. Sandpaper and other consumables used for finishing shall be of suitable grade and quality. All materials shall be new, properly stored, and approved by the Engineer-in-Charge prior to use.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The wall surface shall be thoroughly prepared before application of putty and primer. All dust, dirt, mortar droppings, loose particles, grease, and foreign matter shall be removed by brushing and cleaning to obtain a sound and clean surface. Any irregularities or undulations shall be rectified before starting the work.
  • Two coats of wall putty shall be applied evenly over the surface using appropriate tools, ensuring complete coverage and uniform thickness. Each coat shall be allowed to dry properly and shall be sandpapered smoothly to achieve an even and smooth finish free from marks, ridges, or undulations.
  • After proper drying and surface preparation, two coats of primer shall be applied uniformly over the putty surface using brush, roller, or spray as per manufacturer’s recommendations. Adequate drying time shall be allowed between coats. The application shall be done carefully to achieve an even shade and proper adhesion, avoiding streaks, patches, or unevenness.
  • The finished surface shall be smooth, uniform, and ready for final paint application. The work shall be carried out neatly, and all adjacent surfaces shall be protected from damage or splashes. The completed work shall be as per specifications and directions of the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The work of applying putty and primer shall be measured in square meters (m²) based on the actual area treated, in accordance with IS 1200 Part 13. The rate shall include the cost of all materials such as putty, primer, water, and all labour, tools, and plants required for surface preparation, application, sanding, and finishing.
  • No separate measurement shall be made for surface cleaning, sandpapering, minor surface corrections, or incidental works, as these are deemed to be included in the item rate. The work shall be measured net as completed and accepted, and the rate shall include all incidental charges required to complete the work as per specifications and as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Square Meter.

Description: Supplying & fixing steel lockers measuring 1500 mm H x 1800 mm W x 600 mm D overall with 9 nos. of compartments of equal size approx. 450 mm H x 600 mm W x 600 mm D. Providing a pair of hanging sheet metal door to each compartment individually meade out of 18 G.  C.R. sheet resting on hinges welded fully to the body (a M.S. flat 20mm x 5mm provided as door frame) incl. prov. a stopper inside and locking arrangement outside the door with a pair of handles of 75mm size, back plate, inside vertical partitions and out side walls meade out of 20 G. C.R. sheet and horizontal partition out of 18 G. C.R. sheet incl. providing 1 coat of red oxide and successive 2 coats of stoving enamel (TA grey) backed in electric oven etc. comp. as directed.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• All materials used for supplying and fixing steel lockers shall conform to relevant Indian Standards and approved specifications. The locker shall be fabricated from cold rolled (C.R.) steel sheets of required thickness, where outer body, back plate, and vertical partitions shall be made from 20 gauge C.R. sheet, and horizontal partitions and doors shall be made from 18 gauge C.R. sheet, conforming to IS 513. The locker shall be of overall size approximately 1500 mm height × 1800 mm width × 600 mm depth, divided into 9 equal compartments of approximate size 450 mm × 600 mm × 600 mm.
  • Each compartment shall be provided with a pair of sheet metal doors, supported on fully welded hinges of approved quality. A door frame made of M.S. flat of size 20 mm × 5 mm shall be provided for rigidity. Locking arrangement shall consist of suitable locking mechanism with a pair of handles of approximately 75 mm size, along with back plate and internal stopper. All fittings and accessories shall be of approved quality and corrosion-resistant.
  • All steel surfaces shall be treated with one coat of red oxide primer and finished with two coats of stoving enamel paint (TA grey shade), baked in an electric oven to achieve a durable and uniform finish. All materials shall be new, of approved make, and shall be inspected and approved by the Engineer-in-Charge prior to use.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The steel locker shall be fabricated in accordance with approved drawings and specifications. The C.R. sheets shall be cut, bent, and assembled accurately to form the outer body, partitions, and doors, ensuring proper dimensions and alignment. All joints shall be welded properly to form a rigid and stable structure, and welds shall be ground smooth and finished neatly.
  • The internal vertical and horizontal partitions shall be fixed securely to form 9 equal compartments. Doors shall be fabricated and fixed with fully welded hinges to ensure smooth operation. Locking arrangements, handles, and stoppers shall be properly installed to each compartment, ensuring ease of use and security.
  • The entire surface shall be cleaned, degreased, and treated before application of paint. One coat of red oxide primer shall be applied, followed by two coats of stoving enamel paint, which shall be oven baked to achieve a smooth, durable, and uniform finish. Care shall be taken to avoid dents, scratches, or distortions during fabrication and handling.
  • The locker shall be installed in proper position, ensuring level and stability. The finished unit shall be free from defects, with smooth edges, proper alignment of doors, and uniform paint finish. The completed work shall be handed over in clean and satisfactory condition as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The steel locker shall be measured on a per number (Each) basis for the specified size and configuration, in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include the cost of all materials such as C.R. sheets, M.S. flats, hinges, handles, locking arrangements, primer, paint, and all labour, tools, and plants required for fabrication, assembly, painting, and fixing.
  • No separate measurement shall be made for partitions, doors, hardware fittings, painting, welding, or incidental works, as these are deemed to be included in the item rate. The work shall be measured as completed and accepted, and the rate shall include all incidental charges such as transportation, loading, unloading, and installation required to complete the work as per specifications and as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of One Nos.

Description: Applying priming coat over new steel and other metel surface after and including preparing the surface by throughly cleaning, oil,grease, dirt and other foreign matter and scoured with brushes fine steel wood,scrapers and sand paper with ready mixed priming paint brushing red lead.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• The ready mixed primer, brushing red shall conform to I.S. 102-1962.
  • The thinner (linseed oil) shall conform to I.S. 75-1973. If for any reason, thinning is necessary m case of ready mix paint the brand of thinner recommended by manufacture shall be used.

subsections.title: Preparation of surfaces
subsections.description: • The surfaces painting shall be cleaned of all rust, scale, dirt and other foreign matter sticking to it with wire brushes, steel wool, scrapers, sand paper etc. This surface shall then be wiped finally with mineral turpentine which shall also remove grease and perspiration of hand marks. The surface shall then be allowed to dry.

subsections.title: Application of primer
subsections.description:
• After the preparation of the surface, the priming coat shall be applied immediately. The brushing operations are to be adjusted to the spreading capacity advised by the manufacturer of the particular primer. The paint shall be applied evenly and smoothly by means of crossing and laying off. The crossing and laying off consists of covering the area over with paint, brushing alternately in opposite directions, two or three times and then finally brushing lightly in a direction at right angles to the same. In this process, no brush marks shall be left after the laying off is finished. The full process of crossing and laying off wall constitute one coat.
  • During painting, every time, after the priming coat has been worked out of the brush bristles or after the brush has been unloaded, the bristles of the brush shall be opened up by striking the brush against portion of the unpainted surface with the end of the bristles, held at right angles to the surface, so that bristles thereafter will collect the correct amount of paint when dipped again in to a paint container The prima/y coat shall be allowed to dry completely before painting is started.
  • No hair marks from the brush or clogging at pain puddles in the corner of panels angles of molding etc. shall be left on the work.
  • Special care shall be taken while painting over bolts, nuts, rivets, overlaps etc.
  • The container when not in use shall be kept close and free from air so that paint does not thickness and also shall be kept guarded from dust.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The new steel and other metal surface shall be measured under this item.
  • All the work shall be measured net in the decimal system, as executed subject to the following limits unless otherwise stated hereinafter.
  • Dimensions shall be measured to the nearest 0.01 meter.
  • Areas shall be worked out to the nearest 0.01 sq. meter.
  • No deductions shall be made for openings not exceeding 0.5 sq. mt. each and no addition shall be made for painting to beddings, moldings, edges, jambs, soffits, sills etc. of such opening.
  • In case of fabricated structural steel and iron work, priming coat of paint shall be included with frabation. In case of trusses if measured in sq. m. compound girders, stanchions, lattices, grader and similar work, actual area shall be measured in sq. m. and no extra shall be paid for painting on bolts heads, nuts, washers etc. No addition shall be made to the weight calculated for the purpose of measurements of steel and iron works for paint applied on shop or at site.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Square Meter.

Description: Providing upto floor two level precast cement concrete jali or grill 1:2:4 mix (1- Cement : 2- coarse sand :4-graded stone aggregate 6mm nominal size) reinforced with 1.6 mm dia. Mild steel wire including roughening,cleaning, fixing and finishing in cement mortar 1:3 and curing complete. (D) 75mm thick

sections.title: Materials
sections.description: • Water shall conform to M-1. Cement shall conform to M-3. Sand shall conform to M-6. Mortar shall conform to M-11. Aggregates shall conform to M-12. Mild steel wire shall conform to M-21. Shattering shall conform to M-26.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description: • It shall be cement concrete 1:2:4 (1 cement : 2 coarse sand : 4 graded stone aggregate 6 mm. nominal size), reinforced with 1.6 mm. dia mild steel wire unless otherwise specified. The thickness of the jali shall be as specified in the item. The jali shall be set in position true to line and level before the jambs sills and soffits to the opening are. plastered. It shall then be properly cemented with cement mortar 1:3 (1 cement : 3 sand) and rechecked for levels. Finally the jambs, sills and soffits shall be plastered gripping the jali uniformly on all sides.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The item shall be measured in square meter.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of One running meter.

Description: Applying two coats oil paint with synthetic enamel paint, brushing  to given an even shade including  cleaning the surface of all dirst, dust and other foreign matter. (A) Steel Surface

sections.title: Materials
sections.description: • The Synthetic enamel paint shall conform to I.S. 1932-1964.

subsections.title: General
subsections.description:
• The materials required for work of painting work shall be obtained directly from approved manufactures or approved dealer and brought to the site in maker's drums; kegs. etc. with seal unbroken.
  • All materials not in actual use shall be kept properly protected, lids of containers shall be kept closed and surface of paint in open or partially open containers covered with a thin layer of turpentine to prevent formation of skin. The materials which have become state or flat due to improper and long storage shall not be used. The paint shall be stirred thoroughly in its container before pouring into small containers. While applying also, the paint shall be continuously stirred in smaller container. No left over paint shall be put back into stock tins. When not in use the containers shall be kept properly closed.
  • If for any reasons, things is necessary, the brand of thinner recommended by the manufacturer shall be used.
  • The surface to be painted shall be thoroughly cleaned and dusted. All rust, dirt and grease shall be thoroughly removed before painting is started. No painting on exterior or other exposed part o the work shall be carried out in wet, damp or otherwise unfavorable weather and all the surfaces shall be thoroughly dry before painting work is started.

subsections.title: Application of paint
subsections.description:
• Brushing operations are to be adjusted to the spreading capacity advised by the manufacture of particular paint. The paint shall be applied evenly and smoothly by means of crossing and laying off. The crossing and laying off consists of covering the area over with paint, brushing the surface hard for the first time over and then brushing alternately in opposite directions two or three times and then finally brushing lightly in a direction at right angles to the same. In this process, no brush marks shall be left after the -laying off is finished. The full process of crossing and laying off will constitute one coat.
  • Each coat shall be allowed to dry completely and lightly rubbed with very fine grade of sand-paper and loose particles brushed off before next coat is applied. Each coat shall vary slightly in shade and shall be got approved from Engineer-in-charge before next coat is started.
  • Each coat the last shall be lightly rubbed down with sand paper of fine pumice stone and cleaned of dust before the next coat is applied. No hair marks from the brush of clogging of paint puddles in the corners of panels, angles of moldings etc. shall be left on the work.
  • Special care shall be taken while painting over bolts, nuts, rivets, overlaps etc. Approved best quality brushes shall be used.
  • The Above specifications shall be followed except that the painting shall be carried out with synthetic enamel paint.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The new steel and other metal surface shall be measured under this item.
  • All the work shall be measured net in the decimal system, as executed subject to the following limits unless otherwise stated hereinafter.
  • Dimensions shall be measured to the nearest 0.01 meter.
  • Areas shall be worked out to the nearest 0.01 sq. meter.
  • No deductions shall be made for openings not exceeding 0.5 sq. mt. each and no addition shall be made for painting to beddings, moldings, edges, jambs, soffits, sills etc. of such opening.
  • In case of fabricated structural steel and iron work, priming coat of paint shall be included with frabation. In case of trusses if measured in sq. m. compound girders, stanchions, lattices, grader and similar work, actual area shall be measured in sq. m. and no extra shall be paid for painting on bolts heads, nuts, washers etc. No addition shall be made to the weight calculated for the purpose of measurements of steel and iron works for paint applied on shop or at site.
  • The different surfaces shall be grouped into one general item, areas of uneven surfaces being converted into equivalent plain areas in accordance with the table given as per Annexure-ll for payment.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Square Meter.

Description: Providing & Fixing 3.00m long & 0.75m high CHAIN LINK 2.5  10×10 gauge (Galvenized) Fencing fixed in MS angle frame made from MS angle size 35×35×5mm at top, bottom & sides so as to form a complete rectangular frame. The straightened chain link fencing shall be fixed upon the all around angle iron frame with mild steel flat 30×5mm fix to vertical and horizontal angle frame with 10mm dia nuts and bolts at 0.30m C/C incl. fixing angle iron post in compound wall with 0.35m×0.35m×0.10m block in C.C. (1:2:4) providing at top & bottom in Bela Stone masonary pillars & incl. painting entire fencing with two or more coat of synthetic enamel paint over and incl. priming coat of zinc/ red oxide steel primer etc. cost incl. all labours and materials involved comp. as directed.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• All materials used for providing and fixing chain link fencing shall conform to relevant Indian Standards and approved specifications. The chain link mesh shall be galvanized steel of 10 × 10 gauge (approx.), of approved quality, conforming to IS 2721, uniform in mesh size, properly woven, and free from defects. The supporting frame shall be fabricated from M.S. angle sections of size 35 × 35 × 5 mm, conforming to IS 2062.
  • M.S. flats of size 30 × 5 mm shall be used for fixing the chain link mesh to the frame, and all fasteners such as nuts and bolts (10 mm diameter) shall be of approved quality and corrosion-resistant. The fencing posts shall be embedded in cement concrete blocks of size 0.35 m × 0.35 m × 0.10 m made with concrete mix 1:2:4, using materials conforming to IS 456 and IS 383.
  • All steel components shall be cleaned and provided with one coat of zinc/red oxide primer and finished with two or more coats of approved synthetic enamel paint. Bela stone masonry (if specified for pillars) shall be of approved quality. All materials shall be new, of approved make, and shall be inspected and approved by the Engineer-in-Charge prior to use.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The chain link fencing shall be fabricated and installed as per approved drawings and specifications. The M.S. angle frame shall be cut, aligned, and welded to form a rigid rectangular frame of size approximately 3.00 m length and 0.75 m height. All welds shall be properly finished, and the frame shall be cleaned of rust and scale before painting.
  • The chain link mesh shall be stretched, straightened, and fixed over the angle frame using M.S. flats (30 × 5 mm), which shall be bolted to the frame with 10 mm diameter nuts and bolts at intervals not exceeding 0.30 m center to center, ensuring tight fixing and proper tension in the mesh.
  • The fencing posts shall be fixed securely into the compound wall or ground using cement concrete blocks of specified size, ensuring proper alignment, level, and stability. Bela stone masonry pillars, where provided, shall be constructed in proper line and level to support the fencing.
  • After fabrication and fixing, one coat of zinc/red oxide primer shall be applied to all steel surfaces, followed by two or more coats of approved synthetic enamel paint to achieve a smooth and durable finish. The entire fencing shall be true to line, level, and alignment, free from sagging, distortion, or defects. The completed work shall be neat, strong, and aesthetically acceptable, and shall be carried out as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The chain link fencing shall be measured in running meters (Rmt) based on the actual length of fencing provided and fixed, in accordance with IS 1200. The height shall be as specified, and no separate measurement shall be made for height unless otherwise stated.
  • The rate shall include the cost of all materials such as chain link mesh, M.S. angles, flats, posts, concrete blocks, primer, paint, fasteners, and all labour, tools, and plants required for fabrication, fixing, concreting, painting, and finishing.
  • No separate measurement shall be made for welding, cutting, drilling, painting, concrete foundation, fixing accessories, or incidental works, as these are deemed to be included in the item rate. The work shall be measured net as completed and accepted, and the rate shall include all incidental charges required to complete the work as per specifications and as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of One running meter.

Description: Providing and fixing 1.20 metre high fencing with 2.0 metre long m.s angle posts 40mm x 40mm x 6mm and oil painting 3 coats fixed at 3.0m c/c. with five horizontal line and two diagonals of galvanised steel barbed wire weighting 9.38 kg per 100 metre, strained and fixed to posts with G.I,straples including fixing the posts in ground with 0.5m x 0.5m x 0.5m. block in c.c (1:2:4) etc.complete.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description: • (1) Water shall conform to M-1. (2) Cement shall conform to M-3. (3) Sand shall conform to M-6. (4) Brick bats aggregate shall conform to M-.14, (5) Oil paint shall conform to M-44. (6) Barbed wire shall conform to M-78.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The pits of the size O.5 x 0.5 m. x 0.5 shall fist be excavated, true to line and level to receive the post at 2.5 C/ C. The relevant specifications of item 4.00.1 shall be followed for excavation work.
  • The pits shall be filled with a layer 0.15 m. thick with lean concrete 1:5:10 (1 cement: 5 sand : 10 graded brick bat aggregate 40 mm. nominal size). The M.S. angles 40 mm. x 40 mm. x6 mm shall be filled in with lean concrete 1:5:10 and rammed properly so as to form total 0.5 m. x 0.5 m. x 0.5 m, concrete block. The concrete shall be cured for 7 days to allow it to set.
  • The barbed wire shall be stretched and fixed in 5 horizontal rows and two diagonals. The bottom row shall be 140 mm. above ground and the rest at 125 mm. centre to centre. The diagonal shall be stretched between adjacent post from top wire of one post to the bottom wire of'2nd post. The wires shall be fixed to posts by means of staples. The M.S. Angle posts shall be painted with 3 coats of old paint of approved tint and shade.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The work shall be measured for the finished work from centre to centre of the posts.
  • The rate shall include the cost of labour and materials involved in the operations described above.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of One running meter.

subsections.description:
• Brushing operations are to be adjusted to the spreading capacity advised by the manufacture of particular paint. The paint shall be applied evenly and smoothly by means of crossing and laying off. The crossing and laying off consists of covering the area over with paint, brushing the surface hard for the first time over and then brushing alternately in opposite directions two or three times and then finally brushing lightly in a direction at right angles to the same. In this process, no brush marks shall be left after the -laying off is finished. The full process of crossing and laying off will constitute one coat.
  • Each coat shall be allowed to dry completely and lightly rubbed with very fine grade of sand-paper and loose particles brushed off before next coat is applied. Each coat shall vary slightly in shade and shall be got approved from Engineer-in-charge before next coat is started.
  • Each coat the last shall be lightly rubbed down with sand paper of fine pumice stone and cleaned of dust before the next coat is applied. No hair marks from the brush of clogging of paint puddles in the corners of panels, angles of moldings etc. shall be left on the work.
  • Special care shall be taken while painting over bolts, nuts, rivets, overlaps etc. Approved best quality brushes shall be used.
  • The Above specifications shall be followed for general and application of paint, except that the enamel paint shall be used for painting on new wood/wood based surfaces.
  • In painting doors and windows, the putty, round the glass panes also be painted but care shall be taken to see that no paint, stain etc. are left on the glass. Top of shutters and surfaces in similar hidden locations shall not be left out in painting.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The new wood and other wooden surface shall be measured under this item.
  • All the work shall be measured net in the decimal system, as executed subject to the following limits unless otherwise stated hereinafter.
  • Dimensions shall be measured to the nearest 0.01 meter.
  • Areas shall be worked out to the nearest 0.01 sq. meter.
  • No deductions shall be made for openings not exceeding 0.5 sq. mt. each and no addition shall be made for painting to beddings, moldings, edges, jambs, soffits, sills etc. of such opening.
  • The different surfaces shall be grouped into one general item, areas of uneven surfaces being converted into equivalent plain areas in accordance with the table given as per Annexure-ll for payment.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Square Meter.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• All materials used for supplying and fixing signboards shall conform to relevant Indian Standards and approved specifications. The cladding material shall be 3 mm thick exterior grade Aluminium Composite Panel (ACP) of approved brands such as Aludecor, Alstrong, or Eurobond, having good weather resistance, colour stability, and durability suitable for outdoor applications. The ACP shall be flat, free from defects, and of approved shade and finish.
  • The lettering shall be made using non-reflective vinyl of approved quality, with proper adhesion and durability under external conditions. The supporting framework shall be fabricated from M.S. hollow square sections of size 45 mm × 45 mm and 20 gauge thickness, conforming to IS 4923. Steel sections shall be free from rust, scale, and defects.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The ACP signage shall be fabricated and installed as per approved drawings and instructions. The ACP sheet shall be cut accurately to the required size of 0.60 m × 0.30 m, with smooth and finished edges. The surface shall be cleaned properly before application of vinyl lettering.
  • The non-reflective vinyl letters shall be applied carefully on the ACP surface as per the specified design, ensuring correct alignment, spacing, and uniformity. The application shall be free from air bubbles, wrinkles, or misalignment.
  • The signage shall be fixed directly onto the existing surface (wall/structure) using appropriate methods such as screws, adhesive, or fasteners, ensuring firm and secure fixing without damaging the panel. Proper alignment, level, and positioning shall be maintained during installation. The finished signage shall be neat, properly fixed, and aesthetically acceptable, free from defects or damage, and completed as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The ACP signage shall be measured on a per number (Each) basis for the specified size (0.60 m × 0.30 m), in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include the cost of all materials such as ACP sheet, vinyl lettering, adhesives, fasteners, and all labour, tools, and plants required for cutting, lettering, fixing, and finishing.
  • No separate measurement shall be made for cutting, lettering, fixing accessories, or incidental works, as these are deemed to be included in the item rate. The work shall be measured as completed and accepted, and the rate shall include all incidental charges required to complete the work as per specifications and as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of One Nos.

sections.description:
• The signboard shall be fabricated and installed as per approved drawings and instructions.   • The entire signboard shall be securely fixed in position using suitable anchoring fasteners, ensuring stability and resistance to wind loads. The finished board shall be true to line and level, aesthetically pleasing, and free from defects such as misalignment, uneven surface, or poor finishing. Description: Providing & applying white or colour wash in 3 coats to walls or ceiling to give an even shade incl. scrapping and cleaning the surface with sand paper incl. scaffolding etc. comp. as directed.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• The clear Cole shall be made from glue and boiling water by mixing 1 Kg. mixture shall be suitably tinted where required for use under coloured distemper it directed. Glue shall conform to I.S. 352-1959 (Specifications for animal give)
  • Lime used shall be Freshly burnt class 'C' Lime (fat lime) and white in colour conforming to I S. 712-1973. Water shall conform to M-1. Best quality of gum shall be used in (he preparations of white wash. Ultramarine blue or Indigo : This shall conform to I.S. 55-1970 for points, and shall be used for preparation of white was, Pigments. Mineral colours, not affected by lime shall be used in preparing colour wash.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description: • Preparation of white wash solution Surface already white or colour. The fat lime shall be slaked as site and shall be mixed and stirred with about five liters of water for 1 kg. of unslaked lime to made a trim cream This shall be allowed to stand for d period of 24 hours and then shall be screened through a clean coarse cloth, 4 Kg. of gum dissolves in hot water shall be added to each cubic meter of lime cream Small quantity of ultramarine blue (Up to 3 gins, per kg. of lime) shall also-be added to the last two coats of white wash solution and the whole solution shall be stirred thoroughly before use.

subsections.title: Preparation of surface
subsections.description:
• The surface shall be thoroughly cleaned of all dust, dirt, mortar cropping and other foreign matter before white wash is to be applied.
  • The surface spoiled by smoke soot shall be scrapped with steel wire brushes or steel scrapers 01 shall be rubbed with over-burnt surkhi or brick bats. The surface shall be then broomed to remove all dust dirt and shall he washed with clean water.
  • Oil or grease spots shall be removed by suitable chemical and smooth surface shall be rubber with wire Crushes.
  • All unsound portion of the surface plaster shall be removed to full depth of plaster in rectangular patches and plastered again after raking the masonry joints properly. Such portion shall he wetted and allowed to dry. They shall then be given one coat of white wash
  • All unnecessary nails shall be removed the holes, cracks, patches etc. shall be made good with material similar in composition to the surface to be prepared

subsections.title: Scaffolding
subsections.description: • Wherever scaffolding is necessary it shall be erected in such a way that as far as possible on part of scaffolding shall rest against the surface to be white or colour washed A properly secured strong and well tied suspended platform (Zoola) may be used for white washing. Where ladders are used pieces of old gunny bags shall be tied at top and bottom to prevent scratches to the floors and walls. For white washing of ceilings, proper stage scaffolding shall be erected where necessary.

subsections.title: Application of white wash
subsections.description:
• On the surface so prepared the white wash shall be applied with 'Moon' brush. The first stroke of the brush shall be from top downwards, another from bottom upwards over the first stroke and similarly one stoke from the right another from the left, over the first stroke brush before it dries. This will form one coat each coat shall be allowed to dry before and uniform finish free from brush marks and it should not come oft easily when rubbed with finger
  • Splashing and dropping if any on the doors and windows, ventilators etc shall be removed and the surface cleaned.
  • Priming and Alkali resistant treatments, scraping of surface washing etc. surface spoiled by smoke soot removed of oil and grease spots, treatment for infection with efflorescence moulds moos, fungi, algae and lichen and patch repairs to plaster wherever done shall not be paid extra.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• All the work shall be measured in the decimal system as under:
  • (a) Dimensions shall be measured to the nearest 0.01 m.
  • (b) Area in individual item shall be worked out to the nearest 0.01 sq.m.
  • All the work shall be measured in sq. mt. Deductions for jambs, soffits, sills etc. for openings not exceeding 0.5 sq. mt. each in area, for ends of joists, posts, beams, girders, steps etc. not exceeding 0.5 sq mt. each in area and for openings exceeding 0.5 sq. mt. and not exceeding 3.0. sq. mt. each in area, deductions and additions shall be made as under.
  • No deductions shall be made for ends of joists, beams, posts, etc. and openings not exceeding 0.5 sq mt. each. No addition shall be made for reveals, jambs, soffits, sills etc. of these openings not for finish around ends of joints, beams, posts etc.
  • No deductions for openings exceeding 0.5 sq.mt. but not exceeding 3 sq. mt. each shall be made as follows and no addition will be made for reveals, jambs, soffits etc. of these openings :
  • (a) When both the faces of walls are provided with finish, deduction shall be made for one face only.
  • (b)  When each face of wall is provided with different finish, deduction shall be made for that side of frame for door, windows, etc. on which width of reveals is less than that of the other side. Where width of reveals on both faces of wall are equal, deduction of .50% of area of opening on each face shall be made from total area of finish.
  • (c) When only one face of wall is treated and the other face is not treated, full deduction shall be made if the width of reveal on the treated side is less than that on the untreated side, but if the width of the reveal is equal or more than on the untreated side neither deductions nor additions to be made for reveals, jambs, soffits, sills etc.
  • In case of area of openings exceeding 3 sq. mt. each, deductions shall be made for openings but jambs, soffits, sills shall be measured.
  • No deductions shall be made for attachment such as casing, conducts, pipe, electric wiring and the like.
  • Corrugated surfaces shall be measured flat as fixed and not girth. The quantities so measured shall be increased by the following percentage and the resultant shall be included with the general areas:
  • (a) Corrugated steel sheets 14%
  • (b) Corrugated A.C. sheets - 20%
  • (c)  Semi corrugated A.C. Sheets - 10%
  • (d) Nainital pattern roof (Plain sheeting sheets) - 10%
  • (e) Naintial pattern roof (with corrugated sheets) - 25%
  • Cornices and other wall features, when they are not picked out in a different finish/colour shall be girthed and included in the general area.
  • The rate shall include the cost of ail materials, labour, scaffolding, protective measures etc. involved in all the operations described above.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of One sq. meter.
