Description: Applying general insecticide pest control treatment to floors, cupboards etc including labour materials etc. complete. Using Imidacloprid 30.5 SCas Per IS 6313 part -II( (0.075% concentration by mass) is recommended 10.5ml chemical diluted with 5 liters of water application 0.5 litre chemical /Sqm of surface is recommended as per I.S.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• All materials used for general insecticide pest control treatment shall conform to relevant Indian Standards and approved specifications. The chemical used shall be Imidacloprid 30.5% SC (Suspension Concentrate) or equivalent approved insecticide, applied as per IS 6313 Part 2. The chemical shall be of approved make, properly sealed, and handled as per manufacturer’s instructions.
  • The emulsion shall be prepared to achieve 0.075% concentration by mass, typically by diluting approximately 10.5 ml of Imidacloprid 30.5% SC in 5 litres of water. Water used for dilution shall be clean and free from impurities, conforming to IS 456. All materials shall be new, safe for application in inhabited areas when used as directed, and shall be approved by the Engineer-in-Charge prior to use.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The pest control treatment shall be carried out on floors, cupboards, and other affected or vulnerable areas as directed. The surfaces shall be cleaned to remove dust, dirt, grease, and loose materials prior to application. The prepared chemical emulsion of 0.075% concentration shall be applied uniformly by spraying using suitable equipment to ensure proper coverage and penetration.
  • The application shall be carried out at the rate of approximately 0.5 litres of emulsion per square meter of surface area, ensuring that all corners, joints, crevices, and concealed locations such as cupboards and storage areas are thoroughly treated. Care shall be taken to avoid over-application or spillage.
  • Adequate safety precautions shall be followed during handling and spraying of chemicals, including use of protective equipment. Treated areas shall be left undisturbed for sufficient time to allow the chemical to act effectively. The work shall be carried out systematically to ensure complete coverage and effectiveness. The completed treatment shall be as per specifications and directions of the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The general insecticide pest control treatment shall be measured in square meters (m²) based on the actual surface area treated, in accordance with IS 1200 and relevant provisions of IS 6313. The rate shall include the cost of all materials such as insecticide chemical, water, and all labour, tools, and plants required for preparation, spraying, and completion of the treatment.
  • No separate measurement shall be made for surface preparation, mixing of chemicals, safety measures, or incidental works, as these are deemed to be included in the item rate. The work shall be measured net as completed and accepted, and the rate shall include all incidental charges required to complete the work as per specifications and as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of One sq. meter.

Description: Providing & applying one coat of distemper primer & 2 coats of approved quality like Tractor or its equivalent brand oil bound distemper or required shade after throughly brushing the surface free from mortar droppings & other foreign matter incl. scaffolding, cleaning the wall & preparating the surface even & smooth using putty, filling cracks etc. comp. as directed.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description: • Oil bound washable distemper and primer shall be of approved brand and manufacture. The distemper shall be of required colour and shade and the same shall conform to I.S. : 428-1969.

subsections.title: Scaffolding
subsections.description: • Where scaffolding is required, it shall be erected in such a way that as far as possible no pail of scaffolding shall rest against the surface to be distempered. A properly secured and well tied suspended platform (Joola) may be used for distempering. Where ladders are used, pieces of old gunny bags shall be tied at top and bottom to prevent scratches to the walls and floors. For distempering to ceiling, proper stage scaffolding shall be erected where necessary.

subsections.title: Preparation of surface
subsections.description:
• The undecorated surface to be distempered shall be thoroughly brushed from dust, dirt, grease, mortar dropping and other foreign matter and sand papered smooth. New plaster surface shall be allowed to dry for at least 2 months before applications of distemper.
  • All unnecessary nails shall be removed. Pitting in plaster shall be made good with plaster again with a fine grade sand paper and made smooth. A coat of distemper shall be applied over the patches. The surface shall be allowed to dry thoroughly before the regular coat of distemper is allowed. The surface affected by moulds, moss, fungi, algae lichens, efflorescence etc. shall be treated in accordance with I.S; 2395 (Part 01) 1966. Before applying distempering, any unevenness shall be made good by applying putty made of plaster of pairs mixed with water on entire surface including filling up the undulation and then sand papering the same after it is dry.

subsections.title: Priming Coat
subsections.description:
• A priming coat of distemper primer of approved manufacture and shade shall be applied over the papered surface in case of new work on undecorated surface. If the distemper priming is done after the wall surface dries completely, the distemper primer shall be applied.
  • Application of primer shall be done as under: The primer shall be applied with a brush on the clean dry and smooth surface. Horizontal strokes shall be given first and vertical strokes shall be applied immediately afterwards. This entire operation will constitute on coat. The surface shall be finished as uniformly as possible leaving no brush marks. It shall be allowed to dry for at least 48 hours before oil bound distemper or paint is applied.
  • Oil bound distemper is not recommended to be applied within six months of the completion of wall plaster.

subsections.title: Preparation of oil bound distemper
subsections.description: • The distemper shall be diluted with water or any other prescribed thinner in a manner recommended by the manufacturer only. Sufficient quantity of distemper required for a days work shall be prepared.

subsections.title: Application of Distemper coat
subsections.description:
• For undecorated surfaces, after the primer coat is dried for at least 48 hours, the surface shall be lightly sand papered to make it smooth for receiving the distemper, taking care not to rub out priming coat. All loose particles shall be dusted of after rubbing. Minimum tow coats of distemper shall be applied with brushes in horizontal strokes followed immediately by vertical strokes which together shall constitute one coat. The subsequent coats shall be applied after a time interval of at least 24 hours between consecutive coats to permit proper drying of the proceeding coat. The finished surface shall be even and inform without patches, brush marks, distemper drops etc.
  • Sufficient quantity of distemper shall be mixed to finish one room at a time. The application of a coat in each room shall be finished in one operation and no work shall be striated in any room which cannot be completed on the same day.
  • 15 cm. double bristled distemper brush shall be used. After day's work brushes shall be thoroughly washed in hot water with soap solution and hung down to dry. Old brushes which are dirty and caked with distemper shall not be used on the work.
  • Protective measurements : The surfaces of doors, windows, floors, articles of furniture etc. and such other parts of the buildings as are not to be distempered shall be protected form being splashed upon. Such surfaces shall be cleaned of distemper splashes if any.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• Priming coat of distemper primer, scraping of surface spoiled by struck roots, removal of oil and grease spots, treatment for infraction of effloresces., mould moss, fungi, algae and litchen and patch repairs to plaster shall be included in this item for which nothing extra shall be paid.
  • All the work shall be measured net in the decimal system as in place subject to the following limits unless otherwise stated hereinafter:
  • (a) Dimensions shall be measured to the nearest 0.01 m.
  • (b) Area in individual items shall be worked out to the nearest 0.01 sq. m. All work shall be made for ends of joints, beams, posts etc., and openings, not exceeding 0.5 sq.mt. each and no addition shall be made for reveals, jambs, soffits, sills etc. of these openings not for finish around ends of joints, beams, posts etc.
  • Deductions of opening exceeding 0.5 sq.m. but not exceeding 3 sq. m. each shall be made as follows and net addition shall be made for reveals, jambs, soffits etc. of these openings :
  • (a) When both the faces of wall are provided with same finish, deductions shall be made for one face only.
  • (b) When each face of wall is provided with different finish, deduction shall be made for that side of frame for doors, windows etc. on which width of reveals is less than that of the other side but no deduction shall be made on the other side. Where the width of reveals on the both the fates of wall are equal, deduction of 50% of area of opening on each face shall be made from area of finish.
  • (c) When only one face of wall is treated and the other face is not treated, full deductions shall be made if the width of the reveal on treated side is less than that on untreated side but if the width of the reveal is equal or more than that on untreated side neither deductions nor additions to be made for reveals, jambs, soffits, sills etc.
  • In case of opening of area exceeding 3 sq. m. each deduction shall be made for openings but jambs, sills and soffits shall be measured.
  • No deductions shall be made for attachments such as casings, conduits, pipes, electric wiring and the like.
  • Item includes removing nails, making good holes, patches with materials similar in composition of distemper.
  • The rate includes cost of ail materials, labours, scaffolding, protective measures etc. involved in all the operations described above. This shall also include conveyance, delivery, handing , unloading, storing work etc
  • The rate shall be for a unit of One sq. meter.

Description: Providing & Applying colour plast on exterior surface in 5 mm thickness of approved quality and make as directed incl. making the surface for applying colour plast & making brick pointing impression in different colour incl. necessary scaffolding etc. comp. as directed.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• All materials used for providing and applying colour plast on exterior surfaces shall be of approved quality and conform to relevant Indian Standards. The colour plast (decorative exterior coating) shall be ready-mixed or site-mixed cement-based or acrylic-based textured coating of approved make, suitable for exterior use, weather-resistant, and capable of providing durable finish. The material shall have good adhesion, water resistance, and resistance to cracking and peeling, conforming generally to IS 15489.
  • Cement used (if applicable in mix) shall conform to IS 8112 or IS 12269, and sand or aggregates used for texture shall conform to IS 383. Pigments used for colouring shall be of approved quality, UV resistant, and stable in outdoor conditions. Water used shall conform to IS 456. All materials shall be new, of approved brand, and shall be inspected and approved by the Engineer-in-Charge prior to use.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The surface shall be thoroughly prepared before application of colour plast. All dust, dirt, loose particles, grease, and foreign matter shall be removed by brushing and cleaning to obtain a sound and clean surface. Any unevenness, cracks, or defects shall be rectified to provide a uniform base. Proper scaffolding shall be erected to carry out the work safely and efficiently.
  • The colour plast shall be applied in a uniform thickness of 5 mm over the prepared surface using suitable tools such as trowels or floats. The application shall be carried out carefully to ensure proper adhesion and uniform thickness throughout. While the material is still workable, brick pointing impressions shall be created in the desired pattern and design using appropriate tools, and different colours shall be applied as required to achieve the specified decorative effect.
  • The surface shall be finished neatly with proper alignment of patterns and uniform colour distribution. Adequate curing shall be carried out if cement-based material is used, as per manufacturer’s recommendations. Care shall be taken to protect the finished surface from rain, dust, or damage during curing. The completed work shall be free from cracks, unevenness, or defects, and shall present a consistent and aesthetically pleasing finish as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The colour plast finish shall be measured in square meters (m²) based on the actual area of surface treated, in accordance with IS 1200 Part 13. The rate shall include the cost of all materials such as colour plast, pigments, cement (if used), and all labour, tools, and plants required for surface preparation, scaffolding, application, pattern making, and finishing.
  • No separate measurement shall be made for scaffolding, surface preparation, pattern making, curing, or incidental works, as these are deemed to be included in the item rate. The work shall be measured net as completed and accepted, and the rate shall include all incidental charges required to complete the work as per specifications and as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of One sq. meter.

Description: Carring out plinth treatment to post construction / existing structure by spraying chemical solution for termite control treatment including labour and material consistment with I.S.I specification. Using Chlordene and Chiorpurfiles 20 EC. As Per 6131_paret-II Consentration Weight one percent is recommended i.e one litre 20 EC chemical emulsion with 19 liter give 1 % concrentration inclusive of one litre chemical emulsion appication at the rate of 5 Litre chemical / Sqm of surface is recommended as per I.S.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• All materials used for anti-termite treatment shall conform to relevant Indian Standards and approved specifications. The chemical used shall be approved anti-termite insecticide such as Chlorpyrifos 20% EC (or equivalent), conforming to IS 8944 and applied as per IS 6313 Part 2. (Note: Use of Chlordane is generally restricted/banned; hence only approved chemicals shall be used.)
  • The emulsion shall be prepared by diluting 1 litre of 20% EC chemical with 19 litres of water to obtain 1% concentration as recommended. Water used shall be clean and free from impurities, conforming to IS 456. All chemicals shall be of approved make, properly sealed, and handled with necessary safety precautions. Materials shall be approved by the Engineer-in-Charge prior to application.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The anti-termite treatment shall be carried out on existing structures as per the procedure laid down in IS 6313 Part 2. Holes of approximately 12 mm diameter shall be drilled at regular intervals (generally 300 mm center to center) along the plinth, walls, floors, and junctions as required to reach the soil beneath or along the potential termite entry points.
  • The prepared chemical emulsion (1% concentration) shall be injected or sprayed into these holes and along the surfaces at the rate of approximately 5 litres per square meter or as specified, ensuring uniform distribution and proper penetration into the soil and structural joints. The holes shall then be sealed with cement mortar after treatment.
  • Care shall be taken to treat all critical areas such as wall-floor junctions, expansion joints, and cracks where termite activity is likely. Safety precautions shall be followed during handling and application of chemicals. The treatment shall be carried out in a systematic manner to ensure complete coverage and effectiveness. The completed work shall be checked for proper application and shall be as per specifications and directions of the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The anti-termite treatment shall be measured in square meters (m²) based on the actual area of surface treated, in accordance with IS 1200 and relevant provisions of IS 6313. The rate shall include the cost of all materials such as chemicals, water, and all labour, tools, and plants required for drilling, spraying, injecting, and sealing of holes.
  • No separate measurement shall be made for drilling holes, sealing, preparation of emulsion, safety measures, or incidental works, as these are deemed to be included in the item rate. The work shall be measured net as completed and accepted, and the rate shall include all incidental charges required to complete the work as per specifications and as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of One sq. meter.

Description: Providing and laying coloured Glass mosaic tiles size 20 x 20 mm and  4mm thick in column cladding for any height dedo on 10 mm. thick cement plaster 1:3 (1 cement : 3 coarse sand) on new surface or fixing on column by adhesive material incl. jointed with color cement slurry incl. finished with flush pointing & cleaning the surface etc. complete.as directed by Architect & EIC.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• All materials used for providing and laying coloured glass mosaic tiles shall conform to relevant Indian Standards and approved specifications. The glass mosaic tiles shall be of size 20 mm × 20 mm and 4 mm thickness, of approved make, colour, and design, uniform in size, free from cracks, chips, or surface defects, and suitable for vertical cladding applications. Adhesive used for fixing (if applicable) shall be cement-based or polymer-modified tile adhesive of approved quality, suitable for glass mosaic tiles.
  • Cement used for plastering and slurry shall conform to IS 8112 or IS 12269, and sand shall be clean, well-graded, and conform to IS 383. The base plaster shall be 10 mm thick in cement mortar 1:3. Colour cement slurry used for jointing shall be prepared using white or grey cement mixed with suitable pigments of approved quality. Water used shall conform to IS 456. All materials shall be new, of approved make, and shall be inspected and approved by the Architect/Engineer-in-Charge prior to use.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The surface of the column or wall shall be properly prepared by cleaning, removing dust, dirt, grease, and loose materials, and brought to a sound and even condition. A 10 mm thick cement plaster in cement mortar 1:3 shall be applied where required to provide a smooth and level base. Alternatively, tiles may be fixed directly using approved adhesive on prepared surfaces.
  • The glass mosaic tiles shall be laid carefully in proper alignment and pattern, ensuring uniform spacing and proper bonding with the base. The tiles shall be pressed gently to ensure full contact with the mortar or adhesive bed. Care shall be taken to maintain straight lines, level, and plumb surfaces, especially for column cladding.
  • Joints between tiles shall be filled with coloured cement slurry, ensuring complete filling and flush pointing to achieve a smooth and uniform finish. Excess slurry shall be cleaned off immediately, and the surface shall be wiped clean. After setting, the surface shall be thoroughly cleaned to remove stains, adhesive marks, or residue.
  • The finished work shall be even, true to line and level, with properly aligned tiles and uniform joints. The surface shall be free from cracks, hollowness, or defects and shall present a neat and aesthetic appearance as per architectural requirements and directions of the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The glass mosaic tile cladding shall be measured in square meters (m²) based on the actual area of surface covered, including column faces and dado, in accordance with IS 1200 Part 13. The rate shall include the cost of all materials such as tiles, cement, sand, adhesive, pigments, and all labour, tools, and plants required for surface preparation, plastering, fixing, jointing, and cleaning.
  • No separate measurement shall be made for plaster base, adhesive, joint filling, scaffolding, cutting of tiles, wastage, or incidental works, as these are deemed to be included in the item rate. The work shall be measured net as completed and accepted, and the rate shall include all incidental charges required to complete the work as per specifications and as directed by the Architect/Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of One sq. meter.

Description: Providing and fixing of Ridge flashing for roof panel shall be made out of 0.5 mm thick pre coated PPGI sheet . The Precoated sheet shall be of minimum 240 mpa steel grade confirming to IS 14246:1995 and shall have zinc coating of minimum 120 gsm as per IS:277:1992 , 5-7 microns epoxy primer on both side of the sheet and polyester top coat 15-18 micron. The PPGI Sheet shall have plastic protective guard film of minimum 25 microns to avoid scratches during transportation. The ridge shall be fixed to the steel members by pop rivet or self drilling/self stitching fastners @ maximum 450 mm c/c along length of capping/flashing and all Neccsary febrication work with M.S Box pipe,round pipe,foundation plates with  M-200 Concrete for foundation  etc complete Min weight of MS Febrication 22 kg/smt. (For Parking Shed)

sections.title: Material
sections.description:
• The ridge flashing/capping shall be manufactured from factory made pre-coated galvanized iron (PPGI) sheet of 0.50 mm minimum base metal thickness conforming to IS 14246:1995 with minimum steel yield strength of 240 MPa. The galvanized coating shall be minimum 120 GSM conforming to IS 277:1992. The sheet shall be provided with minimum 5–7 microns epoxy primer coating on both sides and polyester paint top coating of 15–18 microns on exposed surface. The sheet shall have minimum 25 microns thick removable plastic protective guard film for protection against scratches during handling and transportation.
  • The ridge flashing shall be factory formed or machine bent to approved profile and dimensions suitable for roofing arrangement of parking shed.
  • Fixing accessories such as self-drilling/self-stitching screws, aluminium pop rivets, EPDM washers, sealants and fastening accessories shall be of approved make and suitable for exterior applications. Fasteners shall be corrosion resistant and compatible with PPGI roofing system.
  • The supporting structure and fabrication work shall consist of approved quality M.S. box pipes, M.S. round pipes, base plates, cleats, brackets, stiffeners and other required members conforming to relevant IS specifications. All fabricated steel members shall be free from rust, bends, cracks and other defects. Minimum weight of M.S. fabrication shall be 22 kg per sqm of covered area.
  • Cement concrete for foundation/pedestal shall be M-200 grade using approved quality cement, sand and aggregate conforming to relevant IS specifications.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The ridge flashing/capping shall be installed strictly as per approved drawings, manufacturer’s recommendations and direction of Engineer-in-Charge. The flashing shall be fixed in true line, level and slope to ensure proper waterproofing and neat appearance.

  • All sheets shall be carefully handled to avoid scratches, dents or damages to coating. Necessary cutting, bending, curving and shaping shall be carried out using proper tools without damaging protective coating. Damaged sheets shall not be used.

  • The ridge flashing shall be fixed with approved self-drilling/self-stitching fasteners or aluminium pop rivets with EPDM washers at maximum spacing of 450 mm center to center along the length of flashing/capping. Proper overlap shall be maintained to prevent leakage. All joints and overlaps shall be sealed with approved weatherproof sealant wherever required.

  • The M.S. fabrication work shall include cutting, welding, grinding, drilling, fitting, hoisting and erecting complete in position. Welded joints shall be properly finished smooth and all burrs removed. Fabricated members shall be aligned properly and rigidly fixed to withstand wind load and service conditions.

  • All steel members shall be cleaned properly and provided with one coat of approved metal primer and two coats of synthetic enamel paint unless otherwise specified.

  • Foundation work shall include excavation, PCC if required, placing of foundation/base plates, concreting with M-200 grade concrete, curing and finishing complete. Supporting members shall be properly anchored and aligned before concreting.

  • The contractor shall provide all labour, scaffolding, tools, tackles, machinery, safety arrangements and consumables necessary for proper execution of work complete in all respects.

sections.title: Mode of Measurement & Payment
sections.description:
• Payment shall be made at the accepted contract rate per square metre of completed and approved work measured as above.
  • The rate shall be full compensation for supply of all materials, fabrication, transportation, loading/unloading, erection, fixing, concrete foundation, labour, tools & plants, scaffolding, fasteners, sealants, welding, primer, painting, curing, taxes, royalties and all operations necessary to complete the work as per specifications, approved drawings and directions of Engineer-in-Charge.

  • No extra payment shall be made for overlaps, wastage, cutting, lifting, staging, temporary supports, fastening accessories, fabrication details or any incidental works required for proper completion of the item.

    The rate shall be for a unit of One sq. meter.

Description: Providing and fixing curtain wall in front of concurse area i.e. below canopy using powder coated alluminium rectangular box pipe of verious section as per strip theme. Fixed with column as well as beams with clamps & fastening bolt etc.comp. also including ACP sheet patches of approved design presenting the theme of waves as directed by architect.

sections.title: Material
sections.description:
• The curtain wall system shall consist of powder coated aluminium rectangular box sections of approved size, thickness and configuration as per approved architectural strip/wave theme design and drawings. The aluminium sections shall be of approved make, extruded from high strength aluminium alloy conforming to relevant IS specifications and suitable for exterior architectural applications.

  • The aluminium members shall be powder coated with approved shade and finish having minimum coating thickness of 60 microns or as approved by Engineer-in-Charge/Architect. The surface finish shall be uniform, smooth and free from defects such as cracks, blisters, peeling or discoloration.

  • The supporting accessories such as cleats, brackets, clamps, anchor fasteners, stainless steel bolts, nuts, washers, sleeves and fixing hardware shall be of approved quality and corrosion resistant.

  • ACP (Aluminium Composite Panel) sheet patches shall be of approved make, colour, texture and thickness as approved by Architect/Engineer-in-Charge. The ACP sheets shall be weather resistant, exterior grade and suitable for decorative architectural cladding work. The ACP patches shall be fabricated and fixed in required wave pattern/theme as shown in approved drawings.

  • Necessary sealants, gaskets, adhesives and accessories required for complete installation shall be of approved make and compatible with aluminium and ACP surfaces.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall be executed strictly as per approved architectural drawings, strip theme pattern, manufacturer’s specifications and directions of Architect/Engineer-in-Charge.

  • The aluminium rectangular box sections shall be accurately cut, fabricated, assembled and erected in true line, level, plumb and alignment to achieve the required wave/strip architectural appearance. All joints shall be properly aligned and rigidly fixed.

  • The curtain wall framing shall be securely fixed to RCC/steel columns and beams using approved clamps, cleats, anchor fasteners, bolts and fixing arrangements complete. Necessary drilling, cutting, welding (wherever required), grinding and fitting shall be carried out carefully without damaging adjacent surfaces.

  • ACP sheet patches shall be cut, bent and fixed accurately in approved wave theme design with proper alignment, spacing and finishing. All exposed edges shall be neatly finished. Necessary backing support framework, adhesive tapes, sealants and fixing accessories required for complete installation shall be included in the work.

  • All exposed aluminium surfaces shall be cleaned after installation and protected against scratches, dents or damages during execution. Damaged or distorted sections/panels shall not be accepted.

  • The contractor shall provide all scaffolding, staging, labour, tools & plants, lifting equipment, safety arrangements and consumables required for proper completion of work.

sections.title: Mode Of Measurement & Payment
sections.description:
• The curtain wall work shall be measured in square metre of actual visible surface area fixed at site and approved by Engineer-in-Charge. 

  • Measurement shall include aluminium framing system, powder coating, clamps, brackets, anchor fasteners, bolts, ACP decorative patches, fabrication, cutting, bending, fixing, sealants, scaffolding and all necessary accessories required for complete installation.

  • No separate measurement shall be made for overlaps, wastage, cutting, drilling, bends, grooves, supports, edge finishing, temporary supports, fasteners or any incidental works required for completion of item.

  • Openings within the curtain wall area up to 0.50 sqm shall not be deducted. Larger openings shall be deducted and jambs, soffits and sills shall not be measured separately unless otherwise specified.

  • Payment shall be made at the accepted contract rate per square metre of completed and approved curtain wall work measured as above.

  • The rate shall include cost of supply of all materials, aluminium sections, powder coating, ACP sheets, clamps, fasteners, fabrication, erection, fixing, sealants, scaffolding, labour, tools & plants, transportation, loading/unloading, lifting, staging, taxes, royalties and all incidental expenses necessary to complete the work as per approved drawings, specifications and directions of Architect/Engineer-in-Charge.

  • No extra payment shall be made for cutting, wastage, overlaps, curved profiles, wave patterns, temporary supports, edge finishing, lifting arrangements or any ancillary work necessary for satisfactory completion of the item.

  • The rate shall be for a unit of One sq. meter.

Description: Removing dry or oil bound distemper by a washing and scraping and sand papering the wall surface smooth including necessary repairs to scratches complete.

sections.title: Materials & Workmanship
sections.description: •         All loose pieces and scales shall be removed by sand papering and surface shall be cleared of all greascay. dust, dirt, etc. On decorated wall surfaces. Where heavy scaling has taken place, the entire surface shall be scrapped by means of steel scrappers so as to remove all accumulated distemper, leaving clean surfaces. Necessary repairs to the scratches shall be made as directed.

sections.title: Mode of measurements and payment
sections.description:
•            All the work shall be measured in the decimal system as under :

  •        (a)  Dimensions shall be measured to be nearest 0.01. M.

  •        (b) Area in individual items shall be worked out to the nearest 0.01 Sq.M.

  •        All the walls shall be measured in sq. mt. Deductions for jambs, soffits, sills etc. for openings not exceeding 0.5 sq.mt. each in area, for ends of joints, posts, beams, girders, steps etc. not exceeding 0.5 sq. mt. each in area and for openings exceeding 0.5 sq.mt. and not. exceeding 3.0 sq. mi. each in area, deductions and additions shall be made as under :

  •        No deductions shall be made for ends of joists, beams, posts, etc. and openings not exceeding o„5 sq. nit. each. No addition shall be made for reveals, jambs, soffits, sills etc. of these openings nor for finish around ends of joints, beams, posts, etc.Deductionsforopeningsexceeding0.5sq.mt.butnotexceeding3sq.mt.eachshallbemadeas follows and no addition will be made for reveals, jambs, soffits, etc. of these openings:

  •       (a) When both the faces of walls are provided with finish, deduction shall be made for one faceonly.

  •       (b) When each face of wall is provided with a different finish, deduction shall be made for that side of frame for door, windows, etc. on which width of reveals is less than that of the other wise, where width of reveals on both faces of wall are equal, deduction of 50% of area of opening on each face shall be made from total area of finish.

  •      (c) When only one face of wall is treated and the otlie lace is not treated, full deduction shall be made if the width of reveal on the treated side is less than that on the untreated side, but if the width of the reveal is equal or more than on the untreated side neither deductions not additions to be made for reveals, jambs, soffits, sills etc. In case of area of openings exceeding 3 sq. mt. each, deduction shall be made for openings but jambs, soffits, sills shall be measured. No deductions shall be made for attachment such as casing, conducts, pipe, electric wiring and the like. Corrugated surfaces shall be measured flat as fixed and not girth.

  •         The quantities so measured shall be increased by the following percentage and the resultant shall be included with the general areas:

    (a)            Corrugated steel sheets. 14%

    (b)            Corrugated A.C.Sheets. 20%

    (c)            Semi corrugated A.C. Sheets. 10%

    (d)            Nainital pattern roof (Plain sheeting with rolls) 10%

    (e)            Nainital pattern roof (with corrugated sheets) 25%

  •      Cornices and other wall features, when they are not picked out in a different finish/colour shall be girthed and included in the general area. The rate shall include the cost of all materials, labour, scaffolding, protective measures etc. involved in all the operations described above.

  •     The rate shall be,for a unit of One sq. metre.

Description: Box cutting the road surface to proper slope and camber for making a base for road work including removing the excavated stuff and depositing on the road side slope as directed upto all Lead & Lift.

sections.title: Material
sections.description:
• No material shall generally be required for this item except use of water for dust suppression and compaction wherever directed by Engineer-in-Charge.

  • The work shall involve excavation of existing road crust, soil, murum, gravel or other road surface material to the required depth, width, slope and camber as shown in drawings or as directed by Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The existing road surface shall be cut and excavated to the required lines, grades, levels, slope and camber for preparation of road formation/base for further pavement work.

  • The work shall be carried out using suitable machinery such as excavator, grader, road cutting machine or manually wherever required. Before commencement of excavation, necessary setting out and marking shall be done.

  • The excavation shall be carried out carefully to avoid disturbance to adjacent structures, utilities or finished road portions. The finished surface after box cutting shall be properly dressed, trimmed and compacted to required profile and camber. Soft spots, loose material or unsuitable strata encountered during excavation shall be removed and disposed as directed by Engineer-in-Charge.

  • The excavated material shall be removed simultaneously and deposited along roadside slopes or at locations as directed by Engineer-in-Charge including all lead and lift involved.

  • Necessary barricading, diversion arrangements, traffic safety measures, warning signs and lighting during execution shall be provided by contractor at his own cost.

  • The contractor shall arrange all labour, machinery, fuel, tools & plants, watering, dressing and other incidental operations required for proper completion of work.

sections.title: Mode of Measurement & Payment
sections.description:
• The box cutting shall be measured in cubic metre based on actual quantity of excavation carried out from existing road surface to required depth, width, slope and camber as approved by Engineer-in-Charge.

  • The quantity shall be calculated from measured dimensions before and after excavation.

  • The rate shall include excavation, dressing, trimming, maintaining required slope and camber, loading, unloading, removing excavated material, depositing on roadside slope or directed location, all lead and lift, barricading, traffic management, labour, machinery, fuel, tools & plants and all incidental charges necessary for completion of work.

  • No separate payment shall be made for dressing, trimming, watering, traffic diversion, dewatering, temporary supports or disposal within all leads and lifts.

  • The rate shall be for a unit of One cubic meter.

Description: Providing & Laying cement concrete M-250 for all type of R.C.C. Work using 12 to 20 mm size black trap metal of approved quality as an aggregate incl. watering, curing, scaffolding, centering incl. cost of formwork and using machine mixed design cement concrete & compacted with vibrators incl. finishing the surface etc. as directed as per detailed drawing & design & as instructed by the engineer incharge etc.complete.(A) Ground Beam

sections.title: Materials
sections.description: • Water shall conform to M-1. Cement shall conform to M-3. Sand shall conform to M-6. Grit shall conform to M-8 Course aggregate shall conform M-12.

subsections.title: General
subsections.description:
• The concrete mix is not required to be designed by preliminary testes. The proportion of the concrete mix shall be 1:2:4 (1 cement : 2 coarse sand : 4 graded stone aggregate 20 mm. nominal size) by volume concrete work shall have exposed concrete surface or as specified in the item.
  • The designation ordinary M-100, M-150, M-200, M-250 specified as per I.S. correspond approximately to 1:3:6, 1.2:4, 1:1:1/2:3 and 1:1:2 nominal mix of ordinary concrete by volume respectively.
  • The water cement ratios shall not be more than specified in the above table. The cement content of the mix specified in the table shall be increased if the quantity of water in mix has to be met eased to overcome the difficulties of placements and compaction so that the water-cement ratio specified in the table is not exceeded.
  • Workability of the concrete shall be controlled by maintaining a water -cement-ratio that is found to give a concrete mix which is just sufficient wet to be placed and compacted without difficulty with the means available.
  • The maximum size of course aggregate shall be as large as possible within the limits specified but in no case greater than one forth of the minimum thickness of the member provided that the concrete can be placed without difficulty so as to surround all reinforcement thoroughly and to fill the corners of the form. 
  • For reinforced concrete work; coarse aggregates having a nominal size of 20 mm. are generally considered satisfactory.
  • For heavily reinforced concrete members as in the case of ribs of main beams, the nominal maximum size of coarse aggregate should usually be restricted to 5 mm. less than the minimum clear distance between the main bar or 5 mm. less than the minimum cover to the reinforcement whichever is smaller.
  • Where the reinforcement is widely spaced as in solid slabs, limitations of size of the aggregate may not be so important, and the nominal maximum size may some times be as great as or greater than the minimum cover.
  • Admixture maybe used in concrete only with approval of Engineer-in-charge based upon the evidence that with the passage of time neither the compressive strength of concrete is reduced not are other requisite qualities of concrete and steel impaired by the use of such admixtures.

subsections.title: Workmanship
subsections.description: • Proportioning shall be done by volume, except which shall be measured in terms of bags of 50 kg. weight, the volume of one such bag being taken as 0.0342 cu. meter Boxes of suitable size shall be used for measuring sand aggregate. The size of boxes (internal) shall be 35 x 25 cms. and 40 cms deep while measuring the aggregate and sand the boxes shall be filled without shaking ramming or hammering. The proportioning of sand shall be on the basis of its dry volume and in case of damp saner, allowances for bulk age shall be made.

subsections.title: Mixing
subsections.description:
• The concrete shall be handed from the place, of mixing to the final position in not more than 15 minutes by the method as directed and shall be placed into its final-position, compacted and finished within 30 minutes of mixing with water i.e. before the setting commences.
  • The concrete shall be laid in layers of 15 cms. to 20 cms.
  • For all work, concrete shall be mixed in a mechanical mixed which along with other accessories shall be. kept in first class working condition and so maintained throughout the construction Measured quantity of aggregate, sand and cement required for each batch shall be poured into the claim of the mechanical mixer while it is continuously running. After half a minute of dry mixing measured quantity of water required for each batch of concrete mix shall be added gradually and mixing continued for another one and a half minute Mixing shall be continued till materials are uniformly distributed and uniform colour of the entire mass is obtained and each individual particle of the coarse aggregate shows complete coating of mortar containing its proportionate amount of cement. In no case shall the mixing he done for less than 2 minutes after-oil ingredients have been put into the mixer.
  • When hand mixing is permitted by the Engineer-in-charge for small jobs or for certain other reasons, it shall be done on the smooth watertight platform large enough to allow efficient tuning over the ingredients of concrete before and after adding water Mixing platform shall be so arranged that no foreign malarial gets mixed with concrete nor does the mixing water flow out. Cement in required number of bags shall be spread in n layer of uniform thickness on the mixing platform. Dry coarse and fine aggregate and cement shall then be mixed thoroughly be turning over to get a mixture to uniform colour. Specified quantity water shall then be added gradually through a rose can and the mass turned over till a mix of required consistency is obtained. In hand mixing quantity of cement shall be increased by 10 percent above that specified.
  • Mixers which haw been out of use for more than 30 minutes shall be thoroughly cleaned before putting in a new batch. Unless otherwise agreed to by the Engineer in-charge the first batch of concrete from the mixture shall contain only two thirds of normal quantity of coarse aggregate Mixing plant shall be thoroughly cleaned before changing from one type of cement to another.

subsections.title: Consistency
subsections.description: • The degree of consistency which shall depend upon the nature of the work and methods of vibration of concrete, shall be determined by regular slump tests in accordance with I.S. 1199-193. The skimp of 10 mm. to 25 mm shall be adopted when vibrators are used and 80 mm. when vibrators are not used.

subsections.title: Inspection
subsections.description:
• Contractor shall give the Engineer-in-charge due notice before placing any concrete in the forms to permit him to inspect and accept the false work and forms as to their strength, alignment and general fitness but such inspection shall not relieve the contractor of his responsibility for the safely of men machinery materials and for results obtained immediately before concreting all forms shall be thoroughly cleaned.
  • Centering design and its erection shall be got approved from the engineer-in-charge. One carpenter with helper shall invariably be kept present throughout the period of concreting. Movement of labour and other persons shall be totally prohibited for reinforcement laid in position. For access to different parts suitable mobile platforms shall be provided so that steel reinforcement in position is not disturbed. For ensuring proper cover, mortar blocks of suitable size shall be cast and tied to the reinforcement. Timber kapachi or metal pieces shall not be used for this purpose.

subsections.title: Transporting and laying
subsections.description:
• The method of transporting and placing concrete shall be as approved. Concrete shall be so transported and placed that no contamination, segregation or loss of its constituent material takes place. All from work shall be cleaned and made free from standing   water   dust,   show   or   ice   immediately   before   placing   of   concrete. No concrete shall be placed in any part of the structure until the approval of the engineer-in-charge has been obtained.
  • Concreting shall proceed continuously over the area between construction joints. Fresh concrete proper contraction joint is formed. Concrete shall be compacted in its final position within 30 minutes of its discharge from the mixer. Except where otherwise agreed to by the engineer-in-charge, concrete shall be deposited in horizontal layers to a compacted depth of not more than 0.45 meter when internal vibrators are used and not exceeding 0.30 meter in all other cases.
  • Unless otherwise agreed to by the Engineer-in-charge concrete shall be dropped in to place from a height exceeding 2 meters. When trucking or chutes are used they shall be kept close and used in such a way as to avoid segregation. When concreting has to be resumed on a surface which has hardened, it shall be roughened, swept clean, thoroughly wetted and covered with a 13 mm. thick layer of mortar composed of cement and sand in the same ratio as in the concrete mix itself. This 13 mm. layer of mortar shall be freshly mixed and placed immediately before placing of new concrete. Where concrete has not fully hardened, all lateness shall be removed by scrubbing the wet surface with wire or bristle brushes, care being taken to avoid dislodgement of any particles of coarse aggregate. The surface shall then be thoroughly wetted, all free water removed and then coated with neat cement grout. The first layer of concrete to be placed on this surface shall not exceed 150 mm. in thickness and shall be well rammed against old work, particular attention being given to corners and close spots.
  • All concrete shall be compacted to produce a dense homogeneous mass with the assistance of vibrators, unless otherwise permitted by the Engineer-in-charge for exceptional cases, such as concreting under water, where vibrators cannot be used. Sufficient vibrators in serviceable condition shall be kept at site so that spare equipment is always available in the even of breakdowns. Concrete shall be judged to be compacted when the mortar fills the spaces between the coarse aggregate and begins to cream up to form an even surface. Compaction shall be completed before the initial setting stats i.e. within 30 minutes of addition of water to dry mixture. During compaction, it shall be observed that needle vibrators are not applied on reinforcement which is likely to destroy the bond between concrete and reinforcement.

subsections.title: Curing
subsections.description: • Immediately after compaction, concrete weather including rain, running water, shocks, vibration, traffic, rapid temperature charges, frost and drying out process. It shall be covered with wet sacking has Sian or other similar absorbent material approved, soon after the initial set, and shall be kept continuously wet for a period of not less than 14 days from the date of placement. Masonry work over foundation concrete may be started after 48 hours of its laying but curing of concrete shall be continued for a minimum period of 14 days.

subsections.title: Sampling and testing of concrete
subsections.description:
• Samples from fresh concrete shall betaken as per I.S. 1199-1959 and cubes shall be made, cured and tested at 7 days of 28 days as per requirements in accordance with I.S. 526-1959. A random sampling procedure shall be adopted to ensure that each concrete batch shall have a reasonable chance of being tested i.e. the sampling should be spread over the entire period of concreting and cover all mixing units. The minimum frequency of sampling of concrete of each grade shall be in accordance with following:
    Quantity Of Concrete in Work No. Of Samples
     1 - 5 Cmt 1
     6 - 15 Cmt 2
     16  30 Cmt 3
     31 - 50 Cmt 4
  • Note :  At least one simple shall be taken from each shift, Ten test specimens shall be made from each sample, five for testing at 7 days and the remaining five at 28 days. The samples of concrete shall be taken on each day of concreting as per above frequency. The number of specimens may be suitably increased  as  deemed  necessary  by  the  Engineer-in-charge  when  procedure  of  tests  given  above reveals a poor quality of concrete and in other special cases.
  • The average of the group of cubes cast for each day shall not be less than the specified cube strength of 150 K/g Cm 2 at 28 days. 20% of the cubes cast for each day may have value less than the specified strength provided the lowest value is not less than 85% of the specified strength. If the concrete made in accordance with the proportions given for a particular grade does not yield the specified strength, such concrete shall be classified as belonging to the appropriate lower grade. Concrete made in accordance with the Proportions given for a particular grade shall not, however be placed in a higher grade on the ground that the test strength are higher then the minimum specified.

subsections.title: Stripping
subsections.description:
• The Engineer-in-charge shall be informed in advance by the contractor of hr> intention to strike the form work. Adequate arrangement shall be made by the Contractor to safe guard against any settlements of the formwork during the course of concreting and after concreting.

subsections.title: Centering
subsections.description:
• The centering, which has been got approved should be sufficiently strong and safe before, during and after pouring concrete and should be so erected that it would allow removal of forms in proper sequence without damaging either the concrete or the forms to be removed.
  • The props of centering shall be provided on firm foundation or base of sufficient strength to carry the loads, without any settlement.

subsections.title: Scaffolding
subsections.description:
• All scaffolding, hoisting arrangements and ladders etc, required for facilitating of concrete shall be provided and removed on completion work by Contractor, at his own expense. The scaffolding, hoisting arrangement, ladders etc shall be strong enough to withstand all live, dead and impact loads expected to act. The Contractor shall be solely responsible for the safety of the scaffolding, hoisting arrangement, ladders, work and workmen etc.
  • The scaffolding, hoisting arrangement and ladders shall allow easy approach to the work spot and afford easy inspection.

subsections.description: • The degree of consistency which shall depend upon the nature of the work and methods of vibration of concrete, shall be determined by regular slump tests in accordance with I.S. 1199-193.   • All concrete shall be compacted to produce a dense homogeneous mass with the assistance of vibrators, unless otherwise permitted by the Engineer-in-charge for exceptional cases, such as concreting under water, where vibrators cannot be used. Sufficient vibrators in serviceable condition shall be kept at site so that spare equipment is always available in the even of breakdowns. subsections.description: • Immediately after compaction, concrete weather including rain, running water, shocks, vibration, traffic, rapid temperature charges, frost and drying out process. It shall be covered with wet sacking has Sian or other similar absorbent material approved, soon after the initial set, and shall be kept continuously wet for a period of not less than 14 days from the date of placement. Masonry work over foundation concrete may be started after 48 hours of its laying but curing of concrete shall be continued for a minimum period of 14 days.

subsections.description:

Cement in required number of bags shall be spread in n layer of uniform thickness on the mixing platform. Dry coarse and fine aggregate and cement shall then be mixed thoroughly be turning over to get a mixture to uniform colour. Specified quantity water shall then be added gradually through a rose can and the mass turned over till a mix of required consistency is obtained. In hand mixing quantity of cement shall be increased by 10 percent above that specified.
  • Mixers which haw been out of use for more than 30 minutes shall be thoroughly cleaned before putting in a new batch. Unless otherwise agreed to by the Engineer in-charge the first batch of concrete from the mixture shall contain only two thirds of normal quantity of coarse aggregate Mixing plant shall be thoroughly cleaned before changing from one type of cement to another.

subsections.title: Consistency
subsections.description: • The degree of consistency which shall depend upon the nature of the work and methods of vibration of concrete, shall be determined by regular slump tests in accordance with I.S. 1199-193. The skimp of 10 mm. to 25 mm shall be adopted when vibrators are used and 80 mm. when vibrators are not used.

subsections.title: Inspection
subsections.description:
• Contractor shall give the Engineer-in-charge due notice before placing any concrete in the forms to permit him to inspect and accept the false work and forms as to their strength, alignment and general fitness but such inspection shall not relieve the contractor of his responsibility for the safely of men machinery materials and for results obtained immediately before concreting all forms shall be thoroughly cleaned.
  • Centering design and its erection shall be got approved from the engineer-in-charge. One carpenter with helper shall invariably be kept present throughout the period of concreting. Movement of labour and other persons shall be totally prohibited for reinforcement laid in position. For access to different parts suitable mobile platforms shall be provided so that steel reinforcement in position is not disturbed. For ensuring proper cover, mortar blocks of suitable size shall be cast and tied to the reinforcement. Timber kapachi or metal pieces shall not be used for this purpose.

subsections.title: Transporting and laying
subsections.description:
• The method of transporting and placing concrete shall be as approved. Concrete shall be so transported and placed that no contamination, segregation or loss of its constituent material takes place. All from work shall be cleaned and made free from standing   water   dust,   show   or   ice   immediately   before   placing   of   concrete. No concrete shall be placed in any part of the structure until the approval of the engineer-in-charge has been obtained.
  • Concreting shall proceed continuously over the area between construction joints. Fresh concrete proper contraction joint is formed. Concrete shall be compacted in its final position within 30 minutes of its discharge from the mixer. Except where otherwise agreed to by the engineer-in-charge, concrete shall be deposited in horizontal layers to a compacted depth of not more than 0.45 meter when internal vibrators are used and not exceeding 0.30 meter in all other cases.
  • Unless otherwise agreed to by the Engineer-in-charge concrete shall be dropped in to place from a height exceeding 2 meters. When trucking or chutes are used they shall be kept close and used in such a way as to avoid segregation. When concreting has to be resumed on a surface which has hardened, it shall be roughened, swept clean, thoroughly wetted and covered with a 13 mm. thick layer of mortar composed of cement and sand in the same ratio as in the concrete mix itself. This 13 mm. layer of mortar shall be freshly mixed and placed immediately before placing of new concrete. Where concrete has not fully hardened, all lateness shall be removed by scrubbing the wet surface with wire or bristle brushes, care being taken to avoid dislodgement of any particles of coarse aggregate. The surface shall then be thoroughly wetted, all free water removed and then coated with neat cement grout. The first layer of concrete to be placed on this surface shall not exceed 150 mm. in thickness and shall be well rammed against old work, particular attention being given to corners and close spots.

Sufficient vibrators in serviceable condition shall be kept at site so that spare equipment is always available in the even of breakdowns. Concrete shall be judged to be compacted when the mortar fills the spaces between the coarse aggregate and begins to cream up to form an even surface. During compaction, it shall be observed that needle vibrators are not applied on reinforcement which is likely to destroy the bond between concrete and reinforcement.

subsections.title: Curing
subsections.description: • Immediately after compaction, concrete weather including rain, running water, shocks, vibration, traffic, rapid temperature charges, frost and drying out process. It shall be covered with wet sacking has Sian or other similar absorbent material approved, soon after the initial set, and shall be kept continuously wet for a period of not less than 14 days from the date of placement. Masonry work over foundation concrete may be started after 48 hours of its laying but curing of concrete shall be continued for a minimum period of 14 days.

subsections.title: Sampling and testing of concrete
subsections.description:
• Samples from fresh concrete shall betaken as per I.S. 1199-1959 and cubes shall be made, cured and tested at 7 days of 28 days as per requirements in accordance with I.S. 526-1959. A random sampling procedure shall be adopted to ensure that each concrete batch shall have a reasonable chance of being tested i.e. the sampling should be spread over the entire period of concreting and cover all mixing units. The minimum frequency of sampling of concrete of each grade shall be in accordance with following:
    Quantity Of Concrete in Work No. Of Samples
     1 - 5 Cmt 1
     6 - 15 Cmt 2
     16  30 Cmt 3
     31 - 50 Cmt 4
  • Note :  At least one simple shall be taken from each shift, Ten test specimens shall be made from each sample, five for testing at 7 days and the remaining five at 28 days. The samples of concrete shall be taken on each day of concreting as per above frequency. The number of specimens may be suitably increased  as  deemed  necessary  by  the  Engineer-in-charge  when  procedure  of  tests  given  above reveals a poor quality of concrete and in other special cases.
  • The average of the group of cubes cast for each day shall not be less than the specified cube strength of 150 K/g Cm 2 at 28 days. 20% of the cubes cast for each day may have value less than the specified strength provided the lowest value is not less than 85% of the specified strength. If the concrete made in accordance with the proportions given for a particular grade does not yield the specified strength, such concrete shall be classified as belonging to the appropriate lower grade. Concrete made in accordance with the Proportions given for a particular grade shall not, however be placed in a higher grade on the ground that the test strength are higher then the minimum specified.

subsections.title: Stripping

    Grade Concrete Compressive strength of 15 cms. cubes in Kg./Cmt. at 28 days, conducted in accordance with I.S. 516-1959.
    Preliminary test Min.    		 Work test Min.
    M-150 200 150
    M-200 260 200
    M-250 320 250
    M-300 380 300
    M-350 440 350
    M-400 500 400
  • In all cases, the 28 days compressive strength specified in above be the criteria for acceptance or rejection of the concrete. • All scaffolding, hoisting arrangements and ladders etc, required for facilitating of concrete shall be provided and removed on completion work by Contractor, at his own expense. The Contractor shall be solely responsible for the safety of the scaffolding, hoisting arrangement, ladders, work and workmen etc.

Adequate arrangement shall be made by the Contractor to safe guard against any settlements of the formwork during the course of concreting and after concreting.

subsections.description:
• The centering, which has been got approved should be sufficiently strong and safe before, during and after pouring concrete and should be so erected that it would allow removal of forms in proper sequence without damaging either the concrete or the forms to be removed.

subsections.title: Scaffolding

• All scaffolding, hoisting arrangements and ladders etc, required for facilitating of concrete shall be provided and removed on completion work by Contractor, at his own expense. The scaffolding, hoisting arrangement, ladders etc shall be strong enough to withstand all live, dead and impact loads expected to act. The Contractor shall be solely responsible for the safety of the scaffolding, hoisting arrangement, ladders, work and workmen etc.
  • The scaffolding, hoisting arrangement and ladders shall allow easy approach to the work spot and afford easy inspection.

  • The water cement ratios shall not be more than specified in the above table. subsections.description: • Proportioning shall be done by volume, except which shall be measured in terms of bags of 50 kg. weight, the volume of one such bag being taken as 0.0342 cu. meter Boxes of suitable size shall be used for measuring sand aggregate. The proportioning of sand shall be on the basis of its dry volume and in case of damp saner, allowances for bulk age shall be made.

subsections.title: Mixing
subsections.description:
• The concrete shall be handed from the place, of mixing to the final position in not more than 15 minutes by the method as directed and shall be placed into its final-position, compacted and finished within 30 minutes of mixing with water i.e. before the setting commences.
  • The concrete shall be laid in layers of 15 cms. to 20 cms.
  • For all work, concrete shall be mixed in a mechanical mixed which along with other accessories shall be. kept in first class working condition and so maintained throughout the construction Measured quantity of aggregate, sand and cement required for each batch shall be poured into the claim of the mechanical mixer while it is continuously running. After half a minute of dry mixing measured quantity of water required for each batch of concrete mix shall be added gradually and mixing continued for another one and a half minute Mixing shall be continued till materials are uniformly distributed and uniform colour of the entire mass is obtained and each individual particle of the coarse aggregate shows complete coating of mortar containing its proportionate amount of cement. In no case shall the mixing he done for less than 2 minutes after-oil ingredients have been put into the mixer.
  • When hand mixing is permitted by the Engineer-in-charge for small jobs or for certain other reasons, it shall be done on the smooth watertight platform large enough to allow efficient tuning over the ingredients of concrete before and after adding water Mixing platform shall be so arranged that no foreign malarial gets mixed with concrete nor does the mixing water flow out. Dry coarse and fine aggregate and cement shall then be mixed thoroughly be turning over to get a mixture to uniform colour. Specified quantity water shall then be added gradually through a rose can and the mass turned over till a mix of required consistency is obtained. In hand mixing quantity of cement shall be increased by 10 percent above that specified.
  • Mixers which haw been out of use for more than 30 minutes shall be thoroughly cleaned before putting in a new batch. Unless otherwise agreed to by the Engineer in-charge the first batch of concrete from the mixture shall contain only two thirds of normal quantity of coarse aggregate Mixing plant shall be thoroughly cleaned before changing from one type of cement to another.

subsections.title: Consistency
subsections.description: • The degree of consistency which shall depend upon the nature of the work and methods of vibration of concrete, shall be determined by regular slump tests in accordance with I.S. 1199-193. The skimp of 10 mm. to 25 mm shall be adopted when vibrators are used and 80 mm. when vibrators are not used.

subsections.title: Inspection
subsections.description:
• Contractor shall give the Engineer-in-charge due notice before placing any concrete in the forms to permit him to inspect and accept the false work and forms as to their strength, alignment and general fitness but such inspection shall not relieve the contractor of his responsibility for the safely of men machinery materials and for results obtained immediately before concreting all forms shall be thoroughly cleaned.
  • Centering design and its erection shall be got approved from the engineer-in-charge. One carpenter with helper shall invariably be kept present throughout the period of concreting. Movement of labour and other persons shall be totally prohibited for reinforcement laid in position. For access to different parts suitable mobile platforms shall be provided so that steel reinforcement in position is not disturbed. For ensuring proper cover, mortar blocks of suitable size shall be cast and tied to the reinforcement. Timber kapachi or metal pieces shall not be used for this purpose.

subsections.title: Transporting and laying
subsections.description:
• The method of transporting and placing concrete shall be as approved. Concrete shall be so transported and placed that no contamination, segregation or loss of its constituent material takes place. All from work shall be cleaned and made free from standing   water   dust,   show   or   ice   immediately   before   placing   of   concrete. No concrete shall be placed in any part of the structure until the approval of the engineer-in-charge has been obtained.
  • Concreting shall proceed continuously over the area between construction joints. Fresh concrete proper contraction joint is formed. Concrete shall be compacted in its final position within 30 minutes of its discharge from the mixer. Except where otherwise agreed to by the engineer-in-charge, concrete shall be deposited in horizontal layers to a compacted depth of not more than 0.45 meter when internal vibrators are used and not exceeding 0.30 meter in all other cases.
  • Unless otherwise agreed to by the Engineer-in-charge concrete shall be dropped in to place from a height exceeding 2 meters. When trucking or chutes are used they shall be kept close and used in such a way as to avoid segregation. When concreting has to be resumed on a surface which has hardened, it shall be roughened, swept clean, thoroughly wetted and covered with a 13 mm. thick layer of mortar composed of cement and sand in the same ratio as in the concrete mix itself. This 13 mm. layer of mortar shall be freshly mixed and placed immediately before placing of new concrete. Where concrete has not fully hardened, all lateness shall be removed by scrubbing the wet surface with wire or bristle brushes, care being taken to avoid dislodgement of any particles of coarse aggregate. The surface shall then be thoroughly wetted, all free water removed and then coated with neat cement grout. The first layer of concrete to be placed on this surface shall not exceed 150 mm. in thickness and shall be well rammed against old work, particular attention being given to corners and close spots.
  • All concrete shall be compacted to produce a dense homogeneous mass with the assistance of vibrators, unless otherwise permitted by the Engineer-in-charge for exceptional cases, such as concreting under water, where vibrators cannot be used. Sufficient vibrators in serviceable condition shall be kept at site so that spare equipment is always available in the even of breakdowns. Concrete shall be judged to be compacted when the mortar fills the spaces between the coarse aggregate and begins to cream up to form an even surface. Compaction shall be completed before the initial setting stats i.e. within 30 minutes of addition of water to dry mixture. During compaction, it shall be observed that needle vibrators are not applied on reinforcement which is likely to destroy the bond between concrete and reinforcement.

subsections.title: Curing
subsections.description: • Immediately after compaction, concrete weather including rain, running water, shocks, vibration, traffic, rapid temperature charges, frost and drying out process. It shall be covered with wet sacking has Sian or other similar absorbent material approved, soon after the initial set, and shall be kept continuously wet for a period of not less than 14 days from the date of placement. Masonry work over foundation concrete may be started after 48 hours of its laying but curing of concrete shall be continued for a minimum period of 14 days.

subsections.title: Sampling and testing of concrete
subsections.description:
• Samples from fresh concrete shall betaken as per I.S. 1199-1959 and cubes shall be made, cured and tested at 7 days of 28 days as per requirements in accordance with I.S. 526-1959. A random sampling procedure shall be adopted to ensure that each concrete batch shall have a reasonable chance of being tested i.e. the sampling should be spread over the entire period of concreting and cover all mixing units. The minimum frequency of sampling of concrete of each grade shall be in accordance with following:
    Quantity Of Concrete in Work No. Of Samples
     1 - 5 Cmt 1
     6 - 15 Cmt 2
     16  30 Cmt 3
     31 - 50 Cmt 4
  • Note :  At least one simple shall be taken from each shift, Ten test specimens shall be made from each sample, five for testing at 7 days and the remaining five at 28 days. The samples of concrete shall be taken on each day of concreting as per above frequency. The number of specimens may be suitably increased  as  deemed  necessary  by  the  Engineer-in-charge  when  procedure  of  tests  given  above reveals a poor quality of concrete and in other special cases.
  • The average of the group of cubes cast for each day shall not be less than the specified cube strength of 150 K/g Cm 2 at 28 days. 20% of the cubes cast for each day may have value less than the specified strength provided the lowest value is not less than 85% of the specified strength. If the concrete made in accordance with the proportions given for a particular grade does not yield the specified strength, such concrete shall be classified as belonging to the appropriate lower grade. Concrete made in accordance with the Proportions given for a particular grade shall not, however be placed in a higher grade on the ground that the test strength are higher then the minimum specified.

subsections.title: Stripping
subsections.description:
• The Engineer-in-charge shall be informed in advance by the contractor of hr> intention to strike the form work. While fixing  the  time  of  removal  of  form  work,  due  consideration  shall  be  given  to  local  conditions, character of the structure, the weather and other conditions that influence the setting of concrete and of the materials used in the mix. In normal circumstances (generally where temperatures are above 20.C) and where ordinary concrete is used, forms may be struck after expire or periods specified in item No.9.1 (A) for respective item of form work.
  • All form work shall be removed without causing any shock or vibration as would damage the concrete. Before the soft and struts are removed, the concrete surface shall be gradually exposed, where necessary in order to ascertain that concrete has sufficiently hardened. Centering shall be gradually and uniformly lowered in such a manner as to permit the concrete to take stresses due to its own weight uniformly and gradually. Where internal metal tiles are permitted, they or their removable parts shall be extracted without causing any damage to the concrete and remaining holes filled with mortar. No permanently embedded metal part shall have less than 25 mm. cover to the finished concrete surface. Where it is intended to re-use the form work, it shall be cleaned and made good to the satisfaction of the Engineer-in-charge. After removal of form work and shutting, the Executive Engineer shall inspect the work and satisfy by random checks that concrete produced is of good quality.
  • Immediately after the removal of forms, all exposed bolts etc. passing through the cement concrete member and used for stuttering or any other purpose shall be cut inside the cement concrete member to a depth of at least 25 m. below the surface of the concrete and the resulting holes be filled by cement mortar, all fins, caused by form joints, all cavities produced by the removal of form tiles and all other holes and depressions, honeycomb spots, broken edges or comers and other defects, shall be thoroughly cleaned", saturated with water and carefully pointed an rendered true with mortar of cement and fine aggregate mixed in proportions used in the grade of concrete that is being furnished and of as dry consistency as is possible to use. Considerable pressure shall be applied in filling and pointing to ensure through filling in all voids. Surface which are pointed shall be kept moist for a period of 24 hours. If rock pockets/honeycombs in the opinion of the Engineer-in-charge are of such an extent or character as to effect the strength of the structure materially or to endanger the life of the steel reinforcement, he may declare the concrete defective and require the removal and replacement of the portions of structure affected.
  • The Above specification of ordinary concrete shall be followed except that the concrete mix shall be designed form preliminary tests. The proportioning of cement and aggregates shall be done by weight and necessary precautions shall be taken in the production to ensure that the required work cube strength is attained and maintained. The controlled concrete shall be in grades of M-100, M-150, M-200, M-250, M-300, M-350 & M-400 with prefix controlled added to it. The letter M refers to mix and the numbers specify 28 days works cube compressive strength of 150 mm. cubes of the mix expressed in Kg./Crnt.

subsections.title: Proportion of Mix
subsections.description:
• The proportion of cement, sand and coarse aggregate shall be determined of weight. The weight batch machine shall be used for maintaining proper control over the proportion of aggregates as per mix design. The strength requirements of different grades of concrete shall be as under:
    Grade Concrete Compressive strength of 15 cms. cubes in Kg./Cmt. at 28 days, conducted in accordance with I.S. 516-1959.
    Preliminary test Min.    		 Work test Min.
    M-150 200 150
    M-200 260 200
    M-250 320 250
    M-300 380 300
    M-350 440 350
    M-400 500 400
  • In all cases, the 28 days compressive strength specified in above be the criteria for acceptance or rejection of the concrete. Where the strength of a concrete mix as indicated by tests, lies in between the strength of any two grades specified in the above table, such concrete shall be classified in for purpose as concrete belonging to the lower of the grades between which its strength lies.
  • The proportions for ingredients chosen shall be such that concrete has adequate workability for conditions prevailing on the work question and can be property compacted with means available except where ft can be shown to the satisfaction of the Engineer-in-charge, that supply of properly graded aggregate of uniform quality can be maintained till the completion of work, grading of aggregate shall be controlled by obtaining the coarse aggregates in different sizes and bending them in the right proportions as required. Aggregates of different sizes shall be stocked in separate stock piles. The required quantity of material shall be stock piled several hours, preferably a day before use. The grading of coarse and fine aggregate shall be checked as frequently as possible, the frequency for a given job being determined by Engineer-in-charge to ensure that the suppliers are maintaining the uniform grading as approved for samples used in the preliminary tests. 
  • In proportioning concrete, the quantity of both cement and aggregate shall be determined by weight. Where the weight of cement is determined by accepting the maker's weight per bag, a reasonable number of bags shall be weighted separately to check the net weight. Where cement is weighted form bulk stocks at site and not by bags, it shall be weighed separately from the aggregate. Water, shall either be measured by volume in calibrated tanks or weighed. All measuring equipment shall be maintained in clean, and serviceable condition. Their accuracy shall be periodically checked.
  • It is most important to keep the specified water cement ratio constant and at its correct value. To this end, moisture content in both fine and coarse aggregates shall be determined by the Engineer-in-charge according to the weather conditions. The amount of mixing water shall then be adjusted to compensate for variations in the moisture content. For the determination of moisture content in the aggregates. I.S. 2386 (Part-Ill) shall be referred to. Suitable adjustments shah also be made in the weights of aggregates due to variation in their moisture content. Minimum quantity of cement to be used in controlled concrete shall not be less than 220 kg./M-3 in plain concrete and not less than 250 kg/M-3 in reinforced concrete.
