Description: Cutting out cracks of roof terrace to V- section, cleaning out, wetting, grouting with cement and sand slurry 1:1 (1-Cement : 1-Sand) pest using grouting gun and applying fully pressure etc. complete.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description: • Cement shall be Ordinary Portland Cement conforming to IS 269, IS 8112 or IS 12269 as applicable and shall be fresh, dry and free from lumps. Fine sand shall conform to IS 383 and shall be clean, hard, durable and free from dust, clay, silt and organic impurities. Water used for mixing and curing shall conform to IS 456 and shall be clean and free from injurious salts, oils, acids and organic matter. If waterproofing compound or polymer additive is used, the same shall conform to IS 2645 and manufacturer’s specifications. All materials shall be approved by the Engineer-in-Charge prior to use.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall be executed in accordance with relevant provisions of IS 456, IS 9012 and standard engineering practice. Existing cracks in roof terrace shall be carefully inspected and marked. Cracks shall be cut into proper “V” groove shape using mechanical cutter or grinder to the required width and depth without damaging adjoining surface.
  • All loose mortar, laitance, dust and foreign materials shall be removed thoroughly by wire brushing, compressed air or water jet cleaning. The prepared groove shall be thoroughly wetted before application of grout while avoiding free standing water.
  • Cement sand grout in proportion 1:1 (1 Cement : 1 Fine Sand) shall be prepared to uniform consistency and injected/applied into cracks using suitable pressure grouting gun so as to ensure complete penetration and filling of cracks and voids. Grouting pressure shall be controlled to avoid damage to surrounding structure.
  • Excess grout shall be removed immediately and the finished surface shall be finished flush and smooth with adjoining surface. The repaired area shall be kept continuously moist and cured for minimum 7 days as per IS 456. All tools, equipment and workmanship shall be of approved quality and the completed work shall be sound, watertight and free from visible defects.

sections.title: Mode Of Measurement & Payment
sections.description:
• Measurement shall be carried out in accordance with IS 1200. The length of cracks treated shall be measured in Running Metre (RM) correct to nearest centimetre. No separate measurement shall be made for cutting grooves, cleaning, wetting, grouting, curing, scaffolding, tools and plants or incidental operations required for satisfactory completion of work. The rate shall include cost of all materials, labour, equipment, transportation, wastage and all leads and lifts complete.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one running meter.

Description: L.C. for removing the existing and refixing the precast rubbal dying interlocking concrete paver block incl. fixing the blocks by using penumatic compressed mechanical vibrator on 75mm thk. sand layer for levelling and filling the joint with sand etc. comp. as directed by engg. in charge.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall consist of carefully removing the existing precast rubble dyed interlocking concrete paver blocks without causing damage to adjacent blocks or surrounding works. The dismantled paver blocks shall be cleaned properly and stacked systematically for reuse.
  • The existing surface shall be prepared by removing loose materials, debris and uneven portions. A 75 mm thick layer of approved sand shall then be spread uniformly, watered lightly if required and properly levelled to the required line, grade and camber.
  • The cleaned paver blocks shall be refixed manually in proper alignment and pattern as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge. The laid blocks shall be compacted using pneumatic compressed mechanical vibrator/plate compactor until the blocks are properly seated and interlocked uniformly.
  • After compaction, dry fine sand shall be spread over the surface and broomed into joints completely to fill all gaps between blocks. Additional sand shall be applied wherever necessary after vibration. The finished surface shall be true to line, level and slope and free from irregularities, depressions or projections. Broken or damaged blocks shall be replaced by the contractor at no extra cost.

  •

sections.title: Mode Of Measurement & Payment
sections.description:
• The rate shall include careful dismantling, stacking, cleaning, relaying, preparation of sand bed, providing and spreading 75 mm thick sand layer, compacting with pneumatic compressed mechanical vibrator, joint filling with sand, replacement of minor damaged blocks, labour, tools and plants, all leads and lifts and all incidental charges complete. No separate payment shall be made for cutting, alignment, wastage, curing or joint filling operations.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one square meter.

Description: Providing and applying 3 coats water proofing system over existing China mosaic terrace flooring using elastomeric waterproofing coating includes cleaning of surface, primercoat ,crackfilling with PU sealant and 2 coats of water proofing as per manufacturer specs. Application wit brush/ roller in cross directions. All materials, labour, tools and curing included.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• Elastomeric waterproofing coating shall be acrylic/polymer based waterproofing material of approved make conforming to relevant provisions of IS 2645, IS 16506 and manufacturer’s specifications. Primer shall be compatible with the waterproofing system and recommended by the manufacturer. PU sealant used for crack filling shall be of approved grade suitable for terrace waterproofing applications and shall conform to relevant ASTM/IS standards wherever applicable.
  • Water used for surface preparation and curing shall conform to IS 456. Brushes, rollers and application tools shall be of approved quality suitable for elastomeric coating application. All materials shall be brought to site in original sealed containers bearing manufacturer’s name, batch number and specifications.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The existing China mosaic terrace surface shall first be thoroughly cleaned by wire brushing, scraping and washing to remove dust, dirt, algae, loose particles, grease and all foreign materials. The surface shall be made sound, dry and free from laitance before application of waterproofing treatment.
  • Visible cracks, joints and damaged portions shall be opened properly, cleaned and filled with approved PU sealant as per manufacturer’s recommendations. After curing of sealant, compatible primer coat shall be applied uniformly over the entire surface at the specified coverage rate and allowed to dry completely.
  • Thereafter, elastomeric waterproofing coating shall be applied in minimum three coat system consisting of one primer coat and two finishing coats or as specified by manufacturer. The coating shall be applied uniformly by brush or roller in cross directions to ensure proper film formation and full coverage without pinholes, air bubbles or undulations. Each successive coat shall be applied only after proper drying of previous coat.
  • The waterproofing coating shall be extended over junctions, corners, khurras and parapet portions as directed by Engineer-in-Charge. The finished surface shall form a seamless, flexible and watertight membrane capable of resisting weathering and thermal movements.
  • The contractor shall follow manufacturer’s specifications regarding mixing, drying time, coverage, curing and application conditions. The completed work shall be protected from rain, dust and mechanical damage during curing period.

sections.title: Mode Of Measurement & Payment
sections.description:
• No deduction shall be made for openings up to 0.50 sqm. The rate shall include cleaning of surface, preparation, crack treatment with PU sealant, primer application, application of all waterproofing coats, labour, tools and plants, scaffolding, curing, all leads and lifts and incidental charges complete. No separate payment shall be made for overlaps, edge treatment, surface preparation or protection during curing.

    • The rate shall be for a unit of one square meter.

Description: l.c for repairing existing acp sheet of any size and height with all types of acticities / charges including stacking at site etc all directed by engineer incharge. ( measurement should be roofing area)

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• Existing Aluminium Composite Panel (ACP) sheets, aluminium sections, cleats, fasteners and accessories required for repair work shall conform to relevant provisions of IS 733, IS 1285 and manufacturer’s specifications. Replacement screws, rivets, anchor fasteners, sealants, weather silicone and fixing accessories, wherever required during repair, shall be of approved quality compatible with existing ACP system. Any damaged ACP sheet beyond repair shall be replaced only if directed by Engineer-in-Charge and shall match the existing colour, thickness, finish and pattern.

  • Scaffolding, safety belts, ropes, lifting arrangements and tools used for work at height shall conform to standard safety practices and relevant IS safety provisions.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall consist of carefully dismantling, adjusting, repairing and refixing existing ACP sheets of any size, shape and at any height including all necessary operations required for restoring the ACP cladding/roofing system to proper condition.
  • The ACP sheets shall be handled carefully to avoid scratches, dents or damage to adjoining panels, framing members and building components. Necessary scaffolding, staging, ladders, cranes or lifting devices shall be arranged by the contractor for execution of work safely at all heights.
  • The defective ACP sheets shall be removed carefully wherever required, cleaned and repaired by rectifying bends, loose fixing arrangements, damaged joints, sealant failures, alignment defects or other defects as directed by Engineer-in-Charge. The repaired sheets shall then be properly refixed in true line and level using approved fasteners, cleats, rivets and sealants.
  • All removed materials shall be stacked properly at site as directed. The finished ACP surface shall be properly aligned, securely fixed, weatherproof and free from visible waviness, gaps or loose portions. The contractor shall take adequate precautions to prevent water leakage and ensure safety of workers and surrounding property during execution.
  •

sections.title: Mode Of Measurement & Payment
sections.description:
• Measurement shall be carried out in Square Metre (Sqm) based on the actual roofing/cladding surface area repaired and accepted by the Engineer-in-Charge. No separate measurement shall be made for dismantling, stacking, scaffolding, lifting arrangements, sealant application, fasteners, alignment correction, cutting, refixing or other incidental operations. The rate shall include execution of work at all heights, all leads and lifts, labour, tools and plants and complete repair work as directed by Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one square meter.

Description: Preparing surface by brushing with wire brush for removing caked mud. Etc. incl. clearing water bound mecadum surface incl. serrping with brooms and finaly fanning the cleaned surface with air blower and with gunney hags to remove all loose durt etc. comp. incl. preparing surface by 1 coat using 13 kg bitumin tack coat using paving bitumin tack coat using 13 kg bitumin per 10 sc,mt of suraface incl. rolling the surface by 10 to 12 mt cap. road roller etc. comp. as directed by engg. incharge.

sections.title: Material
sections.description:
• Bitumen for tack coat shall be paving bitumen conforming to IS 73 of approved grade suitable for road works and climatic conditions. The binder shall be fresh, homogeneous and free from impurities. Water, if required for cleaning purposes, shall conform to relevant standards and shall be free from harmful contaminants.
  • Tools and equipment such as wire brushes, brooms, air blowers, gunny bags and mechanical road rollers shall be of approved quality and in proper working condition. Road roller used for rolling shall be 10 to 12 metric tonne capacity conforming to MORTH specifications.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The existing Water Bound Macadam (WBM) surface shall first be prepared by removing all caked mud, dust, loose earth and foreign materials using wire brushes, hard brooms and manual scraping wherever necessary. The surface shall then be thoroughly swept and cleaned using brooms.
  • Final cleaning shall be carried out using air blower and gunny bags so as to remove all loose dust and fine particles completely and to obtain a dry, clean and properly prepared surface suitable for tack coat application.
  • After cleaning, tack coat shall be applied uniformly over the prepared surface using approved bitumen sprayer at the rate of 13 kg of paving bitumen per 10 square metre of surface area or as directed by Engineer-in-Charge. The bitumen shall be heated to the specified temperature and applied evenly to ensure proper bonding with subsequent layers.
  • After application of tack coat, the surface shall be rolled properly using 10 to 12 MT capacity road roller to achieve uniform spread and proper adhesion. Care shall be taken to avoid excess accumulation, streaking or uncovered portions. The work shall be executed in accordance with relevant provisions of MORTH Specifications for Road and Bridge Works and as directed by Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode Of Measurement & Payment
sections.description:
• Measurement shall be carried out in Square Metre (Sqm) for the actual surface area prepared and treated with tack coat. The rate shall include cleaning of WBM surface, brushing, brooming, air blowing, removal of loose dirt, supply and application of paving bitumen tack coat, heating, spraying, rolling with 10 to 12 MT roller, labour, tools and plants, fuel, all leads and lifts and incidental charges complete.
  • No separate payment shall be made for surface cleaning, heating of bitumen, rolling, traffic control, protection of finished work or wastage of materials.

Description: Providing & laying 25mm thick compacted carpet in one layer by hot mix plant & paver finish to proper grade and leval using 12 to 20mm size b.t. kapachi grade  vaeiety as per specification of  approved guary and special quality  approved by the engineer in charge precoated with 80/100 asphalt @ 4 % weight of mix using b.t. kapachi 0.375 cmt/10smt  with necessary tools, plants machinery etc. rollingthe surface with 8 to 10 M.T. capacity road roller using  4 % kerosone or socosol as may be approved by the engineer in charge etc. incl supplying & spreading sand or dust comp. as directed by the engineer in charge.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• Paving bitumen shall conform to IS 73 and shall be of VG-10 / 80-100 penetration grade or approved equivalent suitable for bituminous carpet work. Stone aggregates (B.T. Kapchi) of 12 mm to 20 mm size shall be hard, durable, clean and free from dust, clay and organic impurities and shall conform to IS 2386 and MORTH specifications. Aggregates shall be obtained from approved quarry and shall be of specified grade and quality approved by the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • Fine sand or stone dust used for blotting/seal coat preparation shall conform to IS 383. Kerosene or approved release agent such as Socosol used for roller application shall be of approved quality and used strictly as directed by Engineer-in-Charge.
  • All materials shall be tested and approved prior to use.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall consist of providing and laying 25 mm thick compacted bituminous carpet in single layer over properly prepared surface using hot mix plant and mechanical paver finisher.
  • The stone aggregates of 12 mm to 20 mm size shall be thoroughly dried and uniformly precoated with paving bitumen of approved grade at the rate of 4% by weight of total mix. The quantity of B.T. Kapchi shall be approximately 0.375 cubic metre per 10 square metre of finished surface area or as specified.
  • The bituminous mix shall be prepared in approved hot mix plant maintaining specified temperature and uniform coating of aggregates. The prepared mix shall be transported to site without segregation and laid by paver finisher to required line, level, grade and camber.
  • Immediately after laying, the surface shall be rolled with 8 to 10 MT capacity road roller commencing from edges towards centre until proper compaction and smooth finish are achieved. Roller wheels shall be lightly coated with approved quantity of kerosene or Socosol to prevent adhesion of mix. Excess application of kerosene shall not be permitted.
  • Necessary sand or stone dust shall be supplied and spread wherever required for finishing and blotting operations. The finished surface shall be uniform, dense, properly compacted and free from waves, depressions, segregation and surface defects.
  • The entire work shall be carried out as per relevant provisions of MORTH Specifications for Road and Bridge Works and as directed by Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode of Measurement & Payment
sections.description:
• Measurement shall be carried out in Metric Tonne (MT) for actual finished and compacted surface area of 25 mm thick bituminous carpet work. Thickness shall be measured after compaction.
  • The rate shall include supply of all materials, heating of bitumen and aggregates, preparation of mix in hot mix plant, transportation, laying with paver finisher, rolling with 8 to 10 MT road roller, application of kerosene or approved release agent, supply and spreading of sand/dust, labour, fuel, machinery, tools and plants, all leads and lifts and incidental charges complete.
  • No separate payment shall be made for surface correction, testing, wastage, traffic arrangements or rolling operations.

Description: Prov. & laying 12mm thick  compacted seal coat 1 layer by hot mix plant & finish to proper grade & leval using 6mm size b.t. kapachi grade veritified as per specification of approved quality & of special  qulity approved by the Engg. In charge precoating with 80-100 asphalt @ 5.50 % by weight of mix using b.t. kapachi 0.18 cmtper 10 sq.mt. necessary tools plants machinary etc. rolling the surface with 8 to 20 mt. capacityroad roller using 4 % kerosone or socosol as using as approved by the engg. in charge incl. spreading sand or stone dust on seal surface incl. cost of sand or stone dust. etc.comp. as directed.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• Paving bitumen shall conform to IS 73 and shall be of approved 80/100 penetration grade (VG-10 equivalent) suitable for seal coat works. Stone aggregates (B.T. Kapchi) of 6 mm nominal size shall conform to IS 2386 and MORTH specifications and shall be hard, durable, clean and free from dust, clay and organic impurities. Aggregates shall be procured from approved quarry and shall be of verified and approved quality.
  • Fine sand or stone dust used for blotting and surface finishing shall conform to IS 383 and shall be clean and dry. Kerosene or approved release agent such as Socosol used for roller wheels shall be of approved quality.
  • All materials shall be tested and approved by the Engineer-in-Charge before use.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall consist of providing and laying 12 mm thick compacted seal coat in single layer over prepared bituminous surface using hot mix plant and approved laying methods.
  • The 6 mm size stone aggregates shall be dried properly and uniformly precoated with paving bitumen of approved 80/100 grade at the rate of 5.50% by weight of total mix. The quantity of B.T. Kapchi shall be approximately 0.18 cubic metre per 10 square metre of finished surface area or as specified.
  • The bituminous mix shall be prepared in approved hot mix plant maintaining proper temperature control and uniform coating of aggregates. The prepared mix shall be transported carefully to site and spread uniformly to required grade and level without segregation.
  • The laid seal coat shall be compacted immediately using 8 to 10 MT capacity road roller or approved roller until proper compaction and smooth uniform surface are achieved. Roller wheels shall be lightly coated with approved quantity of kerosene or Socosol to prevent sticking of mix.
  • After rolling, fine sand or stone dust shall be spread uniformly over seal coat surface wherever required for blotting and finishing purposes. Excess loose material shall be removed after setting of surface.
  • The completed surface shall be smooth, properly compacted, watertight and free from waviness, depressions, streaking or uncovered patches. The work shall be executed in accordance with relevant MORTH Specifications for Road and Bridge Works and as directed by Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode Of Measurement & Payment
sections.description:
• Measurement shall be carried out in Metric Tonne (MT) for actual finished and compacted surface area of 12 mm thick seal coat work.
  • The rate shall include supply of all materials, heating and mixing of aggregates and bitumen, preparation in hot mix plant, transportation, laying, rolling with road roller, use of kerosene or approved release agent, spreading of sand or stone dust, labour, fuel, tools and plants, machinery, all leads and lifts and incidental charges complete.
  • No separate payment shall be made for heating, testing, surface finishing, wastage, traffic arrangements or rolling operations.

Description: providing & laying asphalt painting by mechinical on b.t. asphalt surface using asphalt at 10kg m3/10 m2 & Spreading stone dust at 0.13 c.mtr / 10 sqmtron Painted surface etc. complete as directed incl. operating cost of contractor own equipments transport cost. Fuel, lubricant, incl all labour & material charges etc.comp. incl cost of asphalt etc complete incl. preparing surface by brushing with wire for removing cacked mud incl.etc. sweeping with brooms  & finally fanning the cleaned  surface.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• Bitumen/asphalt used for painting shall conform to IS 73 and shall be of approved paving grade suitable for bituminous surface treatment works. Stone dust used for blotting shall conform to IS 383 and shall be clean, dry and free from clay, organic matter and deleterious substances.
  • Wire brushes, brooms, mechanical sprayers and other equipment used for surface preparation and application shall be of approved quality and in proper working condition. Fuel, lubricants and consumables required for operation of machinery shall be included in the item rate.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The existing bituminous (B.T.) surface shall first be thoroughly prepared by removing all caked mud, dust, loose earth and foreign materials using wire brushes, manual scraping and hard brooms. Final cleaning shall be carried out by fanning the surface manually or mechanically so as to obtain a clean, dry and dust-free surface suitable for asphalt painting.
  • After proper preparation of surface, asphalt/bitumen shall be heated to the specified temperature and applied uniformly over the prepared B.T. surface by mechanical sprayer at the rate of 10 kg per 10 square metre of surface area or as directed by Engineer-in-Charge.
  • Immediately after application of asphalt, clean and dry stone dust shall be spread uniformly over the painted surface at the rate of 0.13 cubic metre per 10 square metre of surface area to prevent sticking and to provide protective wearing finish.
  • The application shall be carried out evenly without streaking, ponding or uncovered patches. Necessary precautions shall be taken to avoid contamination by dust, moisture or traffic during execution. The finished surface shall be uniform, properly bonded and free from defects.
  • The work shall include operation of contractor’s own machinery, transportation, fuel, lubricants, labour, tools and plants and all incidental operations complete as directed by Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode Of Measurement & Payment
sections.description:
• Measurement shall be carried out in Square Metre (Sqm) for actual area of asphalt painting completed and accepted.
  • The rate shall include preparation and cleaning of existing B.T. surface, brushing with wire brush, broom sweeping, final fanning, heating and application of asphalt by mechanical means, spreading of stone dust, operation of equipment, transportation, fuel, lubricants, labour, tools and plants, all leads and lifts and incidental charges complete.
  • No separate payment shall be made for surface preparation, heating of asphalt, machinery operation, traffic control, wastage or cleaning after completion of work.

Description: Providing and fixing standared extruded of alluminium section of size 63.50 x 38.10 x 1.95 mm,@ Wt 1.094Kg / Rmt with colour anodized alluminium frame with 5 mm thick transparent bronze colour tinted float glass as details etc complete for Fix window.

sections.title: Material
sections.description:
• Aluminium sections shall be standard extruded sections conforming to IS 733 and IS 1285 with size 63.50 × 38.10 × 1.95 mm and weight approximately 1.094 kg per running metre or as approved. The aluminium frame shall be colour anodized/powder coated of approved shade and finish. Transparent bronze colour tinted float glass of 5 mm thickness shall conform to IS 14900 and shall be free from bubbles, waves and other visual defects.
  • All fixing accessories such as cleats, brackets, screws, rubber beading, neoprene packing, weather silicone sealant and fastening materials shall be of approved make and compatible with aluminium glazing system. All materials shall be approved by Engineer-in-Charge before installation.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall consist of providing, fabricating and fixing colour anodized aluminium frame for fixed windows using standard extruded aluminium sections of specified size and weight. The aluminium members shall be accurately cut, machined and assembled true to line, level and plumb with proper joints and rigid connections.
  • The frame shall be securely fixed to masonry, RCC or structural members using approved cleats, holdfasts, anchor fasteners and screws as required. Necessary rubber packing, glazing clips and weather sealants shall be provided to ensure watertight and airtight installation.
  • 5 mm thick transparent bronze colour tinted float glass shall be carefully fixed in aluminium frame with approved glazing beads and neoprene/rubber gaskets without distortion or damage to glass. The glass shall be properly aligned and fixed to avoid rattling, vibration or leakage.
  • All exposed aluminium surfaces shall be smooth, free from scratches, dents or fabrication marks. Joints shall be neatly finished and all corners properly sealed. Protective film on aluminium and glass shall be removed only after completion of work.
  • The contractor shall provide all labour, scaffolding, tools and plants, lifting arrangements and incidental materials required for complete installation as per approved drawings and directions of Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode Of Measurement & Payment
sections.description:
• Measurement shall be carried out in Square Metre (Sqm) of actual fixed window area measured overall inclusive of frame.
  • The rate shall include supply, fabrication and fixing of aluminium frame, anodizing/powder coating, glazing with 5 mm thick tinted float glass, rubber beading, sealants, screws, cleats, anchor fasteners, scaffolding, labour, tools and plants, all leads and lifts and incidental charges complete.
  • No separate payment shall be made for cutting, wastage, sealing, hardware, temporary supports or fixing accessories required for proper completion of work.

Description: Providing and fixing factory mold interlocking cement concrete paver blocks 80mm thick of M30 grade  approved make and shape including leveling the base with 50mm thick send bedding, laying the paver blocks in pattern as directed by the eic, filling the joint with send including watering, rolling and compecting with appropritate tools and plants, all conveyance including loading,unloading of blocks etc. complate in all.

sections.title: Material
sections.description:
• Factory made interlocking cement concrete paver blocks shall conform to IS 15658 and shall be of 80 mm thickness, minimum M-30 grade compressive strength, approved make, colour and shape as specified or directed by Engineer-in-Charge. The paver blocks shall be dense, uniform in texture, free from cracks, chipped edges and other manufacturing defects.
  • Sand used for bedding layer and joint filling shall conform to IS 383 and shall be clean, coarse, well graded and free from clay, silt and organic impurities. Water used for compaction and cleaning shall conform to IS 456.
  • All materials including paver blocks, sand and accessories shall be approved by Engineer-in-Charge before use.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall consist of providing and laying factory moulded interlocking cement concrete paver blocks over prepared surface in approved pattern and alignment.
  • The base surface shall first be properly dressed, cleaned and brought to required line, level and slope. A 50 mm thick bedding layer of approved coarse sand shall then be spread uniformly and levelled properly to receive paver blocks.
  • The interlocking paver blocks shall be laid manually over the prepared bedding layer in approved pattern and design as directed by Engineer-in-Charge. The blocks shall be placed closely with proper interlocking and alignment without disturbing bedding layer.
  • After laying, dry fine sand shall be spread over the surface and broomed into joints completely to fill all gaps between blocks. The surface shall then be lightly watered and compacted using plate compactor, mechanical vibrator or approved compaction equipment until the blocks are properly seated and uniformly interlocked.
  • Any damaged, broken or improperly aligned blocks shall be removed and replaced with new blocks at contractor’s cost. The completed surface shall be true to line, level and slope and free from undulations, depressions or loose joints.
  • The contractor shall include all loading, unloading, conveyance, handling, stacking, labour, tools and plants and all incidental operations necessary for satisfactory completion of work.

sections.title: Mode Of Measurement & Payment
sections.description:
• Measurement shall be carried out in Square Metre (Sqm) for actual area of paver blocks laid and accepted by Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall include supply and laying of 80 mm thick M-30 grade interlocking concrete paver blocks, preparation of surface, providing and spreading 50 mm thick sand bedding layer, laying in required pattern, joint filling with sand, watering, rolling, compacting with approved equipment, conveyance, loading, unloading, labour, tools and plants, all leads and lifts and incidental charges complete.
  • No separate payment shall be made for cutting of blocks, wastage, alignment corrections, edge adjustments or joint filling operations.

Description: Refixing of sheet Roofing including ridges, Hips, Valleys, Gutters etc. stacking of Serviceable materials and disposal of unserviceable materials with all lead & lift.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• Existing roofing sheets, ridges, hips, valleys, gutters, flashing pieces, hooks, bolts, nuts, washers and other accessories to be refixed shall conform to relevant IS specifications such as IS 277, IS 2062 and related roofing standards. Any replacement accessories required during refixing such as J-hooks, bitumen washers, polymer washers, clips, fasteners and sealants shall be of approved quality and compatible with existing roofing system.
  • All serviceable materials obtained during dismantling shall be carefully preserved and stacked properly at site as directed by Engineer-in-Charge. Unserviceable materials shall be removed and disposed off to approved location with all leads and lifts.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall consist of carefully dismantling and refixing existing sheet roofing including ridges, hips, valleys, gutters, flashing and allied accessories complete.
  • The roofing sheets and accessories shall be removed carefully without causing damage to reusable materials, supporting members or adjoining structures. Serviceable materials shall be cleaned and stacked systematically at site as directed by Engineer-in-Charge. Unserviceable and damaged materials shall be separated and disposed off outside the site to approved dumping location with all leads and lifts.
  • Before refixing, the supporting framework, purlins and contact surfaces shall be checked and cleaned properly. The roofing sheets shall then be refixed in correct alignment and slope with proper end laps and side laps using approved hooks, bolts, nuts, washers and fixing accessories to ensure watertight construction.
  • Ridges, hips, valleys and gutters shall be properly aligned and securely fixed to prevent leakage. Necessary sealing and adjustment works shall be carried out wherever required. The completed roof shall be firm, leakproof, properly aligned and free from visible defects, loose sheets or waviness.
  • The contractor shall provide all labour, scaffolding, staging, lifting arrangements, tools and plants and incidental operations complete for execution of work at all heights.

sections.title: Mode Of Measurement & Payment
sections.description:
• Measurement shall be carried out in Square Metre (Sqm) based on actual area of roofing refixed including ridges, hips, valleys and gutters.
  • The rate shall include dismantling, stacking of serviceable materials, disposal of unserviceable materials, refixing of roofing sheets and accessories, fixing materials, scaffolding, staging, labour, tools and plants, transportation, all leads and lifts and incidental charges complete.
  • No separate payment shall be made for overlaps, cutting, wastage, temporary supports, handling charges or alignment corrections required for satisfactory completion of work.

Description: Providing and fixing of Self Supported Structure Less curve Roofing systems with proper overlapping and seaming b/w different sheets without making holes or preventing the overturning the roof by wind addition made up from superior quality, structural grade steel. Base metal width 912 mm, Steel Grade : Grade D and Thickness 1.1 mm BMT, 0.95 mm to 1.05 mm APT with tolerance of +/- 0.04 mm for span up to 17 Mtr, Regular Modified Polyester Imported Color Coated Galvalume Steel having Profiled width of 625 mm +/-10mm. Design, supply, & fabrication of self supported single span arch roof fabricated from mechanically seamed manufactured by American Hydraulic Machines to profiles of Imported Galvalume Cold Rolled Structural Steel coils as per standard ASTM A792, Steel Sheet, Aluminum-Zinc Alloy Coated by Hot-Dip Process. The work should be carried out by specilialize and approved agency only. The rate of item is including fitting as per standard specification.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• The roofing system shall be a self-supported, structure-less curved (arch) roofing system made from superior quality structural grade steel, designed to span up to 17 meters without intermediate supports. The system shall consist of imported Galvalume cold rolled steel coils conforming to ASTM A792 standards, coated with aluminum-zinc alloy by hot-dip process for enhanced corrosion resistance and durability.
  • The base metal width shall be approximately 912 mm, with a profiled width of 625 mm ±10 mm. The steel sheet thickness shall be in the range of 1.1 mm (BMT) and 0.95 mm to 1.05 mm (APT) with a permissible tolerance of ±0.04 mm. The steel shall be of Grade D or equivalent structural grade, with regular modified polyester color coating of approved shade and finish.
  • The roofing sheets shall be mechanically curved and formed using specialized American hydraulic machines to achieve the required arch profile. The system shall be self-supporting and designed to withstand wind loads, live loads, and environmental conditions without the need for additional structural framework. Proper overlapping and seaming between sheets shall be ensured to provide a continuous, leakproof, and rigid roofing system without any perforations or holes in the sheets.
  • All materials shall be of approved make, sourced from specialized and approved agencies only, and shall comply with relevant industry standards and manufacturer specifications.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall include design, supply, fabrication, transportation, and installation of self-supported curved roofing sheets as per approved structural design and drawings. The installation shall be carried out by experienced and approved specialized agencies having expertise in such roofing systems.
  • The roofing sheets shall be erected and mechanically seamed using appropriate seaming machines to ensure tight interlocking between panels, providing structural integrity and weatherproofing. Proper alignment, curvature, and anchoring at supports (if any end supports are provided) shall be ensured to resist wind uplift and other environmental forces.
  • The sheets shall be laid in true alignment with proper overlapping and seaming, without any perforation or drilling on the sheet surface, thereby maintaining the integrity of the roofing system. Care shall be taken during handling and installation to avoid damage to the coating and profile of the sheets.
  • The completed roofing system shall be rigid, leakproof, aesthetically uniform, and capable of withstanding specified loads. All work shall be executed strictly as per manufacturer’s specifications, approved design, and directions of the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The roofing work shall be measured in square meters (Sqm) of finished curved roof area in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include the cost of design, materials, fabrication, transportation, machinery, erection, seaming, labour, and all incidental works required for complete installation.
  • No separate payment shall be made for curvature forming, seaming, overlaps, accessories, machinery usage, or labour, as these shall be deemed included in the item rate. The measurement shall be based on the actual plan projection or surface area as specified in the contract drawings and as accepted by the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one square Meter.

  • The sheets shall be laid in true alignment with proper overlapping and seaming, without any perforation or drilling on the sheet surface, thereby maintaining the integrity of the roofing system. Care shall be taken during handling and installation to avoid damage to the coating and profile of the sheets.
  • The completed roofing system shall be rigid, leakproof, aesthetically uniform, and capable of withstanding specified loads. All work shall be executed strictly as per manufacturer’s specifications, approved design, and directions of the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• Measurement shall be carried out in Square Metre (Sqm) based on actual finished area of Side Wall and Below Gable End Cladding fixed and accepted by Engineer-in-Charge.
  •  The rate shall include the cost of design, materials, fabrication, transportation, machinery, erection, seaming, labour, and all incidental works required for complete installation.
  • No separate payment shall be made for curvature forming, seaming, overlaps, accessories, machinery usage, or labour, as these shall be deemed included in the item rate. The measurement shall be based on the actual plan projection or surface area as specified in the contract drawings and as accepted by the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one square Meter.

Description: Providing upto  floor three  level precast cement concrete 60 mm thick double molded elevation jali Grade M-20 reinforced with 1.6mm dia. Mild steel wire including roughening both side molding with fixing adhesive material and  cleaning, finishing with proper colour shed in  2 coats of Weather proof paints of on  walls surface of required shade even shade after throughly brushing the surface to remove all dirts, mortar drops and remains of loose powdered materials etc. comp. as per directed by engg. incharge.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• The precast elevation jali shall be 60 mm thick, double moulded, and manufactured using design mix cement concrete of Grade M-20 conforming to IS 456. The jali shall be reinforced with 1.6 mm diameter mild steel wire mesh or reinforcement adequately embedded to prevent cracking and ensure structural stability.
  • The precast units shall be machine-cast or approved mould-cast, having uniform dimensions, sharp edges, smooth finish, and free from honeycombing, cracks, chips, or other defects. Both faces of the jali shall be roughened during casting to ensure proper bond with adhesive and surrounding finishes.
  • The fixing adhesive shall be polymer-modified tile/stone adhesive or approved cement-based adhesive suitable for precast concrete elements. The weatherproof paint shall be exterior grade acrylic weather-resistant paint of approved make and shade, capable of resisting ultraviolet rays, moisture, fungus, and atmospheric conditions.
  • All materials shall be new and of approved quality conforming to the relevant Indian Standards.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall include supplying, transporting, handling, and fixing the precast cement concrete jali up to the third floor level in true line, level, and plumb as per approved drawings and directions of the Engineer-in-Charge. The supporting surface shall be thoroughly cleaned and prepared before fixing.
  • The jali panels shall be fixed using approved adhesive, ensuring full contact between the panel and the supporting surface. Necessary temporary supports shall be provided until the adhesive has attained sufficient strength. The joints between adjacent panels shall be uniform, neatly finished, and properly aligned.
  • After completion of fixing, the entire surface shall be cleaned thoroughly by removing dust, mortar splashes, loose particles, and all foreign materials. The exposed surface shall then receive two coats of approved exterior weatherproof paint of the specified colour and shade, applied uniformly after proper surface preparation to obtain an even and durable finish.
  • The completed work shall be rigid, free from cracks, misalignment, or surface defects, and shall present a uniform architectural appearance to the satisfaction of the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode Of Measurement
sections.description:
• The precast cement concrete elevation jali shall be measured in square meters (Sqm) of the actual finished surface fixed in position, in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include manufacture, reinforcement, transportation, loading, unloading, lifting up to the third floor level, adhesive, cutting, fitting, alignment, jointing, cleaning, scaffolding, weatherproof painting, labour, tools and plants, and all materials and incidental operations necessary to complete the work.

  • No separate payment shall be made for reinforcement, adhesive, lifting, cutting, wastage, surface preparation, painting, scaffolding, or joint finishing, as these shall be deemed included in the item rate. The item shall be measured as completed and accepted by the Engineer-in-Charge.

Description: Providing and laying gang saw cut 30 mm thick, mirror polished pre moulded and pre polished machine cut granite stone of required size and shape of approved shade, colour and texture in footpath, flooring in road side plazas and similar locations, laid over 20mm thick base of cement mortar 1:4 (1 cement : 4 coarse sand) including grouting the joints with white cement mixed with matching pigment, epoxy touch ups etc. complete as per direction of Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• The flooring shall consist of 30 mm thick gang saw cut, machine-cut, pre-moulded, and pre-polished granite stone of approved shade, colour, texture, and quality. The granite shall be dense, hard, uniformly coloured, mirror polished, and free from cracks, cavities, veins, chips, stains, or any other defects. The stone shall be accurately cut to the required size and shape with true edges and square corners.
  • The granite shall be laid over a 20 mm thick bed of cement mortar in the proportion of 1:4 (1 cement : 4 coarse sand). Cement shall conform to relevant Indian Standards, and the sand shall be clean, well-graded coarse sand free from organic impurities. The joints shall be filled with white cement mixed with matching colour pigment to obtain a uniform appearance. Approved quality epoxy shall be used for touch-ups and minor surface corrections wherever required.
  • All materials shall conform to relevant standards including IS 456, IS 383, and IS 1200.

sections.title: Workmanship
sections.description:
• The work shall include preparation of the base surface, laying a uniform 20 mm thick cement mortar bed, and placing the granite slabs in true line, level, and slope as shown in the drawings or as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge. Each slab shall be firmly bedded and tapped into position to achieve full bearing without voids.
  • The joints between adjacent slabs shall be kept as thin and uniform as possible and filled with white cement paste mixed with matching pigment. Necessary cutting shall be carried out using mechanical cutting machines to achieve neat edges around columns, drains, walls, and other obstructions. Minor defects and pinholes shall be rectified with matching epoxy filler and the surface shall be cleaned thoroughly after completion.
  • The finished flooring shall be even, smooth, mirror polished, free from lippage, hollow sound, cracks, or stains, and shall present a uniform and aesthetically pleasing appearance. Proper curing and protection shall be provided until the flooring is ready for use.

sections.title: Mode Of Measurement
sections.description:
• The granite flooring shall be measured in square meters (Sqm) of the actual finished surface area laid in position, in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include the cost of granite stone, cement mortar bedding, white cement, matching pigments, epoxy touch-ups, cutting, dressing, laying, joint filling, curing, cleaning, labour, tools and plants, transportation, wastage, and all incidental works necessary to complete the item.

  • No separate payment shall be made for cutting, edge finishing, joint filling, epoxy repairs, polishing touch-ups, curing, or cleaning, as these shall be deemed included in the item rate. The item shall be measured as completed and accepted by the Engineer-in-Charge.

Description: Providing laying (to level or slopes) and jointing reinforced concrete Light duty non-pressure pipes I.S. class NP2 of the following internal diameter with collars and butt ends prepared for collar joints including testing of joints complete.(H) 900mm

sections.title: Materials
sections.description: • The reinforced concrete light duly non-pressure pipes of specified diameter shall conform to I.S. 458- 1971.

subsections.title: The pipes and fittings
subsections.description:
• The pipes and fittings after they are laid shall be tested to hydraulic pressure of 6 Kg./sq.cm.  The pipe shall be slowly and carefully charged with water allowing all air to escape and avoiding all stock and water hammer. The draw off takes and stock shall then be closed and specified hydraulic pressure shall be applied gradually. The pressure gauge must be accurate . The pipes and fittings shall be tested in sections as the work of laying proceeds, veeping the joints exposed for inspection during the testing.
  • The width and depth of the trenches shall be 30 cms. and depth of trenches 60 cms.
  • At joints, the trench width shall be widened where necessary. The work of excavation and refilling shall be done true to line, and gradient in accordance with general specifications of earth work in trenches.
  • The pipes shall be painted with two coats of anti-corrosive bitumastic paint of approved quality. The pipe shall be laid on a layer of 75 mm. sand filled upto 150 mm. above the pipe if so specified. The remaining portion of trench shall be then filled with excavated earth. The surplus earth shall be disposed of as directed.
  • When the excavation is done in rock the bottom shall be cut deep enough to permit the pipe to be laid and cushion of sand 75 mm. In case of bigger diameter of tube where the pressure is very high, thrust block of cement concrete 1:2:4(1 cement :2 coarse sand:4 grade stone aggregate of 20 mm. nominal size) shall be constructed on all bends to transmit the hydraulic thrust without in pairing the ground and spreading it over' a sufficient area if sospecified.
  • The Above Specifications shall be followed for work of trenches except that the excavation in trenches shall be for reinforced concrete pipes of specified diameter.

subsections.title: Laying
subsections.description:
• The pipes shall be lowered into the trenches carefully. Mechanical appliances may be used. Where necessary pipe shall be laid in straight lines or with easy curves and true to line and gradient as specified. The laying of pipe shall proceed upgrade of a slope. In the pipe spigot and socket joints, the socket ends shall face upstream. In case of pipes with joints to be made with loose collars, the collars shall be slipped on before the next pipe is laid.
  • In case where the foundation conditions are unusual such as the proximity of tress or holes, under existing or proposed alround in 150 mm. thick cement concrete 1:5:10 (1 cement : 5 fine sand : 10 graded stone aggregate 40 mm. nominal size) or compacted sand or gravel.
  • In case where the natural foundation is inadequate the pipes shall be laid either in concrete cradle, supported on proper foundations or on any other suitably designed structure. If concrete bedding is used, the depth of concrete, below bottom of the pipe shall be at least 1/4 of the internal dia metre of the pipe subject to a minimum of 100 mm. and a maximum 300 mm. The concrete shall be extended up the sides of the pipe at least to a distance of 1/4 of the outside diameter for pipes 300 mm. and over in diameter.
  • The pipes shall be laid in the concrete bedding before the concrete has set. Pipes laid in trenches in earth shall be bedded evenly and firmly and as far as upto the naunches of the pipe as to safely transmit the load expected from the back fill through the pipe to the bed. This shall be done either by excavating the bottom of the trenches to fit the curve of the pipe or by compacting the earth under a round curve of the pipe to form an even bed. Necessary provision shall be made for joints wherever required.

subsections.title: Jointing
subsections.description:
• The joints shall be done by. slipping the collar over and clear of the end of the pipe. The recess of the end of the pipe shall be filled with jute threading in hot bitumen. The new pipe shall then be brought forwarded until the bitumen ring in recess of first pipe is set into the recess of the second pipe.
  • The process shall be repeated for two or three pipes which shall then jacked up so as to thoroughly compress the bitumen. The quantity of jute and bitumen shall be just enough to fill the recess when pressed hard by jacking, care being taken that no offset of the jute braiding shall be just enough to fill the recess when pressed hard by jacking, care being taken that no offset of the jute braiding shall be visible either outside or inside of pipe. The collar shall then be set up over the joints covering equally both the pipe and leaving an even caulking space all round. Cement and sand mortar 1:1:1/2 shall then be well punched or pressed home with a caulking tool within this caulking space. Care shall be taken that the underside of the joints is properly filled with mortar.

subsections.title: Curing
subsections.description:
• Every joint shall be kept wet for about 10 day for maturing. The section of the pipe line laid and jointed shall be covered immediately to protect from weather effects. Minimum bore of 100 mm. is considered adequate.
  • The joints shall be left exposed for observation.

subsections.title: Testing of joints
subsections.description:
• Testing of Joints - After laying and jointing, the pipes and fittings shall be inspected under working conditions of pressure and flow. Any joint found leaking shall be redone, and all leaking pipes removed and replaced without extra cost.
  • The pipes and fittings after they are laid shall be tested to hydraulic pressure of 6 Kg./sq.cm.  The pipe shall be slowly and carefully charged with water allowing all air to escape and avoiding all stock and water hammer. The draw off takes and stock shall then be closed and specified hydraulic pressure shall be applied gradually. The pressure gauge must be accurate . The pipes and fittings shall be tested in sections as the work of laying proceeds, veeping the joints exposed for inspection during the testing.
  • The testing of joints shall be done as per above specifications except that the testing of reinforced concrete pipes shall be done.

sections.title: Mode measurements & payment
sections.description:
• The description of each item, shall unless otherwise stated, be held to include where necessary, conveyances and delivery, handling, unloading, storing,  fabrication hoisting, all labour for finishing to required shape and size setting fitting in position, straight, cutting and waste, return of packing etc.
  • The length shall be measured on running metre basis of finished work. The length shall be taken along the centre line of the pipe and fittings. The pipes fixed to walls, ceiling, floors etc. shall be measured and paid under this item.
  • All the work shall be measured in decimal system as fixed in its place, subject to tolerance given below unless otherwise stated.
    • [i] Dimension shall be measured to the nearest 0.01 metre.
    • [ii] Area shall be worked out to the nesrest 0.01 Sq.mt.
  • In case of fittings of unequal bore, the largest bore shall be measured for the test.
  • Testing of pipe lines, fittings and joints included for providing all plant and appliances necessary for obtaining access to the work to be tested and carrying out the tests.
  • The rate include painting of pipes and sand filling all round tubes for which separate payment shall not be made. The length shall be measured on running metre basis.
  • The Above Specifications shall be followed except that the rate includes for laying to level or slope in trenches etc. (measured separately), making the joints as indicated and testing to stand the water test.
  • No separate measurement shall be made for fittings, excavation, refilling, jointing materials, or labour, as these shall be deemed included in the item rate. The work shall be measured as completed and accepted as per the directions of the Engineer-in-Charge.
  • The measurements shall be net without any allowance for cutting and waste. The length of bends, junctions and other connections (measured along the centre line) shall be included in the total length of the pipes, the connections being numbered after-wards and paid for extra over pipes.
  • The size of the bends, junctions, etc. shall suit the size of pipe. The bore (internal diameter of pipe) shall be the criterion for payment .
  • Nothing extra shall be paid separately for the use of mechanical appliances, where necessary, as described above.
  • The rate shall be for a unit of one Running Meter.

Description: Providing, casting, supplying, transporting and fixing 80 mm thick self-supported Fiber Reinforced Concrete (FRC) decorative Jali/Screen Panels of approved design, pattern, size and shape, manufactured in factory under controlled conditions using white/grey cement, graded silica sand, alkali-resistant (AR) glass fibers, admixtures, pigments (if required) and other approved ingredients conforming to relevant standards. The FRC panels shall be of uniform thickness, free from cracks, honeycombing, warping and surface defects and shall be capable of withstanding all design loads including self-weight as per approved design.

sections.title: Materials
sections.description:
• The decorative Jali/Screen Panels shall be 80 mm thick, self-supported, factory manufactured Fiber Reinforced Concrete (FRC) panels of approved design, pattern, size, and shape. The panels shall be manufactured under controlled factory conditions using Ordinary Portland Cement or White Cement of approved grade, well-graded silica sand, alkali-resistant (AR) glass fibers conforming to relevant standards, approved mineral admixtures, pigments where specified, water-reducing admixtures, and other approved constituents. The FRC mix shall be proportioned to achieve the required compressive, flexural, and impact strength suitable for exterior architectural applications.

  • The panels shall be dense, homogeneous, accurately cast, and free from cracks, honeycombing, shrinkage, warping, surface blemishes, chipped edges, or any manufacturing defects. The finished surface shall be smooth, uniform, and true to the approved pattern. The panels shall be designed to safely withstand self-weight, wind load, handling stresses, and service loads without distortion or failure. All embedded inserts, lifting anchors, fixing brackets, stainless steel anchors, galvanized steel inserts, or other accessories required for installation shall be factory-fixed wherever applicable. All materials shall conform to relevant Indian Standards, including IS 456, IS 10262 and other applicable standards for Fiber Reinforced Concrete products.

sections.title: Mode Of Measurement
sections.description:
• The work shall include casting, curing, finishing, supplying, loading, transporting, unloading, handling, hoisting, and fixing the Fiber Reinforced Concrete decorative panels complete in position as per approved architectural drawings and the directions of the Engineer-in-Charge. The supporting structure shall be checked for correct alignment before installation.
  • The panels shall be fixed using approved stainless steel or galvanized steel brackets, anchor fasteners, inserts, bolts, chemical anchors, or other approved fixing systems as recommended by the manufacturer. All panels shall be erected in true line, level, plumb, and alignment with uniform joints. Necessary cutting, drilling, edge finishing, joint sealing with approved weather-resistant sealant, temporary supports, lifting arrangements, scaffolding, and access equipment shall be provided as required.

  • After installation, all exposed surfaces shall be thoroughly cleaned and any minor damages occurring during transportation or erection shall be repaired using approved matching repair materials. The completed installation shall be rigid, secure, aesthetically uniform, and free from cracks, deflection, vibration, stains, or visible defects, to the complete satisfaction of the Engineer-in-Charge.

sections.title: Mode Of Measurement
sections.description:
• The Fiber Reinforced Concrete decorative Jali/Screen Panels shall be measured in square meters (Sqm) of the actual exposed finished surface fixed in position, in accordance with IS 1200. The rate shall include design, mould preparation, casting, curing, reinforcement with alkali-resistant glass fibers, pigments, embedded inserts, lifting anchors, loading, transportation, unloading, hoisting, scaffolding, cutting, drilling, stainless steel or galvanized fixing hardware, brackets, anchor fasteners, sealants, alignment, cleaning, labour, tools and plants, wastage, and all materials and incidental operations required to complete the work.

  • No separate payment shall be made for moulds, embedded fittings, anchors, brackets, sealants, lifting arrangements, temporary supports, scaffolding, joint finishing, repairs, or any other accessories required for proper installation, as these shall be deemed included in the item rate. The item shall be measured as completed and accepted by the Engineer-in-Charge.
